惟化之入人者深，斯澤之所被者遠。夫道洽政治，化之入人者深矣，其澤生民而庇四夷也，有以哉！康王期畢公之意，若曰：至治無近效，王者務廣德。惟茲東郊，尤四方之極，中外之觀化恒於斯也。三后固協心同道矣，化之成也如何？蓋道以運治，而政爲之具，是澤所從出者也。道之運而不洽者，心之異向也。心同則施之有本末焉，精神心術之運，流通於歷世者，融液於無方，
translation_en:
… praised as a communion of spirit for a thousand ages. Suppose the ruler had said, "I am sage," and the minister had said, "I shall merely comply"; then the intention of perfecting assistance would have been ruined [? 慶, error for 廢]—how then could he have been Fu Yue? Alas! A ruler who accepts remonstrance guides his ministers to speak, and a minister who excels at remonstrance guides his ruler to listen. Was this not how Fu Yue and his sovereign met one another in spirit and bound one another through words!

"The Way penetrated and governance was well-ordered; beneficence moistened the living people, and the four barbarian tribes with left-fastened lapels all without exception relied upon them."
Hao Weide 郝維德
Associate Examiner, Instructor Liu 劉, comments: Its bearing is warm and pure, and its thread of argument is thoroughly coherent. The meaning of uniting in the Way to transform the people is encompassed within the essay. Record it.
Examiner, Instructor Lun 倫, comments: Neat, clear, and graceful.
Examiner, Instructor Qiao 譙, comments: Refined, serene, and elegant; it rewards repeated savoring.

Only when transformation enters deeply into people does the reach of beneficence extend far. Now, when the Way penetrates and governance is well-ordered, transformation has indeed entered deeply into people; that its beneficence moistens the living people and shelters the four barbarian tribes has good reason indeed! The intention of King Kang 康王 in placing his hopes in the Duke of Bi 畢公 was as if to say: Supreme governance has no immediate effect; a true king devotes himself to broadening his virtue. This eastern suburb in particular is the pivot of the four quarters, where those within and without constantly look to observe moral transformation. The Three Sovereigns truly united their minds and shared the same Way; how was their transformation brought to completion? For the Way is that by which governance is set in motion, and administrative measures are its instruments; it is from these that beneficence issues forth. When the Way is set in motion yet fails to penetrate everywhere, it is because minds are directed toward different ends. When minds are united, its implementation has both root and branch; the movement of spiritual energy and mental craft, flowing through successive generations, blends pervasively without bounds, …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
理道之洽盎如也政之紊而不治者道之多岐
也道同則爲之有次第焉紀綱法度之施整齊
於三世者脩舉而罔墜庶政之治秩如也道化
流行久而益遍舉凌德之民潤於膏澤蓋形神
俱釋而放心其盡泯也已德教孚洽久而彌深
胥滅義之衆潤於厚澤蓋身心咸裕而旌别可
無用也已由是四夷左衽其人雖王者所不臣
也然洛民化則四夷俱化傾心內向賴吾餘澤
之施者無間於華也其視四方無虞之日不尤
===
盛矣乎其俗雖冠裳所不被也然邇人安則遠
人亦安輸誠納款賴吾餘潤之布者無間於近
也其視大猷允升之世不益隆矣乎吁此化殷
之成也愼始和中者於今爲烈公之成終者於
前有光吾其樂觀厥成矣公也得無意於是耶
吾於是而知周過其曆也周以忠厚基命歷千
餘年而後大統克集蕞尒殷民治越三紀康王
猶惓惓於道洽政治之命無忿心無怠志何其
厚也是宜刑措而過曆也至四夷咸賴卽於澤
punctuated:
理道之洽，盎如也。政之紊而不治者，道之多岐也；道同，則爲之有次第焉。紀綱法度之施，整齊於三世者，脩舉而罔墜，庶政之治，秩如也。道化流行，久而益遍，舉凌德之民，潤於膏澤，蓋形神俱釋，而放心其盡泯也已。德教孚洽，久而彌深，胥滅義之衆，潤於厚澤，蓋身心咸裕，而旌别可無用也已。由是，四夷左衽，其人雖王者所不臣也，然洛民化則四夷俱化，傾心內向，賴吾餘澤之施者，無間於華也。其視四方無虞之日，不尤盛矣乎！其俗雖冠裳所不被也，然邇人安則遠人亦安，輸誠納款，賴吾餘潤之布者，無間於近也。其視大猷允升之世，不益隆矣乎！吁！此化殷之成也。愼始和中者，於今爲烈；公之成終者，於前有光。吾其樂觀厥成矣，公也得無意於是耶？
吾於是而知周過其曆也。周以忠厚基命，歷千餘年而後大統克集。蕞尒殷民，治越三紀，康王猶惓惓於道洽政治之命，無忿心，無怠志，何其厚也！是宜刑措而過曆也。至四夷咸賴，卽於澤
translation_en:
…and the pervasive harmony of principle and the Way is abundant indeed. When governance is disordered and not well-regulated, it is because the Way has diverged into many paths; when the Way is shared, action proceeds in proper sequence. The implementation of guiding norms and legal measures, brought into order across three reigns, is maintained and uplifted without lapse, and the ordering of the myriad affairs of governance is regular indeed. As the transforming influence of the Way flows forth, over time it becomes ever more widespread, so that all the people who once transgressed against virtue are steeped in rich beneficence; indeed, both form and spirit are set at ease, and their wayward minds completely vanish. As moral instruction inspires trust and harmony, over time it grows ever deeper, so that the multitude who once cast aside righteousness are steeped in generous beneficence; indeed, both body and mind are made tranquil and abundant, and distinguishing the good from the bad may no longer be needed. From this, as for the four barbarian peoples with their left-fastened robes—although those people are not treated as subjects by a true king, yet when the people of Luo are transformed, the four barbarian peoples are all transformed as well, turning their hearts inward in allegiance and relying on the bestowal of our overflowing beneficence no differently from the Chinese. Compared to the days when the four quarters were merely free from anxiety, is this not even more flourishing? Although their customs are untouched by cap and robe, yet when those near at hand are at peace, those far away are also at peace, offering their sincerity and submitting in tribute, relying on the spread of our overflowing moisture no differently from those who are near. Compared to an age when the great plan truly ascends, is this not even more glorious? Ah! This is the completion of transforming Yin. Those who were cautious at the beginning and harmonizing in the middle are glorious in the present; what the Duke brings to completion at the end sheds luster upon what came before. I shall happily behold its completion—could the Duke fail to set his mind upon this?

From this I know why Zhou surpassed its destined span of years. Zhou founded its Mandate on loyalty and generosity, passing through more than a thousand years before the Great Unity could be brought together. Over the tiny remnant people of Yin, governance had already passed through three twelve-year cycles, yet King Kang was still earnestly devoted to the charge that the Way be pervasive and governance well-ordered, without a resentful heart or an idle will—how generous indeed! Thus it was fitting that punishments were set aside and the dynasty surpassed its predicted span. As for all the four barbarian peoples relying upon them, this was obtained precisely from…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
潤生民得之彼海內粗安遂疲中國以事外夷
者於忠厚之道何如
詩
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
張輔辰
同考試官訓導周　批雍容深厚真得詩人祝君
語意而詞彩煒然醒心奪目
考試官教諭倫　批刊削枝蔓旨趣淵永
考試官教諭譙　批格整詞能
===
詩人願王嗣之多德足以宜其位也夫王嗣天
下之本也多而且賢王者之福孰大於此哉想
其答鳬鷖之意若曰吾王備假樂之德而膺保
右之命固將合萬世之福以爲福者其可願何
如哉彼王者之子孫君王之統繫焉然非多不
足以盛其傳非德不足以宜其任也吾願吾王
福在子孫其多則千億焉太和之在宇宙者萃
於我周益以衍螽斯之慶忠厚之傳先世者流
於今日益以兆麟趾之祥帝王相傳以敬者也
punctuated:
潤生民得之。彼海內粗安，遂疲中國以事外夷者，於忠厚之道何如？

詩
子孫千億，穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。
張輔辰
同考試官訓導周　批：雍容深厚，真得詩人祝君語意，而詞彩煒然，醒心奪目。
考試官教諭倫　批：刊削枝蔓，旨趣淵永。
考試官教諭譙　批：格整詞能。

詩人願王嗣之多，德足以宜其位也。夫王嗣，天下之本也。多而且賢，王者之福孰大於此哉！想其答《鳧鷖》之意，若曰：吾王備假樂之德，而膺保右之命，固將合萬世之福以為福者，其可願何如哉！彼王者之子孫，君王之統繫焉。然非多不足以盛其傳，非德不足以宜其任也。吾願吾王，福在子孫，其多則千億焉。太和之在宇宙者，萃於我周，益以衍《螽斯》之慶；忠厚之傳先世者，流於今日，益以兆《麟趾》之祥。帝王相傳以敬者也，
translation_en:
… saturating the living people. As for those who, once the realm within the seas is barely at peace, immediately exhaust the Central Kingdom in order to deal with foreign barbarians—how does that compare to the Way of loyalty and generosity?

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"Look at his sons and grandsons, in thousands and hundreds of thousands; / Reverent, august, / Well suited to be lords, well suited to be kings." [Ode 249, Jia le]
By Zhang Fuchen

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhou, comments: Graceful, poised, and deeply substantial, it truly captures the tone and intent of the poet's blessing for his sovereign, while its rhetorical brilliance shines forth, awakening the mind and dazzling the eyes.
Examiner, Instructor Lun, comments: Pruning away all superfluous branches and vines, its purport is profound and enduring.
Examiner, Instructor Qiao, comments: The structure is orderly and the diction capable.

The poet wishes that the king's heirs be numerous, and that their virtue be sufficient to suit their stations. Now, the royal heirs are the foundation of the realm. When they are both numerous and worthy, what blessing of a true king could be greater than this? Imagining the poet's intent in replying to the "Wild Ducks and Widgeons" (Fu yi), it is as if he said: Our king possesses the admirable virtue praised in "Felicitous and Joyous" (Jia le) and receives the Mandate that protects and assists him; since he will surely gather the blessings of ten thousand generations to make up his own blessing, what then should we wish for him? To the sons and grandsons of a true king is tied the succession of lords and kings. Yet unless they are numerous, it is insufficient to make their line flourish; unless they have virtue, it is insufficient to make them suited to their charges. I wish that for our king, blessing may reside in his sons and grandsons, so numerous as to reach thousands and hundreds of thousands! The supreme harmony present in the cosmos gathers in our Zhou house, all the more extending the felicity of the "Locusts" (Zhong si); the loyalty and generosity transmitted from former generations flows down to the present day, all the more heralding the auspiciousness of the "Unicorn's Hoof" (Lin zhi). Emperors and kings transmit their heritage through reverence; …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
皆穆穆而敬寅畏中存儼乎緝熙執競之遺矩
帝王世濟其美者也皆皇皇而美精純內蘊宛
乎徽柔於皇之懿範以之而屛翰一國非徒永
帶礪之盟已也而咸宜於其君焉以謹侯度以
揚王休一自敬美者出之周其世有顯諸侯乎
以之而君臨萬邦非徒膺曆數之傳已也而咸
宜於其王焉以建皇極以端元良一自敬美者
出之周其世有明天子乎至是則令顯之德自
今日而衍其休民人之宜垂萬世而永其烈天
===
之保右申命也不徒在吾王而且及其子孫矣
所謂干祿百福者孰加於此抑論周家王業之
興雖一德爲之本而周官之法度盡善盡美又
可守之萬世無斁者此則有家法以貽子孫固
宜其開有道之長也詩人福君既願其子孫之
敬美而必終之以率由舊章豈非欲其以敬法
祖而爲祈天永命之本歟彼後之人臣導其君
以祖宗不足法者抑獨何哉
數時繹思我徂維求定時周之命
punctuated:
皆穆穆而敬，寅畏中存，儼乎緝熙執競之遺矩；帝王世濟其美者也，皆皇皇而美，精純內蘊，宛乎徽柔於皇之懿範。以之而屛翰一國，非徒永帶礪之盟已也，而咸宜於其君焉，以謹侯度，以揚王休，一自敬美者出之，周其世有顯諸侯乎！以之而君臨萬邦，非徒膺曆數之傳已也，而咸宜於其王焉，以建皇極，以端元良，一自敬美者出之，周其世有明天子乎！至是，則令顯之德自今日而衍其休，民人之宜垂萬世而永其烈，天之保右申命也，不徒在吾王，而且及其子孫矣。所謂「干祿百福」者，孰加於此？抑論周家王業之興，雖一德爲之本，而《周官》之法度盡善盡美，又可守之萬世無斁者。此則有家法以貽子孫，固宜其開有道之長也。詩人福君，既願其子孫之敬美，而必終之以「率由舊章」，豈非欲其以敬法祖，而爲祈天永命之本歟？彼後之人臣，導其君以「祖宗不足法」者，抑獨何哉？
「數時繹思，我徂維求定，時周之命。」
translation_en:
…they are all solemn in their reverence, with respectful awe preserved within, dignified after the inherited standard of "continuing bright" and "holding fast with vigor"; as emperors and kings who across generations carry forward their excellence, they are all splendid in their beauty, with pure essence harbored inside, the very image of the admirable model of "gentle softness" and "oh, august!" With this to act as a screen and bulwark for a state, they do not merely perpetuate the covenant of the girdle-band and whetstone, but are all well-suited to be feudal lords—observing the regulations of princes and exalting the royal grace, all proceeding from their reverence and excellence. Shall not Zhou have illustrious feudal lords for generations! With this to rule over the myriad states, they do not merely receive the transmission of the heavenly succession, but are all well-suited to be kings—establishing the august ultimate and rectifying the supreme goodness, all proceeding from their reverence and excellence. Shall not Zhou have enlightened Sons of Heaven for generations! When it comes to this, the admirable and illustrious virtue extends its grace from this day onward, and the suitability toward the common people and officers hands down its glory perpetually for ten thousand generations. Heaven's protection, assistance, and repeated mandate rest not only upon our king, but extend also to his sons and grandsons. As for what is called "seeking emolument and a hundred blessings," what could surpass this? Furthermore, if we discuss the rise of the royal enterprise of the House of Zhou, although pure virtue served as its foundation, the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) were utterly good and utterly fine, such that they could be maintained for ten thousand generations without weariness. Having such family regulations to bequeath to their descendants, it was indeed fitting that they inaugurated the long endurance of a righteous reign. When the poet wished blessings upon his ruler, having prayed for the reverence and excellence of his sons and grandsons, he inevitably concluded with "following the old statutes"—was this not a desire that they should reverently emulate their ancestors as the basis for praying to Heaven for a perpetual mandate? As for those ministers of later ages who misled their rulers by saying that "the ancestors are not worth emulating," why on earth did they do so?

"Ever and again we cherish these thoughts; we go forth only to seek stability; this is the mandate of Zhou."

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
黃學皐
同考試官訓導周　批繹前功而布新命武王討
安天下盛心是作能發之詞旨溫潤讀之如封周人語也
考試官教諭倫　批典暢精融迥異他作
考試官教諭譙　批沉鬱豐腴
周王敘分封圖治之意而表其爲新命也蓋封
建者帝王之所以計安天下也周王以之其命
不維新乎頌大賚者曰帝王受命而興所丕承
者先德所利賴者功臣凡以爲天下計也今我
之大封何如哉彼開天下以一統之業者文王
勤止之功也所可繹思也貽天下以萬世之安
者亦文王勤止之心也所當仰體也我也以世
澤之在人者不能忘而布之爲大賚之典先烈
之垂後者可深念而公之爲懋賞之仁文王所
遺之土宇吾不敢私也而與有功者共理焉藩
屏之衆建維往求邦國之敉寧務使旣集之業
永綏於底定斯已矣文王所遺之人民吾不敢
專也而與有功者共治焉侯封之廣樹維往求
punctuated:
黃學皐
同考試官訓導周　批：繹前功而布新命，武王討安天下盛心，是作能發之。詞旨溫潤，讀之如封周人語也。
考試官教諭倫　批：典暢精融，迥異他作。
考試官教諭譙　批：沉鬱豐腴。

周王敘分封圖治之意，而表其爲新命也。蓋封建者，帝王之所以計安天下也。周王以之，其命不維新乎？頌《大賚》者曰：帝王受命而興，所丕承者先德，所利賴者功臣，凡以爲天下計也。今我之大封何如哉？彼開天下以一統之業者，文王勤止之功也，所可繹思也；貽天下以萬世之安者，亦文王勤止之心也，所當仰體也。我也，以世澤之在人者不能忘，而布之爲大賚之典；先烈之垂後者可深念，而公之爲懋賞之仁。文王所遺之土宇，吾不敢私也，而與有功者共理焉。藩屏之衆建，維往求邦國之敉寧，務使旣集之業，永綏於底定斯已矣。文王所遺之人民，吾不敢專也，而與有功者共治焉。侯封之廣樹，維往求
translation_en:
Huang Xuegao
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhou comments: Reflecting on past achievements to proclaim a new mandate—this essay successfully brings out King Wu's grand intention in planning [reading 討 as 計] for the peace of the world. Its diction and purport are warm and lustrous; reading it is like hearing the words spoken when enfeoffing the men of Zhou.
Examiner and Instructor Lun comments: Classical, fluent, refined, and harmonious, vastly different from other compositions.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: Deep, resonant, rich, and abundant.

The King of Zhou recounts the intent of parceling out fiefs to plan for good governance, and manifests it as a new mandate. Indeed, establishing feudal states is the means by which emperors and kings plan for the peace of the world. Since the King of Zhou employs this, is his mandate not thereby renewed? The one who composed the eulogy "Great Bestowal" (Dalai, i.e., the ode "Wu" in the Book of Odes) says: When emperors and kings receive the Mandate and rise, what they grandly inherit is the virtue of their predecessors, and whom they rely upon for benefit are their meritorious ministers—all in order to plan for the world. Now, what is the nature of my grand enfeoffment? That which opened up the enterprise of unification for the world was the achievement of King Wen's diligence; it is something to be ever reflected upon. That which bequeathed ten thousand generations of peace to the world was likewise the mind of King Wen's diligence; it is something to be reverently embodied. As for myself, because the generational blessings resting among the people cannot be forgotten, I spread them forth as the statute of the Great Bestowal; because the ancestral glories handed down to posterity are worthy of deep remembrance, I share them publicly as the benevolence of generous rewards. The territory left behind by King Wen, I dare not keep as my private possession, but govern it together with those who have merit. By establishing numerous buffer states, we go forth only to seek the pacification and tranquility of the states and realms, striving simply to ensure that the enterprise already accomplished may forever enjoy peace in settled stability. The people left behind by King Wen, I dare not monopolize for myself, but rule them together with those who have merit. By widely planting the fiefs of the feudal lords, we go forth only to seek …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
黎庶之乂安務使已附之衆永臻於克定斯已
矣以之酬勳卽以之保泰煥然昭代之王章以
之班爵卽以之求寧赫然更始之令典天以右
序命我周令我之肇舉乎分封者正以體天之
心也典制頒而天下一新其耳目非復由商之
舊矣文以新命造我周令我之創行乎大封者
正以顯文之謨也皇度彰而天下一易其心志
非復襲殷之故矣時哉我周之命也爾諸臣其
尚念之吁文王有創業垂統之功而武王爲乂
===
安長治之計此二后之所以竝可頌也抑論周
業之興自三后肇基至武王而大定然猶衆建
諸侯以爲萬世治安計信乎公天下之大端大
本莫封建若也後世治不師古裂封建而郡縣
之乃爲之說者曰封建非聖人意也其未知求
定之旨
春秋
秋公會宋人齊人伐徐莊公二十有六年
趙儒
punctuated:
黎庶之乂安，務使已附之衆永臻於克定斯已矣。以之酬勳，卽以之保泰，煥然昭代之王章；以之班爵，卽以之求寧，赫然更始之令典。天以右序命我周，令我之肇舉乎分封者，正以體天之心也。典制頒而天下一新其耳目，非復由商之舊矣。文以新命造我周，令我之創行乎大封者，正以顯文之謨也。皇度彰而天下一易其心志，非復襲殷之故矣。時哉，我周之命也！爾諸臣其尚念之。吁！文王有創業垂統之功，而武王爲乂安長治之計，此二后之所以竝可頌也。抑論周業之興，自三后肇基，至武王而大定，然猶衆建諸侯，以爲萬世治安計。信乎，公天下之大端大本，莫封建若也。後世治不師古，裂封建而郡縣之，乃爲之說者曰：「封建非聖人意也。」其未知求定之旨。

《春秋》
秋，公會宋人、齊人伐徐。莊公二十有六年。
趙儒
translation_en:
… the peace and security of the common people, ensuring only that the multitudes who have already submitted forever attain complete stability, and nothing more. Using this to reward merit is precisely how we preserve great peace—resplendent are the royal statutes of an illustrious era! Using this to distribute noble ranks is precisely how we seek tranquility—glorious are the fine canons of a new beginning! Heaven gave the mandate to our Zhou in rightful succession; that I now initiate the investiture of fiefs is precisely to embody the mind of Heaven. When institutional regulations are promulgated, the eyes and ears of the world are completely renewed, no longer following the old ways of Shang. King Wen founded our Zhou with the new mandate; that I now institute this grand enfeoffment is precisely to manifest the plans of King Wen. When sovereign measures are displayed, the hearts and minds of the world are completely transformed, no longer inheriting the former practices of Yin. Timely indeed is the mandate of our Zhou! May all you ministers ever bear it in mind. Ah! King Wen had the merit of founding the enterprise and bequeathing the succession, while King Wu devised plans for peace, security, and enduring governance; this is why the two sovereigns may both be praised together. Furthermore, if we consider the rise of the Zhou enterprise, from the three former sovereigns who laid the foundation down to King Wu when it was grandly settled, they still established numerous feudal lords in order to plan for ten thousand generations of order and peace. Truly, as the great principle and fundamental basis for sharing the realm in common, nothing compares to feudal enfeoffment (fengjian). In later ages, governance did not take antiquity as its model, tearing apart the feudal system and turning it into commanderies and counties; yet those who make excuses for this say, "Feudal enfeoffment was not the intention of the sages." Surely they do not understand the purport of "seeking stability"!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In autumn, the Duke met with men of Song and men of Qi to attack Xu." (26th year of Duke Zhuang)
Zhao Ru 趙儒

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導靳　批　辭度森嚴詞彩鮮麗且能
緣正出奇若將旗鼓稱節制之兵矣取之
考試官教諭倫　批　調古氣舒麟經擅美
考試官教諭譙　批　整練不浮
春秋紀望國之用兵見其無可危之道焉天師
老勢孤兵家之大戒也魯之伐徐能不蹈此則
安得而危之甞聞徐戎合黨兵連曲阜之墟表
裏爲讎世稔東郊之患莊公連齊宋以會伐焉
我武既揚振旅言歸春秋宜以伐至矣而今獨
===
不書至何哉蓋聞至之者幸之也幸之者危之
也向使徐之伐也師困於久淹莊之行也勢衰
於寡助則春秋得不爲之危乎維兹以秋而伐
卽以秋而返而荷戈閫外者無東山杕杜之懷
也會齊以往復會宋以俱而授甲師中者多有
邦厥隣之助也出則張我魯之威歸則節我軍
之力師貴以律莊其有焉以此行兵而何潰散
之足虞乎伐以除門庭之難會以資犄角之勢
謀貴萬全莊其有焉以此制敵而何撓敗之足
punctuated:
同考試官訓導靳　批：辭度森嚴，詞彩鮮麗，且能緣正出奇，若將旗鼓，稱節制之兵矣。取之。
考試官教諭倫　批：調古氣舒，麟經擅美。
考試官教諭譙　批：整練不浮。

《春秋》紀望國之用兵，見其無可危之道焉。天師老勢孤，兵家之大戒也；魯之伐徐，能不蹈此，則安得而危之？甞聞徐、戎合黨，兵連曲阜之墟；表裏爲讎，世稔東郊之患。莊公連齊、宋以會伐焉。我武既揚，振旅言歸，《春秋》宜以「伐至」矣，而今獨不書「至」，何哉？蓋聞「至」之者，幸之也；幸之者，危之也。向使徐之伐也，師困於久淹；莊之行也，勢衰於寡助，則《春秋》得不爲之危乎？維兹以秋而伐，卽以秋而返，而荷戈閫外者，無《東山》、《杕杜》之懷也。會齊以往，復會宋以俱，而授甲師中者，多有邦厥隣之助也。出則張我魯之威，歸則節我軍之力；「師貴以律」，莊其有焉。以此行兵，而何潰散之足虞乎？伐以除門庭之難，會以資犄角之勢；謀貴萬全，莊其有焉。以此制敵，而何撓敗之足
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Jin, comments: Its diction and bearing are stern and rigorous, its verbal coloring bright andsplendid, and moreover it is able to bring forth the extraordinary from the orthodox; like a general with banners and drums, it may be called a well-disciplined force. Selected.
Examiner, Instructor Lun, comments: Its tone is ancient and its vital breath unhurried; it commands the beauties of the Unicorn Classic [Spring and Autumn Annals].
Examiner, Instructor Qiao, comments: Well-ordered and practiced, without superficiality.

When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the deployment of troops by a prestigious state [Lu], it shows that there was no way in which it could be considered imperiled. Now [reading 天 as 夫], an exhausted army and an isolated position are the great taboos of military strategists; if Lu, in attacking Xu, was able to avoid treading this path, then how could one deem it imperiled? One has heard that the Xu and the Rong joined in faction, their weapons reaching the precincts of Qufu; acting in collusion from within and without as enemies, for generations they ripened troubles on the eastern outskirts [cf. Book of Documents, "Speech at Bi"]. Duke Zhuang allied with Qi and Song to join in a punitive expedition against them. Once our martial prowess had been displayed and we ordered our troops to return home, the Spring and Autumn Annals ought to have recorded his arrival from the expedition, yet here alone it does not record "arrived"—why is this? Indeed, we hear that to record "arrived" is to count it fortunate; and to count it fortunate is to consider it to have been in peril. Suppose that in the expedition against Xu the army had been distressed by long delay, and that in Duke Zhuang's campaign his strength had been weakened by having few allies—then how could the Spring and Autumn Annals not have considered it perilous for him? Yet in this case, he set out to attack in autumn and returned in that very autumn, so that those who shouldered halberds beyond the threshold did not harbor the longings of the "Eastern Hills" (Dongshan) or "Solitary Russet Pear" (Didu) odes. He joined Qi to go forth, and further joined Song to proceed together, so that those who were issued armor in the ranks enjoyed abundant aid from friendly states and neighbors. Going forth, he extended the awe of our state of Lu; returning, he conserved the strength of our forces. "An army values discipline" [Book of Changes, Hexagram 7, Shi]—Duke Zhuang possessed this. Conducting military operations in this manner, what fear could there be of rout and dispersion? He launched the punitive expedition to remove the crisis at his own courtyard, and joined in coalition to avail himself of the advantage of mutual support (jijiao); strategy values complete security, and Duke Zhuang possessed this. Subduing the enemy in this manner, what [worry] could there be of defeat and setback…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
惠乎噫此一伐也昔嘗歷三時而後還君子以
爲殆矣今之役則非昔日所可同者師貞之吉
雖桓文之節制何加焉此一莊也往嘗提孤軍
而深入君子以爲危矣今之行則非往日所可
例者預定之策雖庸蜀之遠連曷過焉故春秋
謂是役也人無怨心師有同力武之善經也全
軍歸國則維其常而何以書至爲哉不然則前
此之伐戎春秋嘗紀其至矣而於今也奚以異
觀此可以知行兵之法矣雖然伐徐之年非即
伐戎之歲乎春出夏歸秋而又復出是魯師無
一暇日也齊人同會亦羌合之衆耳萬一資糧
扉屨之不備而厚誅於我是徐夷起於轂下而
戎兵接軫也不見執轅濤塗乎是故兵者聖人
所甚重毋謂其無危而輕出也
晉欒書帥師救鄭成公六年夏曹公孫會
自鄸出奔宋昭公二十年
滕如蛟
同考試官訓導靳　批　尚功崇賢春秋厚道子能
punctuated:
惠乎？噫！此一伐也，昔嘗歷三時而後還，君子以爲殆矣；今之役，則非昔日所可同者，師貞之吉，雖桓、文之節制何加焉？此一莊也，往嘗提孤軍而深入，君子以爲危矣；今之行，則非往日所可例者，預定之策，雖庸、蜀之遠連曷過焉？故《春秋》謂是役也，人無怨心，師有同力，武之善經也。全軍歸國，則維其常，而何以書至爲哉？不然，則前此之伐戎，《春秋》嘗紀其至矣，而於今也奚以異？觀此可以知行兵之法矣。雖然，伐徐之年，非即伐戎之歲乎？春出夏歸，秋而又復出，是魯師無一暇日也。齊人同會，亦羌合之衆耳，萬一資糧扉屨之不備，而厚誅於我，是徐夷起於轂下，而戎兵接軫也，不見執轅濤塗乎？是故兵者聖人所甚重，毋謂其無危而輕出也。

晉欒書帥師救鄭（成公六年）　夏曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋（昭公二十年）
滕如蛟
同考試官訓導靳　批：尚功崇賢，《春秋》厚道。子能
translation_en:
…worry about[?] [reading 惠 as 患]? Alas! As for such an expedition, in the past troops once passed through three seasons before returning, which the gentleman considered perilous; yet today's campaign cannot be equated with those of bygone days. With the auspiciousness of a righteous army, even the disciplined command of Dukes Huan and Wen could add nothing to it! As for this same Duke Zhuang, in the past he once led a lone army deep into enemy territory, which the gentleman considered dangerous; yet today's march cannot be judged by the precedents of former days. With a prearranged strategy, even the distant alliance of Yong and Shu could not surpass it! Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) holds that in this campaign, the men bore no resentment and the troops shared a united strength—the finest principle of martial affairs. Returning to the state with the entire army intact was thus only the normal course of events, so why record their arrival? Otherwise, in the previous campaign against the Rong, the Spring and Autumn Annals did record their arrival; why then treat the present case differently? Observing this, one may understand the art of conducting war. Even so, was not the year of the campaign against Xu the very same year as the campaign against the Rong? Going forth in spring, returning in summer, and going forth once again in autumn meant that the army of Lu did not have a single day of rest. The men of Qi who joined the assembly were likewise merely a motley crowd[?] [reading 羌合 as 苟合/烏合]. If by any chance provisions and straw sandals were unprepared, and heavy demands were exacted upon us, then the Xu barbarians would rise up right beneath our chariot wheels while the Rong troops followed closely at our heels—have you not seen the seizure of Yuan Taotu? For this reason, warfare is something the sage treats with the utmost gravity; do not say there is no danger and lightly send troops forth.

"Luan Shu of Jin led a force to rescue Zheng" (6th year of Duke Cheng); "In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song" (20th year of Duke Zhao).
Teng Rujiao 滕如蛟

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
推原而典核之而旨遠詞文尤稱奇品
考試官教諭倫　批　嚴峻中有博雅氣象
考試官教諭譙　批　開闔得法組織尤精
春秋紀事嘉世勳而重賢裔焉勳臣者國之輔
賢臣者國之紀也錄其後以示勸春秋義與且
夫故國恒稱乎世臣用人必貴於公選若宋之
華孫藉寵專行春秋無取焉然不曰晉有欒書
者典兵三世而光榮不墜乎曰欒氏之胄不以
世而以勳也彼書之先有欒枝與盾者曳柴僞
遁効力於城濮之師固壘深溝宣猷於令狐之
役其功有足稱矣績載旂常而緒垂奕葉苟無
失德猶當百世祀之況有賢如書者可俾之無
位耶令書也從三卿而主善不遷戮以罷民出
有制闔之勞內昭繩武之烈枝盾之動得書而
有光矣使書也怙寵而擅權晉人廢之不暇誰
能與之又不曰曹有公孫會者鎮國再世而爵
籍未泯乎曰公孫之胄不以世而以賢也彼會
之先有公子喜時者守節逃榮義激於君執之
punctuated:
推原而典核之，而旨遠詞文，尤稱奇品。
考試官教諭倫　批：嚴峻中有博雅氣象。
考試官教諭譙　批：開闔得法，組織尤精。
《春秋》紀事，嘉世勳而重賢裔焉。勳臣者，國之輔；賢臣者，國之紀也。錄其後以示勸，《春秋》義與？且夫故國恒稱乎世臣，用人必貴於公選。若宋之華孫，藉寵專行，《春秋》無取焉。然不曰晉有欒書者，典兵三世而光榮不墜乎？曰：欒氏之胄，不以世而以勳也。彼書之先，有欒枝與盾者，曳柴僞遁，効力於城濮之師；固壘深溝，宣猷於令狐之役，其功有足稱矣。績載旂常，而緒垂奕葉，苟無失德，猶當百世祀之，況有賢如書者，可俾之無位耶？令書也，從三卿而主善，不遷戮以罷民，出有制闔之勞，內昭繩武之烈，枝、盾之動，得書而有光矣。使書也怙寵而擅權，晉人廢之不暇，誰能與之？又不曰曹有公孫會者，鎮國再世而爵籍未泯乎？曰：公孫之胄，不以世而以賢也。彼會之先，有公子喜時者，守節逃榮，義激於君執之
translation_en:
… trace its origins and verify it against the canons; with its far-reaching purport and refined diction, it may especially be called an extraordinary work.
Examiner and Instructor Lun comments: Within its strictness and rigor there is an air of broad learning and elegance.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: The opening and closing follow proper method, and the structure is especially exquisite.

In recording events, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) praises hereditary merit and attaches importance to the descendants of the worthy. Meritorious ministers are the bulwark of the state; worthy ministers are the mainstay of the state. Recording their descendants in order to demonstrate encouragement—is this not the righteous principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Moreover, an ancient state is always recognized by its hereditary ministers, yet in employing men one must prize impartial selection. In a case like Huasun of Song, who relied on favor to act on his own authority, the Spring and Autumn Annals found nothing to approve in him. Yet does it not speak of Luan Shu 欒書 of Jin, whose family commanded the army for three generations without its glory falling into decline? I say: the descendants of the Luan clan held their position not by hereditary right alone, but by merit. Among Shu's forebears were Luan Zhi 欒枝 and Luan Dun 欒盾: one dragged brushwood in a feigned flight, exerting his strength in the campaign at Chengpu; the other fortified ramparts and deepened trenches, displaying his strategy in the battle of Linghu. Their achievements were well worthy of praise. Their deeds were inscribed on the royal banners, and their lineage was handed down through successive generations. If their descendants had no lapses in virtue, they ought still to receive sacrifices for a hundred generations—how much more when there was a worthy man like Shu! Could he be left without office? Now as for Shu [reading 令 as 今], he followed the three ministers and held fast to what was good, refusing to shift hostilities and exhaust the people; abroad he bore the toil of commanding the army in the field [reading 闔 as 閫], and at home he made bright the illustrious enterprise of following in his ancestors' footsteps. The merit [reading 動 as 勳] of Zhi and Dun gained luster through Shu. Had Shu presumed upon favor and usurped power, the men of Jin would scarcely have had time enough to depose him—who would have approved of him? And again, does it not speak of Gongsun Hui 公孫會 of Cao, whose line stabilized the state for two generations with its noble rank and register unextinguished? I say: the descendants of the Gongsun held their position not by hereditary right alone, but by worthiness. Among Hui's forebears was Prince Xishi 公子喜時, who maintained his integrity and fled worldly栄, his righteousness aroused on the [day] his lord was seized…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
日全身致邑名高於國亂之時其節有足尚矣
祚庇後昆而義風百世茍無墜緒猶當十世宥
之況有賢如會者可使之喪位耶今會也放逐
而待命於郊流離而不失其正內無懟主之嫌
遠光讓國之節子臧之義以會而不替矣使會
也凌德而悖道曹人逐之恐後誰其憫之要之
有欒氏之功而後可爲世臣有子臧之賢而後
可膺世爵彼華孫者逆臣之裔視書與會何如
者可委以兵權使之專行不忌耶抑嘗聞鯀殛
===
而禹興蔡叔流而仲以祗德顯聖賢固不繫於
世類也曹會既奔之後不聞代興欒黶不克負
荷而三世之勳遂殞亦何取於功臣之胄哉是
故官人之法惟其人不惟其類
禮記
四者君以正用之故君者立於無過之地
也
楊先春
同考試官訓導董 批此題作者類多牽綴是篇
punctuated:
日，全身致邑，名高於國亂之時，其節有足尚矣。祚庇後昆，而義風百世，茍無墜緒，猶當十世宥之，況有賢如會者，可使之喪位耶？今會也，放逐而待命於郊，流離而不失其正，內無懟主之嫌，遠光讓國之節，子臧之義以會而不替矣。使會也凌德而悖道，曹人逐之恐後，誰其憫之？要之，有欒氏之功而後可爲世臣，有子臧之賢而後可膺世爵。彼華孫者，逆臣之裔，視書與會何如者？可委以兵權，使之專行不忌耶？抑嘗聞鯀殛而禹興，蔡叔流而仲以祗德顯，聖賢固不繫於世類也。曹會既奔之後，不聞代興；欒黶不克負荷，而三世之勳遂殞，亦何取於功臣之胄哉？是故官人之法，惟其人，不惟其類。

《禮記》：「四者，君以正用之，故君者立於無過之地也。」
楊先春
同考試官訓導董批：此題作者類多牽綴，是篇
translation_en:
… [on the] day [his lord was captured], and preserved himself while surrendering his fief, his reputation standing high in a time of state turmoil; his integrity was truly worthy of esteem! His blessings sheltered his descendants, and his righteousness inspired a hundred generations. As long as they did not ruin their heritage, they ought to be pardoned for ten generations—how much more so when there is a worthy man like Gongsun Hui 公孫會; could one allow him to lose his position? Now as for Hui, when banished he awaited orders in the suburbs, and though displaced in exile he did not lose his rectitude. Inwardly he bore no suspicion of resenting his ruler, and across the generations he brought glory to the integrity of yielding the state; the righteousness of Zizang 子臧 did not decline thanks to Hui. Had Hui transgressed virtue and rebelled against the Way, the people of Cao 曹 would have driven him out fearing only to be too slow—who would have pitied him? In sum, only when there is the merit of the Luan 欒 clan may one be a hereditary minister, and only when there is the worthiness of Zizang may one receive a hereditary peerage. As for that Huasun 華孫, the descendant of a traitorous minister, how does he compare with Luan Shu 欒書 and Gongsun Hui? Could he be entrusted with military authority and allowed to act unilaterally without restraint? Moreover, I have heard that Gun 鯀 was executed yet Yu 禹 rose up, and Cai Shu 蔡叔 was banished yet Cai Zhong 蔡仲 became illustrious through his reverent virtue; sages and worthies are certainly not bound to hereditary lineage. After Hui of Cao fled, nothing was heard of a successor rising in his place; Luan Yan 欒黶 was unable to bear the burden of his house, and the merit of three generations thus perished. What, then, is to be gained from the descendants of meritorious ministers? Therefore, the method of appointing men to office depends solely on the man, not on his lineage.

Record of Rites (Liji): "These four things, the ruler employs them with correctness; therefore the ruler stands in a place free from fault."
By Yang Xianchun 楊先春.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
只從本色中指點出來精神態度種種過別
考試官教諭倫　批發端本贊化意明徹可愛
考試官教諭譙　批詞藻郁然
記者推人君贊化之道而端本爲要焉蓋君身
萬化之本也舉天地父師而正用之非立於無
過烏能然哉今夫人君承天地之統據父師之
尊其道至正而其本在身是故天生時地生財
父師則以養以教者也四者皆聯屬於君身而
惟君所用之然用不以正則亦不爲吾之用矣
===
君人將以其身爲天下用必正其身以用天下
以成天地之能本皇極之攸建者以化裁之爲
明時爲阜財而覆載之有偏者吾取而兼用之
用於吾之正也以終父師之功本元良之克端
者以左右之爲厚生爲正德而生成之未全者
吾取而咸用之亦用於吾之正也故君者匪徒
立乎崇高之位已也三極之用備於身必納此
身於軌物之中不徒立乎兆庶之上已也萬化
之原起於身務範其身於中正之域天地以正
punctuated:
只從本色中指點出來，精神態度，種種過別。
考試官教諭倫　批：發端本贊化意，明徹可愛。
考試官教諭譙　批：詞藻郁然。
記者推人君贊化之道，而端本爲要焉。蓋君身，萬化之本也。舉天地父師而正用之，非立於無過，烏能然哉？今夫人君承天地之統，據父師之尊，其道至正，而其本在身。是故天生時，地生財，父師則以養以教者也。四者皆聯屬於君身，而惟君所用之。然用不以正，則亦不爲吾之用矣。君人將以其身爲天下用，必正其身以用天下。以成天地之能，本皇極之攸建者以化裁之，爲明時、爲阜財，而覆載之有偏者，吾取而兼用之，用於吾之正也；以終父師之功，本元良之克端者以左右之，爲厚生、爲正德，而生成之未全者，吾取而咸用之，亦用於吾之正也。故君者，匪徒立乎崇高之位已也，三極之用備於身，必納此身於軌物之中；不徒立乎兆庶之上已也，萬化之原起於身，務範其身於中正之域。天地以正
translation_en:
…simply points out the meaning from the inherent nature of the text itself; in spirit and bearing, every aspect stands far apart from the ordinary.
Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: It brings out the meaning of rectifying the root and assisting transformation, with admirable clarity and penetration.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: Richly elegant in diction.
The compiler of the Record deduces the Way by which a ruler assists in cosmic transformation, holding that rectifying the fundamental root is essential. Indeed, the ruler's own person is the root of the myriad transformations. To take up Heaven, Earth, parent, and teacher and employ them with rectitude—if he does not stand in a place free of transgression, how could he do so? Now, the ruler inherits the succession of Heaven and Earth and occupies the exalted position of parent and teacher; his Way is supremely upright, and its root lies in his own person. Therefore, Heaven produces the seasons, Earth produces wealth, and parents and teachers are those who nurture and instruct. All four are joined to the ruler's person, and it is solely for the ruler to employ them. Yet if he does not employ them with rectitude, they will not serve his use. When one who rules over men is about to put his own person to the service of the world, he must first rectify his person in order to employ the world. To bring to completion the capacities of Heaven and Earth, he bases himself on the establishment of the August Ultimate to transform and regulate them—clarifying the seasons and making wealth abundant; and where the sheltering of Heaven and the bearing up of Earth have any partiality, I take them both and employ them together, employing them through my own rectitude. To bring to consummation the achievements of parent and teacher, he bases himself on the ability to rectify supreme goodness in order to assist and guide them—enriching livelihood and rectifying virtue; and where birth and completion are not yet whole, I take them all and employ them in full, likewise employing them through my own rectitude. Thus, the ruler does not merely stand in an exalted position and nothing more: the functions of the Three Ultimates are complete within his person, so he must place this person within the bounds of regular norms. He does not merely stand above the millions of common people and nothing more: the source of the myriad transformations arises from his person, so he must strive to mold his person within the realm of impartiality and rectitude. If Heaven and Earth are [employed] with rectitude…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
用即寡過於身君德猶未純也其所置身者必
於無偏無黨之地焉蓋所立正而後所用正合
天地之用而善用之者此也父師以正用即補
過於身君道猶未光也其所安身者必於無反
無側之地焉蓋立無過斯用無不正聯父師之
用而咸用之者此也苟以有過之身爲四者之
用奚其正蓋君之於民有天地之尊有父師之
親故君之立身必建之而不悖俯之而不怍所
用者四所以用者一正而已矣然是正也天地
===
之道也父之生師之教皆是物也顧人君中天
地爲綱常主所用者甚大所立者尤宜慎記者
舉而歸之正推君道合天道也然務學要矣親
賢急焉君天下者愼諸
詩言其志也歌咏其聲也舞動其容也三
者本於心然後樂器從之
趙　捷
同考試官訓導董　批
有雅趣者擲之作金石聲矣用式多士　繡意摘詞精融俊爽文之
punctuated:
用，即寡過於身，君德猶未純也。其所置身者，必於無偏無黨之地焉。蓋所立正而後所用正，合天地之用而善用之者，此也。父師以正用，即補過於身，君道猶未光也。其所安身者，必於無反無側之地焉。蓋立無過斯用無不正，聯父師之用而咸用之者，此也。苟以有過之身爲四者之用，奚其正？蓋君之於民，有天地之尊，有父師之親。故君之立身，必建之而不悖，俯之而不怍。所用者四，所以用者一，正而已矣。然是正也，天地之道也，父之生、師之教，皆是物也。顧人君中天地、爲綱常主，所用者甚大，所立者尤宜慎。記者舉而歸之正，推君道合天道也。然務學要矣，親賢急焉，君天下者愼諸。
詩，言其志也；歌，咏其聲也；舞，動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。
趙捷
同考試官訓導董批：繡意摘詞，精融俊爽，文之有雅趣者，擲之作金石聲矣，用式多士。
translation_en:
…function through rectitude; yet even if one merely reduces faults in one's person, the ruler's virtue is still not pure. Where he places himself must be on ground free of partiality and partisanship. For only when where he stands is upright will what he employs be upright; this is what it means to unite the functions of Heaven and Earth and employ them well. Father and teacher function through rectitude; yet even if one merely mends faults in one's person, the ruler's Way is still not illustrious. Where he rests himself must be on ground free of perversity and unevenness. For when one stands without fault, there is nothing in one's functioning that is not upright; this is what it means to join the functions of father and teacher and employ them all. If one were to use a fault-ridden person to carry out the functions of these four, how could that be upright? Indeed, in his relation to the people, the ruler has the exaltedness of Heaven and Earth and the closeness of father and teacher. Therefore, in establishing himself, the ruler must set himself up without contravening Heaven and Earth, and look down without feeling shame before father and teacher. What he employs are four, yet that by which he employs them is one: rectitude, and nothing more. Yet this rectitude is the Way of Heaven and Earth; the life given by the father and the teaching of the teacher are all this very thing. Considering that the ruler stands at the center of Heaven and Earth and is the master of the cardinal moral bonds and constant virtues, what he employs is عظيم (very great), and how he establishes himself ought especially to be attended to with caution. The compiler of the Record sums this up and attributes it to rectitude, extending the Way of the ruler to accord with the Way of Heaven. Yet devoting oneself to learning is essential, and drawing close to the worthy is urgent; let him who rules All under Heaven be cautious in this!

"Poetry expresses the intent; song prolongs the voice; dance animates the bearing. All three originate in the mind, and only afterward do the musical instruments follow them."
Zhao Jie 趙捷
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Dong 董 comments: With embroidered ideas and plucked phrases, refined, harmonious, brisk, and clear—this is writing of elegant sensibility; cast it to the ground and it rings with the sound of metal and stone! It is selected to serve as a model for the many scholars.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭倫　批　語意婉足神彩媚人
考試官教諭譙　批　義精詞朗
記者論樂而推其所本焉夫心樂之本也本諸
心而器從之此樂之所以爲華也記樂者蓋謂
德蘊於心樂被於器其機常相通而其本自有
在也所謂樂爲德之華者何哉彼播之詩歌形
之舞蹈皆樂也是未涉於器者也詩何爲也志
動於中機不容默而詩也者則言其欲言之志
也歌何爲也言不盡志言因以永而歌也者則
===
詠其未竟之聲也舞何以動也歌而成聲即動
而成象舞蹈之發一德容之動也夫由詩而歌
而舞其愈發而愈暢者是樂之華也由容而聲
而志其愈約而愈精者皆心之運也是三者本
於心也涵之爲聲氣之元淵然深矣然後假善
鳴者以鳴焉而金石從之所以合兩階而交應
者皆是心之流通奕而爲文者也蘊之爲性天
之妙盎然融矣然後假有聲者以聲焉而絲竹
從之所以比五色而成文者皆是心之和動昭
punctuated:
考試官教諭倫　批：語意婉足，神彩媚人。
考試官教諭譙　批：義精詞朗。
記者論樂，而推其所本焉。夫心，樂之本也。本諸心而器從之，此樂之所以爲華也。記樂者蓋謂：德蘊於心，樂被於器，其機常相通，而其本自有在也。所謂「樂爲德之華」者，何哉？彼播之詩歌，形之舞蹈，皆樂也，是未涉於器者也。詩何爲也？志動於中，機不容默，而詩也者，則言其欲言之志也。歌何爲也？言不盡志，言因以永，而歌也者，則詠其未竟之聲也。舞何以動也？歌而成聲，即動而成象，舞蹈之發，一德容之動也。夫由詩而歌而舞，其愈發而愈暢者，是樂之華也；由容而聲而志，其愈約而愈精者，皆心之運也。是三者本於心也。涵之爲聲氣之元，淵然深矣；然後假善鳴者以鳴焉，而金石從之，所以合兩階而交應者，皆是心之流通，奕而爲文者也。蘊之爲性天之妙，盎然融矣；然後假有聲者以聲焉，而絲竹從之，所以比五色而成文者，皆是心之和動，昭
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: The phrasing and meaning are gracefully complete, and the spirit and brilliance are captivating.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: The meaning is precise and the diction clear.
The recorder of the Rites discusses music and traces it to its root. Now the mind is the root of music. When it is rooted in the mind and the musical instruments follow it, this is how music becomes the efflorescence [of virtue]. He who recorded the discourse on music meant to say: Virtue is stored within the mind, and music is imparted to the instruments; their subtle springs constantly communicate with one another, yet its root naturally has its own place. What is meant by saying that "music is the efflorescence of virtue"? That which is disseminated in poetry and song and given form in dance is all music, even before it involves musical instruments. What is poetry for? When intent stirs within, its impulse cannot remain silent; thus poetry is that which expresses in words the intent one wishes to speak. What is song for? When words do not fully exhaust the intent, the words are consequently prolonged; thus song is that which chants the unexhausted sound. Why does dance move? When chanting forms a melody, movement immediately forms a figure; the manifestation of dance is entirely the movement of virtuous demeanor. Now, proceeding from poetry to song and to dance, that which becomes ever more expansive as it is expressed is the efflorescence of music; proceeding backward from demeanor to sound and to intent, that which becomes ever moreEssential and refined as it is condensed is entirely the operation of the mind. Therefore, these three are rooted in the mind. Cherished within as the primal source of sound and vital breath, it is abyssally deep; only then does it borrow things good at sounding to give it voice, and bells and chimes follow it—whereby they harmonize between the two staircases and respond to one another is entirely the flowing circulation of this mind, shining forth as patterned elegance. Stored within as the subtlety of innate nature and Heaven, it is brimmingly harmonious; only then does it borrow things possessing sound to give it voice, and strings and bamboo pipes follow it—whereby they align the five tones to form patterned elegance is entirely the harmonious movement of this mind, manifesting…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而爲華者也豈徒器焉而已耶是心爲無聲之
樂而因樂以宣之則心有所寄樂爲形下之器
而有心以本之則器因以神外心以言樂本之
則無矣如樂何信乎樂爲德之華也然必養吾
心之太和以端作樂之本然後氣和形和而天
地之和應之古聖王所以陶性靈移風俗者其
德茂其本深也豈鍾鼓云乎哉彼房中之樂七
德之舞非不從之以器也而古樂之不復者則
徒以其器也是故君子反情以和志
===
第貳場
論
帝王心法之要
鄒祖孔
同考試官教諭劉　批　此作命意精深根極理要
縱横辯博馳騁不羈至以天下治其心立論尤奇偉卓絕非大
手筆不能
考試官教諭倫　批　氣格高古議論剴切末歸
重守成是通達治體者
punctuated:
而爲華者也。豈徒器焉而已耶？是心爲無聲之樂，而因樂以宣之，則心有所寄；樂爲形下之器，而有心以本之，則器因以神。外心以言樂，本之則無矣，如樂何？信乎，樂爲德之華也！然必養吾心之太和，以端作樂之本，然後氣和、形和，而天地之和應之。古聖王所以陶性靈、移風俗者，其德茂，其本深也，豈鍾鼓云乎哉？彼房中之樂、七德之舞，非不從之以器也，而古樂之不復者，則徒以其器也。是故君子反情以和志。

第貳場
論
《帝王心法之要》
鄒祖孔
同考試官教諭劉批：此作命意精深，根極理要，縱横辯博，馳騁不羈。至「以天下治其心」，立論尤奇偉卓絕，非大手筆不能。
考試官教諭倫批：氣格高古，議論剴切，末歸重守成，是通達治體者。
translation_en:
…and shines forth as its splendor. How could it merely be a matter of instruments and nothing more? Thus, the mind is soundless music, and when expressed through music, the mind has something in which to lodge; music consists of concrete instruments below the level of form, and when rooted in the mind, the instruments thereby become numinous. To speak of music apart from the mind is to lack its root—what then can one do with music? Truly, music is the splendor of virtue! Yet one must nourish the supreme harmony of one's own mind so as to rectify the root of making music; only then will vital energy be harmonious, bodily form be harmonious, and the harmony of Heaven and Earth respond to it. That whereby the ancient sage-kings molded innate sensibilities and transformed customs was the abundance of their virtue and the depth of their root—how could it merely be a matter of bells and drums? Those such as the "Music Within the Chambers" and the "Dance of the Seven Virtues" did not fail to accompany them with instruments, yet the reason ancient music was not restored was that they relied solely on its instruments. Therefore, the noble man returns to his genuine feelings in order to harmonize his will.

Second Session
Discourse (lun)
"The Essentials of the Method of the Mind of Emperors and Kings" (Diwang xinfa zhi yao)
Zou Zukong 鄒祖孔
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Liu 劉 comments: The conception of this piece is profound and penetrating, grounded in the ultimate essentials of principle. Its argumentation ranges widely and learnedly, galloping unrestrained. When it comes to the proposition of "governing one's mind by means of the realm," the argument established is especially extraordinary, grand, and unsurpassed—something none but a master writer could achieve.
Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: Its spirit and style are lofty and antique, and its discussions are incisive and to the point. At the end, it places the weight of its conclusion on preserving existing achievements; this is someone who thoroughly understands the principles of governance.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭譙　批〔意宏雄健直追史漢〕
人主欲致天下之治其要在乎以天下治其心
而已夫天下大矣人君舉其身兼蒞而總攝之
苟不能治其心即天下何繇而治顧人主之於
天下甚尊也天下處其卑而吾處其尊則其心
易縱而難檢苟不時時舉天下之故悚惕而警
厲之其究將至於知有己不知有人崇高富貴
之形近在耳目見聞之間者常見以爲可恃艱
難勞苦之形遠在四海九州之間者常見以爲
===
可忽然後驕淫邪侈日滋月茂無所厎止即其
心又何繇而治故心者人主之所以治天下之
本也天下者又人主之所以治其心之本也夫
惟能以天下治其心而後能以心治其天下張
子論知農事爲帝王心法之要意蓋如此予誦
其言未嘗不三嘆也嗟乎天下孰有急於農事
者哉元元之衆孰有勞苦於農事者哉然而世
之人主鮮克留意乎其間何也其故有二其一
謂之壅其一謂之玩謂之壅者君民之判久矣
punctuated:
考試官教諭譙批〔意宏雄健，直追史、漢。〕
人主欲致天下之治，其要在乎以天下治其心而已。夫天下大矣，人君舉其身兼蒞而總攝之，苟不能治其心，即天下何繇而治？顧人主之於天下，甚尊也。天下處其卑而吾處其尊，則其心易縱而難檢。苟不時時舉天下之故，悚惕而警厲之，其究將至於知有己、不知有人。崇高富貴之形，近在耳目見聞之間者，常見以爲可恃；艱難勞苦之形，遠在四海九州之間者，常見以爲可忽。然後驕淫邪侈，日滋月茂，無所厎止，即其心又何繇而治？故心者，人主之所以治天下之本也；天下者，又人主之所以治其心之本也。夫惟能以天下治其心，而後能以心治其天下。張子論知農事爲帝王心法之要，意蓋如此。予誦其言，未嘗不三嘆也。嗟乎！天下孰有急於農事者哉？元元之衆，孰有勞苦於農事者哉？然而世之人主鮮克留意乎其間，何也？其故有二：其一謂之壅，其一謂之玩。謂之壅者，君民之判久矣。
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: 〔Its conception is grand and its vigor robust, directly rivaling the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) and the Book of Han (Hanshu).〕

If a ruler wishes to bring about order in the realm, the essential point lies simply in using the realm to govern his own mind. Now, the realm is vast. The sovereign, in his own person, presides over it all and holds it in comprehensive control; if he cannot govern his own mind, how then can the realm be governed? Yet the ruler's position in relation to the realm is supremely exalted. When the realm occupies a lowly place and oneself occupies an exalted one, the mind becomes easy to indulge and difficult to restrain. If he does not constantly take up the affairs of the realm to fill himself with awe and rouse himself to vigilance, in the end he will come to know only of himself and know nothing of others. The manifestations of exalted status, wealth, and honor, being close at hand within the reach of his own eyes and ears, are constantly seen and deemed reliable; the manifestations of hardship, toil, and suffering, being far off across the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, are constantly seen as things that can be neglected. Thereafter, arrogance, license, perversity, and extravagance grow day by day and flourish month by month without end—how then can his mind be governed? Therefore, the mind is the foundation by which a ruler governs the realm, and the realm in turn is the foundation by which a ruler governs his mind. Only when one is able to use the realm to govern his mind can he then use his mind to govern the realm. When Master Zhang [Zhang Shi 張栻] argued that understanding agricultural affairs is the essential point of the method of the mind of emperors and kings, his meaning was surely just this. Whenever I recite his words, I never fail to sigh repeatedly in admiration. Alas! In all the realm, what is more urgent than agriculture? Among the common masses, what involves greater toil and suffering than agriculture? And yet among the rulers of the world, few are able to pay heed to it. Why is this? There are two reasons: the first is called obstruction, and the second is called trifling neglect. As for what is called obstruction, the separation between sovereign and people has existed for a long time. …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
是故其分殊而勢不相習也其勢而事不相
習也其事殊而跡不相習也其跡殊而情不相
習也是之曰褻謂之玩者以是爲瑣屑委鄙不
足務也吾從而深求之民生之所繫以蕃此也
民俗之所繫以美此也禮樂刑政之所繫以四
達而不悖此也泛而觀之則以爲是瑣屑委鄙
不足務也是之曰玩玩始乎上褻積乎下其恝
然不以留意無足怪也夫褻則蔽蔽則不明玩
則惰惰則不恭人主之心業已憒於二者之間
===
於是乎內之一切謬戾頗僻之端從之而出者
既蕩而莫禁其往外之一切可欣可喜可矜可
羨之欲從之而入者又紛然投間抵隙而莫禦
其來如是而求心之治不可得也心既不治矣
如是而求天下之治不可得也昔者考其詩書
竊計古之帝王其於天下莫不綢繆其文物敦
固其典章纖密其法制至其告戒之間所謂跂
容變色叮嚀而反覆者獨民事爲兢兢而其說
最著於七月無逸二篇七月之篇詳在下而未
punctuated: 是故其分殊而勢不相習也，其勢而事不相習也，其事殊而跡不相習也，其跡殊而情不相習也，是之曰褻。謂之玩者，以是爲瑣屑委鄙，不足務也。吾從而深求之，民生之所繫以蕃，此也；民俗之所繫以美，此也；禮樂刑政之所繫以四達而不悖，此也。泛而觀之，則以爲是瑣屑委鄙，不足務也，是之曰玩。玩始乎上，褻積乎下，其恝然不以留意，無足怪也。夫褻則蔽，蔽則不明；玩則惰，惰則不恭。人主之心，業已憒於二者之間，於是乎內之一切謬戾頗僻之端從之而出者，既蕩而莫禁其往；外之一切可欣可喜可矜可羨之欲從之而入者，又紛然投間抵隙而莫禦其來。如是而求心之治，不可得也；心既不治矣，如是而求天下之治，不可得也。昔者考其《詩》《書》，竊計古之帝王，其於天下，莫不綢繆其文物，敦固其典章，纖密其法制。至其告戒之間，所謂跂容變色、叮嚀而反覆者，獨民事爲兢兢。而其說最著於《七月》、《無逸》二篇。《七月》之篇，詳在下而未
translation_en: Therefore, because their stations differ, their circumstances are unfamiliar to one another; because their circumstances [differ?], their affairs are unfamiliar to one another; because their affairs differ, their experiences are unfamiliar to one another; and because their experiences differ, their feelings are unfamiliar to one another. This is what is called obstruction [? reading 壅 for 褻]. As for what is called trifling with it, that is regarding these matters as petty, mean, and vulgar, not worth attending to. Yet if we examine them deeply, that upon which the people's livelihood depends in order to flourish is this; that upon which the people's customs depend in order to be fine is this; and that upon which rites, music, punishments, and governance depend in order to reach everywhere without contradiction is this. Viewed superficially, however, one takes them to be petty, mean, and vulgar, not worth attending to—this is what is called trifling. When trifling begins above and obstruction [?] accumulates below, it is no wonder that rulers are indifferent and pay no heed to it. Now, obstruction [?] leads to blindness, and blindness to a lack of clarity; trifling leads to indolence, and indolence to a lack of reverence. Once the ruler's mind is already muddled between these two, all the perverse, errant, and biased impulses from within that issue forth from it run wild with nothing to check their departure; and all the desires for things delightful, pleasing, boastworthy, and enviable from without that enter into it crowd in through every opening and crevice with nothing to ward off their arrival. To seek the ordering of the mind under such conditions is impossible; and once the mind is not ordered, to seek the ordering of the realm under such conditions is impossible. In the past, examining the Odes (Shi) and the Documents (Shu), I privately reckoned that the emperors and kings of antiquity, in dealing with the realm, never failed to carefully weave its cultural institutions, consolidate its canons and statutes, and make minute its laws and regulations. Yet when it came to their admonitions and warnings—where they stood on tiptoe, changed countenance [? reading 跂容變色 for 動容變色], and enjoined repeatedly—it was solely over the affairs of the people that they were anxiously cautious. And this doctrine is most clearly manifested in the two chapters "Seventh Month" (Qiyue) and "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi). The "Seventh Month" chapter is detailed regarding those below, yet never…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
始不歸之上實其言可以無疚於壅無逸之篇
詳在上而未始不歸之下實其言可以無疚於
玩爲天下者甚不可不省也是故人主五齊八
珍而爲之民者何其役役然終歲疾耕而不足
於食也試於此有思焉則知憂矣人主重錦文
繡而爲之民者何其汲汲然終歲勤織而不足
於衣也試於此有思焉則知勞矣人主璇宮玉
宇而爲之民者何其閔閔然郊棲露處而不得
寧也試於此有思焉則知艱矣人主出有警入
===
有蹕雍容揖讓而爲之民者何其皇皇然胼手
胝足而不得休也試於此有思焉則知懼矣人
主春有觀夏有游秋有豫冬有息而爲之民者
何其咨咨然吁嗟噫嘅於祁寒暑雨之中而不
得怡也試於此有思焉則知危矣夫人心未有
無所用者也其用也未有無所假者也夫人主
當其左圖右書義之晝堯之典舜之歌禹之訓
湯之銘文之命武之誓若日月而揭諸前未嘗
不有悚於志也俄然而離去之則其志亦次第
punctuated: 始不歸之上，實其言可以無疚於壅；《無逸》之篇詳在上，而未始不歸之下，實其言可以無疚於玩。爲天下者，甚不可不省也。是故人主五齊八珍，而爲之民者，何其役役然終歲疾耕而不足於食也？試於此有思焉，則知憂矣。人主重錦文繡，而爲之民者，何其汲汲然終歲勤織而不足於衣也？試於此有思焉，則知勞矣。人主璇宮玉宇，而爲之民者，何其閔閔然郊棲露處而不得寧也？試於此有思焉，則知艱矣。人主出有警，入有蹕，雍容揖讓，而爲之民者，何其皇皇然胼手胝足而不得休也？試於此有思焉，則知懼矣。人主春有觀，夏有游，秋有豫，冬有息，而爲之民者，何其咨咨然吁嗟噫嘅於祁寒暑雨之中而不得怡也？試於此有思焉，則知危矣。夫人心未有無所用者也，其用也未有無所假者也。夫人主當其左圖右書，義之晝、堯之典、舜之歌、禹之訓、湯之銘、文之命、武之誓，若日月而揭諸前，未嘗不有悚於志也；俄然而離去之，則其志亦次第
translation_en: … ever fails to trace back to those above; by substantiating its words, one can be free from the fault of obstruction. The "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) chapter is detailed regarding those above, yet never fails to trace back to those below; by substantiating its words, one can be free from the fault of negligence. Those who govern the realm must not fail to examine this thoroughly. Therefore, while the ruler enjoys the five ceremonial wines and eight delicacies, why is it that those who are his people toil away, plowing strenuously all year round, yet do not have enough to eat? If he but reflects upon this, he will know anxiety. While the ruler wears layered brocades and patterned embroideries, why is it that those who are his people bustle about, weaving diligently all year round, yet do not have enough to wear? If he but reflects upon this, he will know toil. While the ruler dwells in palaces of jasper and halls of jade, why is it that those who are his people live in distress, lodging in the wilds and exposed to the elements, unable to find peace? If he but reflects upon this, he will know hardship. While the ruler has heralds clearing the way upon going out and guards securing the route upon coming in, comporting himself with poised grace and courteous deference, why is it that those who are his people are so frantic, with calloused hands and feet, unable to rest? If he but reflects upon this, he will know fear. While the ruler has his sightseeing in spring, excursions in summer,jaunts in autumn, and repose in winter, why is it that those who are his people sigh and groan in lamentation amid severe cold and sultry rain, unable to find joy? If he but reflects upon this, he will know peril. Now, the human mind is never without something to which it applies itself, and in its application, it is never without something upon which it relies. When the ruler has charts to his left and books to his right, and the trigrams of Fuxi [? 義之晝 for 羲之畫], the Canon of Yao, the Songs of Shun, the Instructions of Yu, the Inscriptions of Tang, the Commands of King Wen, and the Harangues of King Wu are held up before him like the sun and the moon, he never fails to feel a stirring of awe in his will. Yet as soon as he leaves them behind, his will likewise gradually…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而銷落彼所假者遠而不切也當其左三公右
三孤卿獻規史爲書瞽爲詩工誦大夫箴士傳
言苟語及於善未嘗不躍然喜也苟語及於不
善未嘗不瞿然起也俄然而已則其躍然瞿然
者亦次第而無存彼所假者近而有限也故不
若假之於天下夫天下者人主之所有事也無
時而非是也無之而非是也其休戚禍福又遞
相藉也是故知憂則不敢言樂恐其病天下也
知勞則不敢言逸恐其妨天下也知艱則不敢
言縱恐其擾天下也知懼則不敢言侈恐其殘
天下也知危則不敢言安恐其亡天下也夫如
是可謂善假而知所以用其心者矣故能祓除
洗濯使精神日奮志慮日澄而其心治心治而
天下治無難也蓋嘗觀三代以還英君誼辟繼
踵而起相望於後先乃其名能知農事者何廑
廑也夫秦皇漢武非不亦雄才大略也徒侈然
聽其意氣之所至以見奇而不能退而自克者
誠奉奮以檢束其心也西京之元東京之章非
punctuated: 而銷落，彼所假者遠而不切也。當其左三公、右三孤，卿獻規，史爲書，瞽爲詩，工誦，大夫箴，士傳言，苟語及於善，未嘗不躍然喜也；苟語及於不善，未嘗不瞿然起也。俄然而已，則其躍然、瞿然者亦次第而無存，彼所假者近而有限也。故不若假之於天下。夫天下者，人主之所有事也，無時而非是也，無之而非是也，其休戚禍福又遞相藉也。是故知憂則不敢言樂，恐其病天下也；知勞則不敢言逸，恐其妨天下也；知艱則不敢言縱，恐其擾天下也；知懼則不敢言侈，恐其殘天下也；知危則不敢言安，恐其亡天下也。夫如是，可謂善假而知所以用其心者矣。故能祓除洗濯，使精神日奮，志慮日澄，而其心治；心治，而天下治無難也。蓋嘗觀三代以還，英君誼辟繼踵而起，相望於後先，乃其名能知農事者，何廑廑也？夫秦皇、漢武，非不亦雄才大略也，徒侈然聽其意氣之所至以見奇，而不能退而自克者，誠奉奮以檢束其心也。西京之元、東京之章，非
translation_en:
…and fade away, because what he draws upon is distant and not immediately pressing. And when he has the Three Dukes on his left and the Three Solitaries on his right, while high ministers offer remonstrances, scribes keep records, blind musicians present odes, artisans chant, grandees offer admonitions, and servicemen transmit popular sayings—if the talk touches upon what is good, he never fails to leap with joy; if it touches upon what is not good, he never fails to start up in alarm. Yet as soon as this ceases, that joy and alarm likewise vanish one after another, because what he draws upon, though close at hand, is circumscribed. Therefore, nothing compares to drawing upon the realm itself.

Now, the realm is that with which the ruler is constantly occupied: there is no time when it is not this, no place he goes where it is not this, and its joys and sorrows, blessings and calamities are mutually intertwined with his own. For this reason, knowing anxiety, he dares not speak of pleasure, lest he harm the realm; knowing toil, he dares not speak of ease, lest he hinder the realm; knowing hardship, he dares not speak of indulgence, lest he disturb the realm; knowing fear, he dares not speak of extravagance, lest he ravage the realm; knowing peril, he dares not speak of security, lest he ruin the realm. Being thus, he may be called one who is skilled at drawing upon things and knows how to employ his mind. Thus he is able to cleanse and purify himself, causing his spirit to be daily roused and his resolve and deliberations to become daily clearer, so that his mind is well governed; and when the mind is well governed, governing the realm presents no difficulty.

Indeed, if we observe the eras since the Three Dynasties, heroic lords and righteous rulers have arisen one on the heels of another, looking upon each other across the ages; yet why is it that those renowned for understanding the affairs of agriculture are so exceedingly few? Now, the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han were not without heroic talent and grand strategy; yet they merely gave extravagant rein to wherever their spirit and ambition carried them in order to display extraordinary feats, and could not step back to master themselves, truly lacking [?] the means to restrain their minds [誠奉奮以檢束其心也?]. As for Emperor Yuan of the Western Capital [Western Han] and Emperor Zhang of the Eastern Capital [Eastern Han], it is not…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
皇穹眷
德旋霑靈澤之敷合萬姓而咸濡普九天而皆
潤歡騰海宇慶溢臣鄰臣等誠懽誠忭稽
首頓首竊惟天道遠人道邇視徵信以交
孚肅時雨乂時暘鑒明馨而是若惟天心
之仁愛莫測肆人君之對越宜虔六事責
躬殷切桑林之禱孑遺憫下周懷雲漢之
憂夙星駕而稅於桑田衛美中興之令主
甘雨祈而介我稷黍詩稱有道之曾孫魯
===
不焚巫文仲忠言是聽齊常避殿晏嬰善
諭猶傳漢皇詔布乾封矯誣彰失唐帝術
行縮水荒誕貽譏蓋應天不貴以文而捄
災亦惟在德自非有
聖敬之昭假焉能致
玄昊之潛通玆蓋伏遇
○○○○
聰明天縱
恭儉性成
punctuated: 皇穹眷德，旋霑靈澤之敷；合萬姓而咸濡，普九天而皆潤。歡騰海宇，慶溢臣鄰。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟天道遠，人道邇，視徵信以交孚；肅時雨，乂時暘，鑒明馨而是若。惟天心之仁愛莫測，肆人君之對越宜虔。六事責躬，殷切桑林之禱；孑遺憫下，周懷雲漢之憂。夙星駕而稅於桑田，衛美中興之令主；甘雨祈而介我稷黍，詩稱有道之曾孫。魯不焚巫，文仲忠言是聽；齊常避殿，晏嬰善諭猶傳。漢皇詔布乾封，矯誣彰失；唐帝術行縮水，荒誕貽譏。蓋應天不貴以文，而捄災亦惟在德。自非有聖敬之昭假，焉能致玄昊之潛通？玆蓋伏遇○○○○聰明天縱，恭儉性成，
translation_en:
…Imperial Heaven looks with favor upon Your virtue, and swiftly the spread of miraculous grace moistens the land; uniting the myriad people, all are steeped in it, and extending across the nine heavens, everything is nourished. Joy surges throughout the realm within the seas, and celebration brims over among Your ministers and aides. Your servants, truly joyful and truly elated, bow our heads to the ground.

We humbly reflect that the Way of Heaven is distant while the Way of Man is near, yet they respond to each other in mutual trust through verified signs; gravity brings timely rain and orderliness brings timely sunshine, as Heaven beholds bright virtue and approves. Because the benevolent love of the mind of Heaven is unfathomable, the ruler of men ought to be reverent in standing before it. Reproaching himself on six counts, the ruler of Yin was earnest in his prayer at the Mulberry Forest; pitying the surviving remnant of his subjects, the king of Zhou harbored the sorrow of the "Milky Way" ode. Ordering his carriage by the morning stars to halt in the mulberry fields, the state of Wei praised the fine ruler of its restoration; praying for sweet rain to bless our millet, the Book of Odes acclaims the virtuous "Great-Grandson." When Lu did not burn the shaman, it heeded the loyal words of Zang Wenzhong; when the ruler of Qi vacated his palace hall, the good admonition of Yan Ying was passed down. The Han emperor issued an edict proclaiming the "Qianfeng" reign era, yet his pretentiousness and deceit only exposed his faults; the Tang emperor practiced the magic of shrinking water, and its absurdity invited ridicule. Truly, responding to Heaven does not value mere outward form, and relieving disaster lies solely in virtue. Without the radiant reach of sagely reverence, how could one bring about unseen communion with Mysterious Heaven?

Now we humbly encounter Your Majesty [○○○○], whose intelligence and discernment are endowed by Heaven, and whose reverence and frugality are formed by nature…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
法駕荷
帝德而蕩蕩難名舞効商羊鳴同垤鸖伏願
慮先未雨
戒豫履冰
圖豐大於日中
萃戩穀於天保
恤民瘼常如
命駕出郊之時
敬天心不攺
===
卻蓋回
鑾之日
玉燭調而三光正永綿
聖曆於無疆金穰足而九土安胥樂
太平於有象臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖忻躍屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
punctuated: 法駕，荷帝德而蕩蕩難名，舞効商羊，鳴同垤鸖。伏願慮先未雨，戒豫履冰；圖豐大於日中，萃戩穀於天保；恤民瘼常如命駕出郊之時，敬天心不攺卻蓋回鑾之日。玉燭調而三光正，永綿聖曆於無疆；金穰足而九土安，胥樂太平於有象。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、忻躍屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以…
translation_en: …the Imperial Carriage; receiving the Emperor's virtue, which is vast beyond description, we dance like the shangyang rain-bird and cry out like the crane on the anthill. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will take thought before the rain falls, and remain cautious in advance as if treading on thin ice; plan for abundance and greatness as when the sun is at its zenith, and gather all blessings and goodness as in the "Heaven Protects" [Tianbao] ode; show compassion for the people's sufferings always as at the moment of ordering the carriage to go out to the suburbs, and revere the mind of Heaven unchanged from the day of setting aside the canopy and returning in the imperial carriage. May the jade candle of the seasons be in harmony and the three luminaries rectified, forever extending the Sacred Calendar without limit; may golden harvests be plentiful and the nine regions at peace, all rejoicing in the visible signs of Great Peace. Your servants, unable to contain our extreme joy and awe as we gaze up at Heaven and look toward the Sage, respectfully present this memorial of congratulation to…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
鄒祖孔
同考試官訓導董　批　更化善治在守法而不在
變法是作援引證據確有定論而敷陳義
聖祖開天立法
皇上守法致治之意惋切詳盡具占經世之學宜錄以式
考試官教諭倫　批　以正大之論發古健之詞
推原治亂得失如指諸掌蓋究心於理道者
考試官教諭譙　批　沉鬱而有精思簡嚴而有
奇氣博雅士也錄之
===
帝王之興必立法以垂後世而後之紹鴻
圖臻上理者必善守其法然後善其治於
不窮所謂守法不安無事而怠不喜多事
而擾斯守之善也開基創業之主其歷變
深其揆事熟故穆然淵思者其仁也燦然
punctuated:
聞。

第叄場

策

第一問

鄒祖孔
同考試官訓導董　批：更化善治，在守法而不在變法。是作援引證據，確有定論，而敷陳義〔？〕，聖祖開天立法、皇上守法致治之意，惋切詳盡，具占經世之學，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭倫　批：以正大之論，發古健之詞，推原治亂得失，如指諸掌，蓋究心於理道者。
考試官教諭譙　批：沉鬱而有精思，簡嚴而有奇氣，博雅士也。錄之。

帝王之興，必立法以垂後世；而後之紹鴻圖、臻上理者，必善守其法，然後善其治於不窮。所謂守法，不安無事而怠，不喜多事而擾，斯守之善也。開基創業之主，其歷變深，其揆事熟，故穆然淵思者，其仁也；燦然
translation_en:
… for Your Majesty's information.

Third Session

Policy Essays (ce)

First Question

Zou Zukong 鄒祖孔
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Dong 董 comments: Reforming customs and perfecting governance lie in upholding the laws rather than altering them. This essay cites evidence and precedents to establish a definitive argument. In setting forth the principles [?] regarding the Sacred Ancestor's (Shengzu, i.e., Emperor Taizu) founding of the dynasty and establishment of its laws, as well as the reigning Emperor's upholding of those laws to achieve good governance, it is earnest, incisive, and thorough. It demonstrates practical statecraft and should be selected as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: With upright and grand arguments expressed in vigorous, archaic prose, he traces the origins of order and disorder, success and failure, as clearly as pointing to one's own palm. He is truly one who has devoted his mind to the principles of governance.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: Profound and deliberate yet possessing refined thought; concise and rigorous yet imbued with an extraordinary spirit. He is a scholar of broad learning and elegance. Select it.

When sovereigns arise, they invariably establish laws to hand down to future generations; and those who subsequently inherit the great enterprise and attain supreme governance must excel at upholding those laws, only then perfecting their rule without end. What is meant by upholding the laws is neither growing lax out of complacency in times of peace, nor causing disturbance out of a fondness for meddling; this is the excellence of upholding the laws. A sovereign who lays the foundation and establishes a dynasty has experienced deep vicissitudes and weighed affairs with mature deliberation. Therefore, that which he contemplates with solemn and profound thought is his benevolence; that which shines forth in resplendent…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
畢備者其法也夫是又安海宇而永詒後
範守成之主邃處深宮章縫之士類持獨
見豈無奮發圖治通達國體者藉令竭智
殫慮僅可補偏救敝其大經大法孰能易
之三代而下英君誼辟不少矣若其撫盈
成之運當時稱善後世無貶詞惟曰恪遵
成憲耳已名臣碩輔獻納巖廊亦曰明習
典章耳已喜多事而務更張者不與焉書
曰鑒於先王成憲其永無愆後儒王通氏
===
曰不以三代之禮統天下終危邦也即三
王之興皆儀鑒先代未有變更自用者况
後王耶夏之興也有典有則詒厥子孫而
曰聖有謨訓明徵定保禹不自作也而嗣
禹之業者不敢變禹也商之興也三風十
愆儆於有位而曰纘禹舊服茲率厥常湯
不自作也而嗣湯之業者不敢變湯也周
之興也立政立事董正治官而曰監於二
代武王周公不自作也而嗣周之業者不
punctuated: 畢備者，其法也。夫是又安海宇而永詒後範。守成之主，邃處深宮；章縫之士，類持獨見。豈無奮發圖治、通達國體者？藉令竭智殫慮，僅可補偏救敝；其大經大法，孰能易之？三代而下，英君誼辟不少矣，若其撫盈成之運，當時稱善，後世無貶詞，惟曰恪遵成憲耳已；名臣碩輔，獻納巖廊，亦曰明習典章耳已。喜多事而務更張者，不與焉。《書》曰：「鑒於先王成憲，其永無愆。」後儒王通氏曰：「不以三代之禮統天下，終危邦也。」即三王之興，皆儀鑒先代，未有變更自用者，况後王耶？夏之興也，有典有則，詒厥子孫，而曰：「聖有謨訓，明徵定保。」禹不自作也，而嗣禹之業者，不敢變禹也。商之興也，三風十愆，儆於有位，而曰：「纘禹舊服，茲率厥常。」湯不自作也，而嗣湯之業者，不敢變湯也。周之興也，立政立事，董正治官，而曰：「監於二代。」武王、周公不自作也，而嗣周之業者，不
translation_en: … is thoroughly complete is his system of laws. By this means he brings peace to the realm [reading 又 as 乂] and eternally bequeaths a model for posterity. Rulers who preserve an established enterprise dwell secluded in the depths of the palace, while scholars in ceremonial caps and robes generally hold to their own peculiar views. How could there not be among them those who rouse themselves to seek good governance and thoroughly understand the fundamental principles of the state? Yet even if they exhaust their wisdom and deplete their thoughts, they can do no more than mend partial defects and remedy abuses; as for the great norms and fundamental laws, who could alter them? From the Three Dynasties downward, there have been no few heroic rulers and righteous sovereigns. Yet as for those who presided over eras of abundant accomplishment, who were praised as good in their own time and incurred no disparagement in later ages, it was simply said of them that they reverently observed the established constitutions, and nothing more; and of renowned ministers and great counselors who offered advice in the lofty halls of court, it was likewise simply said that they clearly understood and were well-versed in the institutional statutes, and nothing more. Those who delighted in multiplying affairs and busied themselves with sweeping alterations had no part in this. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Take as your mirror the established constitutions of the former kings, and you will forever be free from error." The later Confucian master Wang Tong 王通 said: "If one does not unify All under Heaven through the rites of the Three Dynasties, in the end the state will be in peril." Even when the Three Kings arose, they all took the preceding eras as their model and mirror, and none ever altered things out of self-willed presumption—how much less should later kings do so! When the Xia dynasty arose, it had canons and rules to bequeath to its descendants, and yet it was said: "The sage had counsels and lessons, clearly verified for securing stability and preservation." Yu 禹 did not invent them on his own, and those who succeeded to Yu's enterprise dared not alter what Yu had established. When the Shang dynasty arose, it warned those in official positions against the three decadent customs and ten faults, and yet it was said: "Continuing the old ways of Yu, we follow his constant norms." Tang 湯 did not invent them on his own, and those who succeeded to Tang's enterprise dared not alter what Tang had established. When the Zhou dynasty arose, in establishing government and administration and supervising and rectifying the governing officials, it was said that it "took the two preceding dynasties as its mirror." King Wu 武王 and the Duke of Zhou 周公 did not invent things on their own, and those who succeeded to the enterprise of Zhou [dared] not…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
敢變周也其子孫治安咸數百年而其祖
宗之法實與之相爲終始漢承秦敝而上
討周緒迨及唐宋所因所革同道同事大
可攷見孰有不遵道而興戾道而亂者乎
漢宣綜核名實曰漢家自有制度魏相稱
上意惟條奏漢家故事及賈誼鼂錯之言
而已夫漢制襲秦自三章約法十五定賦
數事外君子無取焉後世且惜其不復古
禮然而民安吏稱侔德商周者彼其所守
===
雖非三代之法實漢祖之法也史臣所稱
庶幾無愧矣有宋立國大綱雖正治具未
張神宗勵精圖治排衆論而用安石彼其
君臣之間語道則稱堯舜議法則軌周官
其所置法如經義免役保甲義倉之類至
今用之厥有成效豈無一當於時務然釀
紹聖之紛紛啓靖康之奇禍者以其所行
者安石之法也非藝祖太宗之法也引用
羣小爲一切趨事赴功之計此神宗所以
punctuated: 敢變周也。其子孫治安咸數百年，而其祖宗之法實與之相爲終始。漢承秦敝而上討周緒，迨及唐、宋，所因所革，同道同事，大可攷見。孰有不遵道而興，戾道而亂者乎？漢宣綜核名實，曰：「漢家自有制度。」魏相稱上意，惟條奏漢家故事及賈誼、鼂錯之言而已。夫漢制襲秦，自三章約法、十五定賦數事外，君子無取焉，後世且惜其不復古禮。然而民安吏稱，侔德商、周者，彼其所守，雖非三代之法，實漢祖之法也。史臣所稱，庶幾無愧矣。有宋立國，大綱雖正，治具未張。神宗勵精圖治，排衆論而用安石。彼其君臣之間，語道則稱堯、舜，議法則軌《周官》。其所置法，如經義、免役、保甲、義倉之類，至今用之，厥有成效，豈無一當於時務？然釀紹聖之紛紛，啓靖康之奇禍者，以其所行者，安石之法也，非藝祖、太宗之法也。引用羣小，爲一切趨事赴功之計，此神宗所以
translation_en: … dare to alter those of Zhou. Their descendants enjoyed peace and order for several hundred years in each case, and the laws of their ancestors were truly bound up with them from beginning to end. When the Han succeeded to the failings of the Qin and looked back to examine the heritage of the Zhou, and down to the Tang and Song, what they continued and what they reformed followed the same Way and the same enterprise, as can be broadly examined and seen. Who has ever flourished without following the Way, or fallen into disorder without violating the Way? Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣 comprehensively verified names and realities, saying, "The House of Han has its own institutions." Wei Xiang 魏相, matching the Emperor's intentions, merely submitted itemized memorials on the precedents of the House of Han and the words of Jia Yi 賈誼 and Chao Cuo 鼂錯, and nothing more. Now, Han institutions were inherited from the Qin; apart from a few matters such as theThree-Article Pact of Laws and fixing the land tax at one-fifteenth, superior men found nothing worth adopting in them, and later generations even regretted that they did not restore ancient rites. Yet the reason the people were at peace, the officials were equal to their duties, and their virtue rivaled that of the Shang and Zhou, is that what they upheld, though not the laws of the Three Dynasties, were truly the laws of the Han founder. The praise of the court historians is nearly without shame! When the Song founded the state, although its great outlines were upright, its instruments of governance were not yet fully deployed. Emperor Shenzong 神宗 exerted himself to seek good governance, brushing aside the opinions of the multitude to employ Wang Anshi 安石. Between that ruler and his minister, when speaking of the Way they invoked Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, and when deliberating on laws they modeled themselves on the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官). The laws they established—such as classic-meaning essays (jingyi 經義) in the examinations, service exemption (mianyi 免役), mutual security (baojia 保甲), and charitable granaries (yicang 義倉)—are still used to this day with proven effectiveness; how could they have had nothing at all suited to the affairs of the time? Yet they brewed the turmoil of the Shaosheng 紹聖 era (1094–1098) and opened the way to the extraordinary disaster of the Jingkang 靖康 era (1126–1127), because what they put into practice were the laws of Wang Anshi, not the laws of Taizu 藝祖 and Taizong 太宗. Drawing in a pack of petty men and making all manner of schemes to rush into action and chase quick results—this is why Shenzong…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
爲宋室基禍之主也夫天下一人之身也
祖宗之法元氣也氣之强弱稟於有生卽
爲定命順其氣而宣變之保聚之則身安
且壽厭其爲弱而日投丹餌將有裂膚潰
腸之患治天下者觀於身而已矣漢興立
國最强董賈之議時見施行至地節時猶
然壯固也孝宣又以信必守之故强者益
强宋弱不支比冗西父畢畢謹守范仲淹
稍變十數事卽以罷去至元豐號錮疾矣
神宗顧欲以强政濟弱勢是秦瀛之夫而
金丹之餌也其何能濟夫孝宣不敢議漢
法神宗乃輕議於宋仲淹不能得之仁宗
安石於神宗欲行所志多見其不知量也
洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
神武獨秉肅清中華
宵旰思皇恇營
憲令夫是
punctuated: 爲宋室基禍之主也。夫天下，一人之身也；祖宗之法，元氣也。氣之强弱，稟於有生，卽爲定命。順其氣而宣變之、保聚之，則身安且壽；厭其爲弱而日投丹餌，將有裂膚潰腸之患。治天下者，觀於身而已矣。漢興，立國最强，董、賈之議時見施行，至地節時猶然壯固也。孝宣又以信必守之，故强者益强。宋弱不支，比冗西父，畢畢謹守，范仲淹稍變十數事，卽以罷去，至元豐號錮疾矣。神宗顧欲以强政濟弱勢，是秦瀛之夫而金丹之餌也，其何能濟？夫孝宣不敢議漢法，神宗乃輕議於宋；仲淹不能得之仁宗，安石於神宗欲行所志，多見其不知量也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，神武獨秉，肅清中華，宵旰思皇，恇營憲令。夫是
translation_en: …became the ruler who laid the foundations of disaster for the Song house. Now, the Empire is like the body of a single person, and the laws of the ancestors are its vital energy (yuanqi). The strength or weakness of this vital energy is endowed at birth and thereby becomes one's fixed destiny. If one follows the flow of this energy to channel and adapt it, preserving and gathering it, the body will enjoy peace and longevity. If, disliking its weakness, one daily administers alchemical elixirs, there will arise the calamity of splitting skin and ruptured bowels. One who governs the Empire need only observe the human body! When the Han arose, the founding of the state was most vigorous; the proposals of Dong [Zhongshu] and Jia [Yi] were adopted from time to time, and by the Dijie era (69–66 BCE) it remained robust and secure. Emperor Xiaoxuan furthermore upheld it with trustworthiness and certainty, so what was strong grew stronger still. The Song was weak and unable to sustain itself; beset by redundancy and the Western Xia [? 比冗西父], its rulers painstakingly and cautiously maintained the status quo [?]. When Fan Zhongyan slightly altered a dozen or so matters, he was immediately dismissed and sent away, and by the Yuanfeng era (1078–1085) the condition was described as a chronic, incurable malady. Yet Emperor Shenzong wished to rescue a weak situation with aggressive governance—this was like feeding golden elixirs to an emaciated man [? 秦瀛之夫, reading 秦羸之夫]. How could that possibly succeed? Now, Emperor Xiaoxuan did not dare to call Han laws into question, yet Shenzong lightly called them into question in the Song; [Fan] Zhongyan could not gain approval for his reforms from Emperor Renzong, yet [Wang] Anshi sought to carry out his ambitions under Shenzong—this only shows all the more that he did not know his own measure! Humbly reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), endowed alone with divine martial valor, he cleansed and pacified the Central Realm; dressing before dawn and eating after dusk in anxious thought for august governance, he planned and established [? 恇營, reading 經營] the constitutional ordinances. Thus these…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
一代典章考衷千古六卿分職則周官之制三
壤定賦則夏王之法五禮節民則周禮之
遺律令採漢祖庸準唐經義取宋曆法仍
勝國至於
郊社合祀
宮府一體府部相維內外輕重相制其斟酌
前代參伍
宸衷焉
聖子
神孫肇萬世丕丕基者纖鉅畢舉善美兼盡蓋
===
我
聖祖之龍興也歷試諸艱閱世也最深其
御天也三十六禩
經制也最審其
立國也有漢之強固而道則純王其
治內也有宋之家法而國無弱政其由身心
而建之天地措之四海眞若元氣含暢於
一身之中心志虛明百體康逸毛髮膚爪
punctuated: 一代典章，考衷千古。六卿分職，則周官之制；三壤定賦，則夏王之法；五禮節民，則周禮之遺。律令採漢，租庸準唐，經義取宋，曆法仍勝國。至於郊社合祀，宮府一體，府部相維，內外輕重相制，其斟酌前代，參伍宸衷，焉聖子神孫肇萬世丕丕基者，纖鉅畢舉，善美兼盡。蓋我聖祖之龍興也，歷試諸艱，閱世也最深；其御天也三十六禩，經制也最審。其立國也，有漢之強固，而道則純王；其治內也，有宋之家法，而國無弱政。其由身心而建之天地、措之四海，眞若元氣含暢於一身之中，心志虛明，百體康逸，毛髮膚爪…
translation_en: …the institutions and statutes of a dynasty, examining and weighing the lessons of all antiquity. The division of offices among the Six Ministers followed the system of the Offices of Zhou; the fixing of revenues according to the three grades of soil followed the laws of the Xia kings; the regulation of the people by the Five Rites followed the legacy of the Rites of Zhou. For penal statutes and ordinances, He drew upon the Han; for the land-and-labor tax system, He modeled it on the Tang; for examination essays on the meaning of the Classics, He adopted from the Song; and for the calendrical system, He retained that of the conquered dynasty [Yuan]. As for the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars, the unity of the Imperial Palace and the administrative government, the mutual support between the Five Chief Military Commissions and the Six Ministries, and the mutual checks and balances of weight between the inner court and the outer provinces—in deliberating upon previous dynasties and synthesizing them within His imperial mind, thereby founding a vast and glorious heritage of ten thousand generations for His sacred sons and divine grandsons [where 焉 seems to be a variant or printing error for 為], everything from the smallest detail to the greatest matter was comprehensively instituted, combining both perfection and beauty. Indeed, in Our Sacred Ancestor's dragon-like rise to the throne, He experienced all manner of hardships, and His knowledge of the world was most profound; He reigned over Heaven's realm for thirty-six years [counting from the founding of the Wu regime in 1364 or similar], and His institutional planning was most meticulous. In establishing the state, He possessed the strength and solidity of the Han, yet His Way was that of pure true kingship; in governing the inner court, He possessed the family discipline of the Song, yet the state suffered no weak governance. Extending this from His own body and mind to establish it between Heaven and Earth and apply it across the Four Seas, it was truly as if primordial vitality permeated and flowed freely throughout a single body: the mind and will clear and tranquil, the hundred limbs healthy and at ease, and the hair, skin, and nails…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
無不潤澤其綜之有要行之無壅又若肢
體之咸隸於心心運於中手持足行臂指
相使而無壅腫不通之患當其時
天人協順華夷尊親
道化蒸融禎祥輻輳
身致太平法垂
後世至明備也嗣是
成祖繼統而潤色之
列聖綦隆而敬守之
===
一代治法纘爲治統肆我
皇上
冲齡睿質
握紀承休
嗣極以來孜孜化理與二三元老飭法
興治不遺餘力是故禋祀
郊廟豫協
慈闈
仁孝孚矣日
punctuated: 無不潤澤；其綜之有要，行之無壅，又若肢體之咸隸於心，心運於中，手持足行，臂指相使，而無壅腫不通之患。當其時，天人協順，華夷尊親，道化蒸融，禎祥輻輳，身致太平，法垂後世，至明備也。嗣是成祖繼統而潤色之，列聖綦隆而敬守之，一代治法，纘爲治統。肆我皇上冲齡睿質，握紀承休，嗣極以來，孜孜化理，與二三元老飭法興治，不遺餘力。是故禋祀郊廟，豫協慈闈，仁孝孚矣；日
translation_en: …is not moistened and nourished. Furthermore, his synthesizing of affairs had essential principles and his execution of them was without obstruction, just like the limbs all being subordinate to the mind: as the mind operates at the center, the hands grasp and the feet walk, the arms and fingers command one another, without the affliction of swelling or blockage. At that time, Heaven and humanity were in harmonious accord, Chinese and barbarians alike honored and cherished him, the transformative influence of the Way permeated everywhere, and auspicious omens converged like spokes at a hub. In his own person he brought about Great Peace, and his institutions were handed down to later generations, utmost in clarity and completeness. Thereafter, the Chengzu Emperor succeeded to the line of rule and embellished them, and the successive sacred emperors at the height of prosperity reverently preserved them, continuing the governing institutions of an entire dynasty as an unbroken tradition of governance. Now His Majesty the Emperor, endowed with sagely qualities at a tender age, holds the threads of rule and inherits the dynastic blessings. Since ascending the throne, he has been tirelessly devoted to transformative governance, working with two or three elder statesmen to rectify the laws and promote good rule, sparing no effort. Therefore, he offers pure sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, brings joy and harmony to the maternal palace apartments, and thus his benevolence and filial piety inspire confidence; daily…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
御經筵脩明
典制治本正矣懲貪汰冗卻貢蠲逋
恩澤流矣臣工振肅民物昌阜夷酋款貢
治化隆矣蓋法
聖祖之法而治亦
聖祖之治守
成業而光
前烈先後無兩廼執事舉漢宋之故事謇
昭代之法程若曰法敝相沿治湮所忽誠深慮
===
也夫法之立也未始不肅而終乎弛人之
行法也未始不奮而卒乎怠通變之際聖
人兢兢彼覩乎吏治之偷窳不如先代之
儼翼民俗之澆漓不如先代之龐固邊鄙
之繹騷夷狄之匪茹不如先代之烝皇孔
淑也遂謂法不足以繩天下各以所見而
爭議法聽其言則甚美實無當於事而祇
以取擾天下臣民無所遵守疑耳目而亂
心志則信乎議法之難也攷漢宋往事可
punctuated: 御經筵，脩明典制，治本正矣；懲貪汰冗，卻貢蠲逋，恩澤流矣；臣工振肅，民物昌阜，夷酋款貢，治化隆矣。蓋法聖祖之法，而治亦聖祖之治，守成業而光前烈，先後無兩。廼執事舉漢、宋之故事，謇昭代之法程，若曰「法敝相沿，治湮所忽」，誠深慮也。夫法之立也，未始不肅，而終乎弛；人之行法也，未始不奮，而卒乎怠。通變之際，聖人兢兢。彼覩乎吏治之偷窳不如先代之儼翼，民俗之澆漓不如先代之龐固，邊鄙之繹騷、夷狄之匪茹不如先代之烝皇孔淑也，遂謂法不足以繩天下，各以所見而爭議法。聽其言則甚美，實無當於事，而祇以取擾天下，臣民無所遵守，疑耳目而亂心志，則信乎議法之難也。攷漢、宋往事，可
translation_en:
… attends the Classics Colloquium, and clarifies the statutory institutions—thus the root of governance is rectified; he punishes the corrupt and winnows out superfluous personnel, declines tribute offerings and remits tax arrears—thus his grace and beneficence flow forth; the officials are roused to discipline, the people and all things flourish in abundance, and foreign chieftains submit in allegiance and offer tribute—thus the transformative governance reaches its height. Indeed, he models himself upon the laws of the Sacred Ancestor, and his governance is likewise the governance of the Sacred Ancestor; he preserves the established patrimony and glorifies the achievements of his predecessors, unmatched before or since. Yet Your Excellency cites precedents from the Han and Song dynasties and speaks forthrightly about the legal standards of our Illustrious Dynasty, as if to say that "when laws decay through passive continuation, good governance sinks into neglect through what is overlooked." This is truly a profound concern.

Now, when laws are first established, they never fail to be strict, yet they end in laxity; when men enforce the laws, they never fail to be energetic at first, yet they end in indolence. At moments requiring adaptation and change, the sages are ever cautious and circumspect. Those who observe that the laxity and negligence of official administration do not match the庄reverent diligence of earlier generations, that the thinness and decadence of popular customs do not match the simple solidity of earlier generations, and that the unrest on the frontiers and the recalcitrance of the border tribes do not match the grand flourishing and great goodness of earlier generations, thereupon declare that the existing laws are insufficient to regulate the empire, and each, according to his own views, vies to debate reforming the laws. When one listens to their words, they sound admirable indeed; yet in reality they are ill-suited to practical affairs and serve only to bring disturbance to the empire.
