Officials and people are left with nothing to abide by, their eyes and ears confounded and their minds and intentions thrown into confusion. Truly, then, debating the laws is difficult! If we examine the past affairs of the Han and Song…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
長非古也凡一切行法之中皆確守
成憲而不敢紊而尤深求立法之意不敢於法
外有所牽合焉出於法者舉成法以正之
故有據而不疑怠於法者振其法以作之
故有漸而不驚舍此不務而輒以己意橫
鶩振迅曰立法曰善治云者滋擾而已愚
嘗俯仰古今法久則敝雖三代聖王不能
制其流而守成之君不恃其治安而玩以
廢法則騁其私智而輕以變法不知重熙
===
累洽之後賢人君子之振培雖多而奸蠹
不無侵蝕生齒之蕃殖雖夥而物力不無
凋耗譬諸强仕以往者其膚革充盈智識
廣覽非不加於曩時乃精氣之日蝕月銷
者亦不少矣於此而圖攝生葆壽要在用
靜而不用動漢宣用靜者也神宗用動者
也故收効異也我
國家治安二百餘年是
祖法之維持古所希覯者顧忠賢之協贊多矣
punctuated: 長，非古也。」凡一切行法之中，皆確守成憲而不敢紊，而尤深求立法之意，不敢於法外有所牽合焉。出於法者，舉成法以正之，故有據而不疑；怠於法者，振其法以作之，故有漸而不驚。舍此不務，而輒以己意橫鶩振迅，曰「立法」、曰「善治」云者，滋擾而已。愚嘗俯仰古今，法久則敝，雖三代聖王不能制其流。而守成之君，不恃其治安而玩以廢法，則騁其私智而輕以變法。不知重熙累洽之後，賢人君子之振培雖多，而奸蠹不無侵蝕；生齒之蕃殖雖夥，而物力不無凋耗。譬諸强仕以往者，其膚革充盈、智識廣覽，非不加於曩時，乃精氣之日蝕月銷者，亦不少矣。於此而圖攝生葆壽，要在用靜而不用動。漢宣用靜者也，神宗用動者也，故收効異也。我國家治安二百餘年，是祖法之維持，古所希覯者。顧忠賢之協贊多矣，
translation_en:
… length [?]; it is not the way of antiquity." In every aspect of enforcing the laws, one should firmly uphold the established statutes without daring to throw them into disorder, and above all deeply seek out the original intent behind the establishment of the laws, without daring to make forced applications beyond the law. For those who overstep the law, one cites the established laws to correct them, so there is a firm basis without doubt; for those who are lax in the law, one invigorates the laws to rouse them, so it proceeds gradually without causing alarm. To set this aside and not attend to it, and instead impulsively gallop forth according to one's own whims in a burst of zeal, speaking of "establishing laws" and "good governance," merely creates further disturbance.

I have reflected upon antiquity and the present: when laws have been in place for a long time, they inevitably deteriorate, and even the sage kings of the Three Dynasties could not halt their decline. Yet sovereigns who preserve an established realm, if they do not rely on peace and order to neglect and abandon the laws, give free rein to their private cleverness and lightly alter the laws. They do not realize that after generations of cumulative peace and harmony, although the fostering and cultivation of worthy men and gentlemen has been abundant, treacherous parasites have not failed to erode the state; although the population has multiplied greatly, material resources have not failed to be depleted and exhausted. It is like a man past the age of forty: his flesh and skin are full, and his knowledge and experience are broad—not that they haven't increased compared to former times, yet the vital essence that is eroded day by day and wasted month by month is also not slight. At such a point, if one seeks to nourish life and preserve longevity, the essential thing lies in employing quiescence rather than activity. Emperor Xuan of Han (Han Xuan 漢宣) was one who employed quiescence; Emperor Shenzong of Song (Shenzong 神宗) was one who employed activity. Therefore, the results they achieved were different.

Our dynasty has enjoyed peace and order for over two hundred years; this maintenance through our ancestral laws is something rarely seen in antiquity. Yet while the cooperative assistance of loyal and worthy men has been abundant,…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
生齒之蕃殖廣矣其陰蝕潛耗容亦有之
亦用靜時也則蕩滌邪穢保聚太和以綿
國脉於無疆者實在於守法而不在於變法
然守法非飾法不可此漢宣之綜核所以
爲善守而輕變如神宗雖有一二小善而
卒無救於其敗甚不可也然天下之事易
怠忽而難振作所謂振作與紛更事若相
類而實不同況習之錮也而人心之私也
有無借作新之說以濟其紛更者乎有無
===
借避紛更以文其苟安怠廢者乎是皆以
私智處事而不以公心視天下故不可不
察也宋儒之言曰祖宗德澤不可恃法度
不可廢然則緣祖宗德意以守祖宗家法
不尤盡善盡美乎我
祖宗功德遠企商周有以延億萬年無疆之緒
聖天子躬行仁儉
厲精圖治
明君賢臣作新化理眞千載一時區區宜帝神
punctuated: 生齒之蕃殖廣矣，其陰蝕潛耗，容亦有之，亦用靜時也。則蕩滌邪穢、保聚太和，以綿國脉於無疆者，實在於守法而不在於變法。然守法非飾法不可，此漢宣之綜核，所以爲善守；而輕變如神宗，雖有一二小善，而卒無救於其敗，甚不可也。然天下之事，易怠忽而難振作，所謂振作與紛更，事若相類而實不同。況習之錮也，而人心之私也，有無借作新之說，以濟其紛更者乎？有無借避紛更，以文其苟安怠廢者乎？是皆以私智處事，而不以公心視天下，故不可不察也。宋儒之言曰：「祖宗德澤不可恃，法度不可廢。」然則緣祖宗德意，以守祖宗家法，不尤盡善盡美乎？我祖宗功德，遠企商、周，有以延億萬年無疆之緒。聖天子躬行仁儉，厲精圖治，明君賢臣，作新化理，眞千載一時。區區宜帝、神
translation_en: … and the growth of the population has been vast. Yet unseen erosion and hidden depletion may perhaps also exist, so this too is a time for employing quietude. Thus, cleansing away evil and filth, preserving and gathering supreme harmony, so as to prolong the lifeblood of the state without bound, truly lies in upholding the laws and not in altering the laws. Yet upholding the laws cannot be done without rectifying the application of the laws. This is why Emperor Xuan of Han's (Han Xuan 漢宣) comprehensive verification of nominal and actual performance constituted skillful upholding; whereas lightly altering them like Emperor Shenzong (神宗) [of Song], even though he had one or two minor achievements, in the end could not save him from failure—that is utterly impermissible. However, in the affairs of the world, it is easy to grow lax and neglectful and difficult to rouse and invigorate. What is called rousing and invigorating and what is called tumultuous alteration seem similar in practice, yet in reality are different. Moreover, when habits become entrenched and human minds are selfish, are there not those who borrow the doctrine of renewal in order to accomplish their tumultuous alterations? And are there not those who borrow the avoidance of tumultuous alteration in order to gloss over theirimprovised ease and lazy neglect? All of these handle affairs with selfish cleverness and do not view the world with a public-spirited mind; therefore they must be examined carefully. A Song Confucian said: "The virtuous beneficence of the ancestors cannot be relied upon passively; the laws and institutions cannot be abandoned." If that is so, then following the virtuous intentions of the ancestors in order to uphold the family laws of the ancestors—is this not even more completely good and completely perfected? The meritorious achievements and virtue of our Imperial Ancestors reach far back to rival the Shang and Zhou dynasties, having the means to extend a boundless patrimony for hundreds of millions of years. The Sacred Son of Heaven personally practices benevolence and frugality, rousing his spirit to seek good governance; an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers renew transformation and order—truly a once-in-a-millennium opportunity. Mere Emperor Xuan [written 宜帝 in text] and Shen[zong]…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
日詳詔令數下人將玩之弗信矣而況於
天乎知此則古帝王之克謹天戒曁我
聖祖
皇上之所以
祇德格天者可仰窺萬一而洪範春秋之義
晰如也甞謂天地爲萬民父母天子者代
天子之其胥爲一體若心志膚革聯貫而
不離互爲保愛若榮衛脉絡宣變而罔間
故天道遠矣祁寒暑雨必感於民民雖眇
===
矣忻戚悲愉常徹於天天之愛民甚矣豈
其使一人侈然於民上而不知所以恤之
哉君人者必體天心以爲吾心而又保合
民心以順天心天戒未形也不敢曰天命
在我而懼天之忘我天戒有象也不敢曰
天道之適然而脩人事之當然蓋無時無
之而非天也古之善言天人之際者必稽
洪範其言休徵曰肅時雨乂時暘哲時燠
謀時寒聖時風其言咎徵曰狂恒雨僭恒
punctuated:
日詳，詔令數下，人將玩之弗信矣，而況於天乎？知此，則古帝王之克謹天戒，曁我聖祖、皇上之所以祇德格天者，可仰窺萬一，而《洪範》、《春秋》之義晰如也。

甞謂天地爲萬民父母，天子者，代天子之。其胥爲一體，若心志膚革，聯貫而不離；互爲保愛，若榮衛脉絡，宣變而罔間。故天道遠矣，祁寒暑雨，必感於民；民雖眇矣，忻戚悲愉，常徹於天。天之愛民甚矣，豈其使一人侈然於民上，而不知所以恤之哉？君人者，必體天心以爲吾心，而又保合民心以順天心。天戒未形也，不敢曰天命在我，而懼天之忘我；天戒有象也，不敢曰天道之適然，而脩人事之當然。蓋無時無之而非天也。

古之善言天人之際者，必稽《洪範》。其言休徵曰：肅時雨，乂時暘，哲時燠，謀時寒，聖時風。其言咎徵曰：狂恒雨，僭恒
translation_en:
… become daily more detailed and edicts and commands are issued repeatedly, people will treat them lightly and lose faith in them—how much more so with Heaven? Understanding this, one can look up and catch a glimpse of how the emperors and kings of antiquity were able to heed the admonitions of Heaven, as well as how our Sacred Ancestor and His Majesty the Emperor have moved Heaven through reverent virtue; and the meanings of the Great Plan (Hongfan) and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) become perfectly clear.

I have held that Heaven and Earth are the parents of the myriad people, and the Son of Heaven governs them as a son on Heaven's behalf. Their forming a single body together is like the mind and skin, connected and inseparable; their mutual care and affection are like the nutritive blood, defensive vital breath, and vessels, circulating and transforming without interruption. Thus, although the Way of Heaven is distant, extreme cold and summer rain inevitably affect the people; although the people are insignificant, their joys, sorrows, griefs, and pleasures always reach through to Heaven. Heaven's love for the people is profound indeed—how could It place one man in arrogance above the people without his knowing how to show them compassion? He who rules over men must embody the mind of Heaven as his own mind, and further preserve and unite the minds of the people so as to accord with the mind of Heaven. When Heaven's warnings have not yet taken form, he does not dare say that the Mandate of Heaven rests with him, but fears that Heaven might forget him; when Heaven's warnings manifest in signs, he does not dare say that the Way of Heaven is mere coincidence, but cultivates what ought to be done in human affairs. Indeed, there is no time and no place where Heaven is not present.

In antiquity, those skilled at discussing the relationship between Heaven and humanity invariably consulted the Great Plan (Hongfan). Speaking of auspicious verifications, it says: "Gravity is verified by timely rain; orderliness, by timely sunshine; wisdom, by timely warmth; deliberation, by timely cold; sagacity, by timely wind." Speaking of inauspicious verifications, it says: "Wildness is verified by constant rain;僭 [arrogance/overstepping], by constant…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
暘豫恒燠急恒寒蒙恒風以五行配五事
休咎各以類應其說精矣乃孔子作春秋
書災異不書事應揆之洪範庶徵之說不
必盡然者茲曷故哉夫人君之事天猶事
親天之愛君猶愛子故義方可教不廢於
克家之子其或弗豫於東而徵色而發聲
而勞之威之要之不失爲愛而爲愉色爲
順志爲愛其所愛以求自媚於親者亦不
一其道故未然而防者父道也亦天道也
===
先意承志者子道也亦君道也如曰某事
失某災應是父之用愛發於聲者不移於
色徵於色者不移於聲威之勞之舉不相
通此慈父不能瑣瑣於其子天烏得而用
之於君若書大雨必求事之狂書大旱必
求事之僭書無冰必求事之豫書隕霜殺
菽六鷁退飛必求事之急與蒙即有偶合
所舛必多非所以訓也故春秋不書事應
者以此胡安國氏又謂春秋雖不書事應
punctuated: 暘，豫恒燠，急恒寒，蒙恒風。」以五行配五事，休咎各以類應，其說精矣。乃孔子作《春秋》，書災異不書事應，揆之《洪範》庶徵之說，不必盡然者，茲曷故哉？夫人君之事天，猶事親；天之愛君，猶愛子。故義方可教，不廢於克家之子。其或弗豫於東，而徵色、而發聲、而勞之、威之，要之不失爲愛；而爲愉色、爲順志、爲愛其所愛，以求自媚於親者，亦不一其道。故未然而防者，父道也，亦天道也；先意承志者，子道也，亦君道也。如曰某事失、某災應，是父之用愛，發於聲者不移於色，徵於色者不移於聲，威之勞之，舉不相通。此慈父不能瑣瑣於其子，天烏得而用之於君？若書大雨必求事之狂，書大旱必求事之僭，書無冰必求事之豫，書隕霜殺菽、六鷁退飛必求事之急與蒙，即有偶合，所舛必多，非所以訓也。故《春秋》不書事應者，以此。胡安國氏又謂《春秋》雖不書事應，
translation_en:
…constant sunshine; indolence, by constant heat; haste, by constant cold; and obtuseness, by constant wind." By matching the Five Phases with the Five Demeanors, auspicious and inauspicious signs each respond according to their kind—this theory is subtle indeed. Yet when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), he recorded calamities and anomalies without recording the corresponding human affairs. Measured against the theory of the Various Verifications in the "Great Plan" (Hongfan), it is not necessarily entirely so. Why is this?

Now, a ruler serving Heaven is like serving his parents, and Heaven loving the ruler is like loving a son. Therefore, instruction in righteous principles is not neglected even for a son capable of managing the household. Should the father happen to be displeased in the eastern step [?], whether it shows in his countenance, is uttered in his voice, or takes the form of toiling him or overawing him, in essence it never ceases to be love; and as for putting on a pleasant countenance, obeying his wishes, and loving what he loves in order to endear oneself to one's parents, the ways to do so are likewise not confined to one. Thus, to guard against things before they happen is the way of a father, and also the way of Heaven; to anticipate wishes and carry out intentions is the way of a son, and also the way of a ruler.

If one were to say that a certain failing in affairs is answered by a certain calamity, this would mean that in a father's exercise of love, what is uttered in the voice does not carry over to the countenance, what shows in the countenance does not carry over to the voice, and overawing him and toiling him have no connection with each other at all. Even an affectionate father cannot be so petty and compartmentalized toward his son; how then could Heaven apply such a method to the ruler? If, upon recording heavy rain, one must seek out an affair of wildness; upon recording a great drought, one must seek out an affair of arrogance; upon recording the absence of ice, one must seek out an affair of indolence; and upon recording frost falling and killing the beans or six waterbirds flying backward, one must seek out affairs of haste and obtuseness—even if there are occasional coincidences, the discrepancies will certainly be many, and this is no way to provide instruction. It is for this reason that the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record the corresponding affairs. Hu Anguo 胡安國 further said that although the Spring and Autumn Annals does not explicitly record the corresponding affairs,…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而事應具存如雷雹雨雪兆鍾巫之難春
雨木冰兆沙隨之變日食星孛皆有徵應
是春秋志災之意未嘗不與範同特不質
言所應則夫子之慮深矣是故九年之水
豈堯之失德致之而洚水警予堯不以黎
民於變有怠心焉此所以則天也七年之
旱豈湯之失政致之而六事責躬湯不以
九圍承式有侈心焉此所以配命也宣王
赫然中興胡爲有旱魃之虐而靡有孑遺
===
形諸雲漢之什者兢兢焉此所以過曆也
蓋其始也畏天而其終也回天惟其遇災
而懼故能反災爲祥皇皇乎聖喆弗可尚
也已後世誣天旱爲乾封謂天變不足畏
者無論已如京房劉向諸人日討事應以
談災異是泥洪範之旨而失之而僅得春
秋之意者惟日奏水旱之魏相奏四方災
異之李沆而已治之不古無惑也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
punctuated: 而事應具存。如雷電雨雪，兆鍾巫之難；春雨木冰，兆沙隨之變；日食、星孛，皆有徵應。是《春秋》志災之意，未嘗不與《範》同，特不質言所應，則夫子之慮深矣。是故九年之水，豈堯之失德致之？而「洚水警予」，堯不以黎民於變有怠心焉，此所以則天也。七年之旱，豈湯之失政致之？而六事責躬，湯不以九圍承式有侈心焉，此所以配命也。宣王赫然中興，胡爲有旱魃之虐？而「靡有孑遺」，形諸《雲漢》之什者兢兢焉，此所以過曆也。蓋其始也畏天，而其終也回天；惟其遇災而懼，故能反災爲祥。皇皇乎！聖喆弗可尚也已。後世誣天旱爲乾封，謂天變不足畏者，無論已。如京房、劉向諸人，日討事應以談災異，是泥《洪範》之旨而失之；而僅得《春秋》之意者，惟日奏水旱之魏相、奏四方災異之李沆而已。治之不古，無惑也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，
translation_en:
…yet the corresponding events are fully preserved within it. For instance, thunder, hail, rain, and snow presaged the disaster at Zhongwu; spring rain and tree-ice presaged the upheaval at Shasui; and solar eclipses and comets all had their verified responses. Thus, the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in recording disasters was never different from that of the "Great Plan" (Hongfan); it merely refrained from explicitly stating what each disaster corresponded to, showing how profound the Master's consideration was.

Therefore, how could the nine years of floods have been brought about by any lapse in virtue on the part of Yao? Yet saying, "The inundating waters are a warning to me," Yao did not allow his heart to grow negligent even though the black-haired people had been transformed—and this was how he patterned himself after Heaven. How could the seven years of drought have been brought about by any failure in governance on the part of Tang? Yet reproaching himself on six counts, Tang did not allow his heart to grow extravagant even though the nine regions took him as their model—and this was how he matched the Mandate. King Xuan achieved a glorious restoration, so why was there the tyranny of the drought-demon? Yet the words "there are no survivors left," expressed in the ode "River of Stars" (Yunhan), show how cautiously fearful he was—and this was how the dynasty's allotted years were extended. Indeed, in the beginning they stood in awe of Heaven, and in the end they turned Heaven's will back; precisely because they were fearful upon encountering disaster, they were able to turn disaster into auspiciousness. How magnificent! The sage-kings and wise rulers cannot be surpassed.

In later ages, as for those who falsely called a heavenly drought a "dry feng sacrifice," or who claimed that celestial anomalies are not worth fearing, they are not even worth discussing. Men such as Jing Fang 京房 and Liu Xiang 劉向 daily sought out corresponding human affairs in order to expound upon disasters and anomalies, thereby clinging rigidly to the purport of the "Great Plan" and losing its true meaning. Those who even partially grasped the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals were none other than Wei Xiang 魏相, who daily memorialized on floods and droughts, and Li Hang 李沆, who memorialized on disasters and anomalies from all four quarters. That governance does not match antiquity is no wonder.

Humbly reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor, the Emperor Gao…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
神聖開天
欽明立極
講洪範庶徵之應曰天道微妙難知人事感
通易見脩德則災害不生不脩則災異疊
見
睿知聖謨誠折衷箕孔洞悉天人之際矣
至治休徵溢爲嘉祥未易殫述而於七曜袤度
京師大旱惕然靡寧
求直言
===
錄獄因不一而足而又有
精誠錄其旨大約有三以
敬天首焉博採經傳旁及左國用備
省覽昭然顧諟之衷也有
存心錄凡祭祀之有感於災祥者皆載焉思
感召之由求消復之道以祇
天戒惕然時幾之勅也其所以
欽崇畏愼者何其詳且切也故運諸
淵衷沛於事業貽之
punctuated: 神聖開天，欽明立極。講《洪範》庶徵之應，曰：「天道微妙難知，人事感通易見。脩德則災害不生，不脩則災異疊見。」睿知聖謨，誠折衷箕、孔，洞悉天人之際矣！至治休徵，溢爲嘉祥，未易殫述；而於七曜袤度、京師大旱，惕然靡寧，求直言、錄獄因，不一而足。而又有《精誠錄》，其旨大約有三，以敬天首焉，博採經傳，旁及《左》、《國》，用備省覽，昭然顧諟之衷也。有《存心錄》，凡祭祀之有感於災祥者皆載焉，思感召之由，求消復之道，以祇天戒，惕然時幾之勅也。其所以欽崇畏愼者，何其詳且切也！故運諸淵衷，沛於事業，貽之
translation_en: …with divine sagacity founded the dynasty and with reverent brilliance established the supreme standard. In expounding upon the responses of the "Various Verifications" in the "Great Plan" (Hongfan), He said: "The Way of Heaven is subtle and difficult to know, whereas the sympathetic resonance of human affairs is easy to see. If one cultivates virtue, calamities and harm will not arise; if one does not cultivate it, calamities and anomalies will repeatedly appear." His perspicacious wisdom and sacred counsels truly synthesized the teachings of Jizi and Confucius, thoroughly penetrating the relationship between Heaven and humankind! The auspicious verifications of His consummate governance overflowed into felicitous omens that cannot easily be recounted in full. Yet when the seven luminaries strayed from their degrees [?] or when a great drought struck the capital, He grew apprehensive and knew no peace, seeking forthright words and reviewing prison cases [?] not once, but time and again. Furthermore, there was the Record of Utmost Sincerity (Jingcheng lu), the purport of which comprised roughly three parts, beginning first with revering Heaven; it drew broadly from the Classics and commentaries and extended sideways to the Zuo Commentary (Zuozhuan) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu) to provide for His personal perusal—a luminous manifestation of a heart ever mindful of Heaven's bright mandate. And there was the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu), in which all sacrifices having a bearing on calamities and auspicious portents were recorded, reflecting on the causes that called them forth and seeking the ways to dispel misfortune and restore harmony so as to respect the warnings of Heaven—an apprehensive admonition to attend to the timely and the incipient. How detailed and earnest were the ways in which He revered, honored, feared, and exercised caution! Thus, revolving these principles within His profound mind, He poured them forth into His grand enterprises, bequeathing them as…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
典則布之四方濬祥集福民殷物阜蓋二百
餘禩而海內宴如也執事謂
功德過堯湯而周宣不足侔者旨哉言乎肆我
皇上躬
上聖之資撫
郅隆之運
御極以來
懋學親賢內寧外謐庶幾哉我
太祖配天之治矣頃因
===
玄象示異雨澤愆期
京輔疫沴之災四方水旱之
奏致塵
宸慮
宮廷有禱同成湯桑林之敬賑恤有
詔敷帝堯不虐之仁羣臣有
勑切周宣雲漢之憂所以焦勞其心思交儆乎
中外者亦至詳且切粹然一我
太祖憲天之心也乃執事猶欲因
punctuated: 典則，布之四方，濬祥集福，民殷物阜，蓋二百餘禩而海內宴如也。執事謂功德過堯、湯而周宣不足侔者，旨哉言乎！肆我皇上躬上聖之資，撫郅隆之運，御極以來，懋學親賢，內寧外謐，庶幾哉我太祖配天之治矣。頃因玄象示異，雨澤愆期，京輔疫沴之災，四方水旱之奏，致塵宸慮：宮廷有禱，同成湯桑林之敬；賑恤有詔，敷帝堯不虐之仁；羣臣有勑，切周宣雲漢之憂。所以焦勞其心思，交儆乎中外者，亦至詳且切，粹然一我太祖憲天之心也。乃執事猶欲因
translation_en:
…canonical statutes and promulgated them throughout the four quarters, thereby deepening auspicious signs and gathering blessings, with the people prosperous and goods abundant; thus for over two hundred years all within the seas has remained at peace. When you, sir, state that his merit and virtue surpass those of Yao and Tang, and that King Xuan of Zhou is not worthy to be compared with him—how profound are your words!

Now Our Sovereign Emperor, endowed in his own person with the qualities of a supreme sage, presides over an era of utmost flourishing. Since ascending the throne, he has devoted himself to learning and drawn close to the worthy; with the interior at peace and the frontiers tranquil, he has nearly attained the heaven-matching governance of Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu). Recently, because the celestial phenomena manifested anomalies, timely rains failed to arrive, disasters of pestilence struck the capital region, and memorials reporting floods and droughts came in from the four quarters, the Imperial mind was troubled with concern: prayers were offered in the palace precincts, matching the reverence of Tang the Successful at the Mulberry Forest; edicts were issued for famine relief, spreading the benevolence of Emperor Yao who did not oppress the helpless; and precepts were addressed to the assembled officials, sharing the earnest anxiety of King Xuan of Zhou in the ode "Milky Way" (Yunhan). The manner in which he has burdened his mind and thoughts with anxious toil, mutually admonishing both the court and the provinces, is likewise most detailed and earnest—purely identical in spirit with the heart of Our Grand Progenitor in modeling himself upon Heaven. Yet you, sir, still wish on account of…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天象以陳謨此憂治危明之心匪過計也甞莊
誦
聖祖有曰天人之理無二人當以心爲天言求
天於心也又曰欲求事
天必先恤民言求天於民也大哉
王言誠昭事之龜鑑也已
皇上心天心而恤民艱得諸
天性固無間然但天道至精天子者必肖天惟
天惠民天子者必恤民是在
皇上加之意而已是故
帝典王謨日廑
講幄湛然心之清矣退而
燕間師保離次清者得無少滓耶
薦圭主鬯昭對
清廟穆然心之敬矣出而御下尊卑易分敬者
得無少肆耶
端冕垂裳
尊臨
punctuated: 天象以陳謨，此憂治危明之心，匪過計也。甞莊誦聖祖有曰：「天人之理無二，人當以心爲天。」言求天於心也。又曰：「欲求事天，必先恤民。」言求天於民也。大哉王言，誠昭事之龜鑑也已！皇上心天心而恤民艱，得諸天性，固無間然。但天道至精，天子者必肖天；惟天惠民，天子者必恤民，是在皇上加之意而已。是故帝典王謨日廑講幄，湛然心之清矣；退而燕間，師保離次，清者得無少滓耶？薦圭主鬯，昭對清廟，穆然心之敬矣；出而御下，尊卑易分，敬者得無少肆耶？端冕垂裳，尊臨
translation_en: …celestial phenomena in order to set forth counsels; this is a mind that worries in times of order and feels peril in times of enlightenment—it is by no means an excessive concern. I have reverently recited the words of the Sacred Ancestor, who said: "The principle of Heaven and humanity is not dual; a person ought to take his own mind as Heaven." This means seeking Heaven within the mind. He also said: "If one wishes to seek to serve Heaven, one must first show compassion for the people." This means seeking Heaven among the people. Great indeed are the King's words—truly a mirror and touchstone for brightly serving Heaven! His Majesty makes the mind of Heaven his own mind and shows compassion for the hardships of the people; having obtained this from his heavenly nature, there is indeed no flaw to be found in him. Yet the Way of Heaven is most subtle, and the Son of Heaven must resemble Heaven; it is Heaven alone that shows grace to the people, and the Son of Heaven must show compassion for the people—this rests simply in His Majesty giving even greater attention to it. Therefore, when the canons of emperors and counsels of kings daily occupy the lecturing tent, his mind is limpidly pure; yet when he retires to his leisure and his tutors and guardians leave their posts, might that purity not become slightly sullied? When he presents the jade tablets and presides over the sacrificial wine, brightly facing the Pure Temple, his mind is solemnly reverent; yet when he goes out to rule over his subordinates, where the distinction between exalted and lowly easily sets them apart, might that reverence not become slightly lax? Wearing the ceremonial cap and letting hang his robes, he exaltedly presides over…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
左道妖僧悍卒頑民蔑如於投鼠之忌安
可不芟刈之而窮其黨夫匹夫匹婦每能
勝予而一夫懷憤天爲飛霜一女抱冤天
爲大旱尤有不可不爲之慮者
皇上誠寛良民而不貸亂民顯良吏而不貸奸
吏使民得遂其有生之樂則怨讟不作民
心悅而天意得而災異有不弭者否也夫
天不以君無失道而忘儆戒之心人君不
以世無疵化而忘脩省之念茲
===
天心垂儆如此
聖心幾微如此民隱之可慮又如此則夫
聖不自聖以心爲天雖休
勿休以勤民爲務使志氣交動清和咸理五
事順而休徵應諸福集而萬邦和近符
聖祖遠媲堯湯
帝德協
天道同流
國祚倂
punctuated: 左道妖僧、悍卒頑民，蔑如於投鼠之忌，安可不芟刈之而窮其黨？夫匹夫匹婦，每能勝予；而一夫懷憤，天爲飛霜，一女抱冤，天爲大旱，尤有不可不爲之慮者。皇上誠寛良民而不貸亂民，顯良吏而不貸奸吏，使民得遂其有生之樂，則怨讟不作，民心悅而天意得，而災異有不弭者否也？夫天不以君無失道而忘儆戒之心，人君不以世無疵化而忘脩省之念。茲天心垂儆如此，聖心幾微如此，民隱之可慮又如此。則夫聖不自聖，以心爲天；雖休勿休，以勤民爲務。使志氣交動，清和咸理，五事順而休徵應，諸福集而萬邦和，近符聖祖，遠媲堯、湯，帝德協天道同流，國祚倂
translation_en: …heterodox monks, unruly soldiers, and recalcitrant commoners show utter disregard, counting on the hesitation to "pelt the rat for fear of breaking the vessel." How could one fail to weed them out and thoroughly eradicate their factions? Indeed, ordinary men and women can often prevail over a ruler; when a single man harbors indignation, Heaven sends down unseasonal frost, and when a single woman nurses a grievance, Heaven brings on a great drought—this is something that must all the more be taken into consideration. If Your Majesty truly shows leniency to good subjects while not pardoning rebellious ones, and honors upright officials while not sparing corrupt ones, enabling the people to fulfill the joy of their livelihoods, then resentment and slander will not arise. When the people's hearts are pleased, Heaven's favor is won—would calamities and anomalies then fail to subside? Now, Heaven does not forget its intent to admonish just because a ruler has not strayed from the Way, nor does a ruler forget the thought of self-cultivation and introspection just because the age has no flaws in its moral transformation. Today, the mind of Heaven sends down admonitions in such a manner, the Imperial mind attends to the subtle incipient signs in such a manner, and the hidden sufferings of the people warrant concern in such a manner. Therefore, being sagely without considering oneself a sage, take the mind as Heaven; though things be auspicious, do not rest in auspiciousness, taking diligence toward the people as the foremost duty. Cause will and vital energy to move in mutual resonance, clarity and harmony to prevail in governance, the Five Conducts to be in accord so that auspicious verifications respond, and all blessings to gather so that the myriad states are at peace. Matching the Sacred Ancestor in recent times and rivaling Yao and Tang in antiquity, Imperial virtue will flow in harmony with the Way of Heaven, and the dynasty's longevity will, together with…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天運無極是重有望於
皇上者也若粉飾文具是
清朝所斥申飭臣工則
明詔森然愚生安敢復贅
第三問
張輔辰
同考試官教諭劉　批　詩之意深矣此作上下古
今折衷人物足定千古權衡大要歸於關性靈裨風化蓋言哉
予其言之也敬服敬服
===
考試官教諭倫　批　博綜揚花深得說詩之旨
考試官教諭譙　批　有風骨有思致渢渢大雅
之音
論古人之詩者取其詞足以攄性靈義足
以裨風化言與人不得而相掩也夫詩者
言之有律者也六情絨於中百物盪於外
情緣物感物易情遷而言因之撰其要領
惟有關於彝教之大可以導人於善而祓
除其邪心形之歌詠被之管絃可以中律
punctuated:
天運無極，是重有望於皇上者也。若粉飾文具，是清朝所斥；申飭臣工，則明詔森然，愚生安敢復贅？

第三問

張輔辰

同考試官教諭劉　批：詩之意深矣。此作上下古今，折衷人物，足定千古權衡。大要歸於關性靈、裨風化，蓋言哉！予其言之也，敬服，敬服！
考試官教諭倫　批：博綜揚花，深得說詩之旨。
考試官教諭譙　批：有風骨，有思致，渢渢大雅之音。

論古人之詩者，取其詞足以攄性靈，義足以裨風化，言與人不得而相掩也。夫詩者，言之有律者也。六情絨於中，百物盪於外，情緣物感，物易情遷，而言因之。撰其要領，惟有關於彝教之大，可以導人於善而祓除其邪心；形之歌詠，被之管絃，可以中律
translation_en:
… and the fortune of the state will be boundless along with the destiny of Heaven—this is what is earnestly hoped of His Majesty. As for window-dressing with empty formalities, that is what our pure court rejects; as for admonishing the officials, the radiant edicts are sternly clear, so how would this ignorant student dare to add superfluous words?

Third Policy Question

Zhang Fuchen 張輔辰

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Liu 劉, comments: The meaning of poetry is profound indeed. This essay surveys the past and present and weighs historical figures with balanced judgment, sufficient to establish a standard for all ages. Its main thrust comes down to bearing upon innate sensibility and aiding moral transformation through custom—how well spoken [?]! I approve of what he says; admirable, admirable!
Examiner, Instructor Lun 倫, comments: Broadly comprehensive and displaying literary brilliance [揚花, for 揚華], it deeply grasps the import of discussing poetry.
Examiner, Instructor Qiao 譙, comments: It possesses vigor of style and depth of thought—the grand, flowing tones of high elegance.

Those who discuss the poetry of the ancients select diction sufficient to express innate sensibility and meaning sufficient to aid moral transformation through custom, so that words and the person cannot obscure one another. Now poetry is speech regulated by rhythm. The six emotions are enclosed [絨, for 緘] within, while the myriad things stir from without; emotions are moved by things, and as things change, emotions shift, with speech following accordingly. When one grasps its essentials, only when it relates to the great principles of constant moral teaching can it guide people toward goodness and cleanse away their depraved thoughts; given form in song and chant, and set to pipes and strings, it can accord with the musical pitches…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
呂而鼓羣動君子取焉是故列之三經錯
之三緯綜之四始釐之五際發乎性情止
乎禮義可攷而知也已運與世移質隨人
異格緣習靡音逐氣漓言人人殊矣所貴
談詩者尚論其人不徒以言也粵自扶徠
啓咏堯壤行歌詩教興矣三代盛時采詩
觀風詩爲有用之文三代以下徒騁才情
無當實用而詩之義廢有王者作采而立
教詎無可以諧宮商薦郊廟嗣百篇之餘
===
響者耶曰匪然也夫詩天地之籟也而人
籟生乎其中矣禮曰感物而動故形於聲
言之不足故長言之嗟嘆之是詩者天籟
之自鳴性術之所流也教化融徹即庸孺
矢口有老師宿儒所不能道而亦因政俗
以爲汙隆故先王采之爲之示儉示禮以
防其邪而導之正要之頌其所美則善心
生以善勸善不教而成頌其所刺則惡心
熄以惡懲惡不肅而嚴是詩之爲教也聖
punctuated:
呂而鼓羣動，君子取焉。是故列之三經，錯之三緯，綜之四始，釐之五際，發乎性情，止乎禮義，可攷而知也已。運與世移，質隨人異，格緣習靡，音逐氣漓，言人人殊矣。所貴談詩者，尚論其人，不徒以言也。粵自《扶徠》啓咏，堯壤行歌，詩教興矣。三代盛時，采詩觀風，詩爲有用之文；三代以下，徒騁才情，無當實用，而詩之義廢。有王者作，采而立教，詎無可以諧宮商、薦郊廟、嗣《百篇》之餘響者耶？
曰：匪然也。夫詩，天地之籟也，而人籟生乎其中矣。《禮》曰：「感物而動，故形於聲。言之不足，故長言之、嗟嘆之。」是詩者，天籟之自鳴，性術之所流也。教化融徹，即庸孺矢口，有老師宿儒所不能道；而亦因政俗以爲汙隆。故先王采之，爲之示儉示禮，以防其邪而導之正。要之，頌其所美則善心生，以善勸善，不教而成；頌其所刺則惡心熄，以惡懲惡，不肅而嚴。是詩之爲教也，聖
translation_en:
… pitch-pipes and stir the myriad creatures—these the gentleman selects. Therefore, arranged in the Three Warps (Feng, Ya, and Song) and interwoven with the Three Woofs (Fu, Bi, and Xing), synthesized in the Four Beginnings and ordered according to the Five Junctures, they spring from human nature and emotions and come to rest in ritual and righteousness; this may be examined and known. Yet as fortune shifts with the ages and substance varies with the person, styles grow decadent through habit and tones become thin as the vital spirit wanes, so that the words of every person differ. What is valued in discussing poetry is critically evaluating the person in his own time, not merely judging by his words. Ever since the "Fulai" song inaugurated chanting and travelers sang by the wayside on the soil of Yao, the teaching of poetry has flourished. In the flourishing era of the Three Dynasties, poetry was collected to observe local customs, and poetry served as useful writing; from the Three Dynasties onward, writers merely gave free rein to talent and sentiment without serving practical use, and the true meaning of poetry fell into neglect. Should a true king arise to collect poetry and establish teachings, how could there be none fit to harmonize the musical modes, be presented at the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples, and carry on the lingering echoes of the Three Hundred Odes?

I say: Not so. Poetry is the piping of Heaven and Earth, and the piping of man is born within it. The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "Being stirred by external things, one is moved, and therefore this takes form in sound. When speaking is not enough, one draws out the words and sighs over them." Thus poetry is the spontaneous sounding of Heaven's piping and the natural outflow of inborn nature. When moral transformation thoroughly pervades the realm, even what ordinary folk and children utter offhand may contain things that aged masters and erudite scholars cannot express; yet poetry also rises and falls in purity according to governance and customs. Therefore the former kings collected it, using it to display frugality and ritual propriety, so as to guard against depravity and guide people toward correctness. In sum, when one recites what is praised in poetry, a heart of goodness is born—encouraging goodness with goodness, it succeeds without formal instruction; when one recites what is criticized in poetry, a heart of evil is extinguished—deterring evil with evil, it inspires awe without severity. Such is poetry as a teaching, and the Sage…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
人刪之爲經也是故詩奏於郊廟天神格
地祇出奏於朝廷羣后德讓鳥獸蹌蹌奏
於閨門肅雍溫惠珩璜琚瑀之節備播於
邦國天下以諧萬民以洽賓旅以鼓動植
而乖僻疵厲之氣消故曰感天地動鬼神
莫近於詩季札觀上國而卜德祚盛衰左
丘明以歌詩歷徵大夫善敗詩之義淵乎
深矣然觀詩於三百之中里巷歌謠男女
荅贈淫蕩鄙俚之什不妨兼收觀詩於三
===
百之外祁招可以畜君巧笑可以崇質翹
車可以責善清河可以謀國涓水可以防
微而不爲聖人所取彼槩言刪後無詩亦
逐場之見非通論也安知當時歌謠贈答
不出於薦紳先生有所託而寄其情夫子
刪之而去其名不可得而見耳後世莊人
雅士孤臣孼子攄忠愛之悃陳感慨之臆
發抒志意陶寫情景豈無一言之幾於道
世無尼父評品乖律取舍靡公人各以意
punctuated: 人刪之爲經也。是故詩奏於郊廟，天神格、地祇出；奏於朝廷，羣后德讓、鳥獸蹌蹌；奏於閨門，肅雍溫惠、珩璜琚瑀之節備；播於邦國天下，以諧萬民，以洽賓旅，以鼓動植，而乖僻疵厲之氣消。故曰：「感天地、動鬼神，莫近於詩。」季札觀上國而卜德祚盛衰，左丘明以歌詩歷徵大夫善敗，詩之義淵乎深矣！然觀詩於三百之中，里巷歌謠、男女荅贈、淫蕩鄙俚之什，不妨兼收；觀詩於三百之外，《祁招》可以畜君，巧笑可以崇質，翹車可以責善，清河可以謀國，涓水可以防微，而不爲聖人所取。彼槩言刪後無詩，亦逐場之見，非通論也。安知當時歌謠贈答，不出於薦紳先生有所託而寄其情，夫子刪之而去其名，不可得而見耳？後世莊人雅士、孤臣孼子，攄忠愛之悃，陳感慨之臆，發抒志意，陶寫情景，豈無一言之幾於道？世無尼父，評品乖律，取舍靡公，人各以意…
translation_en: …the Sage edited them into a Classic. Therefore, when the Odes are performed at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, the heavenly spirits descend and the earthly deities emerge; when performed at court, the assembled rulers yield to one another in virtue and the birds and beasts dance in rhythm; when performed within the inner quarters, reverence, harmony, gentleness, and kindness prevail, and the measured pace of jade pendants is complete; when disseminated throughout the states and the empire, they harmonize the myriad people, bring concord to guests and travelers, invigorate animals and plants, and dispel perverse, noxious, and pestilential vapors. Thus it is said: "To move heaven and earth and stir ghosts and spirits, nothing comes closer than poetry." When Ji Zha 季札 observed the music of the central states, he divined the rise and fall of their virtue and blessings; Zuo Qiuming 左丘明 repeatedly verified the successes and failures of great officers through the Odes they sang. Profound indeed is the meaning of the Odes! Yet when we examine the Odes within the Three Hundred, ballads of the lanes and alleys, exchanges of gifts and replies between men and women, and licentious or vulgar pieces were nonetheless included together. Conversely, when we look at poems outside the Three Hundred—"Qizhao" could restrain a ruler, "Artful Smiles" could exalt unadorned substance, "The High-Riding Chariot" could urge men to goodness, "The Clear River" could guide state counsels, and "Trickling Water" could guard againstincipient perils—yet they were not selected by the Sage. Those who sweepingly claim that there was no true poetry after the Sage's editing merely echo the crowd; theirs is no comprehensive judgment. How do we know that the ballads and exchanges of that era did not come from gentlemen of official rank who used allegory to lodge their feelings, and that the Master, in editing them, simply removed their names so that they can no longer be known? In later ages, when upright men and refined scholars, or isolated ministers and unfavored sons, poured forth their sincere loyalty and affection, voiced their heartfelt sighs, expressed their aspirations, and gave form to their circumstances and emotions, how could there not be a single utterance that approached the Way? Because the world no longer has a Confucius (Nifu 尼父), critical evaluations violate the proper standards, selection and rejection lack impartiality, and each person according to his own whim…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
互相排讚無所取衷焉耳詩變而爲騷騷
變爲五言最後變爲近體極矣騷於詩爲
近以騷言之屈子懷絕代之才抱貞孤之
操不得於君流離放逐而作離騷千載而
下玩其詞探其藴奧如駕風鞭霆不可得
而窺測甞考劉勰辨騷謂騷有典誥之體
有規諷之旨有比興之義忠怨之辭四者
同於風雅似也至託詭譚怪狷狹荒淫摘
其四事斥其異於經傳斯誠異矣抑豈知
===
原者哉葢騷之旨主於規諷而義兼風雅
觀者惟察其情出於忠款而無乖於禮義
至其詞之泛濫假託要當以意攝之譬之
用兵貪詐奸驁頑鈍無恥之夫皆編之部
曲至其用之或動於九天之上或潛於九
地之下使人莫可窺測斯用兵之善者也
今觀於騷如稱堯舜禹湯雅之體也假雲
龍蘭芷風之遺也稱黨人靈脩之類雅之
變也蛾眉謠諑宓妃豐隆之類風之變也
punctuated: 互相排讚，無所取衷焉耳。詩變而爲騷，騷變爲五言，最後變爲近體，極矣。騷於詩爲近，以騷言之：屈子懷絕代之才，抱貞孤之操，不得於君，流離放逐，而作《離騷》。千載而下，玩其詞，探其藴奧，如駕風鞭霆，不可得而窺測。甞考劉勰《辨騷》，謂騷有典誥之體，有規諷之旨，有比興之義，忠怨之辭，四者同於風雅，似也；至託詭譚怪，狷狹荒淫，摘其四事，斥其異於經傳，斯誠異矣，抑豈知原者哉？葢騷之旨，主於規諷，而義兼風雅，觀者惟察其情出於忠款而無乖於禮義；至其詞之泛濫假託，要當以意攝之。譬之用兵，貪詐、奸驁、頑鈍、無恥之夫，皆編之部曲，至其用之，或動於九天之上，或潛於九地之下，使人莫可窺測，斯用兵之善者也。今觀於騷，如稱堯、舜、禹、湯，雅之體也；假雲龍、蘭芷，風之遺也；稱黨人、靈脩之類，雅之變也；蛾眉、謠諑、宓妃、豐隆之類，風之變也。
translation_en: … disparaging or praising one another, with no authoritative standard to settle upon. The Odes (Shi 詩) transformed into the Elegies (Sao 騷), the Elegies transformed into pentasyllabic verse, and finally into recent-style verse (jinti 近體), reaching the ultimate limit. The Elegies are closest to the Odes. To speak in terms of the Elegies: Master Qu [Qu Yuan 屈原] possessed peerless talent and held to pure and solitary integrity; failing to win the favor of his lord, he wandered in exile and composed "Encountering Sorrow" (Li Sao 離騷). A thousand years later, when one savors its words and probes its profound depths, it is like riding the wind and whipping the thunderbolts—impossible to fathom. I have examined Liu Xie's 劉勰 "Evaluating the Elegies" (Bian Sao 辨騷), which states that the Elegies possess the form of the canons and announcements, the intent of admonition and remonstrance, the principle of comparison and evocative image (bi xing 比興), and expressions of loyal resentment—that in these four respects they are the same as the Airs and Odes (Feng Ya 風雅) seems right. Yet when it comes to invoking the诡異 [strange] and speaking of anomalies, or being narrowly impetuous and wildly licentious, he singles out four aspects and criticizes them as diverging from the Classics and their commentaries. These are indeed divergences, yet how could that be called truly understanding [Qu] Yuan? For the intent of the Elegies is centered on admonition and remonstrance, while their principles encompass both the Airs and the Odes. The reader should simply observe that their sentiments arise from loyal sincerity and do not violate ritual propriety and righteousness; as for the extravagant and allegorical nature of their diction, one ought in essence to grasp them through their underlying meaning. Compare this to the art of war: greedy, deceitful, treacherous, arrogant, obtuse, and shameless men are all enrolled into the ranks and divisions; yet when it comes to deploying them, one may strike above the nine heavens or lie hidden beneath the nine earths, making it impossible for anyone to fathom—such is one who excels at using troops. Now, if we look at the Elegies: praising Yao 堯, Shun 舜, Yu 禹, and Tang 湯 is the form of the Odes; borrowing the imagery of cloud-dragons, thoroughwort, and angelica is the legacy of the Airs; speaking of the "factious men" (dangren 黨人), the "Numen Fair" (Lingxiu 靈脩), and the like is the mutated form (bian 變) of the Odes; and speaking of "moth-eyebrows" (emei 蛾眉), slanderous rumors, Consort Fu (Fufei 宓妃), the Thunder Lord (Fenglong 豐隆), and the like is the mutated form of the Airs.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
鳳見者媚焉柴桑之詩悠然孤鶴與其人
俱邈矣靈均出入風雅變化不測其猶龍
乎大都發於性情止於禮義無愧於三百
篇之大旨均之不詭於詩者也籍令離騷
非以靈修哀志則驚采奪色絕豔埋光雖
使揚雄息喙班固回嘲亦不號詞賦之祖
陶杜非以忠貞鑄詞則晉眞無文章唐亦
失詩聖雖使昌黎推轂永叔退舍亦不登
著作之壇知此可以論詩矣我
===
國家道化淪洽風氣淳龐
中和之極建於
上詩書之澤陶於下其奏之
郊廟陳之
宴享洋洋乎雅頌之休聲矣而鴻工哲匠繼
踵摩肩往往孕杜苞陶卽靈均且奴隸使
之執事猶欲總異歸同以鳴
國家之盛抑豈有出於三百篇之旨哉蓋詩
首二南以風敎也風起於上而動於下惟
punctuated: 鳳，見者媚焉；柴桑之詩，悠然孤鶴，與其人俱邈矣；靈均出入《風》、《雅》，變化不測，其猶龍乎！大都發於性情，止於禮義，無愧於三百篇之大旨，均之不詭於詩者也。籍令《離騷》非以靈修哀志，則驚采奪色，絕豔埋光，雖使揚雄息喙、班固回嘲，亦不號詞賦之祖；陶、杜非以忠貞鑄詞，則晉眞無文章，唐亦失詩聖，雖使昌黎推轂、永叔退舍，亦不登著作之壇。知此可以論詩矣。我國家道化淪洽，風氣淳龐，中和之極建於上，詩書之澤陶於下。其奏之郊廟，陳之宴享，洋洋乎《雅》、《頌》之休聲矣！而鴻工哲匠，繼踵摩肩，往往孕杜苞陶，卽靈均且奴隸使之。執事猶欲總異歸同，以鳴國家之盛，抑豈有出於三百篇之旨哉？蓋《詩》首《二南》，以風敎也。風起於上而動於下，惟
translation_en:
… [like a] phoenix, so that those who behold it are charmed by it; the poetry of the master of Chaisang [Tao Qian 陶潛] is like a solitary crane in leisurely flight, as remote and transcendent as the man himself; and Lingjun [Qu Yuan 屈原] moves in and out of the Airs (Feng) and Odes (Ya), his transformations unfathomable—is he not like a dragon! In general, all of them issue from human nature and emotion and halt within the bounds of ritual and righteousness; they are worthy of the great purport of the Three Hundred Poems [the Classic of Poetry (Shijing)] and alike do not deviate from the true way of poetry. Supposing that Encountering Sorrow (Lisao) had not been written to grieve over his aspiration for the Divine Fair One [his lord], then its startling brilliance would lose its color and its peerless beauty would bury its light; even if Yang Xiong 揚雄 had held his tongue and Ban Gu 班固 had withdrawn his ridicule, he still would not be hailed as the progenitor of verse-prose (cifu). And if Tao [Qian] and Du [Fu 杜甫] had not forged their words out of loyalty and integrity, then the Jin dynasty would truly have had no belles-lettres, and the Tang would likewise have lost its Sage of Poetry; even if Han Yu 韓愈 (Changli 昌黎) had sung their praises and Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修 (Yongshu 永叔) had yielded before them, they still would not have ascended the altar of great authors. Once one understands this, one can discuss poetry.

In our Dynasty, moral transformation has permeated everywhere, and customs and ethos are pure and generous. The supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony is established above, while the beneficent influence of the Classic of Poetry and the Classic of History molds the people below. What is performed at the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples, and what is presented at state banquets and feasts—how vast and magnificent are these auspicious sounds of the Odes (Ya) and Hymns (Song)! Moreover, great masters and wise artisans follow closely upon one another's heels and rub shoulders, time and again encompassing Du [Fu] and embracing Tao [Qian], and even ordering Lingjun [Qu Yuan] about like a servant. Yet Your Excellency still wishes to gather together the diverse and bring them into unity so as to proclaim the flourishing of the Dynasty—how could this go beyond the purport of the Three Hundred Poems? For the Classic of Poetry places the "Two Nan" [Zhou nan 周南 and Shao nan 召南] at its head because of their transformative teaching by moral wind. The wind arises from above and stirs those below; I only…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
冀
朝廷之上本關雎麟趾之心廣菁莪棫樸之
化崇緇衣素絲之風黜蜉蝣貝錦之習敦
尚爾雅剗滌浮澆則化行俗美歌謠里巷
之詩宜有可采而爲之士者又博綜羣籍
涵養性靈本之二南以求其端參之列國
以盡其變正之於雅以大其規和之於頌
以要其止而又推之天下國家以驗其實
際則詩之養性情達政事者此爲得之是
===
深於詩者也由是而言所志過則風雅及
則騷不及亦不失爲陶杜謂之鳴
國家之盛疇曰不宜否則牽性情而逐光景
工藻繪而鑿天真卽拾香草於江潭獵奇
葩於楚畹採東籬之落英襲杜陵之賸馥
享其敝帚自謂千金亦優孟之學孫嫫姆
而處子態也識者見且唾矣奚其詩記曰
誦詩三百不足以當一獻而不達於政雖
多奚爲致用君子詎可徒詩爲也請以是
punctuated: 冀朝廷之上，本《關雎》、《麟趾》之心，廣《菁莪》、《棫樸》之化，崇《緇衣》、《素絲》之風，黜《蜉蝣》、《貝錦》之習，敦尚爾雅，剗滌浮澆。則化行俗美，歌謠里巷之詩宜有可采。而爲之士者，又博綜羣籍，涵養性靈，本之二《南》以求其端，參之列國以盡其變，正之於《雅》以大其規，和之於《頌》以要其止，而又推之天下國家以驗其實際。則詩之養性情、達政事者，此爲得之，是深於詩者也。由是而言所志，過則《風》、《雅》，及則《騷》，不及亦不失爲陶、杜，謂之鳴國家之盛，疇曰不宜？否則牽性情而逐光景，工藻繪而鑿天真，卽拾香草於江潭，獵奇葩於楚畹，採東籬之落英，襲杜陵之賸馥，享其敝帚，自謂千金，亦優孟之學孫、嫫姆而處子態也。識者見且唾矣，奚其詩！《記》曰：「誦《詩》三百，不足以當一獻。」而不達於政，雖多奚爲？致用君子，詎可徒詩爲也！請以是
translation_en: … only hope that at court above, grounded in the heart-mind of "Ospreys Cry" (Guanju) and "Feet of the Unicorn" (Linzhi), they will broaden the transformative teaching of "Luxuriant Tarragon" (Jing'e) and "Scrub Oak" (Yupu), exalt the ethos of "Black Robes" (Ziyi) and "White Silk" (Susi) [of "Lambskin" (Gaoyang)], reject the habits of "Mayfly" (Fuyou) and "Shell Brocade" (Beijin) [of "Stately" (Xiangbo)], esteem refined elegance, and pare away superficiality and frivolity. Then transformative teaching will prevail and customs will become admirable, and among the songs and ballads of the lanes and alleys there will surely be poems worthy of collection. Meanwhile, those who are scholars will also broadly synthesize the multitude of books and nurture their innate spirit: grounding themselves in the Two Nan [Odes of Zhou and the South, and Odes of Shao and the South] to seek the beginnings, consulting the Airs of the various states to exhaust the variations, rectifying them through the Major and Minor Odes (Ya) to enlarge the scale, harmonizing them through the Hymns (Song) to bring them to their ultimate resting point, and furthermore extending them to the realm and the state to verify their practical reality. Thus, as for poetry's nurturing of human nature and emotions and its mastery of governance, in this way it will be attained; such a person is truly profound in poetry. Speaking of what the mind expresses from this standpoint: if it surpasses, it matches the Airs (Feng) and Odes (Ya); if it reaches the mark, it matches the Elegies (Sao); and even if it falls short, it will still not fail to be like Tao [Qian 陶潛] and Du [Fu 杜甫]. To call this sounding forth the flourishing of the state—who would say it is unfitting? Otherwise, if one forces one's nature and emotions to chase after fleeting scenery, or labors at ornate embellishment while carving away natural genuineness—even if one gathers fragrant herbs by the river depths, hunts rare blossoms in the gardens of Chu, plucks fallen petals by the eastern fence, or borrows the lingering fragrance of Duling [Du Fu], cherishing one's worn-out broom and boasting that it is worth a thousand pieces of gold—this is merely You Meng 優孟 imitating Sun [Shu'ao 孫叔敖], or the ugly nurse Mo Mu 嫫姆 putting on the airs of a maiden. Discerning people will spit at the sight of it; what kind of poetry is that! The Record [of Music] (Ji) says: "Reciting the three hundred Poems (Shi) is not enough to match a single libation." And if one cannot apply them to governance, though one recites many, of what use are they? How could a gentleman devoted to practical application engage merely in making poetry! I beg to offer this…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
為明問復
第四問
劉信徵
同考試官訓導靳　批　度田均賦我
皇上鼎惠元元
盛心子能博綜古今宜揚
德意且爲濟人畫爻遠計匪徒剿說已也具占經濟實用錄之
考試官教諭倫　批　詳經制酌時宜惟此作得
之
===
考試官教諭譙　批　良法美意粲然畢陳
爲政之道其猶張弓乎高者仰之下者俯
之高下隨機而應手惟其中而已矣其猶
調瑟乎緩則急之急則緩之緩急隨宜以
諧聲惟其適而已矣養由基之於射也伯
牙之於琴也帝王之於天下也亦大都若
此矣是故高岸爲谷深谷爲陵言時勢之
有變更而不可常也冬日則飲湯夏日則
飲水言處事之貴識時而不可泥也夫運
punctuated:
為明問復。

第四問
劉信徵
同考試官訓導靳　批：度田均賦，我皇上鼎惠元元盛心。子能博綜古今，宜揚德意，且爲濟人畫爻遠計，匪徒剿說已也。具占經濟實用，錄之。
考試官教諭倫　批：詳經制，酌時宜，惟此作得之。
考試官教諭譙　批：良法美意，粲然畢陳。

爲政之道，其猶張弓乎！高者仰之，下者俯之，高下隨機而應手，惟其中而已矣。其猶調瑟乎！緩則急之，急則緩之，緩急隨宜以諧聲，惟其適而已矣。養由基之於射也，伯牙之於琴也，帝王之於天下也，亦大都若此矣。是故高岸爲谷，深谷爲陵，言時勢之有變更而不可常也；冬日則飲湯，夏日則飲水，言處事之貴識時而不可泥也。夫運
translation_en:
…in reply to the enlightened inquiry.

Fourth Policy Essay
Liu Xinzheng 劉信徵
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Jin 靳 comments: Measuring the fields and equalizing taxes is the grand intention of Our Sovereign to newly bestow favor upon the common people. You are able to synthesize ancient and modern precedents broadly, proclaim His virtuous intent [宜 is a graphic error for 宣], and moreover devise long-lasting plans [爻 is a graphic error for 久] for the people of Yunnan [濟 is a graphic error for 滇][?], not merely repeating hackneyed phrases. This fully demonstrates practical statecraft and utility; it is selected for inclusion.
Examiner Instructor Lun 倫 comments: Detailed in institutional regulations and judicious regarding timely expediency—only this composition achieves it.
Examiner Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: Good laws and admirable intentions are brilliantly set forth in full.

Is not the Way of governance like drawing a bow? What is high is lowered [or: aimed upward], and what is low is lowered; high and low respond to the hand according to the moment, seeking only to hit the mark. Is it not like tuning a zither? What is loose is tightened, and what is tight is loosened; loose and tight are adjusted as appropriate to harmonize the sound, seeking only what is fitting. Yang Youji 養由基 in archery, Bo Ya 伯牙 with the lute, and emperors and kings with the realm—all are generally like this. Therefore, "high banks become valleys, and deep valleys become hills" speaks of how temporal circumstances undergo change and cannot be held constant; "in winter days one drinks hot broth, and in summer days one drinks cold water" speaks of how in handling affairs one values recognizing the times and must not be rigidly bound. Now, as fortune [shifts?]…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而人從時至而事起不師古人致治之迹
而師古人用意之精不爲一切苟且之圖
而爲經义可行之計斯則君子之所以神
化宜民而善其治於不窮者爾夫自載籍
以來其所稱至治之世至周焉極矣周人
致治之法則莫善於井田然而非始於周
也盖聞黄帝時八家爲井井開四道而分
八宅鑿井於其中是井田之所由來者遠
矣唐虞夏商大率相沿至周而始大備今
===
考其田在鄉遂者掌之以遂人周禮所謂
十夫有畛百夫有涂千夫有道萬夫有路
者其職也在都鄙者掌之以匠人周禮所
謂二耜爲耦九夫爲井十里爲成百里爲
同者其職也當此之時田有定分民有恒
業雖恣睢武悍之夫無所用其兼併古云
和協輯睦於是乎興敦龎純固於是乎成
其周人制産之法之謂乎夷考其賦則徵
財屬之遂師使入野賦於王府矣而又有
punctuated: 而人從，時至而事起。不師古人致治之迹，而師古人用意之精；不爲一切苟且之圖，而爲經义可行之計。斯則君子之所以神化宜民，而善其治於不窮者爾。夫自載籍以來，其所稱至治之世，至周焉極矣。周人致治之法，則莫善於井田，然而非始於周也。盖聞黄帝時八家爲井，井開四道而分八宅，鑿井於其中，是井田之所由來者遠矣。唐、虞、夏、商大率相沿，至周而始大備。今考其田：在鄉遂者，掌之以遂人，《周禮》所謂「十夫有畛，百夫有涂，千夫有道，萬夫有路」者，其職也；在都鄙者，掌之以匠人，《周禮》所謂「二耜爲耦，九夫爲井，十里爲成，百里爲同」者，其職也。當此之時，田有定分，民有恒業，雖恣睢武悍之夫，無所用其兼併。古云：「和協輯睦，於是乎興；敦龎純固，於是乎成。」其周人制産之法之謂乎？夷考其賦，則徵財屬之遂師，使入野賦於王府矣，而又有
translation_en:
… [revolves] and people follow; the time arrives and affairs arise. One does not imitate the outward traces of how the ancients achieved order, but rather imitates the essence of the ancients' intentions; one does not make temporary, makeshift plans, but rather devises enduring [?] (經久, printed 經义), practicable strategies. This is how the noble man miraculously transforms and adapts to the people, perfecting his governance inexhaustibly.

Now, ever since written records began, what have been praised as eras of supreme governance reached their pinnacle in the Zhou dynasty. Among the methods by which the men of Zhou achieved order, none was better than the well-field (jingtian) system—yet it did not begin with the Zhou. Indeed, it is heard that in the time of the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi), eight families formed a well (jing); the well opened onto four paths and was divided into eight homesteads, with a water well dug in the center. Thus, the origins of the well-field system go back very far. The Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang dynasties generally followed this practice in turn, and only in the Zhou did it become fully developed.

If we now examine their fields: those in the districts and outlying districts (xiangsui) were managed by the Grand Master of Outlying Districts (Suiren), whose duty is what the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) describes as "ten households have a footpath along the ditch (zhen), a hundred households have a cart-track (tu), a thousand households have a road (dao), and ten thousand households have a highway (lu)"; those in the capital fiefs and borderlands (dubi) were managed by the Master Craftsman (Jiangren), whose duty is what the Rites of Zhou describes as "two plowshares form a pair (ou), nine households form a well (jing), ten li square form a cheng, and a hundred li square form a tong." At that time, fields had fixed allotments and the people had constant livelihoods; even arrogant, fierce, and aggressive men had no way to practice land annexation. As the ancients said: "Harmony, cooperation, and concord arose therefrom; generous simplicity and pure solidarity were completed thereby." Does this not refer to the Zhou people's method of regulating property?

When we further examine their taxation, the levying of wealth was assigned to the Master of Outlying Districts (Suishi), who was charged with delivering the revenues of the countryside into the Royal Treasury (Wangfu), and there was also…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
縣師掌邦國都鄙稍甸郊里之地域而辨
其夫家人民田萊之數及其六畜車輦之
稽以歲時徵其賦貢總之皆惟正之供也
任衆屬之鄉大夫使定公事之征舍矣而
又有均人掌均力政豐年則公旬用三日
中年則公旬用二日無年則公旬用一日
凶札則無力政無財賦總之皆撙節之意
也當此之時賦有定法下有常供雖饕餮
猛鷙之吏無所肆其多取古云事之共給
===
於是乎在民之蕃庶於是乎生其周人經
賦之法之謂乎秦不師古佐以商君於是
阡陌開而良法廢人皆以此爲秦罪固也
而說者謂非自秦始蓋自魯宣初稅畝而
什一之制始壞自李悝盡地力而溝塗之
界無存是秦人之阡陌固已濫觴於此矣
嗟夫世道之不古猶水之愈趨而愈下也
秦爲不道蕩滅古法罪蓋未易更僕數乃
其壞井田而阡陌之者勢實使之而於秦
punctuated:
縣師，掌邦國、都鄙、稍、甸、郊、里之地域，而辨其夫家、人民、田萊之數，及其六畜、車輦之稽，以歲時徵其賦貢，總之皆惟正之供也。任衆屬之鄉大夫，使定公事之征舍矣；而又有均人，掌均力政，豐年則公旬用三日，中年則公旬用二日，無年則公旬用一日，凶札則無力政、無財賦，總之皆撙節之意也。當此之時，賦有定法，下有常供，雖饕餮猛鷙之吏，無所肆其多取。古云：「事之共給，於是乎在；民之蕃庶，於是乎生。」其周人經賦之法之謂乎？

秦不師古，佐以商君，於是阡陌開而良法廢，人皆以此爲秦罪，固也。而說者謂非自秦始：蓋自魯宣初稅畝，而什一之制始壞；自李悝盡地力，而溝塗之界無存，是秦人之阡陌，固已濫觴於此矣。嗟夫！世道之不古，猶水之愈趨而愈下也。秦爲不道，蕩滅古法，罪蓋未易更僕數；乃其壞井田而阡陌之者，勢實使之，而於秦
translation_en:
… the Preceptor of Regions (xianshi), who took charge of the territorial divisions of the states, capital domains, outer domains, royal domains, suburbs, and neighborhoods, distinguishing the numbers of households, people, cultivated fields, and fallow lands, as well as auditing their six domestic animals and carts and hand-carriages, so as to levy their taxes and tributes according to the seasons of the year—in sum, all were strictly regular statutory contributions. The employment of the multitude was assigned to the Township Grandees (xiang dafu), who were charged with determining the levies and exemptions for public service; and there were also the Equalizers (junren), who took charge of equalizing corvée labor: in years of abundance, public corvée used three days; in average years, public corvée used two days; in poor years, public corvée used one day; and in times of famine and epidemic, there was neither corvée labor nor revenue taxation—in sum, all reflected the intention of moderation and restraint. At this time, taxation had fixed laws and those below had constant contributions; even greedy and rapacious officials had no way to indulge in excessive exactions. As the ancients said: "The supply of public affairs rests upon this; the flourishing multitude of the people arises from this." Does this not refer to the Zhou people's method of regulating taxation?

Qin did not model itself on antiquity; assisted by Lord Shang (Shang Yang 商鞅), ridge-paths (qianmo) were opened up and the good laws were abolished. Everyone holds this to be the crime of Qin, which is certainly true. Yet commentators say that it did not begin with Qin: for ever since Duke Xuan of Lu (Lu Xuan 魯宣) first taxed by the acre (mu), the system of the one-tenth tax began to break down; and ever since Li Kui 李悝 exhausted the productivity of the soil, the boundaries of ditches and paths ceased to exist—thus the ridge-paths of the people of Qin had indeed already originated here. Alas! That the ways of the world do not match antiquity is just like water flowing ever further downward. Qin acted without principle and swept away ancient laws; its crimes are so numerous that they could not easily be counted even by changing attendants. Yet as for its destroying the well-field system (jingtian) and turning it into ridge-paths, the trend of circumstances truly caused this, so toward Qin…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
又何誅焉赤帝受命去古未遠顧獨不能
變秦法以復井田人皆以此爲漢咎固也
而說者又曰復古難夫以智如酇侯能收
前代之圖籍賢如子房猶有儒者之氣象
使井田而可復則漢人當先爲之矣嗟夫
書契苟可觀固不必結繩而後爲古也昔
人謂欲復井田非數百年專力不可又云
古者自治其國終歲惟井田一事今統一
天下吏數代易就使爲之終無成效而於
===
漢又何惑焉自是而後法制代變得失世
殊以田言之漢武行代田之法孝哀下限
田之議唐人有授田之制宋人定方田之
等是皆不失爲一代之美意而求其最近
古者其惟唐之授田乎考其制成人者人
授一頃其田十畝爲口分二十畝爲永業
凡徙鄉及貧無以葬者得鬻世業自狹鄉
徙寬鄉者得鬻口分已鬻者不復受此殆
庶幾於周人一夫百畝之法可謂得矣然
punctuated: 又何誅焉？赤帝受命，去古未遠，顧獨不能變秦法以復井田，人皆以此爲漢咎，固也。而說者又曰：「復古難。」夫以智如酇侯，能收前代之圖籍；賢如子房，猶有儒者之氣象。使井田而可復，則漢人當先爲之矣。嗟夫！書契苟可觀，固不必結繩而後爲古也。昔人謂欲復井田，非數百年專力不可。又云：「古者自治其國，終歲惟井田一事；今統一天下，吏數代易，就使爲之，終無成效。」而於漢又何惑焉？自是而後，法制代變，得失世殊。以田言之，漢武行代田之法，孝哀下限田之議，唐人有授田之制，宋人定方田之等，是皆不失爲一代之美意。而求其最近古者，其惟唐之授田乎！考其制，成人者人授一頃，其田十畝爲口分，二十畝爲永業。凡徙鄉及貧無以葬者，得鬻世業；自狹鄉徙寬鄉者，得鬻口分，已鬻者不復受。此殆庶幾於周人一夫百畝之法，可謂得矣。然
translation_en: … what then is there to condemn in Qin? When the Red Emperor [Liu Bang 劉邦, Emperor Gaozu of Han] received the Mandate, antiquity was not yet far off, yet he alone was unable to alter the laws of Qin to restore the well-field system. Everyone faults the Han for this, and understandably so. Yet commentators also say that restoring antiquity is difficult. With someone as wise as the Marquis of Zan [Xiao He 蕭何], who knew to gather the maps and registers of the preceding dynasty, and someone as worthy as Zifang [Zhang Liang 張良], who still possessed the bearing of a Confucian scholar, had the well-field system been restorable, the men of Han would surely have been the first to do it. Alas! So long as written documents and tallies are serviceable, one need not return to knotted cords in order to be true to antiquity. Men of the past said that if one wished to restore the well-field system, nothing less than several hundred years of dedicated effort would suffice. They also said: "In antiquity, when rulers governed their own states, throughout the entire year the well-field system was their sole great undertaking; today the realm is unified, and officials are repeatedly replaced, so even if one attempted it, in the end there would be no tangible results." What then is there to be puzzled about in the case of Han? From this time onward, laws and institutions changed from dynasty to dynasty, and their merits and defects varied from age to age. Speaking in terms of land: Emperor Wu of Han practiced the method of alternating fields (daitian), Emperor Xiao'ai [Emperor Ai of Han] sent down proposals for limiting landholdings (xiantian), the men of Tang had the system of land allotment (shoutian), and the men of Song established the grades of square fields (fangtian). None of these failed to represent the admirable intentions of an era; yet if we seek the one closest to antiquity, would it not be the land allotment of the Tang? Examining its regulations, each adult was allotted one qing [one hundred mu], of which eighty [text reads "ten" 十, likely a misprint for 八十] mu served as personal share land (koufen) and twenty mu as hereditary land (yongye). All who moved to another district or were too poor to bury their dead were permitted to sell their hereditary land; those who moved from congested districts to spacious districts were permitted to sell their personal share land, though once sold they would not receive another grant. This came quite close to the Zhou method of one hundred mu per husbandman, and may be called a success. Yet …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其後也羨田無厲禁而鬻田遂多惰民不
嚴驅而遊食日衆此則弊生於法乆亦其
末流之所必至者固不可以是而病授田
也以賦言之漢初十五而稅一光武稅一
於三十唐有租庸調之名宋有均稅之限
是皆不失爲一時之良法而求其最近古
者其惟唐之租庸調乎考其制有田則有
租歲無過二石也有家則有調隨其土之
所出也有身則有庸役無過二十日也此
殆髣髴於周人粟布力役之征可謂得矣
然其失也户口之盛衰不一而怨起於取
盈流移之虛實難稽而奸生於避役故其
後行兩稅而專主資產葢所以矯其專主
户口之弊固未可以是而病楊炎也洪惟
我
國家法古爲治不惟其迹而惟其意田有官
民是殷人助法之遺也賦有等則是夏后
則壤之制也限有夏秋是周官以時徵財
punctuated: 其後也，羨田無厲禁，而鬻田遂多；惰民不嚴驅，而遊食日衆。此則弊生於法乆，亦其末流之所必至者，固不可以是而病授田也。以賦言之：漢初十五而稅一，光武稅一於三十，唐有租庸調之名，宋有均稅之限，是皆不失爲一時之良法。而求其最近古者，其惟唐之租庸調乎？考其制：有田則有租，歲無過二石也；有家則有調，隨其土之所出也；有身則有庸，役無過二十日也。此殆髣髴於周人粟布力役之征，可謂得矣。然其失也，户口之盛衰不一，而怨起於取盈；流移之虛實難稽，而奸生於避役。故其後行兩稅而專主資產，葢所以矯其專主户口之弊，固未可以是而病楊炎也。洪惟我國家法古爲治，不惟其迹而惟其意。田有官民，是殷人助法之遺也；賦有等則，是夏后則壤之制也；限有夏秋，是周官以時徵財
translation_en:
… Later on, surplus land was not strictly prohibited, and consequently the selling of land became widespread; idle people were not rigorously driven back to farming, and vagrant idlers grew more numerous by the day. These were abuses arising from the law having been in place for a long time, an inevitable result of its later degeneration; certainly one cannot on this account fault the system of land allotment itself.

Speaking in terms of taxation: at the beginning of the Han, the tax was one part in fifteen, while Emperor Guangwu (光武) taxed one part in thirty; the Tang had the system known as the grain tax, corvée exemption tax, and household cloth tax (zuyongdiao 租庸調), and the Song had quotas for equalized taxation (junshui 均稅). All of these may be considered good laws for their respective times. Yet if we seek the one closest to antiquity, is it not the zuyongdiao system of the Tang? Examining its regulations: where there was land, there was the grain tax (zu 租), not exceeding two piculs (shi 石) per year; where there was a household, there was the cloth or local-product levy (diao 調), according to what the local soil produced; where there was an adult male, there was the labor duty (yong 庸), with service not exceeding twenty days. This closely resembled the Zhou requisitions of grain, cloth, and labor service, and may be said to have hit the mark. Yet in its decline, the growth and shrinkage of registered households were uneven, and resentment arose from demands to fill fixed quotas; the truth or falsity of migration and displacement was difficult to verify, and fraud grew out of attempts to evade service. Therefore, when the Two-Tax System (liangshui 兩稅) was later implemented, focusing exclusively on property and assets, it was intended to correct the abuses of focusing exclusively on household registration; certainly one cannot on this account fault Yang Yan (楊炎).

Looking upon our August Dynasty, it models its governance on antiquity, following not its mere outward traces but its underlying spirit. That land is divided into official and private is a legacy of the Yin people's mutual-aid system (zhu 助); that taxes are graded by ranks and rates is the system of the Xia sovereigns' assessment according to soil quality; that collection deadlines are set in summer and autumn is the Rites of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官) principle of levying revenue according to the season …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之義也其間經畫之詳意義之精盖陋漢
唐宋於不足言陸贄所謂其取法也遠其
立意也深其斂財也均其成人也固其裁
規也簡其備患也周此六言者我
國家田賦之法足以當之矣第法行日久弊
亦潛滋侵隱詭射至難究詰我
皇上軫念民瘼謂此弊且不可長會有以度田
請者
上於是可其奏
===
令天下徧度民田焉百年來伏奸積弊一旦掃
而更之即滇省僻在萬里外亦有以荷
天子之仁窮荒父老扶杖相呼願少須臾無死
此千載而一時也執事又欲以此時定經
久之計愚生末學其焉能知之顧聞之道
路則曰稽籍之法不可不嚴也導利之政
不可不講也仁言之須不可不信也夫今
度田且竣矣其田畝之廣狹賦額之多
寡業且書之于版籍矣覈之不嚴則奸民
punctuated: 之義也。其間經畫之詳、意義之精，盖陋漢、唐、宋於不足言。陸贄所謂「其取法也遠，其立意也深，其斂財也均，其成人也固，其裁規也簡，其備患也周」，此六言者，我國家田賦之法足以當之矣。第法行日久，弊亦潛滋，侵隱詭射，至難究詰。我皇上軫念民瘼，謂此弊且不可長。會有以度田請者，上於是可其奏，令天下徧度民田焉。百年來伏奸積弊，一旦掃而更之，即滇省僻在萬里外，亦有以荷天子之仁，窮荒父老扶杖相呼，願少須臾無死，此千載而一時也。執事又欲以此時定經久之計，愚生末學，其焉能知之？顧聞之道路，則曰：稽籍之法不可不嚴也，導利之政不可不講也，仁言之須不可不信也。夫今度田且竣矣，其田畝之廣狹、賦額之多寡，業且書之于版籍矣。覈之不嚴，則奸民
translation_en: … principle [of collecting revenue at the proper seasons]. In the thoroughness of its planning and the subtlety of its underlying meaning, it renders Han, Tang, and Song dynasty practices too crude to be worth mentioning. As Lu Zhi 陸贄 put it: "Its models are drawn from afar, its founding intent is profound, its collection of wealth is equitable, its sustaining of the people is secure, its regulations are simple, and its precautions against trouble are comprehensive." Our Dynasty's land-tax system is truly worthy of these six statements. Yet when a law has been in effect for a long time, abuses secretly multiply; encroachment, concealment, fraudulent registration, and tax evasion have become extremely difficult to investigate and prosecute. Our Emperor, deeply concerned for the sufferings of the people, declared that such abuses must not be allowed to grow. When someone submitted a memorial requesting a land survey, His Majesty approved the memorial and ordered a comprehensive survey of private lands throughout the Empire. The hidden frauds and accumulated abuses of a hundred years were swept away and reformed in a single morning. Even Yunnan province, remote as it is ten thousand li away, has been able to receive the benevolence of the Son of Heaven; elders in the farthest wilds lean on their staffs and call out to one another, wishing to linger a little longer before dying [to witness this]. This is an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. Now Your Excellency wishes to seize this moment to establish a permanent plan. How could an ignorant student of superficial learning like myself know how to do so? Yet from what I have heard in the streets, people say: the methods for auditing the registers must be made strict; policies for channeling economic benefit must be studied; and the promulgation [? 須, perhaps for 頒] of benevolent words must be made trustworthy. Now the measurement of the land is nearly complete, and the breadth or narrowness of the acreage and the size of the tax quotas are already being recorded in the registers. If the verification is not strict, then unscrupulous commoners …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
富室私與胥吏爲市其田必以廣爲狹其
賦必以多爲寡甚則盡其數而隱之以爲
無而且以其所隱所損之數移而加之貧
懦之夫是小民之所以受毒而無告也至
其尤甚者則或惡其害已而去其籍是故
周官書版之職掌之以司民令而後知聖
人之爲慮遠也爲今之計其必專稽覈之
官而密收藏之地重欺隱之懲而嚴去籍
之禁此弊庶幾少戢乎夫
===
今天下財賦盛於東南而吳越其首稱也以
全滇財賦乃不及彼一大縣此何以故哉
吳越沮洳之地水利弘多故能化荒瘠爲
沃壤滇之爲田者大半皆狐貍嘷聚之區
而荊榛莽棘之所翳也今田則清矣賦則
均矣然或昊天不惠玄冥失職則雖漢陰
丈人何所負而灌焉是故周禮治野之制
必有溝澮以時其畜洩聖人固非樂爲是
多事也茲欲爲久計其必遍山畦而溝洫
punctuated:
富室私與胥吏爲市，其田必以廣爲狹，其賦必以多爲寡，甚則盡其數而隱之以爲無，而且以其所隱所損之數，移而加之貧懦之夫，是小民之所以受毒而無告也。至其尤甚者，則或惡其害已而去其籍。是故《周官》書版之職掌之以司民，令而後知聖人之爲慮遠也。爲今之計，其必專稽覈之官，而密收藏之地，重欺隱之懲，而嚴去籍之禁，此弊庶幾少戢乎！

夫今天下財賦盛於東南，而吳、越其首稱也。以全滇財賦，乃不及彼一大縣，此何以故哉？吳、越沮洳之地，水利弘多，故能化荒瘠爲沃壤；滇之爲田者，大半皆狐貍嘷聚之區，而荊榛莽棘之所翳也。今田則清矣，賦則均矣，然或昊天不惠，玄冥失職，則雖漢陰丈人，何所負而灌焉？是故《周禮》治野之制，必有溝澮以時其畜洩，聖人固非樂爲是多事也。茲欲爲久計，其必遍山畦而溝洫
translation_en:
…and wealthy households privately collude with petty clerks to strike deals: their fields will surely be recorded as narrow when they are wide, and their taxes as small when they are large. In extreme cases, they conceal the entire amount and claim to have nothing at all, while furthermore shifting the amounts they have concealed and reduced onto poor and timid men. This is why the common people suffer harm with no one to appeal to. As for the most egregious cases, some even destroy the registers out of hatred that the records harm their own interests. Therefore, in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the duty of inscribing the registers was entrusted to the Director of the Populace (Simin); looking at present [?] circumstances, one realizes how far-sighted the sages' concern was! In planning for the present, we must assign dedicated officials for auditing and verification, secure the places where registers are stored, stiffen punishments for fraudulent concealment, and strictly enforce prohibitions against destroying registers—then this abuse may perhaps be somewhat curbed!

Now today, the fiscal revenues of the empire flourish in the southeast, with Wu and Yue foremost among them. Yet the fiscal revenue of the entire province of Yunnan does not even match that of a single large county there—why is this so? In the low-lying, marshy lands of Wu and Yue, waterworks are abundant, enabling them to transform barren and poor soil into fertile farmland. What serves as farmland in Yunnan is for the most part territory where foxes howl and gather, overgrown with brambles, thorns, and thickets. Now the fields have been surveyed and cleared, and the taxes have been equalized; yet if vast Heaven should be unkind and Xuanming [the god of water and winter] fail in his duty, then even if one were the old man from south of the Han River, what water would he carry on his back to irrigate with? Therefore, in the system of managing the countryside in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), there always had to be ditches and channels to regulate storage and drainage according to the seasons; the sages certainly did not create all this extra trouble out of mere pleasure. If we now wish to make a long-term plan, we must construct irrigation ditches and channels across all the mountain fields…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
理國猶治身然形氣壯實則精神充盛血
脉流通則痿痺之患不作人民者邦之形
氣山川險要關隘道路者邦之血脉也人
民寡鮮氣勢卑弱則外侮得以侵凌封壤
阻塞鄰援隔絶則窺伺負固之徒萌跋扈
之心而漸不可長善固國者必使吾民生
養蕃息足耕足戰民不攺聚而擅富强之
勝至於水陸要害可嚴則嚴可關則關使
吾之中國聲勢聯絡唇齒相依出則折衝
===
外侮內則釁蘖不萌而磐石之固在我矣
舍此不圖是自坐深穽而不顧凌壓之虞
非計之得者也執事察全滇之形勝籌保
國之令圖洛諏及此遐方之士生長四塞
之中日夜念此至熟也夫良醫之治病也
察其形色觀其脉理閼塞不通必加劑砭
以疏決之而後其人可以望壽考而無病
故參苓之與烏附竝行不廢否則人之病
蹶然不瘳矣理國何以異此夫今日之滇
punctuated:
理國猶治身然。形氣壯實，則精神充盛；血脉流通，則痿痺之患不作。人民者，邦之形氣；山川險要、關隘道路者，邦之血脉也。人民寡鮮，氣勢卑弱，則外侮得以侵凌；封壤阻塞，鄰援隔絶，則窺伺負固之徒萌跋扈之心，而漸不可長。善固國者，必使吾民生養蕃息，足耕足戰，民不攺聚而擅富强之勝；至於水陸要害，可嚴則嚴，可關則關，使吾之中國聲勢聯絡，唇齒相依，出則折衝外侮，內則釁蘖不萌，而磐石之固在我矣。舍此不圖，是自坐深穽而不顧凌壓之虞，非計之得者也。

執事察全滇之形勝，籌保國之令圖，洛諏及此。遐方之士，生長四塞之中，日夜念此至熟也。夫良醫之治病也，察其形色，觀其脉理，閼塞不通，必加劑砭以疏決之，而後其人可以望壽考而無病，故參苓之與烏附竝行不廢，否則人之病蹶然不瘳矣。理國何以異此？夫今日之滇，
translation_en:
Governing a state is like treating the human body. When one's physical form and vital energy are robust and solid, the spirit is full and vigorous; when the blood and vessels circulate smoothly, the affliction of paralysis and numbness does not arise. The people are the physical form and vital energy of the state; the strategic mountains and rivers, passes, defiles, and roads are the blood and vessels of the state. If the people are few and scarce and their vigor and momentum are low and weak, external aggressors can encroach upon and bully them; if the borders and territories are obstructed and blocked and aid from neighbors is cut off, then opportunists who rely on natural strongholds will harbor unruly ambitions, a tendency that must not be allowed to grow. Those who are skilled at securing the state must ensure that our people are nourished and multiply, sufficient for both farming and warfare, so that without even altering how the people are gathered, we command the advantage of wealth and strength. As for strategic chokepoints by water and land, where they should be strictly guarded, guard them strictly; where they should be opened up [or: barred with passes], open [or: bar] them. This ensures that the prestige and influence of our Central Plain are interconnected, mutually dependent like lips and teeth; going forth, we can repel external insults, and within, seeds of strife will not sprout, so that rock-solid security rests with us. To set this aside and fail to plan for it is to sit oneself at the bottom of a deep pit while ignoring the danger of being crushed from above—this is not a sound strategy.

Your Excellency has examined the strategic topography of all of Dian [Yunnan], planned admirable schemes for safeguarding the state, and extended your inquiries [reading 洛 as 咨] on this matter to us. As a scholar from a distant region, born and raised amidst territories hemmed in on all four sides, I have pondered this day and night until I am thoroughly familiar with it. Now, when a skilled physician treats an illness, he examines the patient's physical appearance and complexion and observes the principles of his pulse. Where there is blockage and obstruction, he must apply medicinaldecoctions and stone needles to dredge and clear it, and only then can the person hope for longevity and freedom from illness. Therefore, ginseng and poria are used alongside aconite and monkshood without either being discarded; otherwise, a person's illness would end in collapse without recovery. How is governing a state any different from this? Now, in the Dian [Yunnan] of today,…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
土司謂晏然寧謐如强壯之人也無故而
煩民畚鍤以興得已之役不以爲紓則擾
故曰非常之原黎民懼焉然深憂遠慮之
士玄究往牒指畫方輿圖險易於目前計
興衰於事外安能徇尋常之尠議而忽豪
傑之沉謀哉何者滇土天下之遠藩處夷
落之中爲中國屛蔽其守與內地異周禮
孟冬之月有司坏城郭固封疆完要塞塞
蹊徑此爲備外者言之也若滇則孤懸萬
里恃中國以爲聲援其地遼闊廣遠實東
===
則西虛南顧則北單弱不患無地而患無
人以守外有窺伺之虞而內有負固之漸
如秦之函谷蜀之劒門一夫當關萬夫莫
開非如中州之四通五達一號召之間士
馬雲集無仰哺待救之難也甞考自古入
滇之路有三楚將莊蹻略巴黔以西威定
屬楚其所由入則今之貴州古之牂牁郡
也南越以財物役屬夜郎漢王然于乘誅
punctuated: 土司謂晏然寧謐，如强壯之人也，無故而煩民畚鍤，以興得已之役，不以爲紓則擾。故曰：「非常之原，黎民懼焉。」然深憂遠慮之士，玄究往牒，指畫方輿，圖險易於目前，計興衰於事外，安能徇尋常之尠議，而忽豪傑之沉謀哉？何者？滇土，天下之遠藩，處夷落之中，爲中國屛蔽，其守與內地異。《周禮》，孟冬之月，有司坏城郭，固封疆，完要塞，塞蹊徑，此爲備外者言之也。若滇則孤懸萬里，恃中國以爲聲援。其地遼闊廣遠，實東則西虛，南顧則北單弱，不患無地，而患無人以守；外有窺伺之虞，而內有負固之漸。如秦之函谷、蜀之劒門，一夫當關，萬夫莫開，非如中州之四通五達，一號召之間，士馬雲集，無仰哺待救之難也。甞考自古入滇之路有三：楚將莊蹻略巴、黔以西，威定屬楚，其所由入，則今之貴州，古之牂牁郡也；南越以財物役屬夜郎，漢王然于乘誅
translation_en: … native chieftains (tusi) seem peaceful and tranquil, like a strong and healthy person. If, without cause, we burden the people with baskets and spades to undertake corvée labor that could well be dispensed with, they will regard it not as relief, but as harassment. Thus it is said: "At the inception of extraordinary undertakings, the common people are afraid." Yet how could men of deep concern and far-reaching foresight—who profoundly investigate past records, map out the terrain, assess strategic difficulties and advantages before their eyes, and calculate rise and decline beyond immediate events—yield to ordinary, shallow opinions and neglect the deep counsels of heroic minds? Why is this? The land of Dian [Yunnan] is a distant frontier screen of the Empire, situated amidst non-Chinese settlements, serving as a protective shield for the Central Kingdom; its defense differs from that of the interior. In the Rites of Zhou [actually the "Monthly Ordinances" of the Record of Rites], in the first month of winter, the authorities repair city walls and ramparts, secure frontier boundaries, mend strategic passes, and block mountain paths—this was spoken with reference to guarding against external foes. As for Dian, however, it hangs isolated ten thousand li away, relying on the Central Kingdom for support and reinforcement. Its territory is vast and far-flung: if we reinforce the east, the west is left empty; if we attend to the south, the north becomes thin and weak. The worry is not a lack of land, but a lack of men to defend it; externally there is the danger of opportunistic encroachment, while internally there is the creeping tendency to rely on natural strongholds in defiance. Like Hangu Pass in Qin or Jianmen Pass in Shu, where one man holding the pass can keep ten thousand at bay, it is unlike the Central Plains with their thoroughfares extending in all directions, where at a single summons troops and horses gather like clouds, free from the difficulty of waiting to be fed and rescued. I have examined the routes for entering Dian since antiquity and found there are three. The Chu general Zhuang Qiao conquered the regions west of Ba and Qian, establishing his authority and annexing them to Chu; the route by which he entered is present-day Guizhou, the ancient commandery of Zangke. Southern Yue (Nanyue) used wealth and goods to subordinate Yelang, and Wang Ranyu of the Han took advantage of the military might from the execution of…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
南越之威脅取滇土史稱牂牁江出番禺
城下其源在田州泗城之境與雲之廣南
貴之普安實相接壤輕舟東下徑達南海
所謂南路也司馬相如持檄喻西南夷諸
葛武侯渡瀘深入皆由益部取道南中非
古所謂西路耶自昔經略西南掃蕩草竊
其故道章章若是此三道不通則全滇郡
縣四望阻塞而扼我之吭拊我之背勢所
必致矣又以其形勢言之東爲黔中在今
===
日爲内地固勿論若南蔽元江元江之外
爲車里此又外則爲交阯西蔽永昌永昌
之外爲麓川又外則爲緬甸西北則羈縻
麗江以爲捍蔽此外則爲吐蕃氣勢稍弱
則吐蕃西伺南交外竊西南諸夷不受約
束此又其小者天寶間張虔陀暴使滇人
唐有南詔之衂連結吐蕃終唐之世不入
職貢宋室不競遂棄爲異域蒙段二氏崛
據數百年計其士馬不足當中國一大郡
punctuated: 南越之威，脅取滇土。史稱牂牁江出番禺城下，其源在田州、泗城之境，與雲之廣南、貴之普安實相接壤，輕舟東下，徑達南海，所謂南路也。司馬相如持檄喻西南夷，諸葛武侯渡瀘深入，皆由益部取道南中，非古所謂西路耶？自昔經略西南，掃蕩草竊，其故道章章若是。此三道不通，則全滇郡縣四望阻塞，而扼我之吭，拊我之背，勢所必致矣。又以其形勢言之，東爲黔中，在今日爲内地，固勿論。若南蔽元江，元江之外爲車里，此又外則爲交阯；西蔽永昌，永昌之外爲麓川，又外則爲緬甸；西北則羈縻麗江以爲捍蔽，此外則爲吐蕃。氣勢稍弱，則吐蕃西伺，南交外竊，西南諸夷不受約束，此又其小者。天寶間，張虔陀暴使滇人，唐有南詔之衂，連結吐蕃，終唐之世不入職貢。宋室不競，遂棄爲異域。蒙、段二氏崛據數百年，計其士馬，不足當中國一大郡，
translation_en: … the prestige of destroying Nanyue 南越 to intimidate and seize the lands of Dian 滇. The histories state that the Zangke River 牂牁江 emerges below the city walls of Panyu 番禺, and that its source lies within the borders of Tianzhou 田州 and Sicheng 泗城, which actually adjoin Guangnan 廣南 in Yunnan and Pu'an 普安 in Guizhou; light boats descending eastward reach the Southern Sea directly—this is what is called the Southern Route. Sima Xiangru 司馬相如 bearing a proclamation to instruct the Southwestern Barbarians (Xinan Yi 西南夷) and Marquis Wu, Zhuge Liang 諸葛武侯, crossing the Lu River 瀘水 to penetrate deeply, both proceeded from Yizhou 益部 via Nanzhong 南中—is this not what was anciently called the Western Route? Since antiquity, in pacifying and administering the Southwest and sweeping away bandits and rebels, the old routes have been as clearly evident as this. If these three routes are blocked, then the prefectures and counties of all Dian will be obstructed in every direction, and having our throat throttled and our back struck is an inevitable outcome. Furthermore, speaking in terms of its strategic topography: to the east is Qianzhong 黔中, which today is interior territory and thus needs no discussion. As for the south, it is shielded by Yuanjiang 元江; beyond Yuanjiang is Cheli 車里, and still further beyond that is Jiaozhi 交阯. To the west, it is shielded by Yongchang 永昌; beyond Yongchang is Luchuan 麓川, and still further beyond that is Burma (Miandian 緬甸). To the northwest, Lijiang 麗江 is held under loose-rein (jimi 羈縻) control as a defensive screen, and beyond that is Tibet (Tuban 吐蕃). Whenever imperial vigor weakens even slightly, Tibet spies from the west, Jiaozhi in the south encroaches from outside, and the various barbarians of the southwest refuse to abide by restraint—and even these are the lesser dangers. During the Tianbao 天寶 era (742–756), Zhang Qiantuo 張虔陀 tyrannically mistreated the people of Dian, leading to the Tang dynasty's defeat at the hands of Nanzhao 南詔, which allied itself with Tibet and to the end of the Tang dynasty never again entered to present regular tribute. The Song house lacked martial strength and consequently abandoned it as foreign territory. The Meng 蒙 and Duan 段 clans rose up and held it for several hundred years; yet if one calculates their troops and horses, they were not enough to match a single large commandery of China, …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
然窮天下之力不能下者則以憑恃險遠
下流仰攻形不便勢不利也我
太祖高皇帝剷平僭僞混一區宇戡定西夷置
立州郡二百年來夷鞣之風變爲中土編
辮之習易爲冠裳一方之人如脫陰翳而
覩日月之昭融
神功
聖德輝映古今矣然執事之問若有隱憂然者
何也爲滇人之慮遠也且執事所謂紆遲
===
驛遞則病於官蹂遠侵掠則病於民是固
然矣然又有甚者焉中原之人入滇其道
里自西至者上荊門涉瀘水登陸陟烏撒
自南至者遡流上郴桂泛洞庭巨浸又數
千里始達沅州攀緣關嶺其烏道盤鬱苗
夷出没四旁於危磴中壘土築堡憑高瞭
遠晝柝宵鉦日晏啓閉游徼之兵負弩尾
躡而後敢啓行士旅往來若履虎尾而蹈
春冰儻或白晝之中剽人而奪之金如比
punctuated: 然窮天下之力不能下者，則以憑恃險遠，下流仰攻，形不便，勢不利也。我太祖高皇帝剷平僭僞，混一區宇，戡定西夷，置立州郡。二百年來，夷鞣之風變爲中土，編辮之習易爲冠裳，一方之人如脫陰翳而覩日月之昭融，神功聖德，輝映古今矣！然執事之問若有隱憂然者，何也？爲滇人之慮遠也。且執事所謂「紆遲驛遞則病於官，蹂遠侵掠則病於民」，是固然矣；然又有甚者焉。中原之人入滇，其道里：自西至者，上荊門，涉瀘水，登陸陟烏撒；自南至者，遡流上郴、桂，泛洞庭巨浸，又數千里始達沅州。攀緣關嶺，其烏道盤鬱，苗夷出没四旁，於危磴中壘土築堡，憑高瞭遠，晝柝宵鉦，日晏啓閉，游徼之兵負弩尾躡，而後敢啓行。士旅往來，若履虎尾而蹈春冰，儻或白晝之中，剽人而奪之金，如比
translation_en:
…Yet the reason the full strength of the realm could not subdue them was that they relied on their precipitous and distant terrain; attacking upward from lower ground, the topography was inconvenient and the strategic position disadvantageous.

Our Grand Progenitor the Lofty Emperor (Taizu Gao Huangdi) eradicated the usurpers and pretenders, unified the realm, pacified the western non-Chinese peoples (yi), and established prefectures and counties. For two hundred years, the customs of the non-Chinese territories [?] have been transformed into those of the Central Lands, and the practice of braiding hair has been exchanged for caps and robes. The people of this region are as though freed from dark gloom to behold the bright radiance of the sun and moon. His divine achievements and sagely virtue shine across past and present!

Yet Your Excellency's question seems to harbor a hidden concern—why is this? It is because your concern for the people of Dian (Yunnan) is far-reaching. Moreover, what Your Excellency refers to—that "circuitous and delayed postal relay stations are an affliction to officials, while distant trampling and plundering raids are an affliction to the common people"—is certainly true. Yet there are matters even worse than this.

When people from the Central Plain enter Dian, as for their routes: those arriving from the west ascend past Jingmen, cross the Lu River, and go ashore to climb toward Wusa; those arriving from the south go upstream past Chen and Gui, cross the vast expanse of Lake Dongting, and travel several thousand li further before finally reaching Yuanzhou. Clambering over mountain passes and ridges, where the bird-paths [鳥道, printed 烏道] wind through dense growth, Miao and other non-Chinese peoples (yi) appear and disappear on all sides. Amid the perilous stone steps, earthen ramparts and forts are built to look out far from the heights, with wooden clappers by day and gongs by night, opening and closing the gates only late in the day. Only when patrolling soldiers carry crossbows and follow closely at their heels do travelers dare to set out. Scholars and merchants traveling back and forth are as if treading on a tiger's tail or walking on spring ice. Should someone in broad daylight rob people and seize their gold, as in recent [比, for 近?]…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text: 者惟執事財擇幸甚
punctuated: 者。惟執事財擇，幸甚。
translation_en: … I would be most fortunate if Your Excellency would deign to select from these according to your judgment.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
萬曆壬午秋滇南復大比郡
國士御史董裕祇奉
明詔諸凡虔毖而其申飭文體特
勤貞一惟文章關乎世運蓋
自古記之考信先代始未嘗
不務體要而後乃漸漓也在
===
人挽之而已我
國家以經術取士洪永之文醇
朴藴藉雖有巧心不可論工
拙所傳可觀也已更而奇再
更而麗乃今又異焉羣率而
爲玄虛謂之近體甚者去離
經傳踰越準繩以爲鮮而氣
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序
萬曆壬午秋，滇南復大比郡國士。御史董裕祇奉明詔，諸凡虔毖，而其申飭文體特勤。貞一惟文章關乎世運，蓋自古記之。考信先代，始未嘗不務體要，而後乃漸漓也，在人挽之而已。我國家以經術取士，洪、永之文，醇朴藴藉，雖有巧心，不可論工拙，所傳可觀也。已更而奇，再更而麗，乃今又異焉：羣率而爲玄虛，謂之「近體」；甚者去離經傳，踰越準繩，以爲鮮，而氣
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the renwu year of the Wanli era (1582), Yunnan once again held the great triennial examination of scholars from its prefectures and subprefectures. The Censor Dong Yu 董裕 respectfully received the enlightened imperial edict, attending to every matter with reverent care, and was especially diligent in his injunctions regarding literary style.

I, Zhenyi 貞一, reflect that literature is bound up with the fortunes of the age—a truth recorded since antiquity. Examining the reliable records of former dynasties, we find that in the beginning they never failed to strive for substance and essentials, yet later gradually declined into superficiality; it simply depends on people to restore it. Our Dynasty selects scholars on the basis of mastery of the Classics. The writing of the Hongwu (1368–1398) and Yongle (1403–1424) eras was pure, unadorned, and rich with restrained meaning; even where there was ingenious thought, one could not judge it in terms of mere technical skill or clumsiness, as can be seen in what has been handed down. Later it changed toward the strange, and changed again toward the ornate, until today it has become different once more: people follow one another in producing abstruse emptiness, calling it the "modern style" (jinti 近體). In extreme cases, they depart from the Classics and commentaries and overstep the established standards, taking this to be fresh and novel, while the vital force…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
薄矣雖數勤
詔旨則曰有司者悅是也若是是
以訓之之道戒之也又何異
焉貞一令不自意獲執事於
此貞一不佞竊有慕夫王師
旦歐陽脩之能任也滇郎非
四方所視夫孰非聲教之區
===
焉拜聘以來矢天自許以爲
明
上指信士心是在今日故頃所推
擇主於矯偏習有能持循矩
矱雖質必錄非是雖工必黜
即雅有時名或不在選然貞
一無顧也嗟夫亦足明貞一
punctuated: 薄矣。雖數勤詔旨，則曰：「有司者悅是也。」若是，是以訓之之道戒之也，又何異焉？貞一令不自意獲執事於此，貞一不佞，竊有慕夫王師旦、歐陽脩之能任也。滇郎非四方所視，夫孰非聲教之區焉？拜聘以來，矢天自許，以爲明上指、信士心，是在今日。故頃所推擇，主於矯偏習：有能持循矩矱，雖質必錄；非是，雖工必黜。即雅有時名，或不在選，然貞一無顧也。嗟夫！亦足明貞一
translation_en: … becomes thin. Even though imperial edicts have repeatedly urged reform, they say, "This is what the officials in charge are pleased with." If it is like this, then what is used to warn them is the very way they are being taught—so what is strange about the result?
