Now [? 令 for 今], I, Zhenyi, unexpectedly obtained the task of officiating here. Unworthy as I, Zhenyi, am, I privately admire how Wang Shidan 王師旦 and Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 were able to shoulder their responsibilities. Even if [? 郎 for 即] Yunnan is not a place toward which the four quarters look as a model, how is it not a region within the reach of the dynasty's civilizing teaching? Ever since receiving my appointment, I have sworn before Heaven and vowed to myself that clarifying the Emperor's intent and winning the trust of the scholars' hearts rests upon today. Therefore, in the selections I have just made, my main purpose was to rectify biased habits: if someone was able to adhere to proper standards and rules, even if his writing was plain, he was必ず recorded; if not, even if his writing was artfully wrought, he was rejected. Even those who have long enjoyed contemporary renown were in some cases not among those chosen, yet I, Zhenyi, had no qualms about it. Alas! This is also enough to show my, Zhenyi's…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之不量其力也而又私惟濾
僻壤耳假令吳越諸國較短
論長不可同年語也猶然以
實求之未甞缺人如皆有意
世運不以爲細故也者而力
挽之則所稱體要何渠不如
往也文旣錄御史又顧而問
===
士行貞一則沉思乆之然後
敢對卽不盡中其實也庶幾
得五乎嚮者貞一觀其深矣
夫士之注思也神行其間其
平其陂若或傳之此非在其
聲律色澤也又非在其能深
談理趣而慷慨當時也貞一
punctuated: 之不量其力也。而又私惟濾僻壤耳，假令吳、越諸國較短論長，不可同年語也，猶然以實求之，未甞缺人。如皆有意世運，不以爲細故也者，而力挽之，則所稱體要，何渠不如往也？文旣錄，御史又顧而問士行。貞一則沉思乆之，然後敢對：卽不盡中其實也，庶幾得五乎？嚮者貞一觀其深矣。夫士之注思也，神行其間，其平其陂，若或傳之。此非在其聲律、色澤也，又非在其能深談理趣而慷慨當時也。貞一
translation_en:
…failed to measure my own strength! Yet I also privately reflected that Dian [濾?] is merely a remote region; if one were to compare strengths and weaknesses with the various territories of Wu and Yue, they could not be spoken of in the same breath. Even so, when one seeks on the basis of substance, there is never a lack of men. If all set their minds on the fortunes of the age, not regarding this as a trifling matter, and strive with all their might to turn the tide, then as for what is called fundamental substance and essentials, why should it quickly not equal the past?

Once the essays had been selected for the record, the Censor turned and asked about the conduct of the scholars. I, Zhenyi, pondered deeply for a long time before daring to reply: Even if I have not hit the mark entirely as to their true substance, perhaps I have succeeded in half the cases? Previously, I, Zhenyi, have observed what lies deep within them. Now, when a scholar concentrates his thoughts, his spirit moves through his writing; whether his mind is level or inclined, it is as if something conveys it. This does not lie in its tonal regulation or ornamental luster, nor does it lie in being able to discourse deeply on the subtleties of principle or hold forth indignantly on current affairs. I, Zhenyi…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
嘗虛以遇之十不失一二惟
是今有心而求或不逮無心
也故曰五之云耳雖然固才
是求一或不適貞一又焉逃
貞一請以實要之夫實言乎
心之眞也知其一不知其二
之謂眞勵其始不倦其成之
===
謂眞故祿爵有所不動毀譽
有所不搖髮膚有所不愛惟
我
社稷之有利焉如營家室其有
二於事也若是者自古帝王
所側席而求拊髀而思者也
諸士無亦是務乎且今
punctuated: 嘗虛以遇之，十不失一二。惟是今有心而求，或不逮無心也，故曰五之云耳。雖然，固才是求，一或不適，貞一又焉逃責？貞一請以實要之。夫實，言乎心之眞也。知其一不知其二之謂眞，勵其始不倦其成之謂眞。故祿爵有所不動，毀譽有所不搖，髮膚有所不愛，惟我社稷之有利焉，如營家室，其有二於事也？若是者，自古帝王所側席而求、拊髀而思者也。諸士無亦是務乎！且今
translation_en: …have in the past met them with an open and unprejudiced mind, and out of ten I did not miss more than one or two. Only now, when I seek them with deliberate intent, I may not match what I achieved without deliberate intent; that is why I said I might get about half. Even so, since it is truly talent that we seek, if even a single one should prove unsuitable, how could I, Zhenyi, escape blame [reading 一 as 責 or taking 貞一又焉逃 as "how could I, Zhenyi, escape it? — I, Zhenyi, beg to press the point with the notion of substance"]? I, Zhenyi, beg to hold them to the standard of substance. Now "substance" refers to the genuineness of the mind. Knowing the one thing and knowing no second—that is called genuineness; striving at the beginning and not growing weary through to completion—that is called genuineness. Therefore, there are emoluments and ranks that cannot move him, slander and praise that cannot shake him, and hair and skin that he does not begrudge, caring only for what benefits our altars of soil and grain [the dynasty], just like managing one's own household—how could there be any duplicity in his service? Men such as this are those whom emperors and kings since antiquity have waited for on the edge of their mats to seek out, and slapped their thighs in longing for. Should you gentlemen not devote yourselves to this! Moreover, at present…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
主上加意名實其所登進必其朴
忠者其所廢辱必其儇媚者
固不得復籍云用非其求也
諸士朂哉貞一望諸士遠且
大不敢爲一方之說以隘若
心若無忘不佞之祝詞惟
天子使具能有裨世運則爾無畔
===
質貞一無虛要不佞與多士
果相與以有成也顧不休與
諸士朂哉
浙江處州府青田縣儒學教
諭倫貞一謹序
punctuated:
主上加意名實，其所登進必其朴忠者，其所廢辱必其儇媚者，固不得復籍云用非其求也。諸士朂哉！貞一望諸士遠且大，不敢爲一方之說以隘若心。若無忘不佞之祝詞，惟天子使，具能有裨世運，則爾無畔質，貞一無虛要，不佞與多士果相與以有成也，顧不休與？諸士朂哉！
浙江處州府青田縣儒學教諭倫貞一謹序。
translation_en:
…His Majesty pays keen attention to whether name and reality correspond. Those whom he promotes and advances are invariably the simple and loyal, while those whom he casts aside and disgraces are invariably the glib and sycophantic; one can certainly no longer make the excuse that those employed are not the ones sought! Strive on, gentlemen! I, Zhenyi, hold far-reaching and grand hopes for you gentlemen, and dare not offer parochial doctrines that would narrow your minds. If you do not forget my words of exhortation, and in obeying the Son of Heaven's commands are all able to benefit the fortunes of the age, then you will not have betrayed your pledge, I, Zhenyi, will not have made an empty compact, and you many scholars and I will truly have helped one another to achieve success. Would that not be splendid? Strive on, gentlemen!
Respectfully prefaced by Lun Zhenyi 倫貞一, Instructor in the Confucian School of Qingtian County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text: （此頁為空白書衣，只有一方印章，沒有可轉錄的印刷文字。）
punctuated: （此頁為空白書衣，只有一方印章，沒有可轉錄的印刷文字。）

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄序
萬曆壬午秋御史董裕監臨
雲南鄉試精白乃心祇肅乃
度用帥先百執事百執事罔
敢不共闈以外提調則左布
政使徐作右布政使魏體明
監試則按察使徐元氣副使
===
胡心得以職至闈以內典試
則士淳與教諭倫貞一同試
則教諭劉止訓導靳惟賢董
以道周效良以聘至諸旣集
乃裒士而三試之先是提學
副使荊光裕遴簡待試一千
三百五十人至是則收雋四
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄序
萬曆壬午秋，御史董裕監臨雲南鄉試，精白乃心，祇肅乃度，用帥先百執事，百執事罔敢不共。闈以外，提調則左布政使徐作、右布政使魏體明，監試則按察使徐元氣、副使胡心得，以職至；闈以內，典試則士淳與教諭倫貞一，同試則教諭劉止、訓導靳惟賢、董以道、周效良，以聘至。諸旣集，乃裒士而三試之。先是，提學副使荊光裕遴簡待試一千三百五十人，至是則收雋四
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination
In the autumn of the renwu year of the Wanli era (1582), Censor Dong Yu 董裕 served as Supervising Official for the Yunnan Provincial Examination. Keeping his mind pure and bright and his deportment reverent and solemn, he set an example for all the officials in charge, and none among them dared be anything less than diligent. Outside the examination compound, Left Administration Commissioner Xu Zuo 徐作 and Right Administration Commissioner Wei Timing 魏體明 served as Proctors, while Surveillance Commissioner Xu Yuanqi 徐元氣 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Hu Xinde 胡心得 served as Monitoring Officials, all attending by virtue of their offices. Inside the examination compound, I, [Han] Shichun 士淳, together with Instructor Lun Zhenyi 倫貞一, served as Examiners, while Instructor Liu Zhi 劉止 and Assistant Instructors Jin Weixian 靳惟賢, Dong Yidao 董以道, and Zhou Xiaoliang 周效良 served as Associate Examiners, all attending by invitation. Once everyone had assembled, the scholars were gathered and tested in three sessions. Prior to this, Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Jing Guangyu 荊光裕 had selected 1,350 candidates to await the examination; now, forty-… [fifty men of talent were chosen…]

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
十五人錄文二十首謹籍而
獻之
闕下御史乃顧百執事而宣言
今天下輿圖西南萬里以滇爲
徼滇在六籍時不稱遐裔荒
服哉入秦紀以來葢嘗置守
吏奉約束亦往往自擅不討
===
其後君長與守吏雜治雖無
相侵害然聲教未一也已乃
畫大渡河而棄之至於勝國
胥之爲夷
明德象覆載罔有疎逖爰始冠帶
其民郡縣其土燿曶昧以光
明迨於
punctuated: 十五人，錄文二十首，謹籍而獻之闕下。御史乃顧百執事而宣言：「今天下輿圖，西南萬里，以滇爲徼。滇在《六籍》時，不稱遐裔荒服哉？入秦紀以來，葢嘗置守吏、奉約束，亦往往自擅不討。其後，君長與守吏雜治，雖無相侵害，然聲教未一也。已乃畫大渡河而棄之；至於勝國，胥之爲夷。明德象覆載，罔有疎逖，爰始冠帶其民，郡縣其土，燿曶昧以光明，迨於
translation_en: … [forty-]five men, and recorded twenty model compositions, respectfully registering and presenting them before the Imperial Throne. The Censor then turned to all the officiating functionaries and proclaimed: "Today, across the map of the empire, ten thousand li to the southwest, Dian [Yunnan] forms the frontier. In the era of the Six Classics, was Dian not called a distant borderland and a wild domain? Since entering the annals of the Qin dynasty, although prefectural officials were at times appointed and imperial covenants accepted, its rulers also frequently acted on their own authority without being punished. Thereafter, native chieftains and imperial officials governed in a mixed administration; although they did not encroach upon one another, prestigious instruction and moral transformation were not yet unified. Later still, a boundary was drawn at the Dadu River and the region was abandoned; by the time of the defeated [Yuan] dynasty, all had been reduced to barbarian ways. The virtue of the Ming emulates the all-covering heaven and all-supporting earth, leaving nothing estranged or remote. Thus for the first time it clothed its people in caps and sashes, organized its territory into prefectures and counties, and illuminated its dim obscurity with brilliant light, until by…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
今兹斌斌濟濟埒乎中州矣由
今遡天造之初孰知
帝力爲士者宜知之自昔列辟直
甌脫視滇耳一再不易莽然
荊榛狐貍豺狼嘷而穴其中
明興披其莽翳驅其嘷跳漸次修
葺迄有寧宇絃誦之士緌帶
===
而脩其業惡可不思所從來
夫滇在昔豈伊異域其見於
經爲南交昧谷之交羲叔和
仲之所宅而平秩也爲華陽
黑水禹之所表而志也爲濮
人周王之所杖鉞秉旄以麾
而誓之者也其見於史爲西
punctuated: 今兹，斌斌濟濟，埒乎中州矣。由今遡天造之初，孰知帝力？爲士者宜知之。自昔列辟，直甌脫視滇耳，一再不易，莽然荊榛，狐貍豺狼嘷而穴其中。明興，披其莽翳，驅其嘷跳，漸次修葺，迄有寧宇。絃誦之士，緌帶而脩其業，惡可不思所從來？夫滇在昔，豈伊異域？其見於經，爲南交、昧谷之交，羲叔、和仲之所宅而平秩也；爲華陽、黑水，禹之所表而志也；爲濮人，周王之所杖鉞秉旄以麾而誓之者也。其見於史，爲西
translation_en: … the present day, in cultural refinement and abundance of talent, it is now equal to the Central Plains! Tracing back from today to the beginning of its Heaven-made founding, who knows the power of the emperors? Those who are scholars ought to know it. Since antiquity, successive rulers merely regarded Dian as a border wasteland; through one or two changes of eras, it remained an overgrown thicket of thorns and brambles, where foxes, jackals, and wolves howled and made their dens. With the rise of the Ming, the overgrown thickets were cleared away and the howling, leaping beasts were driven out; it was gradually put in order until at last there were peaceful dwellings. When scholars who chant to stringed instruments wear trailing sashes and cultivate their studies, how can they not reflect upon whence this came? Now, in antiquity, how was Dian a foreign land? As it appears in the Classics, it was the junction of Southern Jiao and the Vale of Obscurity, where Xi Shu and He Zhong resided and regulated the seasonal order; it was the region south of Mount Hua and the Black Water, which Yu demarcated and recorded; and it was the land of the Pu people, whom the King of Zhou, grasping the battle-axe and holding the pennon, commanded and addressed in his oath. As it appears in the Histories, it was the…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
南夷滇嶲昆明牂牁楪榆邛
筰之屬漢武宣之所遺幣而
求馳檄而諭鑿池象而習戰
者也蓋元封初司馬遷奉使
南略邛筰昆明次年相如持
節開越嶲而土人盛覽傳其
學以教於鄉是時按道侯開
===
益州建學授經人文於是乎
始然稽之職方僅乃關沬若
梁孫原而已詞臣尚夸以爲
遠撫長駕中外禔福方之於
今孰爲一體乎洪永之際
武功底定
文教勃興二百年來數增解額
punctuated: 南夷滇、嶲、昆明、牂牁、楪榆、邛、筰之屬，漢武、宣之所遺幣而求、馳檄而諭、鑿池象而習戰者也。蓋元封初，司馬遷奉使南略邛、筰、昆明，次年相如持節開越嶲，而土人盛覽傳其學以教於鄉。是時，按道侯開益州，建學授經，人文於是乎始。然稽之職方，僅乃關沬、若，梁孫原而已，詞臣尚夸以爲遠撫長駕，中外禔福。方之於今，孰爲一體乎？洪、永之際，武功底定，文教勃興。二百年來，數增解額，
translation_en: … the Southwestern Peoples (Xinan Yi), including such groups as Dian, Sui, Kunming, Zangke, Yeyu, Qiong, and Zuo—those whom Emperors Wu and Xuan of the Han sought out with gifts of silk, instructed by dispatching proclamations, and prepared to fight by excavating a lake modeled on theirs for naval drills. Indeed, at the beginning of the Yuanfeng era, Sima Qian 司馬遷 went on an imperial mission south to pacify Qiong, Zuo, and Kunming; the following year, Sima Xiangru 司馬相如 held the imperial insignia to open up Yuesui, and a local native, Sheng Lan 盛覽, transmitted his learning to teach in his home region. At that time, the Marquis of Andao opened up Yizhou, establishing schools and imparting the Classics, and literary culture thus had its beginning there. Yet if one examines the territorial registers, they had merely set up passes at the Mei and Ruo rivers and bridged the valley of the Sun River, nothing more; even so, court men of letters boasted of this as pacifying distant lands and reining in far-flung peoples, bringing tranquil blessings within and without. Compared with the present day, which is truly unified into a single body? During the Hongwu and Yongle eras, military achievements brought final pacification, and literary education flourished vigorously. Over the past two hundred years, the quota of provincial graduates has been repeatedly increased, …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
且鴈行蜀粵而肩隨之名世
將相之業稍稍間出
主上承
列聖休養之緒廣厲學官申布
功令日月懸於天窮陬僻壤靡
不照臨雨露被於物微荄弱
株靡不沾溉萬里之外曠然
爲家倫軌書文猶在
===
輦轂夫一統之盛悉土悉民棄
而蠻夷之則蠻夷進而中國
之則中國
天子不夷鄙滇人而飭以儒雅士
故得與聞中原之文獻登昭
明之途而益重自棄覽所爲
punctuated: 且鴈行蜀、粵而肩隨之，名世將相之業，稍稍間出。主上承列聖休養之緒，廣厲學官，申布功令。日月懸於天，窮陬僻壤靡不照臨；雨露被於物，微荄弱株靡不沾溉。萬里之外，曠然爲家，倫軌書文，猶在輦轂。夫一統之盛，悉土悉民，棄而蠻夷之則蠻夷，進而中國之則中國。天子不夷鄙滇人，而飭以儒雅，士故得與聞中原之文獻，登昭明之途，而益重自棄。覽所爲
translation_en:
…and moreover, it flies in formation alongside Shu and Yue and follows close behind them, while the achievements of world-renowned generals and chief ministers have gradually begun to appear from time to time.

His Majesty has inherited the legacy of nurturing and restocking left by the successive sacred emperors, broadly encouraging the Confucian school officials and reiterating and promulgating the regulations governing the examinations. As the sun and moon hang in the heavens, there is no remote corner or isolated region they do not illuminate; as rain and dew cover all things, there is no tiny root or fragile sapling they do not moisten and nourish. Ten thousand li away, all is expansively united as a single household; human moral standards, carriage gauges, and written script are just as they are at the imperial capital. Now, in the flourishing of a great unification, when all lands and all peoples are included, if one abandons them and treats them as barbarian tribes, they behave as barbarian tribes; if one advances them and treats them as part of the Central States, they behave as part of the Central States. The Son of Heaven does not disdain the people of Dian as barbarians, but instead instructs them in Confucian refinement. The scholars there have thus been able to share in hearing the literary and historical heritage of the Central Plain, ascend the path of bright enlightenment, and hold self-abandonment in ever greater aversion. Looking over the compositions they have produced…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
詞本原經術通達世務依希
乎有漢兩司馬之槩焉昔西
鄙野人竝耦而游於都市其
一明禮義習威儀歸見於父
兄甚都里中椎魯者慕而效
之其一秉堅策肥崇夸滋侈
歸見於父兄亦甚都而里中
===
竊笑之今之滇非昔之滇也
蓋耦而游都市矣禮義夸侈
於是焉在惟士所取之金礦
受鎔鎔則不復爲礦玉璞受
雕雕則不復爲璞吾聞滇俗
樹惇而守終純固一變至魯
於先進之從爲近夫士旣鎔
punctuated: 詞，本原經術，通達世務，依希乎有漢兩司馬之槩焉。昔西鄙野人，竝耦而游於都市。其一明禮義、習威儀，歸見於父兄，甚都，里中椎魯者慕而效之；其一秉堅策肥，崇夸滋侈，歸見於父兄，亦甚都，而里中竊笑之。今之滇，非昔之滇也，蓋耦而游都市矣。禮義、夸侈，於是焉在，惟士所取之。金礦受鎔，鎔則不復爲礦；玉璞受雕，雕則不復爲璞。吾聞滇俗樹惇而守終，純固一變至魯，於先進之從爲近。夫士旣鎔
translation_en: …writings, I see that they are rooted in classical scholarship and well-versed in practical affairs of the world, faintly possessing the spirit of the two Simas of the Han dynasty [Sima Qian 司馬遷 and Sima Xiangru 司馬相如]. In the past, two rustic men from the western frontier went together as companions to travel in the capital city. One of them came to understand ritual propriety and righteousness and practiced dignified deportment; when he returned and presented himself before his fathers and elder brothers, he was most refined, and the simple, unsophisticated folk of the village admired and emulated him. The other rode in sturdy carriages and whipped up fat horses, prizing ostentation and indulging in extravagance; when he returned and presented himself before his fathers and elder brothers, he too seemed most refined, yet those in the village secretly laughed at him. The Dian [Yunnan] of today is not the Dian of the past; indeed, its people now travel side by side in the capital city. Both ritual propriety and righteousness, as well as ostentation and extravagance, are present there—it depends solely on what the scholars choose to adopt. When gold ore undergoes smelting, once smelted it is no longer ore; when uncarved jade undergoes carving, once carved it is no longer uncarved stone. I have heard that the customs of Dian establish honest厚 [generosity/sincerity] and hold fast to the end; being pure and steadfast, with a single transformation they could reach the level of the state of Lu, coming close to following the "men of former times" [praised by Confucius]. Now that the scholars have been smelted…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
既雕幸無忘厥初而徒盛都
市之容猥爲稚魯者所笑也
百執事唯然咸是御史言請
書之屬士淳受簡是舉也鎮
守黔國公沐昌祚振揚
明威靖疆宇以保士巡撫都御史
劉世曾勤宣
===
德意監郡國以造士大理寺左寺
正陳明經恤錄甫竣弼教猶
新左叅政陳誥右叅政邵元
哲右叅政兼僉事趙睿右叅
議胡僖副使賀幼殊辛存仁
僉事楊際熙署都指揮僉事
趙瓊楊循禮協庇於外以賛
punctuated:
既雕，幸無忘厥初，而徒盛都市之容，猥爲稚魯者所笑也。」百執事唯然，咸是御史言，請書之，屬士淳受簡。
是舉也，鎮守黔國公沐昌祚振揚明威，靖疆宇以保士；巡撫都御史劉世曾勤宣德意，監郡國以造士；大理寺左寺正陳明經恤錄甫竣，弼教猶新；左叅政陳誥、右叅政邵元哲、右叅政兼僉事趙睿、右叅議胡僖、副使賀幼殊、辛存仁、僉事楊際熙、署都指揮僉事趙瓊、楊循禮，協庇於外以賛……
translation_en:
… and carved, I hope they will not forget their original state and merely flaunt the airs of the capital, only to be ridiculed by the simple and unsophisticated.” All the officiating functionaries assented, unanimously approving the Censor’s words. They requested that they be recorded and charged me, [Qiao] Shichun 譙士淳, with receiving the writing tablets.

In this undertaking, Grand Defender and Duke of Qianguo Mu Changzuo 沐昌祚 displayed the august majesty of the dynasty, pacifying the borderlands so as to protect the scholars; Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Liu Shizeng 劉世曾 diligently proclaimed the sovereign’s benevolent intentions, overseeing the prefectures and principalities so as to cultivate the scholars; Case Reviewer of the Left of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Mingjing 陳明經 had just completed the compassionate review of penal cases, and his assistance to moral instruction through punishment was still fresh; Left Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Gao 陳誥, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Shao Yuanzhe 邵元哲, Right Administration Vice Commissioner concurrently Assistant Commissioner Zhao Rui 趙睿, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Hu Xi 胡僖, Vice Commissioners He Youshu 賀幼殊 and Xin Cunren 辛存仁, Assistant Commissioner Yang Jixi 楊際熙, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Zhao Qiong 趙瓊 and Yang Xunli 楊循禮 all cooperated in providing support from without to assist in the …

translation_en:
… the ceremonial sending-off of the candidates (binxing). Surveillance Vice Commissioner Ma [Guze 馬顧澤], who departed upon promotion to a new post, as well as Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Zheng [Zongxue 鄭宗學], Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zheng [Kongdao 鄭孔道], and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Wang [Sanpin 王三聘], who departed to present congratulations at court, had all contributed their efforts prior to the event; according to the regulations, their names are worthy of being recorded.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
所謂誠其意者毋自欺也
子聞之曰大宰知我乎吾少也賤故多能
鄙事君子多乎哉不多也
大人者言不必信行不必果惟義所在
易
彖曰大有柔得尊位大中而上下應之曰
大有
===
君子以勞民勸相
鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂
離也者明也萬物皆相見南方之卦也聖
人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
也
書
無教逸欲有邦兢兢業業一日二日萬幾
后克聖臣不命其承疇敢不祗若王之休
命
punctuated:
第壹場
四書：
「所謂誠其意者，毋自欺也。」
「子聞之曰：『大宰知我乎！吾少也賤，故多能鄙事。君子多乎哉？不多也。』」
「大人者，言不必信，行不必果，惟義所在。」

易：
「彖曰：大有，柔得尊位大中，而上下應之，曰大有。」
「君子以勞民勸相。」
「鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂。」
「離也者，明也，萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。」

書：
「無教逸欲有邦。兢兢業業，一日二日萬幾。」
「后克聖，臣不命其承；疇敢不祗若王之休命！」
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books (Sishu):
"What is meant by 'making the thoughts sincere' is allowing no self-deception." [Great Learning (Daxue)]
"The Master heard of it and said, 'Does the Grand Minister know me? When I was young, my condition was low, and therefore I acquired my ability in many鄙 (menial) matters. Must the superior man have such variety of ability? He does not need it.'" [Analects (Lunyu), 9.6]
"The great man does not think beforehand of his words that they may be sincere, nor of his actions that they may be resolute; he simply speaks and does what is right." [Mencius (Mengzi), 4B.11]

Classic of Changes (Yi / Yijing):
"The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: 'Possession in Great Measure (Dayou): the yielding (six in the fifth place) occupies the honored position in the great center, and the upper and lower lines respond to it; hence it is called Possession in Great Measure.'" [Hexagram 14, Dayou]
"Thus the superior man comforts the people and stimulates them to mutual aid." [Hexagram 20, Jing]
"[The operations of Heaven and Earth] drum all things into activity, without sharing the anxieties of the sage." [Great Commentary (Xici shang), 1.5]
"Clinging (Li) means brightness, in which all things are perceived by one another. It is the trigram of the south. That the sage turns his face to the south when he gives audience to all under heaven, governing while facing the light, was probably taken from this." [Discussion of the Trigrams (Shuogua), 5]

Classic of Documents (Shu / Shujing):
"Do not teach idleness and desires to the rulers of states. Be cautious and fearful; in one day or two days there are ten thousand incipient springs of affairs." [Counsels of Gao Yao (Gaoyao mo)]
"When the sovereign is sage, his ministers, even without being commanded, carry out his will; who would dare not to respectfully conform to the king's admirable Charge!" [Charge to Yue, Part I (Yue ming shang)]

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
曰雨曰暘曰燠曰寒曰風曰時
道洽政治澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
詩
彼茁者葭壹發五豝于嗟乎騶虞
菁菁者莪在彼中阿既見君子樂且有儀
菁菁者莪在彼中沚既見君子我心則
喜菁菁者莪在彼中陵既見君子錫我
百朋
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
敷時繹思我徂維求定時周之命
===
春秋
秋公會宋人齊人伐徐〔莊公二十有六年〕
冬十月不雨〔僖公二年〕春王正月不雨
夏四月不雨　六月雨〔俱僖公三年〕
冬公孫歸父會齊侯于穀〔宣公十有四年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕夏曹公孫會
自鄭出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
禮記
punctuated:
曰雨，曰暘，曰燠，曰寒，曰風，曰時。
道洽政治，澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。

詩
彼茁者葭，壹發五豝，于嗟乎騶虞。
菁菁者莪，在彼中阿。既見君子，樂且有儀。菁菁者莪，在彼中沚。既見君子，我心則喜。菁菁者莪，在彼中陵。既見君子，錫我百朋。
子孫千億，穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。
敷時繹思，我徂維求定，時周之命。

春秋
秋，公會宋人、齊人伐徐。〔莊公二十有六年〕
冬，十月，不雨。〔僖公二年〕春，王正月，不雨。夏，四月，不雨。六月，雨。〔俱僖公三年〕
冬，公孫歸父會齊侯于穀。〔宣公十有四年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕夏，曹公孫會自鄭出奔宋。〔昭公二十年〕

禮記
translation_en:
[Questions on the Book of Documents (Shujing), continued:]
"They are called rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, wind, and seasonableness."
"His Way was all-pervading and his governance well-ordered; his beneficence moistened the living people, and the four barbarous tribes who fasten their garments on the left all without exception depended on him."

Book of Odes (Shijing)
"How sprouting are the reeds! At one discharge of the bow, five sows are struck. Oh, the Zouyu!"
"Luxuriant grows the tarragon, in the midst of that large mound. Having seen the lord, we are joyful and observe courtesy. Luxuriant grows the tarragon, in the midst of that islet. Having seen the lord, my heart is delighted. Luxuriant grows the tarragon, in the midst of that high hill. Having seen the lord, he bestows on me a hundred strings of cowries."
"His sons and grandsons are a hundred thousand million; reverent and majestic, they are fit to be rulers, fit to be kings."
"Spreading abroad this cherished thought, we go forth only to seek stability; this is the Mandate of Zhou."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In autumn, the Duke met with men of Song and men of Qi to attack Xu." [Twenty-sixth year of Duke Zhuang]
"In winter, in the tenth month, it did not rain." [Second year of Duke Xi] "In spring, in the King's first month, it did not rain." "In summer, in the fourth month, it did not rain." "In the sixth month, it rained." [All in the third year of Duke Xi]
"In winter, Gongsun Guifu met with the Marquis of Qi at Gu." [Fourteenth year of Duke Xuan]
"Luan Shu of Jin led an army to rescue Zheng." [Sixth year of Duke Cheng] "In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Zheng [Meng] to Song." [Twentieth year of Duke Zhao]

Record of Rites (Liji)

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天子曰辟雍諸侯曰頖宮
四者君以正用之故君者立於無過之地
也
詩言其志也歌咏其聲也舞動其容也三
者本於心然後樂器從之
天下莫不貴者道也
第貳場
論
帝王心法之要
===
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜天下今年田租之半詔〔文帝三年〕
擬唐賜裴度爵晉國公入知政事誥〔元和〕
〔十一年〕
擬宋禱雨太乙宮是日雨輔臣賀表〔慶曆〕
〔七年〕
判語〔五條〕
官員襲廕
賦役不均
punctuated:
天子曰辟雍，諸侯曰頖宮。
四者，君以正用之，故君者立於無過之地也。
詩，言其志也；歌，咏其聲也；舞，動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。
天下莫不貴者，道也。

第貳場
論
帝王心法之要

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜天下今年田租之半詔〔文帝三年〕
擬唐賜裴度爵晉國公入知政事誥〔元和十一年〕
擬宋禱雨太乙宮是日雨輔臣賀表〔慶曆七年〕

判語〔五條〕
官員襲廕
賦役不均
translation_en:
"For the Son of Heaven it is called the Biyong [Royal College]; for the feudal lords it is called the Pangong [State College]."
"These four, the ruler uses with rectitude; therefore, the ruler stands in a position free of transgression."
"Poetry expresses one's intent; song chants its sound; dance moves one's countenance. These three originate in the heart-mind, and only afterward do musical instruments follow them."
"What all under heaven without exception hold precious is the Way."

Second Session
Discourse (lun):
"The Essentials of the Method of the Heart-Mind of Emperors and Kings."

Edicts (zhao), Patents (gao), and Memorials (biao) [candidates are tested on one of these]:
Imitative Han edict granting all under heaven a remission of half of this year's land tax [3rd year of Emperor Wen (177 BCE)].
Imitative Tang patent granting Pei Du 裴度 the title of Duke of Jin and summoning him to Court to Administer State Affairs [11th year of the Yuanhe era (816)].
Imitative Song congratulatory memorial from the auxiliary ministers on praying for rain at the Palace of Supreme Unity (Taiyi gong) and rain falling that very day [7th year of the Qingli era (1047)].

Legal Judgments (panyu) [five items]:
Hereditary succession and protection privilege (yin) of officials
Inequitable land taxes and corvée labor…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
鄉飲酒禮
門禁鎖鑰
修理倉庫
第叄場
策五道
問帝王爲天下萬世計必立治法法以惠無
窮三代盛王其子孫累數百年同底治
安者其法存也觀諸載籍可攷矣後世
勵精求治之主莫過漢宣帝宋神宗然
===
法則仍秦治則雜伯上嘉者陋而不居
也乃其臣條陳之其君守爲家法何遽
侔德殷周宋至元豐法敝滋弱神宗與
其臣所稱則者堯舜也周官也所置新
法未爲盡非何致釀禍紹聖意者在人
而不在政與何得失之異軌也我
太祖高皇帝
創業垂統遠邁百王
經制明備焜燿區宇
punctuated:
鄉飲酒禮。
門禁鎖鑰。
修理倉庫。

第叄場。
策五道。

問：帝王爲天下萬世計，必立治法，法以惠無窮。三代盛王，其子孫累數百年同底治安者，其法存也，觀諸載籍可攷矣。後世勵精求治之主，莫過漢宣帝、宋神宗。然法則仍秦，治則雜伯，上嘉者陋而不居也。乃其臣條陳之，其君守爲家法，何遽侔德殷、周？宋至元豐，法敝滋弱，神宗與其臣所稱則者，堯、舜也，《周官》也。所置新法，未爲盡非，何致釀禍紹聖？意者在人而不在政與？何得失之異軌也？我太祖高皇帝創業垂統，遠邁百王，經制明備，焜燿區宇，

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
一代之治法隆矣
列聖承圖纘爲治統我
皇上
冲聖嗣極碩輔失謨法
祖善治十祼于茲薄海內外承
風順
德眞軼漢唐而儷三代談治統者曷罄名言
顧法常敝於相沿治或湮於所忽茲欲
飭治振起俾
===
成法常新而無敝固憂治世者所欲言亦願治
之主所樂聞也諸士其盡言之吾將持
以爲
獻
問古今善言天人之際者稽諸洪範其言
五事必配以五行而休徵咎徵類應靡
爽乃孔子作春秋書災異不書事應與
洪範之旨異者何詎非以天心之仁愛
人君者甚深人君之克謹天戒者當無
punctuated:
一代之治法隆矣。列聖承圖，纘爲治統。我皇上冲聖嗣極，碩輔失謨，法祖善治，十祼于茲。薄海內外，承風順德，眞軼漢、唐而儷三代，談治統者曷罄名言？顧法常敝於相沿，治或湮於所忽。茲欲飭治振起，俾成法常新而無敝，固憂治世者所欲言，亦願治之主所樂聞也。諸士其盡言之，吾將持以爲獻。

問：古今善言天人之際者，稽諸《洪範》，其言五事必配以五行，而休徵、咎徵類應靡爽；乃孔子作《春秋》，書災異不書事應，與《洪範》之旨異者何？詎非以天心之仁愛人君者甚深，人君之克謹天戒者當無
translation_en:
…thus the governing institutions of an entire dynasty reached their pinnacle. Successive sacred emperors inherited the imperial enterprise, continuing it as the tradition of governance. Our August Emperor succeeded to the throne in his youthful sagehood; with great chief ministers putting forth their counsels [?; 失謨 likely a transcription error for 陳謨 or 矢謨], he has modeled himself on the Ancestors and governed well for ten years now. Within and beyond the seas, all respond to his transforming influence and submit to his virtue, truly surpassing the Han and Tang and rivaling the Three Dynasties—how could those who discuss the tradition of governance exhaust their praise in words? Yet laws often decay through routine continuation, and good order may be obscured through neglect. Now, if we wish to rectify administration and rouse vigor so that established laws remain ever fresh and free from decay, this is surely what those who are concerned for an era of good order wish to speak of, and also what a ruler who desires good governance is pleased to hear. Gentlemen, set forth your views in full, and I shall take them to present to the throne.

Question: Those in ancient and modern times who have spoken well of the relation between Heaven and humanity examine the Great Plan (Hongfan), where the discussion of the Five Demeanors is invariably matched with the Five Phases, and the auspicious verifications and inauspicious verifications respond according to kind without fail. Yet when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), he recorded calamities and anomalies without recording the corresponding human affairs—why does this differ from the purport of the Great Plan? Is it not because the mind of Heaven bears a most profound benevolent love for the ruler of men, and the ruler who is able to heed Heaven's warnings should at no…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
時無事無不致其敬與洚水之儆桑林
之禱雲漢之憂古先帝王之所以遇災
而懼天不能爲之災者蓋有道也洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝
開天啓
聖論洪範庶徵之應獨超千古七曜紊度
詔求直言矣
京師大旱
===
求言錄因矣而
精誠有錄
存心有錄所以欽崇戒謹者尤至詳且切故
比堯而多其功于湯而邁其德周宣不
足侔矣我
皇上挺
聖喆之資撫
郅隆之運
御極以來民物昌阜中外敉寧天下稱極治矣
punctuated: 時無事無不致其敬與？洚水之儆、桑林之禱、雲漢之憂，古先帝王之所以遇災而懼，天不能爲之災者，蓋有道也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，開天啓聖，論《洪範》庶徵之應，獨超千古。七曜紊度，詔求直言矣；京師大旱，求言錄因矣；而《精誠》有錄，《存心》有錄，所以欽崇戒謹者，尤至詳且切。故比堯而多其功，于湯而邁其德，周宣不足侔矣。我皇上挺聖喆之資，撫郅隆之運，御極以來，民物昌阜，中外敉寧，天下稱極治矣。
translation_en: … a time or an affair in which he does not show the utmost reverence? The warning of the inundating waters, the prayer at the Mulberry Forest (Sanglin), and the anxiety expressed in the "Cloudy Milky Way" ("Yunhan" ode)—that the ancient former emperors and kings felt fear upon encountering calamities, so that Heaven could not inflict disaster upon them, was surely because there was a Way to it. Looking upon our Grand Progenitor the Exalted Emperor (Taizu Gao Huangdi), who opened up Heaven and initiated sagehood: his discussions of the responses of the various verifications in the "Great Plan" ("Hongfan") uniquely surpassed all antiquity. When the Seven Luminaries fell out of their regular courses, he issued an edict seeking forthright counsel; when the capital suffered a great drought, he sought counsel and reviewed prisoner cases [reading 囚 for 因]. Moreover, there was the Record of Pure Sincerity (Jingcheng lu) and the Record of Preserving the Mind-and-Heart (Cunxin lu), through which his reverent veneration and cautious vigilance were especially thorough and earnest. Thus, compared to Yao his achievements were greater, compared to Tang his virtue was superior, and King Xuan of Zhou was not enough to equal him. Our August Emperor is endowed with sagely and wise natural qualities and presides over an era of consummate flourishing. Since ascending the throne, the people and all things have prospered and multiplied, within and without all is pacified and tranquil, and all under Heaven acclaims it as the height of good governance.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
頃者雨澤愆期
玄象示異風霾翳日疫沴時行四方水旱屢形
奏牘茲固
天心仁愛之徵也
皇上齋心默禱蠲逋發賑
勑內外大小臣工共圖修省凡所以增修
德政以仰答
天心者未易殫述此其心卽
皇祖
===
敬天之心于
精誠存心錄有深契者粹乎無容議矣茲欲
因
天之垂象者以陳謨承
皇上之
勑下者以交儆則何道而可
皇祖曰天人之理無二人當以心爲天又曰欲
求事
天必先恤民大哉
punctuated: 頃者，雨澤愆期，玄象示異，風霾翳日，疫沴時行，四方水旱屢形奏牘，茲固天心仁愛之徵也。皇上齋心默禱，蠲逋發賑，勑內外大小臣工共圖修省，凡所以增修德政以仰答天心者，未易殫述。此其心卽皇祖敬天之心，于《精誠》、《存心》錄有深契者，粹乎無容議矣。茲欲因天之垂象者以陳謨，承皇上之勑下者以交儆，則何道而可？皇祖曰：「天人之理無二，人當以心爲天。」又曰：「欲求事天，必先恤民。」大哉
translation_en: Recently, timely rains have failed to fall, the celestial phenomena have displayed anomalies, winds and dust haze have obscured the sun, epidemics and pestilence have periodically spread, and floods and droughts across the four quarters have repeatedly appeared in memorials to the throne—these are assuredly signs of the benevolent love of the Mind of Heaven. His Majesty has fasted in mind and prayed in silence, remitted tax arrears and distributed relief, and commanded all officials, great and small, at court and in the provinces, to jointly engage in self-cultivation and self-examination; all the ways by which he has further cultivated benevolent governance in order to respectfully respond to the Mind of Heaven cannot easily be recounted in full. In this, his mind is none other than the Imperial Ancestor's mind of revering Heaven, profoundly in accord with the Record of Utmost Sincerity (Jingcheng lu) and the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu)—so pure that it admits of no discussion! Now, if we wish to set forth counsels in response to the signs sent down by Heaven, and to engage in mutual admonition in compliance with the commands His Majesty has handed down to his subordinates, by what way may this be done? The Imperial Ancestor said: "The principle of Heaven and man is not dual; man ought to take his own mind as Heaven." And he also said: "If one seeks to serve Heaven, one must first show compassion to the people." Great indeed…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聖言誠昭事之龜鑑也諸生達天人之際有能
推原其說可以仰裨
聖天子
敬天之衷者其詳著于篇
問舜命夔曰詩言志孔子曰興於詩詩之
爲敎大矣三百篇而後天子不采風諸
侯不貢俗文人墨士各騁才情以擅一
家故變而爲離騷變而爲五言最後變
而爲近體極矣即以騷談之傳騷者稱
===
其兼風雅光日月似矣太史公采之入
傳無貶詞乃反騷者譏其不能龍蛇序
騷者尤其怨懟沉江抑何說與辯騷者
指其合風雅者四事異經傳者四事可
得詳與夫褒貶任聲抑揚過實非所以
論古人也抑有至當不易之評與後之
擬騷者無慮數家何者爲近與自漢魏
逮齊梁馳聲藝苑者無慮百家固有第
之爲三品者說者惟有取於柴桑之士
punctuated:
聖言！誠昭事之龜鑑也。諸生達天人之際，有能推原其說，可以仰裨聖天子敬天之衷者，其詳著于篇。
問：舜命夔曰：「詩言志。」孔子曰：「興於詩。」詩之爲敎大矣！《三百篇》而後，天子不采風，諸侯不貢俗，文人墨士各騁才情以擅一家，故變而爲《離騷》，變而爲五言，最後變而爲近體，極矣。即以騷談之，傳騷者稱其兼風雅、光日月，似矣；太史公采之入傳，無貶詞。乃《反騷》者譏其不能龍蛇，序騷者尤其怨懟沉江，抑何說與？《辯騷》者指其合風雅者四事、異經傳者四事，可得詳與？夫褒貶任聲，抑揚過實，非所以論古人也，抑有至當不易之評與？後之擬騷者無慮數家，何者爲近與？自漢、魏逮齊、梁，馳聲藝苑者無慮百家，固有第之爲三品者，說者惟有取於柴桑之士，
translation_en:
… these sacred words! Truly they are a mirror and touchstone for reverently serving Heaven. You students understand the relationship between Heaven and man; if you can trace the origins of this teaching so as to humbly assist the Sacred Son of Heaven in his heartfelt reverence for Heaven, set it forth in detail in your essays.

Question: Shun commanded Kui, saying, "Poetry expresses intent." Confucius said, "Be stimulated by the Odes." Great indeed is the teaching of poetry! After the Three Hundred Odes, the Son of Heaven no longer collected airs, and the feudal lords no longer presented local customs as tribute. Literary men and writers of ink each gave free rein to their talents and sentiments to establish their own schools. Thus poetry changed into the Li sao (Encountering Sorrow), changed into five-character verse, and finally changed into regulated verse (jinti), reaching its limit. To speak first of the Sao: he who wrote a commentary on the Sao praised it as combining the Airs (Feng) and Major and Minor Odes (Ya) and vying in brilliance with the sun and moon, which seems apt; and the Grand Historian (Sima Qian) included it in his biography without a word of censure. Yet the author of "Contra Sao" (Fan sao, i.e. Yang Xiong) ridiculed him for being unable to adapt like the dragon and snake, and the author of the preface to the Sao (Ban Gu) blamed him for resentfully drowning himself in the river—what is the explanation for this? The author of "Evaluating the Sao" (Bian sao, i.e. Liu Xie) pointed out four respects in which it accords with the Airs and Odes and four respects in which it diverges from the Classics and commentaries—can you give the details? Now, to praise or blame merely by following reputation, or to disparage or exalt beyond reality, is not the way to judge the ancients; is there, then, a most fitting and unalterable assessment? Among the several later writers who imitated the Sao, which comes closest? From the Han and Wei down to the Qi and Liang dynasties, those who won fame in the garden of letters numbered roughly a hundred schools, and indeed there was one who ranked them into three grades (Zhong Rong's Shipin); yet commentators approve solely of the gentleman of Chaisang (Tao Yuanming), …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而又不爲韓退之所取何與唐自貞觀
以迄開成蜚譽詞林者亦無慮數百家
有詮之爲四唐者說者惟有取於浣花
之叟而不爲歐陽永叔所喜亦何說與
夫詩體以代異調以人殊茲欲揔異歸
同以窺作者之致以鳴
國家之盛何所繇與諸生紬繹風騷必有㮚
然當於心者其詳言之以觀博雅之學
問田賦經國大務其法莫善於井田其所
===
由來遠矣唐虞夏商相沿至周大備周
禮遂人匠人之所掌者是已其賦則遂
師縣師鄉大夫均人掌之其詳可得聞
與秦開阡陌井田廢矣或謂不始於秦
漢興去古未遠乃宜復而不復何與自
漢歷唐宋其制何者爲近古其間變置
得失可得而詳與惟我
國家參酌古今履畝定賦田雖不井取民有
制誠
punctuated:
而又不爲韓退之所取，何與？唐自貞觀以迄開成，蜚譽詞林者亦無慮數百家，有詮之爲四唐者，說者惟有取於浣花之叟，而不爲歐陽永叔所喜，亦何說與？夫詩體以代異，調以人殊，茲欲揔異歸同，以窺作者之致，以鳴國家之盛，何所繇與？諸生紬繹風騷，必有㮚然當於心者，其詳言之，以觀博雅之學。

問：田賦經國大務，其法莫善於井田，其所由來遠矣。唐、虞、夏、商相沿，至周大備，《周禮》遂人、匠人之所掌者是已。其賦則遂師、縣師、鄉大夫、均人掌之，其詳可得聞與？秦開阡陌，井田廢矣，或謂不始於秦。漢興，去古未遠，乃宜復而不復，何與？自漢歷唐、宋，其制何者爲近古？其間變置得失，可得而詳與？惟我國家參酌古今，履畝定賦，田雖不井，取民有制，誠
translation_en:
…and yet he was not approved by Han Tuizhi (Han Yu 韓愈)—why is this? In the Tang, from the Zhenguan (627–649) to the Kaicheng (836–840) eras, those who won fame in the forest of letters likewise numbered some several hundred. There were those who classified them into the Four Tang periods; commentators have singled out for praise only the Old Man of Huanhua (Du Fu 杜甫), yet he was not favored by Ouyang Yongshu (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修)—what is the explanation for this as well? Now, poetic forms differ by era, and tunes vary with the person. If we now wish to bring these differences together into unity, so as to peer into the true spirit of the authors and to sing the praises of our Dynasty's flourishing, by what path may we do so? You students have long drawn out the threads of the Airs and the Elegies and must hold clear, well-ordered views in your minds; set them forth in detail, so that we may observe the breadth and elegance of your learning.

Question: Land taxation is a great affair of statecraft; no method for it is better than the well-field system, whose origins lie in the distant past. Passed down through the Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang eras, it reached full completeness in the Zhou, as seen in what was administered by the Commandant of the Outlying Districts (Suiren) and the Master of Artisans (Jiangren) in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). As for its levies, they were administered by the Preceptor of the Outlying Districts (Suishi), the Preceptor of the Regions (Xianshi), the Grand Master of the Six Districts (Xiang dafu), and the Equalizer of Assessments (Junren)—can their details be heard? When Qin opened up the footpaths and balks between fields, the well-field system was abolished, though some say this did not begin with Qin. When the Han arose, it was not yet far removed from antiquity; why then, when the system ought to have been restored, was it not restored? From the Han through the Tang and Song, which of their systems came closest to antiquity? Can the successes and failures of the changes and arrangements during those periods be recounted in detail? Our own Dynasty, weighing both ancient and modern practices, surveys the acres to fix the tax; although the fields are not divided into wells, levies upon the people are governed by regulation, which is truly…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
經國之良法也但法久弊生侵隱詭射至不
可勝原邇者
皇上軫念民艱
特允當事諸臣之請
詔天下有司度田舉宿弊而釐正之以甦疲瘵
恩至渥也第滇省僻在西南括全省田賦不足
當中州一大縣歲豐民堇堇足食一遇
兵凶公私輒告匱司民命者烏可不爲
之慮也茲欲就履丈之時定經久之計
以大裕滇民而少裨
===
國計晝將安出諸生明習世務於滇當尤切
也其何以告我
問滇南在三代時不列職方自莊蹻略地
至滇因而王之此入滇之始也元封以
後時通中國置郡縣然土流雜治羈靮
靡常既玉斧畫流金沙未渡猶然阻風
教矣我
高皇帝混一區宇拓昆瀰隳鄯闡乃出夷狄而
punctuated:
經國之良法也。但法久弊生，侵隱詭射，至不可勝原。邇者皇上軫念民艱，特允當事諸臣之請，詔天下有司度田，舉宿弊而釐正之，以甦疲瘵，恩至渥也。第滇省僻在西南，括全省田賦不足當中州一大縣。歲豐，民堇堇足食；一遇兵凶，公私輒告匱。司民命者烏可不爲之慮也？茲欲就履丈之時，定經久之計，以大裕滇民而少裨國計，晝將安出？諸生明習世務，於滇當尤切也，其何以告我？
問：滇南在三代時不列職方。自莊蹻略地至滇，因而王之，此入滇之始也。元封以後，時通中國，置郡縣，然土流雜治，羈靮靡常。既玉斧畫流，金沙未渡，猶然阻風教矣。我高皇帝混一區宇，拓昆瀰，隳鄯闡，乃出夷狄而
translation_en:
…a sound method of governing the state. Yet when laws endure for a long time, abuses arise: encroachment, concealment, and fraudulent tax evasion have grown beyond what can be fully traced. Recently, His Majesty, moved by compassion for the hardships of the people, specially granted the requests of the officials in charge and decreed that authorities throughout the empire measure the land, exposing long-standing abuses and rectifying them so as to revive the exhausted and distressed—a grace most abundant indeed. However, Yunnan Province lies isolated in the southwest, and the land tax of the entire province combined is not enough to match that of a single large county in the Central Plain. In years of丰 [good harvest], the people barely have enough to eat; once war or famine strikes, both public and private resources immediately fall into depletion. How could those responsible for the lives of the people not be concerned about this? Now, if we wish to take advantage of this occasion of surveying the land to establish an enduring plan that will greatly enrich the people of Yunnan and provide some small benefit to the finances of the state, whence shall such a plan [reading 畫 for 晝] come? You students are well-versed in worldly affairs, and matters concerning Yunnan should be of particular urgency to you—what have you to tell me?

Question: During the Three Dynasties, southern Yunnan (Diannan) was not listed within the domain of the職方 [Director of All-under-Heaven]. From the time Zhuang Qiao 莊蹻 campaigned for territory as far as Dian 滇 and consequently made himself its king, this marked the beginning of entry into Dian. After the Yuanfeng 元封 era (110–105 BCE), it periodically communicated with the Central States, which established commanderies and counties there; yet native and circulating officials governed in combination, and loose-rein control was inconstant. After the jade axe drew the boundary along the river and the Jinsha 金沙 River remained uncrossed, it was still cut off from civilizing teachings. When Our Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e., Emperor Taizu) unified the realm, opening up Kunmi 昆瀰 (the Erhai region) and bringing down Shanchan 鄯闡 (Kunming), he delivered it from barbarian rule and…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
經國之良法也但法久弊生侵隱詭射至不
可勝原邇者
皇上軫念民艱

教矣我

問：滇南在三代時，不列職方。自莊蹻略地至滇，因而王之，此入滇之始也。元封以後，時通中國，置郡縣；然土流雜治，羈靮靡常。既玉斧畫流，金沙未渡，猶然阻風教矣。我高皇帝混一區宇，拓昆瀰，隮鄯闡，乃出夷狄而
translation_en:
… a fine method for governing the state. However, when laws remain in place for a long time, abuses arise: encroachment, concealment, and fraudulent tax evasion have grown beyond what can be fully traced. Recently, His Majesty, filled with compassion for the hardships of the people, specially approved the request of the officials in charge and issued an edict ordering the local authorities throughout the realm to survey the fields, exposing long-standing abuses and rectifying them so as to revive the exhausted and afflicted populace—a grace most generous indeed. Yet Yunnan Province lies isolated in the southwest, and the entire land tax of the province combined does not equal that of a single large county in the Central Plains. In years of abundant harvest, the people barely have enough to eat; once war or famine strikes, both public treasuries and private households immediately report destitution. How could those responsible for the lives of the people not take thought for this? Now, if we wish to take advantage of this occasion of surveying and measuring the land to establish an enduring plan that will greatly enrich the people of Yunnan and be of some benefit to the finances of the state, from whence shall such a plan come? You students are well versed in practical affairs of the world, and matters concerning Yunnan should be of especially immediate relevance to you; what do you have to tell me?

Question: During the Three Dynasties, southern Yunnan was not listed under the Direction of the Regions (Zhifang). Beginning when Zhuang Qiao (莊蹻) campaigned for territory as far as Dian (滇) and stayed to rule it as king, Chinese entry into Yunnan commenced. From the Yuanfeng reign period (110–105 BCE) onward, it was intermittently in communication with China proper, and commanderies and counties were established; yet native chieftains and regular circulating officials governed side by side, and loose-rein control was never constant. Later, after the jade axe drew the boundary along the river and the Jinsha River (金沙江) remained uncrossed, it was still cut off from civilizing instruction. When Our Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e., Emperor Taizu) unified the realm, he opened up Kunmi (昆瀰) and pacified [?] Shanshan (鄯闡, i.e., Kunming), thereby rescuing the region from the barbarians and…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
入中國按其圖輿右肩吐蕃前臨交阯
西南控緬甸諸夷二百年來聲名文物
駸駸埒中土而物產饒異逐什一之利
者亦視爲陶中而錯趾其間眞西南一
大都會也乃入滇之路廑廑黔中一線
是凡泥可封者卽無論奸宄爲梗則夜
郎以西舉爲可虞而紆遲驛遞則病於
官踔遠侵掠則病於民是尤有可念者
甞考圖志金沙江貫絡滇洱引達江漢
===
因勢疏鑿可通舟楫自廣南抵粵西浮
牂牁可徑下番禺而由普安出田州尤
爲兩粵捷徑茲可闢而通之與昔尉佗
王南越滇王爲役屬輸款相如持節開
越嶲滇南之地道通楚蜀其故道尚可
攷見議者欲水陸通道使北而巴蜀南
而百粵聲勢聯絡潛銷負固之萌永貽
官民之利亦萬世計也圖滇者之所當
講求也夫人情重於慮始築舍難於道
punctuated: 入中國。按其圖輿，右肩吐蕃，前臨交阯，西南控緬甸諸夷。二百年來，聲名文物，駸駸埒中土；而物產饒異，逐什一之利者，亦視爲陶中而錯趾其間，眞西南一大都會也。乃入滇之路，廑廑黔中一線，是凡泥可封者。卽無論奸宄爲梗，則夜郎以西，舉爲可虞；而紆遲驛遞，則病於官；踔遠侵掠，則病於民，是尤有可念者。甞考圖志，金沙江貫絡滇、洱，引達江、漢，因勢疏鑿，可通舟楫。自廣南抵粵西，浮牂牁可徑下番禺；而由普安出田州，尤爲兩粵捷徑。茲可闢而通之與？昔尉佗王南越，滇王爲役屬輸款；相如持節，開越嶲、滇南之地，道通楚、蜀，其故道尚可攷見。議者欲水陸通道，使北而巴、蜀，南而百粵，聲勢聯絡，潛銷負固之萌，永貽官民之利，亦萬世計也，圖滇者之所當講求也。夫人情重於慮始，築舍難於道…
translation_en:
…entered into China. Examining its map and territory, its right shoulder borders Tubo [Tibet], its front faces Jiaozhi [northern Vietnam], and to the southwest it commands the various non-Chinese peoples of Burma (Miandian 緬甸). Over the past two hundred years, its renown and cultural refinement have steadily come to rival those of the Central Plains; and because its products are abundant and exotic, merchants pursuing a ten-percent profit also regard it as a commercial hub like Dingtao (Taozhong 陶中), crisscrossing one another's tracks amidst it—truly it is a great metropolis of the Southwest. Yet the route into Yunnan (Dian 滇) is barely a single thread through Guizhou (Qianzhong 黔中), a pass that could be sealed with a mere pellet of mud. Even setting aside the possibility that traitorous villains might block the way—in which case everything west of Yelang 夜郎 would be cause for alarm—the circuitous delays of the postal relay system are a hardship for officials, and the plundering along such a distant and arduous journey is a hardship for the common people; these are matters that especially warrant concern.

I have examined maps and gazetteers: the Jinsha River (Jinshajiang 金沙江) threads through the Dianchi (Dian 滇) and Erhai (Er 洱) regions and leads all the way to the Yangtze and Han rivers (Jiang Han 江漢); if we follow the terrain to dredge and excavate it, it could be made navigable for boats. Going from Guangnan 廣南 to Guangxi (Yuexi 粵西), one can float down the Zangke 牂牁 River and go straight down to Panyu 番禺 [Canton]; and going from Pu'an 普安 out through Tianzhou 田州 is an even shorter route to Guangdong and Guangxi (Liang Yue 兩粵). Can these routes now be opened and made passable? In the past, when Commandant Tuo (Wei Tuo 尉佗) ruled as King of Nanyue 南越, the King of Dian served as his vassal and offered allegiance; and when Sima Xiangru (Xiangru 相如) held the imperial credentials, he opened up the lands of Yuexi 越嶲 and southern Yunnan, connecting the roads to Chu 楚 and Shu 蜀—can those ancient routes still be investigated and traced? Commentators wish to open up both water and land routes so that, northward to Ba 巴 and Shu [Sichuan] and southward to the Hundred Yue (Baiyue 百粵) [Guangdong and Guangxi], our prestige and strategic power will be linked together, quietly dispelling the incipient threat of rebels relying on natural fastnesses and bequeathing lasting benefit to both officials and the people. This is indeed a plan for ten thousand generations, and something that those who plan for Yunnan ought to carefully investigate. Now, human nature is hesitant when contemplating new undertakings, and building a house by the roadside is difficult because of…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
旁計利便籌因革諸士滇產也宜有石
畫
punctuated: 旁。計利便，籌因革，諸士滇產也，宜有石畫。
translation_en: … the roadside. In calculating the advantages and conveniences, and in planning what to retain and what to reform, you gentlemen are natives of Dian [Yunnan], and ought to have rock-solid plans.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:

translation_en:
Forty-five successful Provincial Graduates (juren):

Second place: Yang Xianchun 楊先春, Prefectural Student of Dali Prefecture, specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji).

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
所謂誠其意者毋自欺也
鄒祖孔
同考試官教諭劉　批　發戒欺意不作影響語直
從人心靈覺處指切言之讀之神竦
考試官教諭倫　批　說理精微措辭警策
考試官教諭譙　批　邃理之文自有關鍵
傳者釋誠意在戒其不誠而已夫不誠莫甚於
===
自欺也欲誠其意而可不戒哉且大學之道未
甞不始於誠意者也然謂之意則不涉於事爲
其端固自我發也謂之誠則不由於假借其機
亦自我決也故知之未致患無以識乎誠知之
既致患有以累乎誠觸於善而知好此眞好也
顧好之一有不實焉無論天下之伺之者何如
卽反而質諸眞好之一念亦甚悖矣得無自欺
其好歟誠意者勿自欺其好也觸於不善而知
惡此眞惡也顧惡之有一不實焉無論天下之
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「所謂誠其意者，毋自欺也。」
鄒祖孔
同考試官教諭劉　批：發戒欺意，不作影響語，直從人心靈覺處指切言之，讀之神竦。
考試官教諭倫　批：說理精微，措辭警策。
考試官教諭譙　批：邃理之文，自有關鍵。
傳者釋誠意，在戒其不誠而已。夫不誠莫甚於自欺也，欲誠其意，而可不戒哉？且《大學》之道，未甞不始於誠意者也。然謂之意，則不涉於事爲，其端固自我發也；謂之誠，則不由於假借，其機亦自我決也。故知之未致，患無以識乎誠；知之既致，患有以累乎誠。觸於善而知好，此眞好也。顧好之一有不實焉，無論天下之伺之者何如，卽反而質諸眞好之一念，亦甚悖矣，得無自欺其好歟？誠意者，勿自欺其好也。觸於不善而知惡，此眞惡也。顧惡之有一不實焉，無論天下之…
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
"What is meant by 'making the thoughts sincere' is allowing no self-deception." (Great Learning, Chapter 6)
Zou Zukong 鄒祖孔
Associate Examiner, Instructor Liu 劉 comments: It brings out the meaning of guarding against self-deception without resorting to vague platitudes; rather, it points directly and incisively to the innate spiritual awareness of the human mind. Reading it stirs the spirit with awe.
Examiner, Instructor Lun 倫 comments: The exposition of principle is subtle and refined; the phrasing is incisive and arresting.
Examiner, Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: A composition of profound principle that naturally grasps the essential pivot.
When the commentator explains "making the thoughts sincere," it lies simply in warning against insincerity. Now, no insincerity is worse than self-deception; if one wishes to make one's thoughts sincere, how could one not guard against this? Moreover, the Way of the Great Learning has never failed to begin with making the thoughts sincere. Yet, to call them "thoughts" means they do not yet involve external actions and deeds—their stirrings inherently originate from within oneself. To call them "sincere" means they do not rely on external borrowing—their pivotal impulse is likewise determined by oneself. Therefore, when knowledge has not yet been extended to the utmost, the worry is having no means to recognize sincerity; once knowledge has been extended to the utmost, the worry is having something that encumbers sincerity. When one encounters goodness and knows to love it, this is true love. Yet if in loving it there is the slightest lack of reality, regardless of how the world watching from without may judge it, even if one turns within and measures it against that initial thought of true love, it is utterly contradictory—is this not deceiving oneself in one's love? One who makes his thoughts sincere does not deceive himself in his love. When one encounters evil and knows to hate it, this is true hatred. Yet if in hating it there is a single lack of reality, regardless of how the world…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
窺之者何如即反而質諸眞惡之一念亦甚悖
矣得無自欺其惡歟誠意者勿自欺其惡也人
之自誠而流于僞也常以心之有所蔽於內苟
當昭然不蔽之中而僞得以叅之是明知其僞
而安焉者也非若蔽於內者尚可冀其有時覺
而悔也使不嚴爲之禁而何以誠乎人之自誠
而淪于妄也恒以心之有所眩於外苟當炯然
不眩之中而妄得以雜之是明知其妄而安焉
者也非若眩於外者尚可望其有時悟而反也
===
苟不力爲之防而何以誠乎蓋意者萌於無形
之介惟無形故入于欺也最易自欺者遂于有
心之私惟有心故其陷乎人也甚深君子必愼
其獨有以夫然則誠意者求諸我足矣又言格
物者何曰其所謂物乃其所謂我也夫我者萬
物咸備者也有其物則有其誠無其物則無其
誠家之齊國之治天下之平均之成其不欺而
已彼老氏之復佛氏之定不可謂無志於誠而
卒未免爲自欺者蓋離物而求我也
punctuated: 窺之者何如，即反而質諸眞惡之一念，亦甚悖矣，得無自欺其惡歟？誠意者，勿自欺其惡也。人之自誠而流于僞也，常以心之有所蔽於內。苟當昭然不蔽之中，而僞得以叅之，是明知其僞而安焉者也，非若蔽於內者尚可冀其有時覺而悔也。使不嚴爲之禁，而何以誠乎？人之自誠而淪于妄也，恒以心之有所眩於外。苟當炯然不眩之中，而妄得以雜之，是明知其妄而安焉者也，非若眩於外者尚可望其有時悟而反也。苟不力爲之防，而何以誠乎？蓋意者，萌於無形之介，惟無形，故入于欺也最易；自欺者，遂于有心之私，惟有心，故其陷乎人也甚深。君子必愼其獨，有以夫！然則誠意者，求諸我足矣，又言格物者何？曰：其所謂物，乃其所謂我也。夫我者，萬物咸備者也。有其物則有其誠，無其物則無其誠。家之齊、國之治、天下之平，均之成其不欺而已。彼老氏之復、佛氏之定，不可謂無志於誠，而卒未免爲自欺者，蓋離物而求我也。
translation_en:
…how those in the world who peer into one's conduct might view it, even if one turns inward and tests it against that single thought of genuine dislike, it is utterly contradictory. Is this not deceiving oneself in one's dislike? Making one's thoughts sincere means not deceiving oneself in one's dislike.

When a person slips from sincerity into hypocrisy, it is usually because the mind is obscured within. If, while in a state of clear and unobscured awareness, hypocrisy is allowed to intrude, then one knowingly acquiesces in that hypocrisy. This is unlike one who is merely obscured within, for whom there is still hope of someday awakening and repenting. If one does not strictly forbid it, how can one achieve sincerity? When a person sinks from sincerity into falsehood, it is constantly because the mind is dazzled by external things. If, while in a state of bright and undazzled clarity, falsehood is allowed to mingle in, then one knowingly acquiesces in that falsehood. This is unlike one who is merely dazzled by external things, for whom there is still hope of someday realizing the truth and turning back. If one does not vigorously guard against it, how can one achieve sincerity?

Indeed, intentions sprout at the threshold of the formless; precisely because they are formless, it is easiest for them to slip into deception. Self-deception is consummated in deliberate selfishness; precisely because it is deliberate, it ensnares a person most deeply. That the superior man must be watchful over himself when alone—there is good reason for it indeed!

If that is so, then to make one's thoughts sincere, seeking it within oneself should suffice; why then does the text also speak of the investigation of things? I say: what it calls "things" is none other than what it calls "oneself." The self is that in which the myriad things are all complete. Where there are things, there is sincerity; where there are no things, there is no sincerity. The regulation of the family, the ordering of the state, and the pacification of the world—all alike are simply the completion of this non-deception. Those doctrines of "returning" in Laozi and "meditative concentration" in the Buddha cannot be said to lack the aspiration toward sincerity, yet in the end they cannot escape being self-deception, because they separate from things in seeking the self.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
子聞之曰大宰知我乎吾少也賤故多能
鄙事君子多乎哉不多也
楊先春
同考試官訓導靳　批　體裁莊整思致弘深發揮
聖人不貴多能之意極盡
考試官教諭倫　批　精邁典雅不落塵筌
考試官教諭譙　批　明妥有致
聖人之論多能無非明其不足貴也蓋多能非
聖人意也君子之學惟務其大者而已奚以多
===
爲且夫子之所以爲聖者惟其不多也大宰之
聖夫子專以其多而智足知聖者亦兼以其多
均之未觀其深矣夫子聞而曉之曰大宰其知
我乎我之所以多能者非聖也以少賤也而其
所以爲能者雖多也特鄙事也蓋內之非有關
於道德性命之微而姑假之以寄其意外之非
有關於天下國家之用而姑託之以適其情若
是乎不足貴也然則君子者其果多乎哉君子
非不有所知也要之其所知者乃斯道之易而
punctuated:
「子聞之，曰：『大宰知我乎！吾少也賤，故多能鄙事。君子多乎哉？不多也。』」

楊先春

同考試官訓導靳批：體裁莊整，思致弘深，發揮聖人不貴多能之意極盡。
考試官教諭倫批：精邁典雅，不落塵筌。
考試官教諭譙批：明妥有致。

聖人之論多能，無非明其不足貴也。蓋多能非聖人意也，君子之學，惟務其大者而已，奚以多爲？且夫子之所以爲聖者，惟其不多也。大宰之聖夫子，專以其多；而智足知聖者，亦兼以其多，均之未觀其深矣。夫子聞而曉之曰：「大宰其知我乎？我之所以多能者，非聖也，以少賤也；而其所以爲能者，雖多也，特鄙事也。」蓋內之非有關於道德性命之微，而姑假之以寄其意；外之非有關於天下國家之用，而姑託之以適其情，若是乎不足貴也。然則君子者，其果多乎哉？君子非不有所知也，要之其所知者，乃斯道之易而
translation_en:
"The Master heard of it and said: 'Does the Grand Minister know me? When I was young, my station was humble, and therefore I acquired many skills in menial matters. Does the gentleman have many skills? No, he does not have many.'"

Yang Xianchun 楊先春

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Jin 靳 comments: The style is dignified and well-ordered, and the thought is broad and profound. It brings out to the fullest the meaning of why the Sage did not value having many skills.
Examiner, Instructor Lun 倫 comments: Refined, surpassing, and classically elegant, not falling into worldly clichés.
Examiner, Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: Clear, fitting, and tasteful.

When the Sage discussed having many skills, it was simply to make clear that they are not worth valuing. Indeed, having many skills was not the Sage's aim; the learning of the gentleman is devoted solely to what is great—what need is there for multiplicity? Moreover, the reason the Master was a sage lay precisely in his not having many skills. When the Grand Minister regarded the Master as a sage, he did so exclusively on account of his many skills; and even the one whose wisdom was sufficient to recognize the Sage [Zigong] also included his many skills alongside his sageliness. Both alike failed to perceive his depths. Upon hearing of this, the Master enlightened them, saying: "Does the Grand Minister really know me? The reason I have many skills is not that I am a sage, but because when young I was of humble station; and the skills that I possess, though numerous, are merely menial matters." Internally, they have nothing to do with the subtleties of morality, human nature, and destiny, even if one temporarily borrows them to lodge one's thoughts; externally, they have nothing to do with the practical needs of the empire, the state, or the family, even if one temporarily turns to them to suit one's feelings. To such an extent are they unworthy of esteem! That being so, does the gentleman truly have many skills? It is not that the gentleman lacks knowledge, but in essence what he knows is known through the ease of this Way…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
知者也不多也非不有所能也要之其所能者
乃斯道之簡而能者也不多也當其始而求乎
道也精神志慮悉凝然其收斂而中不役固未
嘗有多之心當其終而得乎道也才略技藝悉
渾然其融化而外不露亦未嘗有多之跡信乎
道不在多而惟不多然後見君子也大宰觀於
我之所以多又觀於君子之所不多其可以知
我矣而遽擬以爲聖也者無乃不可乎夫子之
言如此則大宰固已失矣子貢亦未得也吾考
===
子貢嘗曰博施濟衆曰回也聞一知十賜也聞
一知二屑屑然惟多之是計夫子憂焉故曰近
取曰弗如曰一貫皆警其多也卒之與聞性與
天道其得於夫子深矣雖然性卽道也道卽性
也兼舉而竝言之其猶未離於多哉
大人者言不必信行不必果惟義所在
張輔辰
同考試官訓導董　批　一洗鉛華天質自瑩末段
入佳境矣結意尤超
punctuated:
知者也，不多也；非不有所能也，要之其所能者，乃斯道之簡而能者也，不多也。當其始而求乎道也，精神志慮悉凝然其收斂，而中不役，固未嘗有多之心；當其終而得乎道也，才略技藝悉渾然其融化，而外不露，亦未嘗有多之跡。信乎道不在多，而惟不多然後見君子也。大宰觀於我之所以多，又觀於君子之所不多，其可以知我矣。而遽擬以爲聖也者，無乃不可乎？夫子之言如此，則大宰固已失矣，子貢亦未得也。吾考子貢嘗曰「博施濟衆」，曰「回也聞一知十，賜也聞一知二」，屑屑然惟多之是計。夫子憂焉，故曰「近取」，曰「弗如」，曰「一貫」，皆警其多也。卒之與聞性與天道，其得於夫子深矣。雖然，性卽道也，道卽性也，兼舉而竝言之，其猶未離於多哉！

大人者，言不必信，行不必果，惟義所在。
張輔辰
同考試官訓導董　批：一洗鉛華，天質自瑩。末段入佳境矣，結意尤超。
translation_en:
…is known through the ease of this Way; it is not a matter of multiplicity. It is not that he has no abilities; in essence, what he is able to do is what is enabled through the simplicity of this Way; it is not a matter of multiplicity. At the beginning, when he seeks the Way, his spirit, will, and thoughts are all concentrated and gathered within, and his mind is not enslaved; truly, he never harbors an intention toward multiplicity. In the end, when he attains the Way, his talents, strategies, and skills are all seamlessly melted into one whole without showing externally; likewise, he never leaves any trace of multiplicity. Truly, the Way does not lie in multiplicity, and only in the absence of multiplicity is the gentleman revealed! If the Grand Minister observes why I have many skills, and further observes why the gentleman does not have many, he will be able to understand me. Yet to hastily presume that I am a sage on that account—is that not wide of the mark? Since the Master spoke thus, the Grand Minister was certainly mistaken, and Zigong had not grasped it either. I note that Zigong once spoke of "bestowing廣泛 benefits and relieving the multitude," and said, "Hui hears one thing and knows ten; I, Ci, hear one thing and know two"—fussing constantly and calculating only in terms of quantity. The Master worried about this, and therefore spoke of "drawing analogies from what is near," of "not being his equal," and of "one thread binding all"—all to caution him against multiplicity. In the end, Zigong was able to hear about human nature and the Way of Heaven, so what he gained from the Master was profound. Even so, human nature is none other than the Way, and the Way is none other than human nature; by citing both and speaking of them side by side, had he still not freed himself from multiplicity?!

"A great man need not be true to his word, nor must he be resolute in his actions; he abides only in what is right."
By Zhang Fuchen 張輔辰.
Comment by Associate Examiner Dong, Assistant Instructor: Washed clean of all artificial ornament, its natural quality shines of itself. The final section enters a fine realm, and the concluding thought is especially transcendent.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭倫　批　詞簡意周宜錄爲式
考試官教諭譙　批　勁爽中更有精思
大人之於言行惟其宜而已夫義者言行之宜
也彼徒以信果焉者遠於義矣大人豈爲之哉
昔孟子之論蓋曰所爲大人者非大於庸衆人
大於理也天下有言而必於信者斯其人亦賢
於不信者矣然而必於信其心遂未免爲信所
繫也乃大人之於言則不必信焉天下有行而
必於果者斯其人亦賢於不果者矣然而必於
===
果其心遂未免爲果所繫也乃大人之於行則
不必果焉夫亦曰有義而已蓋信者確然不可
渝之謂義者確然不可渝之理也果者毅然不
可易之謂義者毅然不可易之理也大人惟能
虛其心而不有自能順乎理而不拘時而言也
惟其宜於言也非我之隨乎言而言之隨乎義
也不必於信其所以爲信乎時而行也惟其宜
於行也非我之隨乎行而行之隨乎義也不必
於果其所以爲果乎蓋不信不果之失易見而
punctuated:
考試官教諭倫批：詞簡意周，宜錄爲式。
考試官教諭譙批：勁爽中更有精思。

大人之於言行，惟其宜而已。夫義者，言行之宜也；彼徒以信果焉者，遠於義矣，大人豈爲之哉？昔孟子之論，蓋曰：所爲大人者，非大於庸衆人，大於理也。天下有言而必於信者，斯其人亦賢於不信者矣；然而必於信，其心遂未免爲信所繫也。乃大人之於言，則不必信焉。天下有行而必於果者，斯其人亦賢於不果者矣；然而必於果，其心遂未免爲果所繫也。乃大人之於行，則不必果焉。夫亦曰有義而已。蓋信者，確然不可渝之謂；義者，確然不可渝之理也。果者，毅然不可易之謂；義者，毅然不可易之理也。大人惟能虛其心而不有，自能順乎理而不拘。時而言也，惟其宜於言也，非我之隨乎言，而言之隨乎義也；不必於信，其所以爲信乎？時而行也，惟其宜於行也，非我之隨乎行，而行之隨乎義也；不必於果，其所以爲果乎？蓋不信不果之失易見，而
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: The wording is concise and the meaning comprehensive; it is fitting to record this as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: Within its vigor and clarity, there is furthermore refined thought.

In his words and actions, a great man seeks only what is fitting. Now rightness (yi 義) is the appropriateness of words and actions; those who merely insist on keeping faith (xin 信) and being resolute (guo 果) are far from rightness—how would a great man do that?

When Mencius discussed this in the past, his meaning was: What makes a great man is not that he is greater than ordinary people, but that he is great in principle (li 理). In the world there are those who speak and insist on keeping their word; such men are indeed worthier than the untrustworthy. Yet by insisting on keeping their word, their minds inevitably become bound by that trustworthiness. A great man, however, in his speech does not insist on keeping his word. In the world there are those who act and insist on seeing their actions through; such men are indeed worthier than the irresolute. Yet by insisting on seeing their actions through, their minds inevitably become bound by that resoluteness. A great man, however, in his actions does not insist on seeing them through. He simply says that there is rightness, and nothing more.

For trustworthiness means being firmly unchangeable, whereas rightness is the principle of what is firmly unchangeable. Resoluteness means being steadfastly unalterable, whereas rightness is the principle of what is steadfastly unalterable. Only because a great man can empty his mind and hold no preconceptions is he naturally able to follow principle without being inflexible. When it is time to speak, he cares only for what is fitting to say; it is not that the self follows the words, but that the words follow rightness. By not insisting on keeping his word, is this not the very way he achieves true trustworthiness? When it is time to act, he cares only for what is fitting to do; it is not that the self follows the action, but that the action follows rightness. By not insisting on seeing his actions through, is this not the very way he achieves true resoluteness? For the faults of untrustworthiness and irresoluteness are easy to see, whereas…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
信果之失難見以其迹之近於義也神而明之
非大人不能也信果有方所之可執而義無方
所之可執以其理之根於心默而成之非大
人不與也學者愼無務硜硜爲哉孟子言此其
下卽繼曰大人者不失赤子之心者也夫赤子
之心純一無僞所謂僞者非必矯飾誕妄之謂
也一心以爲信又一心以必於信一心以爲果
又一心以必於果方寸之中不勝其計較是亦
僞耳故孟子特指心之本體以示人而又甞曰
所惡於智者爲其鑿也夫欲不失赤子之心者
其惟不鑿乎
===
易
象曰大有柔得尊位大中而上下應之曰
大有
鄒祖孔
同考試官訓導周　批　本卦材以寫一統氣象橫
厲莊雅是盛世之文也錄之
考試官教諭倫　批　調新詞彩意復融徹
punctuated:
信果之失難見，以其迹之近於義也，神而明之，非大人不能也。信果有方所之可執，而義無方所之可執，以其理之根於心，默而成之，非大人不與也。學者愼無務硜硜爲哉！孟子言此，其下卽繼曰：「大人者，不失赤子之心者也。」夫赤子之心，純一無僞。所謂僞者，非必矯飾誕妄之謂也。一心以爲信，又一心以必於信；一心以爲果，又一心以必於果，方寸之中，不勝其計較，是亦僞耳。故孟子特指心之本體以示人，而又甞曰：「所惡於智者，爲其鑿也。」夫欲不失赤子之心者，其惟不鑿乎！
易
「《象》曰：『大有，柔得尊位，大中而上下應之，曰大有。』」
鄒祖孔
同考試官訓導周　批：本卦材以寫一統氣象，橫厲莊雅，是盛世之文也，錄之。
考試官教諭倫　批：調新詞彩，意復融徹。
translation_en:
… the failings of insisting on keeping one's word and seeing one's actions through are difficult to discern, because their outward traces closely resemble righteousness; to comprehend this spiritually and illuminate it is something none but a great man can do. Keeping one's word and seeing one's actions through have fixed bounds that can be grasped, whereas righteousness has no fixed bounds that can be grasped; because its principle is rooted in the mind, to accomplish it silently is something in which none but a great man can partake. Let scholars take care not to busy themselves with stubborn narrow-mindedness! After Mencius said this, he immediately followed by saying: "The great man is he who does not lose his childlike heart." Now, the heart of an infant is pure, unified, and without artifice. What is called artifice does not necessarily mean affectation or wild falsehood. To have one thought focused on keeping one's word, and yet another thought bent on insisting upon that word; to have one thought focused on resolute action, and yet another thought bent on insisting upon that action—when within the square inch of the mind there is no end to such calculating deliberation, that too is nothing other than artifice. Therefore, Mencius specifically pointed to the original substance of the mind to show people, and he also once said: "What I dislike in clever men is their forcing of things." Surely, for one who wishes not to lose his childlike heart, the only way is not to force things!

Book of Changes (Yi)

"The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: 'Possession in Great Measure (Dayou): the yielding obtains the honored position, great and central, and both above and below respond to it; therefore it is called Possession in Great Measure.'"

Zou Zukong 鄒祖孔

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhou 周 comments: Grounded in the constituent qualities of the hexagram to depict the grand atmosphere of unified rule, it is vigorous, solemn, and elegant—truly the writing of a flourishing age. Record it for publication.

Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: Its tone is fresh and its diction brilliant, while the meaning is furthermore thoroughly integrated and pellucid.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭譙　批　華實並茂
觀大有之由名而一統之盛見矣夫治以大有
爲極也卦具大一統之義則名之爲大有也固
宜夫子傳大有蓋謂聖人之所以宅中圖大者
德位隆而人心屬也三者不備難以語有一有
未盛尤難語大卦之名大有者慶天下之全盛
也然何以曰大有哉六五柔得位得中而上下
應之是身膺曆數之傳班爵班祿之柄自我操
之聖人之大寶曰位此則尊無二上者矣心涵
===
精一之秘萬事萬化之本自我立之帝王之授
受曰中此爲大中至正者矣上而百辟輸忠有
道之朝委質者無二心也下而羣黎推戴皇極
之主則君者無越志也此其所履者匪偏安之
業已也聖人在位臣妾億兆焉雖中外異地而
其勢不分所圖者匪小康之務已也明主立隆
玉帛萬國焉雖慶讓異施而其權在我謂之曰
大有是以六合爲家天地之富有者吾皆有之
以四海爲富帝王所自有者吾盡有之非大有
punctuated:
考試官教諭譙　批：華實並茂。

觀大有之由名，而一統之盛見矣。夫治以大有爲極也，卦具大一統之義，則名之爲大有也固宜。夫子傳《大有》，蓋謂聖人之所以宅中圖大者，德位隆而人心屬也。三者不備，難以語有；一有未盛，尤難語大。卦之名大有者，慶天下之全盛也。然何以曰大有哉？六五柔得位、得中，而上下應之。是身膺曆數之傳，班爵班祿之柄自我操之。聖人之大寶曰位，此則尊無二上者矣；心涵精一之秘，萬事萬化之本自我立之。帝王之授受曰中，此爲大中至正者矣。上而百辟輸忠有道之朝，委質者無二心也；下而羣黎推戴皇極之主，則君者無越志也。此其所履者，匪偏安之業已也。聖人在位，臣妾億兆焉，雖中外異地而其勢不分；所圖者，匪小康之務已也。明主立隆，玉帛萬國焉，雖慶讓異施而其權在我。謂之曰大有，是以六合爲家，天地之富有者吾皆有之；以四海爲富，帝王所自有者吾盡有之。非大有
translation_en:
Examiner Qiao, Instructor, comments: Both ornament and substance flourish together.

By observing why the hexagram "Great Possession" (Dayou) is so named, the flourishing of grand unity becomes apparent. Governance takes Great Possession as its ultimate culmination; since the hexagram embodies the principle of grand unity, it is indeed fitting that it be named Great Possession. In commenting on Great Possession, the Master meant that the way the sage occupies the center and plans for greatness is through the exaltation of his virtue and position and the allegiance of people's hearts. If these three are not complete, it is difficult to speak of "possession"; if any one of them is not yet flourishing, it is even more difficult to speak of "great." That the hexagram is named Great Possession is to celebrate the complete flourishing of the realm under Heaven. Yet why is it called Great Possession? The yielding line in the fifth place attains the honored position and attains the center, while those above and below respond to it. This means that in his own person he receives the transmission of the Heaven-ordained succession, and the authority to distribute ranks and emoluments is held by him alone. "The great treasure of the sage is called position"—this is indeed the supreme honor above which there is no peer. In his mind he encompasses the subtle secret of "refinement and singleness," and the foundation of the myriad affairs and transformations is established by him alone. What the emperors and kings transmitted and received is called the Mean—this is indeed the great centrality and utmost rectitude. Above, the hundred lords render loyalty to a court that possesses the Way, and those who present pledges of service harbor no duplicity; below, the multitude of common people uphold the sovereign of Supreme Ultimate, and those who pattern themselves after the ruler harbor no transgressive ambitions. What he treads upon here is no mere enterprise of partial peace! When the sage is on the throne, he makes subjects and servants of hundreds of millions; though the interior and exterior are different lands, their momentum is undivided. What he plans for is no mere affair of lesser tranquility! When the enlightened ruler establishes the highest standard, the myriad states bring jade and silk; though rewards and reprimands are differently applied, the authority rests with him. To call it Great Possession means taking the six directions of the universe as one's household, so that all the abundant possessions of Heaven and Earth are possessed by us; and taking everything within the four seas as one's wealth, so that all that emperors and kings naturally possess is completely possessed by us. If this is not Great Possession…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而何吁觀此而大有之義昭矣抑君道貴剛而
大有之君以柔者何也時也時也者中也蓋豫
大之時易生侈心剛毅之主不難自用守成業
而永治安未始不於寅畏謙讓者得之彼六王
一而勤遠略海內富而陋漢規皆用剛之過也
非有大有之道也此大有之君利用柔也用柔
即用中也然一於柔則靡矣不可也彖言遏惡
揚善所以副其柔而成其中也玆所謂大中也
所以保大有也
===
鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂
張良遇
同考試官訓導周　批　藻繪既工淘洗亦盡文之
有超詣者
考試官教諭倫　批　邊幅不窘色相蒼然
考試官教諭譙　批　意完調逸
觀造化鼓物之妙道在是矣夫天地無心故無
憂也此其鼓物不同於聖人也與且斯道通極
於天地而天地則普物無心者也何也萬物待
punctuated:
而何？吁！觀此而大有之義昭矣。抑君道貴剛，而大有之君以柔者，何也？時也。時也者，中也。蓋豫大之時，易生侈心，剛毅之主，不難自用。守成業而永治安，未始不於寅畏謙讓者得之。彼六王一而勤遠略，海內富而陋漢規，皆用剛之過也，非有大有之道也。此大有之君利用柔也，用柔即用中也。然一於柔則靡矣，不可也。《彖》言「遏惡揚善」，所以副其柔而成其中也。玆所謂大中也，所以保大有也。

鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂
張良遇
同考試官訓導周　批：藻繪既工，淘洗亦盡，文之有超詣者。
考試官教諭倫　批：邊幅不窘，色相蒼然。
考試官教諭譙　批：意完調逸。

觀造化鼓物之妙，道在是矣。夫天地無心，故無憂也，此其鼓物不同於聖人也與！且斯道通極於天地，而天地則普物無心者也。何也？萬物待
translation_en:
… is it if not "Possession in Great Measure" (Dayou 大有)? Ah! Looking at this, the meaning of Dayou becomes clear. Yet the way of the ruler prizes firmness, so why is the ruler of Dayou characterized by gentleness? It is because of the time. And time means centrality (the mean). For in times of abundance and greatness, an extravagant mind easily arises, and a firm, resolute ruler readily relies on his own will. Preserving an established enterprise and perpetuating peace and order have never not been achieved through reverent awe and humble modesty. Those who unified the six kingdoms and then labored over distant conquests, or who, once the realm within the seas was rich, scorned the foundational rules of the Han, all erred through an excess of firmness; they did not possess the Way of Dayou. This is why the ruler of Dayou finds it advantageous to employ gentleness, and employing gentleness is precisely employing centrality. However, to be exclusivamente gentle leads to weakness, which will not do. The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan 彖) speaks of "repressing evil and promoting good" (e e yang shan 遏惡揚善) as the means to complement gentleness and bring centrality to completion. This is what is called Great Centrality, and it is whereby Possession in Great Measure is preserved.

"It rouses the myriad things to action, yet does not share the anxieties of the sage" (Gu wanwu er bu yu shengren tong you 鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂)
Zhang Liangyu 張良遇
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhou 周 comments: The rhetorical embellishment is skillful, and the refinement is thorough—a piece of writing that reaches a transcendent level.
Examiner, Instructor Lun 倫 comments: Its scope is uncramped, and its aspect has an antique depth.
Examiner, Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: The conception is complete and the cadence is unrestrained.

When we observe the wondrous way in which the transformative power of nature rouses things to action, we see that the Way lies right here. Now, Heaven and Earth have no deliberate mind and therefore have no anxieties; is this not how their rousing of things differs from that of the sage? Moreover, this Way extends to the utmost through Heaven and Earth, and Heaven and Earth universally pervade all things without a deliberate mind. Why is this? The myriad things await …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
命於天地其顯其藏惟天地鼓之孰不曰彼天
地者任其憂將與聖人同之矣不知一氣司闔
闢之運而玄化妙於無端一理貫通復之機而
神功流於不宰仁一顯而萬物皆向於有其出
也若或鼓之也然賦予萬物而已不勞與聖人
憂民生之未遂而旣竭心思者不同也用一藏
而萬物皆反其眞其入也是孰鼓之也然以美
利利天下不言所利與聖人憂民性之未復而
不遑寧處者不同也聖人嘗先天下之憂天地
則無思無爲無所憂也雖有憂不足爲聖人之
累而無憂益以驗天地之神何者天人之分殊
===
也聖人憂民之心無窮天地則易知簡能無庸
憂也雖有憂然後見聖人而不憂益以見天地
何者神化之用異也鼓萬物而忘萬物鼓者不
知爲所鼓者亦不知道妙天地如此天地其道
乎抑論天地無憂四時之吏五行之佐宣其氣
矣而又舉其責畀之聖人聖人者裁成其道輔
相其宜兢兢焉惟恐一物失所干天地之和凡
punctuated: 命於天地，其顯其藏，惟天地鼓之，孰不曰彼天地者任其憂，將與聖人同之矣？不知一氣司闔闢之運，而玄化妙於無端；一理貫通復之機，而神功流於不宰。仁一顯而萬物皆向於有，其出也，若或鼓之也；然賦予萬物而已不勞，與聖人憂民生之未遂而旣竭心思者不同也。用一藏而萬物皆反其眞，其入也，是孰鼓之也？然以美利利天下，不言所利，與聖人憂民性之未復而不遑寧處者不同也。聖人嘗先天下之憂，天地則無思無爲，無所憂也。雖有憂不足爲聖人之累，而無憂益以驗天地之神，何者？天人之分殊也。聖人憂民之心無窮，天地則易知簡能，無庸憂也。雖有憂然後見聖人，而不憂益以見天地，何者？神化之用異也。鼓萬物而忘萬物，鼓者不知，爲所鼓者亦不知。道妙天地如此，天地其道乎？抑論天地無憂，四時之吏、五行之佐宣其氣矣，而又舉其責畀之聖人。聖人者，裁成其道，輔相其宜，兢兢焉惟恐一物失所，干天地之和，凡
translation_en: … receive their mandate from Heaven and Earth. Whether in their manifestation or in their withdrawal, it is solely Heaven and Earth that rouse them. Who would not say that Heaven and Earth take on this anxiety, sharing it just like the sage? They do not realize that a single vital force governs the cycles of closing and opening, while mysterious transformation operates wondrously without beginning or end; a single principle threads through the mechanisms of expansion and return, while divine achievement flows forth without a conscious ruler. Once benevolence is manifested, the myriad things all tend toward existence; in their coming forth, it is as if something rouses them. Yet Heaven and Earth bestow life upon the myriad things without toiling themselves, which is different from the sage who worries that the people's livelihood is not yet fulfilled and thus exhausts his mind and thoughts. Once function is withdrawn, the myriad things all return to their true state; in their going back, who is it that rouses them? Yet Heaven and Earth benefit the world with fine advantages without speaking of what they benefit, which is different from the sage who worries that the people's nature is not yet restored and thus has no leisure to rest in peace. The sage ever worries before the world worries, whereas Heaven and Earth have neither thought nor action, and have nothing over which to worry. Although having worries is not enough to be a burden to the sage, having no worries all the more demonstrates the divinity of Heaven and Earth. Why is this? Because the distinction between Heaven and man is different. The sage's heart of worry for the people is endless, whereas Heaven and Earth know through ease and accomplish through simplicity, having no need to worry. Although it is only through having worries that the sage is seen, it is through not worrying that Heaven and Earth are all the more seen. Why is this? Because the operations of divine transformation are different. Rousing the myriad things yet forgetting the myriad things, that which rouses does not know it, and those that are roused do not know it either. The Way is wondrous in Heaven and Earth like this—are Heaven and Earth not the Way itself? Or if we discuss how Heaven and Earth have no worries: the officials of the four seasons and the assistants of the Five Phases propagate their vital force, and furthermore they take their responsibility and entrust it to the sage. The sage regulates and completes their Way, and assists and furthers their appropriateness, cautiously fearing only that a single thing might lose its place and disrupt the harmony of Heaven and Earth. All…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以代天地憂也聖人憂則天地可無憂矣然堯
憂不得舜舜憂不得禹臯陶聖人亦求可寄吾
憂者使憂之則吾可無憂也此有憂者卒歸於
無憂故曰聖人心同天地
書
后克聖臣不命其承疇敢不祇若王之休
命
劉信徵
同考試官教諭劉　批　持議甚正用意忠懇是必
===
心傳說之心者足爲得士慶矣
考試官教諭倫　批　氣勁思深具占忠款
考試官教諭譙　批　文有關係不爲浪語
上有聖君則效忠於君者衆矣葢惟聖爲能從
諫也主聖則諫者衆矣尚何患其不言也哉傳
說復於高宗者曰臣能進諫不能必君之受諫
故有欲諫而不敢諫者凡以后弗克聖也后誠
從諫而聖焉躬明哲之資秉以虛懷有聖不自
聖之念純作則之範擴以弘度存不諫亦入之
punctuated:
以代天地憂也。聖人憂，則天地可無憂矣。然堯憂不得舜，舜憂不得禹、臯陶，聖人亦求可寄吾憂者使憂之，則吾可無憂也。此有憂者卒歸於無憂，故曰：「聖人心同天地。」

書
后克聖，臣不命其承，疇敢不祇若王之休命。
劉信徵
同考試官教諭劉　批：持議甚正，用意忠懇，是必心傳說之心者，足爲得士慶矣。
考試官教諭倫　批：氣勁思深，具占忠款。
考試官教諭譙　批：文有關係，不爲浪語。

上有聖君，則效忠於君者衆矣。葢惟聖爲能從諫也，主聖則諫者衆矣，尚何患其不言也哉？傳說復於高宗者曰：臣能進諫，不能必君之受諫，故有欲諫而不敢諫者，凡以后弗克聖也。后誠從諫而聖焉，躬明哲之資，秉以虛懷，有聖不自聖之念；純作則之範，擴以弘度，存不諫亦入之
translation_en:
…in order to worry on behalf of Heaven and Earth. When the sage worries, Heaven and Earth can be free from worry. Yet Yao worried over not finding Shun, and Shun worried over not finding Yu and Gao Yao; the sage likewise seeks those to whom he can entrust his worries and makes them worry over them, so that he himself can be free from worry. Thus, having worries ultimately returns to having no worries; therefore it is said: "The mind of the sage is identical with Heaven and Earth."

Book of Documents (Shu)
"If the sovereign can be sage, his ministers, even without being commanded, will anticipate his wishes; who would dare not respectfully comply with the king's admirable charge?"
Liu Xinzheng 劉信徵
Associate Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: The argument he maintains is most upright, and his intention is loyal and earnest. He must be one whose mind is at one with the mind of Fu Yue [transcribed 傳說]; this is sufficient cause to rejoice at having obtained a true scholar!
Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: Vigorous in vital force and deep in thought; it fully demonstrates loyal sincerity.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: The essay is of genuine consequence and does not indulge in empty talk.

When there is a sage ruler above, those who render loyalty to the ruler will be numerous. For only a sage is able to follow remonstrance; when the sovereign is sage, those who remonstrate are numerous—what worry could there still be that they will not speak out? What Fu Yue [transcribed 傳說] replied to Gaozong 高宗 was to say: Ministers are capable of offering remonstrance, but they cannot guarantee that the ruler will accept their remonstrance; thus there are those who wish to remonstrate yet dare not do so, all because the sovereign fails to be sage. If the sovereign is truly able to follow remonstrance and be sage—personally possessing the endowment of clear wisdom, holding to it with an open mind, and cherishing the thought of being sage without considering himself sage; rendering pure the standard by which he serves as a model, broadening it with magnanimous tolerance, and preserving a [mind] that receives [counsel] even without explicit remonstrance…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
心則不命非以爲咈也命之非以導諛也將見
處有道之朝懷忠者咸樂自盡當聖作之世感
遇者寧忍負君君心默喻於其臣卽不命之將
承之以矢其謨況納誨之命王之啓忠者何休
也疇敢不祗奉厥命以仰副乎舟楫霖雨之思
臣心深諒乎其君未嘗命之亦承意以畢其愚
況匡辟之命王之誘臣者何休也敢不對揚其
休以自效乎啓心沃心之願蓋臣有犯顏敢諫
者矣是萬一於君心之悟也有君如此則忠者
===
益奮不必問命之與否在廷皆繩愆之士臣有
信而後諫者矣是有所待而言也得君如彼則
諛者亦直不必待命之如何在位多弼直之臣
若然則爲王之臣者皆祗承王休不特一說爲
然也然非后之克聖是孰啓之王亦思所以從
諫也哉抑高宗以形肖用說是以神不以言也
乃說要之以從諫者何也蓋君不以治安而忘
納誨之益臣不以主聖而忘進言之忠此明良
交儆之風也說之君臣以之故相與有成千古
punctuated: 心，則不命非以爲咈也，命之非以導諛也。將見處有道之朝，懷忠者咸樂自盡；當聖作之世，感遇者寧忍負君？君心默喻於其臣，卽不命之，將承之以矢其謨；況納誨之命，王之啓忠者何休也！疇敢不祗奉厥命，以仰副乎舟楫霖雨之思？臣心深諒乎其君，未嘗命之，亦承意以畢其愚；況匡辟之命，王之誘臣者何休也！敢不對揚其休，以自效乎啓心沃心之願？蓋臣有犯顏敢諫者矣，是萬一於君心之悟也。有君如此，則忠者益奮，不必問命之與否，在廷皆繩愆之士。臣有信而後諫者矣，是有所待而言也。得君如彼，則諛者亦直，不必待命之如何，在位多弼直之臣。若然，則爲王之臣者，皆祗承王休，不特一說爲然也。然非后之克聖，是孰啓之？王亦思所以從諫也哉！抑高宗以形肖用說，是以神，不以言也；乃說要之以從諫者，何也？蓋君不以治安而忘納誨之益，臣不以主聖而忘進言之忠，此明良交儆之風也。說之君臣以之，故相與有成，千古
translation_en: … mind, then even without a command, they will not consider remonstrance to be defiance; and when commanded, it is not to invite flattery. One will see that, living in a court that possesses the Way, those who harbor loyalty all gladly exert themselves to the utmost; and in an age when a sage arises, how could those moved by his favor bear to fail their ruler? When the ruler's heart is tacitly understood by his ministers, even if he does not command them, they will comply with it to set forth their counsels; how much more so when there is a command to accept instruction—how admirable is the king's inspiration of loyalty! Who would dare not reverently obey his command, so as to look up and fulfill his longing for 'boats and oars' and 'seasonable rain'? When the ministers' hearts deeply trust their ruler, even before he has commanded them, they will heed his intent and pour out their humble thoughts; how much more so when there is a command to correct the sovereign—how admirable is the king's encouragement of his ministers! Would they dare not extol and respond to his grace, so as to devote themselves to fulfilling the wish of 'opening his mind and enriching his heart'? Indeed, there are ministers who dare to remonstrate even at the risk of offending the sovereign's countenance, hoping for the one-in-ten-thousand chance that the ruler's mind will awaken. Having a ruler like this, the loyal will be even more roused; without needing to ask whether a command has been given or not, the court will be filled with gentlemen who correct faults. And there are ministers who remonstrate only after gaining trust, waiting for the right conditions before speaking.
