Finding a ruler like that, even flatterers will become upright; without needing to wait to see what the command is like, those in office will mostly be ministers who assist with uprightness. If this is so, then all who serve as the king's ministers will reverently respond to the king's grace—not only Fu Yue (說) alone! Yet if the sovereign were not capable of being a sage, who could open the way for this? May the king therefore reflect on how to follow remonstrance! Moreover, when Gaozong (高宗) employed Fu Yue by matching his likeness from a dream, it was through spirit, not through words; why then did Fu Yue press him to follow remonstrance? Because a ruler does not, on account of peace and order, forget the benefit of accepting instruction, and a minister does not, on account of his lord's sageliness, forget the loyalty of offering words. This is the custom of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers mutually cautioning one another. Fu Yue and his sovereign practiced this; therefore they achieved success together, and for a thousand ages …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
稱神交也使君曰予聖臣曰將順成弼之意廢
矣何以爲說嗚呼納諫之主導臣使言善諫之
臣導君聽言此說之君臣相遇以神相要以言
也與
道洽政治澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
郝維德
同考試官教諭劉　批　氣度溫醇脉絡融貫同道
考試官教諭倫　批　整潔明秀
化民之意隱括篇中矣錄之
===
考試官教諭譙　批　精練冲雅更耐咀嚼
惟化之入人者深斯澤之所被者遠夫道洽政
治化之入人者深矣其澤生民而庇四夷也有
以哉康王期畢公之意若曰至治無近效王者
務廣德惟兹東郊尤四方之極中外之觀化恒
於斯也三后固協心同道矣化之成也如何蓋
道以運治而政爲之具是澤所從出者也道之
蘊而不洽者心之異向也心同則施之有本末
焉精神心術之運流通於歷世者融液於無方
punctuated:
稱神交也。使君曰「予聖」，臣曰「將順」，成弼之意廢矣，何以爲說？嗚呼！納諫之主，導臣使言；善諫之臣，導君聽言。此說之君臣，相遇以神，相要以言也與！

道洽政治，澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。
郝維德
同考試官教諭劉　批：氣度溫醇，脉絡融貫，同道化民之意，隱括篇中矣，錄之。
考試官教諭倫　批：整潔明秀。
考試官教諭譙　批：精練冲雅，更耐咀嚼。

惟化之入人者深，斯澤之所被者遠。夫道洽政治，化之入人者深矣，其澤生民而庇四夷也，有以哉！康王期畢公之意，若曰：至治無近效，王者務廣德。惟兹東郊，尤四方之極，中外之觀化恒於斯也。三后固協心同道矣，化之成也如何？蓋道以運治，而政爲之具，是澤所從出者也。道之蘊而不洽者，心之異向也。心同則施之有本末焉，精神心術之運，流通於歷世者，融液於無方，
translation_en:
…have praised it as a communion of spirit. Had the sovereign said, "I am sage," and the minister said, "I shall simply comply," the meaning of perfecting and assisting the ruler would have been abandoned—how then could he have been Fu Yue? Alas! A ruler who accepts remonstrance guides his ministers to speak; a minister skilled in remonstrance guides his ruler to listen. Was this not how Fu Yue and his sovereign met in spirit and bound each other through words?

"The Way penetrated and governance was well-ordered; beneficence moistened the living people, and the four barbarian tribes with left-fastened lapels all without exception relied upon them."

Hao Weide 郝維德

Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Liu: Its bearing is gentle and pure, and its thread of argument is thoroughly coherent. The idea of sharing the Way to transform the people is implicitly encompassed within the essay. Selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Lun: Neat, clear, and elegant.
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Qiao: Refined, serene, and graceful; it rewards repeated savoring even more.

Only when transformation enters deeply into people does the reach of its beneficence extend far. Now, when the Way penetrates and governance is well-ordered, transformation has indeed entered deeply into people—is there not good reason that its beneficence moistens the living people and shelters the four barbarian tribes?

The intent of King Kang in charging the Duke of Bi was as if to say: Supreme governance has no instant results; a true king strives to broaden his virtue. This eastern suburb in particular is the pivot of the four quarters, where those within and without constantly look to observe our transformation. The Three Sovereigns indeed united their minds and shared the same Way; what, then, was the completion of their transformation like?

For the Way is that by which governance is set in motion, and administrative measures are its instruments—this is whence beneficence issues forth. When the Way remains pent up and does not penetrate everywhere, it is because minds are directed toward different ends. When minds are united, its implementation has both root and branch: the movement of spirit and mental art, flowing uninterruptedly through successive generations, blends pervasively without bounds,…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
理道之洽盎如也政之紊而不治者道之多岐
也道同則爲之有次第焉紀綱法度之施整齊
於三世者脩舉而罔墜庶政之治秩如也道化
流衍乂而益徧舉凌德之民潤於膏澤蓋形神
俱釋而放心其盡泯也已德教孚洽久而彌深
胥滅義之衆潤於厚澤蓋身心咸裕而旌別可
無用也已由是四夷左衽其人雖王者所不臣
也然洛民化則四夷俱化傾心內向賴吾餘澤
之施者無間於華也其視四方無虞之日不尤
===
盛矣乎其俗雖冠裳所不被也然邇人安則遠
人亦安輸誠納款賴吾餘潤之布者無間於近
也其視大猷允升之世不益隆矣乎吁此化殷
之成也愼始和中者於今爲烈公之成終者於
前有光吾其樂觀厥成矣公也得無意於是耶
吾於是而知周過其曆也周以忠厚基命歷千
餘年而後大統克集蕞尒殷民治越三紀康王
猶惓惓於道洽政治之命無忿心無怠志何其
厚也是宜刑措而過曆也至四夷咸賴卽於澤
punctuated:
理道之洽，盎如也。政之紊而不治者，道之多岐也；道同，則爲之有次第焉。紀綱法度之施，整齊於三世者，脩舉而罔墜，庶政之治，秩如也。道化流衍，乂而益徧，舉凌德之民潤於膏澤，蓋形神俱釋，而放心其盡泯也已。德教孚洽，久而彌深，胥滅義之衆潤於厚澤，蓋身心咸裕，而旌別可無用也已。由是四夷左衽，其人雖王者所不臣也，然洛民化則四夷俱化，傾心內向，賴吾餘澤之施者，無間於華也，其視四方無虞之日，不尤盛矣乎！其俗雖冠裳所不被也，然邇人安則遠人亦安，輸誠納款，賴吾餘潤之布者，無間於近也，其視大猷允升之世，不益隆矣乎！吁！此化殷之成也。愼始和中者，於今爲烈；公之成終者，於前有光。吾其樂觀厥成矣，公也得無意於是耶？
吾於是而知周過其曆也。周以忠厚基命，歷千餘年而後大統克集。蕞尒殷民，治越三紀，康王猶惓惓於道洽政治之命，無忿心，無怠志，何其厚也！是宜刑措而過曆也。至四夷咸賴，卽於澤
translation_en:
…and the pervasive harmony of the Way of principle brims over. When governance is disordered and uncollected, it is because the Way has branched into many paths; when the Way is shared, action follows an orderly sequence. As the application of foundational norms and legal measures—brought into uniformity across three generations—is maintained and upheld without fail, the governance of the manifold administrative affairs is perfectly ordered. As the transformative influence of the Way flows forth, bringing order and spreading ever wider, all the people who once transgressed against virtue are steeped in rich beneficence; indeed, both form and spirit are set at ease, and their wayward minds are completely eradicated. As virtuous instruction inspires trust and harmony, growing ever deeper with time, the multitudes who once obliterated righteousness are all steeped in generous beneficence; indeed, both body and mind are made abundant, and distinguishing the good from the bad may be dispensed with. From this, as for the four barbarian tribes with their left-fastened robes: although their people are not treated as subjects by a true king, once the people of Luo are transformed, the four barbarian tribes are transformed together with them. Turning their hearts inward in allegiance, they rely on the bestowal of our surplus beneficence without any distinction from the Chinese—compared to the days when the four quarters were merely free from alarm, is this not even more flourishing? Although their customs are not reached by cap and skirt, once those near at hand are at peace, those afar are also at peace. Offering up their sincerity and submitting tribute, they rely on the spreading of our surplus moisture without any distinction from those nearby—compared to the age when the great plan truly ascended, is this not even more exalted? Ah! This is the completion of the transformation of Yin. What was begun with caution and harmonized in the middle now shines with splendor; the Duke’s bringing it to completion at the end adds luster to what came before. I shall happily behold its completion—could you, Duke, fail to set your mind upon this?
From this I know why the Zhou surpassed its divined span of years. The Zhou founded its Mandate on loyal generosity, passing through more than a thousand years before the great succession could be brought together. Over these petty people of Yin, governance had extended past three twelve-year cycles, yet King Kang was still earnestly devoted to the charge of the Way permeating and governance being well-ordered—without an angry heart, without an idle will, how generous he was! It was fitting indeed that punishments were set aside and the dynasty surpassed its allotted span. As for the four barbarian tribes all relying on them, this was achieved right within the beneficence that…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
潤生民得之彼海內粗安遂疲中國以事外夷
者於忠厚之道何如
詩
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
張輔辰
同考試官訓導周　批　雍容深厚眞得詩人祝君
語意而詞彩煒然醒心奪目
考試官教諭倫　批　刻剔枝蔓旨趣淵永
考試官教諭譙　批　格整詞葩
===
詩人願王嗣之多德足以宜其位也夫王嗣天
下之本也多而且賢王者之福孰大於此哉想
其答鳧鷖之意若曰吾王備假樂之德而膺保
右之命固將合萬世之福以爲福者其可願何
如哉彼王者之子孫君王之統繫焉然非多不
足以盛其傳非德不足以宜其任也吾願吾王
福在子孫其多則千億焉太和之在宇宙者萃
於我周益以衍螽斯之慶忠厚之傳先世者流
於今日益以兆麟趾之祥帝王相傳以敬者也
punctuated:
潤生民得之。彼海內粗安，遂疲中國以事外夷者，於忠厚之道何如？

《詩》
「子孫千億，穆穆皇皇。宜君宜王。」
張輔辰
同考試官訓導周　批：雍容深厚，眞得詩人祝君語意，而詞彩煒然，醒心奪目。
考試官教諭倫　批：刻剔枝蔓，旨趣淵永。
考試官教諭譙　批：格整詞葩。

詩人願王嗣之多，德足以宜其位也。夫王嗣，天下之本也。多而且賢，王者之福孰大於此哉！想其答《鳧鷖》之意，若曰：吾王備假樂之德，而膺保右之命，固將合萬世之福以爲福者，其可願何如哉！彼王者之子孫，君王之統繫焉。然非多不足以盛其傳，非德不足以宜其任也。吾願吾王福在子孫，其多則千億焉。太和之在宇宙者，萃於我周，益以衍螽斯之慶；忠厚之傳先世者，流於今日，益以兆麟趾之祥。帝王相傳以敬者也，
translation_en:
… the moisturizing of the common people. As for those who, as soon as the realm within the seas is barely at peace, proceed to exhaust the Central Kingdom in order to deal with foreign barbarians, how does that compare to the Way of loyalty and generosity?

Book of Odes (Shi)
"Sons and grandsons in thousands and ratusan of thousands, / Reverent, reverent, majestic, majestic; / Well suited to be lords, well suited to be kings." [Ode "Jia le"]
Zhang Fuchen
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhou comments: Graceful, poised, and deeply substantial, it truly captures the tone and intent of the poet's blessing for his sovereign, while its rhetorical brilliance shines forth, awakening the mind and dazzling the eye.
Examiner and Instructor Lun comments: Pruning away all superfluous branches and vines, its purport and resonance are deep and lasting.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: Well-ordered in structure and resplendent in diction.

The poet wishes for the royal heirs to be numerous and for their virtue to be sufficient to suit their stations. Now, the royal heirs are the foundation of All under Heaven. That they be both numerous and worthy—what blessing for a true king could be greater than this! Imagining his meaning in replying to the "Fu yi" [Wild Ducks and Widgeons] ode, it is as if he said: Our king possesses the admirable and joyful virtue [of "Jia le"] and receives the Mandate that protects and aids him; he will surely gather the blessings of ten thousand generations to make up his own blessing—what should our wishes for him be like! In the sons and grandsons of a true king lies the line of succession of lords and kings. Yet unless they are numerous, it is not enough to make their transmission flourish; and unless they possess virtue, it is not enough to make them suited to their responsibilities. I wish that our king's blessing may reside in his sons and grandsons, and that in number they may reach thousands and hundreds of thousands! The Supreme Harmony present in the universe gathers in our Zhou house, all the more extending the felicity of the "Zhong si" [Locusts] ode; the loyalty and generosity handed down from former generations flows into the present day, all the more heralding the auspicious omen of the "Lin zhi" [Toes of the Unicorn] ode. Emperors and kings hand down their rule through reverence;…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
皆穆穆而敬寅畏中存儼乎緝熙執競之遺矩
帝王世濟其美者也皆皇皇而美精純內蘊宛
乎徽柔於皇之懿範以之而屏翰一國非徒永
帶礪之盟已也而咸宜於其君焉以謹侯度以
揚王休一自敬美者出之周其世有顯諸侯乎
以之而君臨萬邦非徒膺曆數之傳已也而咸
宜於其王焉以建皇極以端元良一自敬美者
出之周其世有明天子乎至是則令顯之德自
今日而衍其休民人之宜垂萬世而永其烈天
之保右申命也不徒在吾王而且及其子孫矣
===
所謂干祿百福者孰加於此抑論周家王業之
興雖一德爲之本而周官之法度盡善盡美又
可守之萬世無斁者此則有家法以貽子孫固
宜其開有道之長也詩人福君既願其子孫之
敬美而必終之以率由舊章豈非欲其以敬法
祖而爲祈天永命之本歟彼後之人臣導其君
以祖宗不足法者抑獨何哉
敷時繹思我徂維求定時周之命
punctuated:
皆穆穆而敬，寅畏中存，儼乎緝熙執競之遺矩；帝王世濟其美者也，皆皇皇而美，精純內蘊，宛乎徽柔於皇之懿範。以之而屏翰一國，非徒永帶礪之盟已也，而咸宜於其君焉，以謹侯度，以揚王休，一自敬美者出之，周其世有顯諸侯乎！以之而君臨萬邦，非徒膺曆數之傳已也，而咸宜於其王焉，以建皇極，以端元良，一自敬美者出之，周其世有明天子乎！至是，則令顯之德自今日而衍其休，民人之宜垂萬世而永其烈，天之保右申命也，不徒在吾王，而且及其子孫矣。所謂干祿百福者，孰加於此？抑論周家王業之興，雖一德爲之本，而周官之法度盡善盡美，又可守之萬世無斁者。此則有家法以貽子孫，固宜其開有道之長也。詩人福君，既願其子孫之敬美，而必終之以率由舊章，豈非欲其以敬法祖，而爲祈天永命之本歟？彼後之人臣，導其君以祖宗不足法者，抑獨何哉！

敷時繹思，我徂維求定，時周之命。
translation_en:
…may they all be deeply solemn and reverent, preserving awe and respect within, truly embodying the inherited standards of continuous brightness and steadfast vigor; emperors and kings bring their excellence to perfection from generation to generation—may they all be splendid and admirable, harboring pure refinement within, vividly reflecting the exemplary models of gentle virtue and august majesty. When by these qualities they serve as the screen and bulwark of a state, they do not merely perpetuate the covenant of the girdle and the whetstone, but are all well suited to be lords—carefully observing the regulations of feudal princes and exalting the royal grace. All this issues from their reverence and excellence; shall Zhou not have illustrious feudal lords for generations to come! When by these qualities they rule over the myriad states, they do not merely receive the transmission of the Heaven-ordained succession, but are all well suited to be kings—establishing the supreme standard of royal perfection and rectifying the great goodness. All this issues from their reverence and excellence; shall Zhou not have enlightened Sons of Heaven for generations to come! Reaching this point, the admirable and illustrious virtue will extend its blessings from this day forward, what is fitting for the common people and the officers will hand down its meritorious achievements to ten thousand generations, and Heaven's protection, assistance, and repeated mandate will rest not merely upon our king, but will also reach his sons and grandsons. As for what is called seeking emolument and a hundred blessings, what could surpass this? Yet if we discuss the rise of the royal enterprise of the House of Zhou, although unified virtue served as its foundation, the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou were utterly good and utterly fine, such that they could be maintained for ten thousand generations without weariness. Having such family laws to bequeath to their descendants, it was certainly fitting that they inaugurated a long-lasting reign of the Way. When the poet wished blessings upon his ruler, having prayed that his sons and grandsons be reverent and admirable, he necessarily concluded with "following the old statutes"—was this not a desire that they should emulate their ancestors with reverence, making this the foundation for praying to Heaven for a perpetual mandate? As for those ministers of later ages who misled their rulers by claiming that the ancestors were not worth emulating—why on earth did they do so!

"We spread abroad this cherished thought, and go forth only to seek stability; this is the mandate of Zhou."

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
黃學皐
同考試官訓導周　批　繹前功而布新命武王計
安天下盛心是作能發之詞旨溫剴讀之如對周人語也
考試官敎諭倫　批　典暢精融迥異他作
考試官敎諭龔　批　沉鬯豐腴
周王敘分封圖治之意而表其爲新命也蓋封
建者帝王之所以計安天下也周王以之其命
不維新乎頌大賚者曰帝王受命而興所丕承
者先德所利賴者功臣凡以爲天下計也今我
===
之大封何如哉彼開天下以一統之業者文王
勤止之功也所可繹思也貽天下以萬世之安
者亦文王勤止之心也所當仰體也我以世
澤之在人者不能忘而布之爲大賚之典先烈
之垂後者可深念而公之爲懋賞之仁文王所
遺之土宇吾不敢私也而與有功者共理焉藩
屛之衆建維往求邦國之敉寧務使旣集之業
永綏於底定斯已矣文王所遺之人民吾不敢
專也而與有功者共治焉侯封之廣樹維往求
punctuated:
黃學皐。
同考試官訓導周批：繹前功而布新命，武王計安天下盛心，是作能發之。詞旨溫剴，讀之如對周人語也。
考試官敎諭倫批：典暢精融，迥異他作。
考試官敎諭龔批：沉鬯豐腴。

周王敘分封圖治之意，而表其爲新命也。蓋封建者，帝王之所以計安天下也。周王以之，其命不維新乎？頌《大賚》者曰：帝王受命而興，所丕承者先德，所利賴者功臣，凡以爲天下計也。今我之大封何如哉？彼開天下以一統之業者，文王勤止之功也，所可繹思也；貽天下以萬世之安者，亦文王勤止之心也，所當仰體也。我以世澤之在人者不能忘，而布之爲大賚之典；先烈之垂後者可深念，而公之爲懋賞之仁。文王所遺之土宇，吾不敢私也，而與有功者共理焉。藩屛之衆建，維往求邦國之敉寧，務使旣集之業，永綏於底定斯已矣。文王所遺之人民，吾不敢專也，而與有功者共治焉。侯封之廣樹，維往求…
translation_en:
Huang Xuegao 黃學皐.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhou 周: Pondering past achievements and proclaiming the new mandate—this essay successfully brings out King Wu's grand intention of planning for the peace of the realm. Its diction and purport are gentle yet incisive; reading it is like conversing with a person of the Zhou dynasty.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫: Classical, fluent, refined, and harmonious; vastly different from other compositions.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Gong 龔: Deeply fluent and richly abundant.

The King of Zhou recounts the intention of enfeoffing territories to plan for good governance, and manifests it as the new Mandate. Indeed, the establishment of feudal domains is the means by which emperors and kings plan for the peace of the realm. When the King of Zhou employs this, is the Mandate not thereby renewed? The one who composed the hymn "Great Bestowal" (Lai 賚) speaks to this effect: When emperors and kings receive the Mandate and rise, what they grandly inherit is the virtue of their ancestors, and whom they rely upon are their meritorious ministers—all in order to plan for the realm. Now, how does our great enfeoffment proceed? That which opened up the enterprise of grand unification for the realm was the achievement of King Wen's tireless diligence—something that should be pondered at length. That which bequeathed ten thousand generations of peace to the realm was likewise the heart of King Wen's tireless diligence—something that ought to be reverently embodied. Because the generational blessings remaining among the people cannot be forgotten, I spread them forth as the statute of great bestowal; because the ancestral merits handed down to posterity are worthy of deep reflection, I share them publicly as the benevolence of generous reward. The territories left behind by King Wen, I dare not keep as my private possession, but administer them together with those of merit. In establishing numerous feudatories as screens and bulwarks, we go forth only to seek the pacification of the states, striving solely to ensure that the enterprise already accomplished is forever secured in settled stability. The people left behind by King Wen, I dare not monopolize for myself, but govern them together with those of merit. In broadly planting the fiefs of the marquises, we go forth only to seek…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
黎庶之乂安務使已附之衆永臻於克定斯已
矣以之酬勳即以之保泰煥然昭代之王章以
之班爵即以之求寧赫然更始之令典天以右
序命我周令我之肇舉乎分封者正以體天之
心也典制頒而天下一新其耳目非復由商之
舊矣文以新命造我周令我之創行乎大封者
正以顯文之謨也皇度彰而天下一易其心志
非復襲殷之故矣時哉我周之命也爾諸臣其
尚念之吁文王有創業垂統之功而武王爲乂
===
安長治之計此二后之所以竝可頌也抑論周
業之興自三后肇基至武王而大定然猶衆建
諸侯以爲萬世治安計信乎公天下之大端大
本莫封建若也後世治不師古裂封建而郡縣
之乃爲之說者曰封建非聖人意也其未知求
定之旨
春秋
秋公會宋人齊人伐徐莊公二十有六年
趙儒
punctuated:
黎庶之乂安，務使已附之衆永臻於克定斯已矣。以之酬勳，即以之保泰，煥然昭代之王章；以之班爵，即以之求寧，赫然更始之令典。天以右序命我周，令我之肇舉乎分封者，正以體天之心也。典制頒而天下一新其耳目，非復由商之舊矣。文以新命造我周，令我之創行乎大封者，正以顯文之謨也。皇度彰而天下一易其心志，非復襲殷之故矣。時哉我周之命也，爾諸臣其尚念之！吁！文王有創業垂統之功，而武王爲乂安長治之計，此二后之所以竝可頌也。抑論周業之興，自三后肇基，至武王而大定，然猶衆建諸侯，以爲萬世治安計。信乎公天下之大端大本，莫封建若也。後世治不師古，裂封建而郡縣之，乃爲之說者曰：「封建非聖人意也。」其未知求定之旨。

春秋
秋，公會宋人、齊人伐徐。（莊公二十有六年）
趙儒
translation_en:
… the peace and security of the common people, ensuring only that the multitudes who have already submitted forever attain settled stability, and nothing more. To use this to reward merit is thereby to preserve great peace—resplendent are the royal statutes of an illustrious era; to use this to distribute ranks of nobility is thereby to seek tranquility—glorious are the fine canons of a new beginning. Heaven, by honoring the rightful succession, gave the Mandate to our Zhou, and my initiating this enfeoffment now is precisely to embody the mind of Heaven. When institutional statutes are promulgated, the eyes and ears of the world are completely renewed, no longer following the old ways of Shang. King Wen, through the new Mandate, founded our Zhou, and my inaugurating this grand enfeoffment now is precisely to manifest the plans of King Wen. When sovereign measures are displayed, the hearts and minds of the world are completely transformed, no longer inheriting the former practices of Yin. Timely indeed is the Mandate of our Zhou! May all you ministers ever bear it in mind!

Alas! King Wen had the merit of founding the enterprise and bequeathing the royal line, while King Wu devised plans for peace, security, and enduring governance—this is why both sovereigns are equally worthy of praise. Moreover, if we consider the rise of the Zhou enterprise, from the time the Three Sovereigns laid the foundation down to King Wu, when it was greatly settled, he nevertheless established numerous feudal lords in order to plan for ten thousand generations of peace and order. Truly, as the great principle and fundamental basis for treating the realm as public, nothing compares to the feudal system (fengjian). In later ages, governance did not take antiquity as its teacher; they tore apart the feudal system and turned it into commanderies and counties. Yet those who made excuses for this said, "The feudal system was not the intention of the sages." Surely they did not understand the meaning of "seeking stability"!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In autumn, the Duke met with a man of Song and a man of Qi to attack Xu." (26th year of Duke Zhuang)

By Zhao Ru 趙儒

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導靳　批　矩度森嚴詞彩鮮麗且能
緣正出奇若將旗鼓稱節制之兵矣取之
考試官教諭倫　批　調古氣舒麟經擅美
考試官教諭譙　批　整練不浮
春秋紀望國之用兵見其無可危之道焉天師
老勢孤兵家之大戒也魯之伐徐能不蹈此則
安得而危之嘗聞徐戎合黨兵連曲阜之墟表
裏爲讎世稔東郊之患莊公連齊宋以會伐焉
我武既揚振旅言歸春秋宜以伐至矣而今獨
===
不書至何哉蓋聞至之者幸之也幸之者危之
也向使徐之伐也師困於久淹莊之行也勢衰
於寡助則春秋得不爲之危乎維兹以秋而伐
卽以秋而返而荷戈閫外者無東山杕杜之懷
也會齊以往復會宋以俱而授甲師中者多有
邦厥隣之助也出則張我魯之威歸則節我軍
之力師貴以律莊其有焉以此行兵而何潰散
之足虞乎伐以除門庭之難會以資犄角之勢
謀貴萬全莊其有焉以此制敵而何撓敗之足
punctuated:
同考試官訓導靳批：矩度森嚴，詞彩鮮麗，且能緣正出奇，若將旗鼓，稱節制之兵矣。取之。
考試官教諭倫批：調古氣舒，麟經擅美。
考試官教諭譙批：整練不浮。

《春秋》紀望國之用兵，見其無可危之道焉。天師老勢孤，兵家之大戒也，魯之伐徐，能不蹈此，則安得而危之？嘗聞徐、戎合黨，兵連曲阜之墟；表裏爲讎，世稔東郊之患。莊公連齊、宋以會伐焉，我武既揚，振旅言歸，《春秋》宜以「伐至」矣，而今獨不書「至」，何哉？蓋聞「至」之者，幸之也；幸之者，危之也。向使徐之伐也，師困於久淹；莊之行也，勢衰於寡助，則《春秋》得不爲之危乎？維兹以秋而伐，卽以秋而返，而荷戈閫外者，無《東山》、《杕杜》之懷也；會齊以往，復會宋以俱，而授甲師中者，多有邦厥隣之助也。出則張我魯之威，歸則節我軍之力，師貴以律，莊其有焉，以此行兵，而何潰散之足虞乎？伐以除門庭之難，會以資犄角之勢，謀貴萬全，莊其有焉，以此制敵，而何撓敗之足
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Jin comments: "Its framework and standards are strictly disciplined, and its diction and style are fresh and splendid. Moreover, it is able to generate the extraordinary out of the orthodox; like commanding banners and drums, it may be called a well-regulated army. Selected."
Examiner and Instructor Lun comments: "The tone is ancient and thevital breath relaxed; it excels in the mastery of the Unicorn Classic [Spring and Autumn Annals]."
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: "Well-ordered and practiced, without superficiality."

When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the deployment of troops by a prestigious state, it shows that there was no way in which it could be considered endangered. Now [reading 天 as 夫], an exhausted army and an isolated position are the great taboos of military strategists; if Lu, in its campaign against Xu, was able to avoid treading this path, how could one regard it as endangered? We have heard that the Xu and the Rong formed a confederacy, bringing warfare straight to the mounds of Qufu; acting in collusion inside and out as enemies, for generations they fostered disaster in our eastern outskirts. Duke Zhuang allied with Qi and Song to join in a punitive expedition against them. Once our martial prowess had been displayed and we ordered our troops to return home, the Spring and Autumn Annals ought to have recorded his arrival from the campaign—yet here alone it does not record "arrived." Why is that? It is because recording "arrived" expresses relief at fortunate survival, and expressing relief implies that there was danger. Suppose that in the campaign against Xu the army had been exhausted by prolonged delay, or that in Duke Zhuang's expedition his position had been weakened by a lack of allies—how then could the Spring and Autumn Annals not have regarded him as endangered? Yet in this instance, he set out on the campaign in autumn and returned in that very same autumn, so those bearing halberds beyond the frontier gates had no occasion for the longing of the poems "Eastern Hills" (Dongshan) or "Solitary Russet Pear" (Didu). He met with Qi to go forth, and further met with Song to proceed together, so those issued armor within the ranks enjoyed the abundant assistance of friendly states and neighbors. In going forth, he extended the majesty of our state of Lu; in returning, he conserved the strength of our forces. An army values discipline, and Duke Zhuang possessed it; marching troops in this manner, what fear could there be of rout and dispersion? He launched the campaign to eliminate a crisis at his very courtyard gates, and he formed an alliance to avail himself of the momentum of mutual pincer support. Strategy values complete thoroughness, and Duke Zhuang possessed it; subduing the enemy in this manner, what [fear] could there be of defeat and setback…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
患乎噫此一伐也昔嘗歷三時而後還君子以
爲殆矣今之役則非昔日所可同者師貞之吉
雖桓文之節制何加焉此一莊也往嘗提孤軍
而深入君子以爲危矣今之行則非往日所可
例者預定之策雖庸蜀之遠連曷過焉故春秋
謂是役也人無怨心師有同力武之善經也全
軍歸國則維其常而何以書至爲哉不然則前
此之伐戎春秋嘗紀其至矣而於今也奚以異
觀此可以知行兵之法矣雖然伐徐之年非卽
===
伐戎之歲乎春出夏歸秋而又復出是魯師無
一暇日也齊人同會亦尨合之衆耳萬一資糧
扉屨之不備而厚誅於我是徐夷起於轂下而
戎兵接軫也不見執轅濤塗乎是故兵者聖人
所甚重毋謂其無危而輕出也
晉欒書帥師救鄭成公六年夏曹公孫會
自鄸出奔宋昭公二十年
滕如蛟
同考試官訓導靳批尚功崇賢春秋厚道子能
punctuated:
患乎？噫！此一伐也，昔嘗歷三時而後還，君子以爲殆矣；今之役，則非昔日所可同者，師貞之吉，雖桓、文之節制何加焉！此一莊也，往嘗提孤軍而深入，君子以爲危矣；今之行，則非往日所可例者，預定之策，雖庸、蜀之遠連曷過焉！故《春秋》謂是役也，人無怨心，師有同力，武之善經也。全軍歸國，則維其常，而何以書至爲哉？不然，則前此之伐戎，《春秋》嘗紀其至矣，而於今也奚以異？觀此可以知行兵之法矣。雖然，伐徐之年，非卽伐戎之歲乎？春出夏歸，秋而又復出，是魯師無一暇日也。齊人同會，亦尨合之衆耳。萬一資糧扉屨之不備，而厚誅於我，是徐夷起於轂下，而戎兵接軫也。不見執轅濤塗乎？是故兵者，聖人所甚重，毋謂其無危而輕出也。

「晉欒書帥師救鄭」〔成公六年〕、「夏曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋」〔昭公二十年〕
滕如蛟
同考試官訓導靳批：尚功崇賢，《春秋》厚道。子能
translation_en:
…be worried about? Alas! As for such a punitive expedition, in the past the army once went through three seasons before returning, which the gentleman considered perilous; the present campaign, however, cannot be equated with past days—with the auspiciousness of a righteous army, even the disciplined command of Dukes Huan and Wen could not surpass it! As for this same Duke Zhuang, in the past he once led a lone force deep into enemy territory, which the gentleman considered dangerous; the present march, however, cannot be judged by the precedent of bygone days—with pre-arranged strategy, even the distant alliance of Yong and Shu could not exceed it! Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals considered that in this campaign the men harbored no resentment and the troops shared a united strength, which is the fine principle of military affairs. Returning to the state with the entire army intact was thus only the norm, so why record his arrival? Otherwise, in the earlier campaign against the Rong, the Spring and Autumn Annals did record his arrival; why then does it differ now? Observing this, one can understand the art of conducting military operations. Even so, was the year of the expedition against Xu not the very same year as the expedition against the Rong? Setting out in spring, returning in summer, and setting out once again in autumn—this meant the troops of Lu did not have a single day of rest. The men of Qi who joined the assembly were also merely a motley crowd. If by chance provisions and straw sandals had been unprepared and they had made heavy demands upon us, it would have been as if the Xu barbarians had risen right beneath our chariot wheels and Rong troops were following right on our tracks. Have you not seen the seizure of Yuan Taotu? Therefore, military action is something the sage takes most seriously; do not say there is no danger and lightly send troops forth.

"Luan Shu of Jin led a force to rescue Zheng" [6th year of Duke Cheng]; "In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song" [20th year of Duke Zhao].
By Teng Rujiao.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Jin comments: Esteeming merit and honoring the worthy is the generous way of the Spring and Autumn Annals. You are able to…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
推原而奬敘之而旨遠詞文尤稱奇品
考試官教諭倫　批　嚴峻中有博雅氣象
考試官教諭譙　批　開闔得法組織尤精
春秋紀事嘉世勳而重賢裔焉勳臣者國之輔
賢臣者國之紀也錄其後以示勸春秋義與且
夫故國恒稱乎世臣用人必貴於公選若宋之
華孫藉寵專行春秋無取焉然不曰晉有欒書
者典兵三世而光榮不墜乎曰欒氏之胄不以
世而以勳也彼書之先有欒枝與盾者曳柴僞
===
遁効力於城濮之師固壘深溝宣猷於令狐之
役其功有足稱矣績載旂常而緒垂奕葉苟無
失德猶當百世祀之况有賢如書者可俾之無
位耶令書也從三卿而主善不遷戮以罷民出
有制闔之勞内昭繩武之烈枝盾之勳得書而
有光矣使書也怙寵而擅權晉人廢之不暇誰
能與之又不曰曹有公孫會者鎮國再世而爵
籍未泯乎曰公孫之胄不以世而以賢也彼會
之先有公子喜時者守節逃榮義激於君執之
punctuated:
推原而奬敘之，而旨遠詞文，尤稱奇品。
考試官教諭倫批：嚴峻中有博雅氣象。
考試官教諭譙批：開闔得法，組織尤精。
《春秋》紀事，嘉世勳而重賢裔焉。勳臣者，國之輔；賢臣者，國之紀也。錄其後以示勸，《春秋》義與？且夫故國恒稱乎世臣，用人必貴於公選。若宋之華孫，藉寵專行，《春秋》無取焉。然不曰晉有欒書者，典兵三世而光榮不墜乎？曰：欒氏之胄，不以世而以勳也。彼書之先有欒枝與盾者，曳柴僞遁，効力於城濮之師；固壘深溝，宣猷於令狐之役，其功有足稱矣。績載旂常，而緒垂奕葉，苟無失德，猶當百世祀之，况有賢如書者，可俾之無位耶？令書也，從三卿而主善，不遷戮以罷民，出有制閫之勞，内昭繩武之烈，枝、盾之勳，得書而有光矣。使書也怙寵而擅權，晉人廢之不暇，誰能與之？又不曰曹有公孫會者，鎮國再世而爵籍未泯乎？曰：公孫之胄，不以世而以賢也。彼會之先有公子喜時者，守節逃榮，義激於君執之
translation_en:
… traces this back to its origins and sets it forth with praise; with its far-reaching import and refined diction, it may especially be called a rare piece.

Examiner and Instructor Lun comments: Amid its strict severity there is an air of broad learning and elegance.

Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: The opening and closing follow proper method, and the structure is especially fine.

In recording events, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) commends hereditary merit and esteems the descendants of the worthy. Meritorious ministers are the bulwark of the state; worthy ministers are the mainstay of the state. Recording their descendants in order to demonstrate encouragement—is this not the righteous principle of the Annals? Moreover, an ancient state is always recognized by its hereditary ministers, yet in employing men one must value impartial selection. Take someone like Huasun of Song, who relied on favor to act arbitrarily—the Annals found nothing to approve in him. Yet does it not say that Jin had Luan Shu, whose family commanded the army for three generations without their glory falling into decline? I say: the descendants of the Luan clan were recorded not on account of hereditary status, but on account of merit. Before Shu, there were Luan Zhi and Luan Dun: one dragged brushwood in a feigned retreat, exerting his strength in the campaign at Chengpu; the other fortified ramparts and deepened trenches, displaying his strategy in the battle of Linghu. Their achievements were well worthy of praise! With their deeds inscribed on the royal banners and their lineage handed down through successive generations, so long as they did not lose their virtue, they ought still to have received sacrifices for a hundred generations—how much more, when there was someone as worthy as Shu, could he be left without office? Now as for Shu [reading 令 as 今], he followed the three ministers in taking goodness as his guide, and did not shift punishment onto an exhausted populace; abroad he bore the toil of commanding on the frontier, and at home he shone forth the illustrious legacy of following in his ancestors' footsteps. The merit of Zhi and Dun gained luster through Shu! Had Shu presumed upon favor and usurped authority, the people of Jin would scarcely have had time enough to depose him—who would have approved of him? And does it not also say that Cao had Gongsun Hui, whose family stabilized the state for two generations with its noble rank and register still unextinguished? I say: the descendants of the Gongsun were recorded not on account of hereditary status, but on account of worthiness. Before Hui, there was Prince Xishi (Zizang), who maintained his integrity and fled from glory, his righteousness stirred on the day his ruler was seized…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
日全身致邑名高於國亂之時其節有足尚矣
祚庇後昆而義風百世苟無墜緒猶當十世宥
之況有賢如會者可使之喪位耶今會也放逐
而待命於郊流離而不失其正内無懟主之嫌
遠光讓國之節子臧之義以會而不替矣使會
也凌德而悖道曹人逐之恐後誰其憫之要之
有欒氏之功而後可爲世臣有子臧之賢而後
可膺世爵彼華孫者逆臣之裔視書與會何如
者可委以兵權使之專行不忌耶抑嘗聞鯀殛
===
而禹興蔡叔流而仲以祇德顯聖賢固不繫於
世類也曹會既奔之後不聞代興欒黶不克負
荷而三世之勳遂殞亦何取於功臣之冑哉是
故官人之法惟其人不惟其類
禮記
四者君以正用之故君者立於無過之地
也
楊先春
同考試官訓導董 批 此題作者類多牽綴是篇
punctuated:
日，全身致邑，名高於國亂之時，其節有足尚矣。祚庇後昆而義風百世，苟無墜緒，猶當十世宥之，況有賢如會者，可使之喪位耶？今會也，放逐而待命於郊，流離而不失其正，内無懟主之嫌，遠光讓國之節，子臧之義以會而不替矣。使會也凌德而悖道，曹人逐之恐後，誰其憫之？要之，有欒氏之功而後可爲世臣，有子臧之賢而後可膺世爵。彼華孫者，逆臣之裔，視書與會何如者，可委以兵權，使之專行不忌耶？抑嘗聞鯀殛而禹興，蔡叔流而仲以祇德顯，聖賢固不繫於世類也。曹會既奔之後，不聞代興，欒黶不克負荷，而三世之勳遂殞，亦何取於功臣之冑哉？是故官人之法，惟其人不惟其類。

禮記
四者，君以正用之，故君者立於無過之地也。
楊先春
同考試官訓導董批：此題作者類多牽綴，是篇
translation_en:
…the day [his lord was captured], and preserved his person while relinquishing his fief, his reputation stood high in a time of national turmoil; his integrity is truly worthy of esteem! His blessings sheltered his descendants and his righteousness inspired a hundred generations. As long as they did not ruin their heritage, they ought to be pardoned for ten generations—how much more so when there was someone as worthy as Gongsun Hui 公孫會! Could he be made to lose his position? Now, when Hui was banished, he awaited orders in the suburbs; though cast adrift, he did not lose his rectitude. Internally, he bore no suspicion of resenting his ruler, and across the generations he brought glory to the integrity of yielding the state; through Hui, the righteousness of Zizang 子臧 did not decline. Had Hui transgressed virtue and violated the Way, the people of Cao 曹 would have feared being too slow to drive him out—who would have pitied him? In sum, only when there is the merit of the Luan 欒 clan can one become a hereditary minister, and only when there is the worthiness of Zizang can one receive a hereditary peerage. As for that Huasun 華孫, the descendant of a traitorous minister, how does he compare with Luan Shu 欒書 and Gongsun Hui, that he could be entrusted with military authority and allowed to act unilaterally without restraint? Moreover, I have heard that Gun 鯀 was executed yet Yu 禹 rose to prominence, and Caishu 蔡叔 was exiled yet Cai Zhong 蔡仲 became illustrious through his reverent virtue; sages and worthies are certainly not bound by hereditary lineage. After Hui of Cao fled into exile, no successor was heard to arise, and because Luan Yan 欒黶 was unable to bear the burden of his heritage, the merit of three generations consequently perished—what, then, is there to value in the scions of meritorious ministers? Therefore, the method of appointing men to office depends solely on the individual, not on his lineage.

Record of Rites (Liji 禮記)
"These four things, the ruler employs with rectitude; therefore, the ruler stands in a place free from fault."
Yang Xianchun 楊先春
Comment by Associate Examiner Dong 董, Assistant Instructor: Writers on this topic generally tend to piece things together awkwardly, whereas this essay…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
只從本色中指點出來精神態度種種迥別
考試官教諭倫　批　發端本賛化意明徹可愛
考試官教諭譙　批　詞藻郁然
記者推人君賛化之道而端本爲要焉蓋君身
萬化之本也舉天地父師而正用之非立於無
過烏能然哉今夫人君承天地之統據父師之
尊其道至正而其本在身是故天生時地生財
父師則以養以教者也四者皆聯屬於君身而
惟君所用之然用不以正則亦不爲吾之用矣
===
君人將以其身爲天下用必正其身以用天下
以成天地之能本皇極之攸建者以化裁之爲
明時爲阜財而覆載之有偏者吾取而兼用之
用於吾之正也以終父師之功本元良之克端
者以左右之爲厚生爲正德而生成之未全者
吾取而咸用之亦用於吾之正也故君者匪徒
立乎崇高之位已也三極之用備於身必納此
身於軌物之中不徒立乎兆庶之上已也萬化
之原起於身務範其身於中正之域天地以正
punctuated:
只從本色中指點出來，精神態度，種種迥別。
考試官教諭倫　批：發端本賛化意，明徹可愛。
考試官教諭譙　批：詞藻郁然。

記者推人君賛化之道，而端本爲要焉。蓋君身，萬化之本也。舉天地父師而正用之，非立於無過，烏能然哉？今夫人君承天地之統，據父師之尊，其道至正，而其本在身。是故天生時，地生財，父師則以養以教者也。四者皆聯屬於君身，而惟君所用之。然用不以正，則亦不爲吾之用矣。君人將以其身爲天下用，必正其身以用天下。以成天地之能，本皇極之攸建者以化裁之，爲明時、爲阜財，而覆載之有偏者，吾取而兼用之，用於吾之正也；以終父師之功，本元良之克端者以左右之，爲厚生、爲正德，而生成之未全者，吾取而咸用之，亦用於吾之正也。故君者，匪徒立乎崇高之位已也，三極之用備於身，必納此身於軌物之中；不徒立乎兆庶之上已也，萬化之原起於身，務範其身於中正之域。天地以正
translation_en:
… simply points it out from the intrinsic meaning of the text; in spirit and bearing, every aspect is distinctly different.
Examiner and Instructor Lun comments: The opening is grounded in the idea of assisting the transforming power of nature, clear, penetrating, and admirable.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: Richly elegant in diction.

The chronicler traces the ruler's Way of assisting the transforming power of nature, taking the rectification of the fundamental as essential. For the person of the ruler is the foundation of the myriad transformations. To take up Heaven, Earth, parent, and teacher and employ them with rectitude—if he did not stand in a position free of transgression, how could he do so? Now, the ruler inherits the succession of Heaven and Earth and occupies the exalted station of parent and teacher; his Way is supremely upright, and its foundation lies in his own person. Therefore, Heaven produces the seasons, Earth produces wealth, and parent and teacher are those who nourish and instruct. All four are joined to the person of the ruler, and it is solely for the ruler to employ them. Yet if he does not employ them with rectitude, they will not serve his use. When one who rules over men would make his own person of service to the world, he must rectify his own person in order to employ the world. To bring to completion the capacities of Heaven and Earth, he grounds himself in the establishment of the Supreme Ultimate so as to transform and regulate them—clarifying the seasons and making wealth abundant; and where the canopy of Heaven and the support of Earth have any partiality, I take them up and employ them together, employing them through my own rectitude. To bring to consummation the achievements of parent and teacher, he grounds himself in the uprightness of the supreme goodness so as to assist and guide them—enriching livelihood and rectifying virtue; and where generation and completion are not yet whole, I take them up and employ them all, likewise employing them through my own rectitude. Therefore, the ruler does not merely stand in an exalted position and nothing more; the functions of the Three Ultimates are complete within his person, so he must place this person within the bounds of regular norms. He does not merely stand above the millions of common people and nothing more; the source of the myriad transformations arises from his person, so he must mold his person within the realm of centrality and rectitude. When Heaven and Earth are employed with rectitude…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
用卽寡過於身君德猶未純也其所置身者必
於無偏無黨之地焉蓋所立正而後所用正合
天地之用而善用之者此也父師以正用卽補
過於身君道猶未先也其所安身者必於無反
無側之地焉蓋立無過斯用無不正聯父師之
用而咸用之者此也苟以有過之身爲四者之
用奚其正蓋君之於民有天地之尊有父師之
親故君之立身必建之而不悖俯之而不怍所
用者四所以用者一正而已矣然是正也天地
===
之道也父之生師之教皆是物也顧人君中天
地爲綱常主所用者甚大所立者尤宜愼記者
舉而歸之正推君道合天道也然務學要矣親
賢急焉君天下者愼諸
詩言其志也歌咏其聲也舞動其容也三
者本於心然後樂器從之
趙　捷
同考試官訓導董　批
鑄意摛詞精融俊爽文之
有雅趣者擲之作金石聲矣用式多士
punctuated:
用。卽寡過於身，君德猶未純也；其所置身者，必於無偏無黨之地焉。蓋所立正而後所用正，合天地之用而善用之者，此也。父師以正用，卽補過於身，君道猶未先也；其所安身者，必於無反無側之地焉。蓋立無過斯用無不正，聯父師之用而咸用之者，此也。苟以有過之身爲四者之用，奚其正？蓋君之於民，有天地之尊，有父師之親；故君之立身，必建之而不悖，俯之而不怍。所用者四，所以用者，一正而已矣。然是正也，天地之道也；父之生、師之教，皆是物也。顧人君中天地、爲綱常主，所用者甚大，所立者尤宜愼。記者舉而歸之正，推君道合天道也。然務學要矣，親賢急焉，君天下者愼諸！
「詩，言其志也；歌，咏其聲也；舞，動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。」
趙捷
同考試官訓導董　批：鑄意摛詞，精融俊爽，文之有雅趣者。擲之作金石聲矣，用式多士。
translation_en:
… function through uprightness. Even if he merely lessens faults in his own person, the sovereign's virtue is still not pure; the place where he positions himself must be entirely without partiality or partisanship. For only when where he stands is upright will what he employs be upright; this is what it means to unite the functions of Heaven and Earth and employ them well. A father and a teacher function through uprightness. Even if he merely mends faults in his own person, the Way of the sovereign still does not take precedence; the place where he rests himself must be entirely without perversity or crookedness. For when one stands without fault, one's functioning is never not upright; this is what it means to join the functions of father and teacher and employ them all. If one were to use a fault-ridden person to carry out the functions of these four, how could that be upright? Indeed, in his relation to the people, the ruler possesses the venerability of Heaven and Earth and the intimacy of father and teacher. Therefore, in establishing himself, the ruler must set up his standard without contradiction and look down without shame. What he employs are four, yet that by which he employs them is simply one thing: uprightness. Yet this uprightness is the Way of Heaven and Earth; the life given by the father and the instruction given by the teacher are both this very thing. Considering that the sovereign stands in the center between Heaven and Earth as the master of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues, what he employs is عظیم (exceedingly great), and how he establishes himself ought especially to be guarded with care. The recorder of the text raises these and归 (traces them back to) uprightness, extending the Way of the ruler to accord with the Way of Heaven. Yet devoting oneself to learning is essential, and drawing close to the worthy is urgent—let him who rules All under Heaven be cautious in this!

"Poetry expresses the intent; singing prolongs the voice; dance animates the bearing. All three originate in the mind, and only then do the musical instruments follow them."
Zhao Jie 趙捷
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Dong 董, comments: Molding ideas and spreading forth words with refined harmony and brisk vigor—this is writing of elegant taste. Cast it down and it rings with the sound of metal and stone! It serves as a model for the multitude of scholars.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭倫　批　語意婉足神彩媚人
考試官教諭譙　批　義精詞朗
記者論樂而推其所本焉夫心樂之本也本諸
心而器從之此樂之所以爲華也記樂者蓋謂
德蘊於心樂被於器其機常相通而其本自有
在也所謂樂爲德之華者何哉彼播之詩歌形
之舞蹈皆樂也是未涉於器者也詩何爲也志
動於中機不容默而詩也者則言其欲言之志
也歌何爲也言不盡志言因以永而歌也者則
===
永其未竟之聲也舞何以動也歌而成聲即動
而成象舞蹈之發一德容之動也夫由詩而歌
而舞其愈發而愈暢者是樂之華也由容而聲
而志其愈約而愈精者皆心之運也是三者本
於心也涵之爲聲氣之元淵然深矣然後假善
鳴者以鳴焉而金石從之所以合兩階而交應
者皆是心之流通奕而爲文者也蘊之爲性天
之妙盎然融矣然後假有聲者以聲焉而絲竹
從之所以比五色而成文者皆是心之和動昭
punctuated:
考試官教諭倫批：「語意婉足，神彩媚人。」
考試官教諭譙批：「義精詞朗。」
記者論樂，而推其所本焉。夫心，樂之本也。本諸心而器從之，此樂之所以爲華也。記樂者蓋謂：德蘊於心，樂被於器，其機常相通，而其本自有在也。所謂「樂爲德之華」者，何哉？彼播之詩歌，形之舞蹈，皆樂也，是未涉於器者也。詩何爲也？志動於中，機不容默，而詩也者，則言其欲言之志也。歌何爲也？言不盡志，言因以永，而歌也者，則永其未竟之聲也。舞何以動也？歌而成聲，即動而成象，舞蹈之發，一德容之動也。夫由詩而歌而舞，其愈發而愈暢者，是樂之華也；由容而聲而志，其愈約而愈精者，皆心之運也。是三者本於心也。涵之爲聲氣之元，淵然深矣，然後假善鳴者以鳴焉，而金石從之，所以合兩階而交應者，皆是心之流通，奕而爲文者也；蘊之爲性天之妙，盎然融矣，然後假有聲者以聲焉，而絲竹從之，所以比五色而成文者，皆是心之和動，昭
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Lun 倫 comments: "The expression and meaning are graceful and complete; its spirit and brilliance are captivating."
Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Qiao 譙 comments: "The meaning is refined and the diction clear."
The author of the Record discusses music and traces it to its root. Now, the mind is the root of music. When it is rooted in the mind and the instruments follow it, this is how music becomes the efflorescence. The author of the "Record of Music" (Yueji) means to say: Virtue is stored within the mind, and music is imparted to instruments; their subtle springs constantly communicate with each other, yet its root naturally has its own abode. What is meant by saying that "music is the efflorescence of virtue"? That which is broadcast in poetry and song and given form in dance is all music, even before it involves instruments. What is poetry for? When intent is stirred within, its impulse cannot remain silent; thus poetry speaks the intent that desires to be spoken. What is song for? When words do not fully exhaust the intent, the words are consequently prolonged; thus song prolongs the unexhausted sounds. Why does dance move? Once sung to form sound, it immediately moves to form figures; the expression of dance is entirely the movement of virtuous demeanor. Now, proceeding from poetry to song and to dance, the more it is expressed, the more freely it flows—this is the efflorescence of music. Proceeding back from demeanor to sound and to intent, the more it is condensed, the more essential it becomes—all this is the operation of the mind. Thus these three are rooted in the mind. Cherished within as the primal source of sound and breath, it is abyssally deep; only then does it borrow things good at sounding to make them sound, and metal and stone follow it. Thus, that by which it harmonizes the two staircases of dancers and answers back and forth is entirely the flowing circulation of this mind, shining forth to become pattern. Stored within as the marvel of inborn nature and Heaven, it is brimmingly harmonious; only then does it borrow things possessing sound to give them voice, and silk and bamboo follow it. Thus, that by which it matches the five colors to form pattern is entirely the harmonious movement of this mind, manifesting…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而爲華者也豈徒器焉而已耶是心爲無聲之
樂而因樂以宣之則心有所寄樂爲形下之器
而有心以本之則器因以神外心以言樂本之
則無矣如樂何信乎樂爲德之華也然必養吾
心之太和以端作樂之本然後氣和形和而天
地之和應之古聖王所以陶性靈移風俗者其
德茂其本深也豈鍾鼓云乎哉彼房中之樂七
德之舞非不從之以器也而古樂之不復者則
徒以其器也是故君子反情以和志
===
第貳場
論
帝王心法之要
鄒祖孔
同考試官教諭劉　批　此作命意精深根極理要
縱橫辯博馳騁不羈至以天下治其心立論尤奇偉卓絶非大
手筆不能
考試官教諭倫　批　氣格高向古議論剴切來歸
重守成是通達治體者
punctuated:
而爲華者也，豈徒器焉而已耶？是心爲無聲之樂，而因樂以宣之，則心有所寄；樂爲形下之器，而有心以本之，則器因以神。外心以言樂，本之則無矣，如樂何？信乎，樂爲德之華也！然必養吾心之太和，以端作樂之本，然後氣和、形和，而天地之和應之。古聖王所以陶性靈、移風俗者，其德茂，其本深也，豈鍾鼓云乎哉？彼房中之樂、七德之舞，非不從之以器也，而古樂之不復者，則徒以其器也。是故君子反情以和志。

第貳場
論
帝王心法之要
鄒祖孔
同考試官教諭劉　批：此作命意精深，根極理要，縱橫辯博，馳騁不羈。至「以天下治其心」，立論尤奇偉卓絶，非大手筆不能。
考試官教諭倫　批：氣格高，向古，議論剴切。來歸重守成，是通達治體者。
translation_en:
…and shines forth as its splendor. How could it merely be a matter of instruments and nothing more? Thus, the mind is soundless music, and when one uses music to express it, the mind has something in which to lodge; music is a physical instrument, and when it has the mind as its foundation, the instrument thereby becomes numinous. To speak of music apart from the mind is to lack the foundation—what then can one do with music? Truly, music is the splendor of virtue! Yet one must nurture the supreme harmony of one's own mind in order to rectify the foundation for creating music; only then will vital energy be harmonious, physical form be harmonious, and the harmony of Heaven and Earth respond to it. That by which the ancient sage-kings cultivated the spirit and transformed customs was the abundance of their virtue and the depth of their foundation—how could it merely be a matter of bells and drums? That "music of the inner chambers" and the "dance of the seven virtues" were not unaccompanied by instruments, yet the reason ancient music was not restored was that they relied solely on instruments. Therefore, the gentleman returns to his true feelings in order to harmonize his will.

Second Session
Discourse
"The Essentials of the Method of the Mind of Emperors and Kings"
Zou Zukong 鄒祖孔
Associate Examiner, Instructor Liu 劉, comments: The central conception of this piece is profound and penetrating, rooted in the utmost essentials of principle. Its argumentation is wide-ranging and learned, galloping onward without restraint. When it comes to the thesis of "using the realm to govern one's mind," the argument it establishes is especially extraordinary, magnificent, and unsurpassed—something only a master writer could achieve.
Examiner, Instructor Lun 倫, comments: Its spirit and style are lofty and incline toward antiquity, and its arguments are incisive and to the point. In the end it places the weight on preserving the dynastic achievement, showing someone who thoroughly understands the essentials of governance.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭譙　批〔豪宕雄健直追史漢〕
人主欲致天下之治其要在乎以天下治其心
而已夫天下大矣人君舉其身兼蒞而總攝之
苟不能治其心即天下何繇而治顧人主之於
天下甚尊也天下處其卑而吾處其尊則其心
易縱而難檢苟不時時舉天下之故悚惕而警
厲之其究將至於知有已不知有人崇高富貴
之形近在耳目見聞之間者常見以爲可恃艱
難勞苦之形遠在四海九州之間者常見以爲
可忽然後驕淫邪侈日滋月茂無所底止即其
===
心又何繇而治故心者人主之所以治天下之
本也天下者又人主之所以治其心之本也夫
惟能以天下治其心而後能以心治其天下張
子論知農事爲帝王心法之要意蓋如此予誦
其言未嘗不三嘆也嗟乎天下孰有急於農事
者哉元元之衆孰有勞苦於農事者哉然而世
之人主鮮克留意乎其間何也其故有二其一
謂之壅其一謂之玩謂之壅者君民之判久矣
punctuated:
考試官教諭譙批：〔豪宕雄健，直追《史》《漢》。〕
人主欲致天下之治，其要在乎以天下治其心而已。夫天下大矣，人君舉其身兼蒞而總攝之，苟不能治其心，即天下何繇而治？顧人主之於天下，甚尊也。天下處其卑，而吾處其尊，則其心易縱而難檢。苟不時時舉天下之故，悚惕而警厲之，其究將至於知有已，不知有人；崇高富貴之形，近在耳目見聞之間者，常見以爲可恃；艱難勞苦之形，遠在四海九州之間者，常見以爲可忽。然後驕淫邪侈，日滋月茂，無所底止，即其心又何繇而治？故心者，人主之所以治天下之本也；天下者，又人主之所以治其心之本也。夫惟能以天下治其心，而後能以心治其天下。張子論知農事爲帝王心法之要，意蓋如此。予誦其言，未嘗不三嘆也。嗟乎！天下孰有急於農事者哉？元元之衆，孰有勞苦於農事者哉？然而世之人主鮮克留意乎其間，何也？其故有二：其一謂之壅，其一謂之玩。謂之壅者，君民之判久矣，
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: [Bold, uninhibited, and vigorous, directly rivaling the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) and the Book of Han (Hanshu).]
If a ruler wishes to bring about good governance throughout the realm, the essential point lies simply in using the realm to govern his own mind. Now, the realm is vast. The ruler, with his single person, presides over it all and holds it under his comprehensive control; if he cannot govern his own mind, how then can the realm be governed? Yet in relation to the realm, the ruler occupies a position of extreme exaltation. While the realm occupies the lowly place and he occupies the exalted one, his mind is easily indulged and difficult to restrain. If he does not constantly take up the affairs of the realm to fill himself with awe, vigilance, and admonition, in the end he will come to know only himself and not know others. The manifestations of exalted rank and wealth and honor, being close at hand within the reach of his own eyes and ears, are constantly seen as things that can be relied upon; the manifestations of hardship and toil, being far off across the Four Seas and the Nine Provinces, are constantly seen as things that can be neglected. Thereafter, arrogance, license, perversity, and extravagance grow day by day and flourish month by month without end—how then can his mind be governed? Therefore, the mind is the root by which the ruler governs the realm, and the realm in turn is the root by which the ruler governs his mind. Only when he is able to use the realm to govern his mind can he then use his mind to govern his realm. When Master Zhang (Zhang Zai) argued that understanding farming is essential to the method of the mind of emperors and kings, his meaning was surely just like this. Whenever I recite his words, I never fail to sigh repeatedly in admiration. Alas! In all the realm, what is more urgent than farming? Among the masses of the common people, what involves greater toil and hardship than farming? And yet, among the rulers of the world, few are able to pay heed to it—why is this? There are two reasons: the first is called "obstruction," and the second is called "trivialization." What is meant by "obstruction" is that the separation between ruler and people has existed for a long time; …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
是故其分殊而勢不相習也其勢殊而事不相
習也其事殊而跡不相習也其跡殊而情不相
習也是之曰褻謂之玩者以是爲瑣屑委鄙不
足務也吾從而深求之民生之所繇以蕃此也
民俗之所繇以美此也禮樂刑政之所繇以四
達而不悖此也泛而觀之則以爲是瑣屑委鄙
不足務也是之曰玩玩始乎上褻積乎下其忽
然不以留意無足怪也夫褻則蔽蔽則不明玩
則惰惰則不恭人主之心業已惰墮於二者之間
===
於是乎內之一切謬戾頗僻之端從之而出者
既蕩而莫禁其往外之一切可欣可喜可矜可
羨之欲從之而入者又紛然投間抵隙而莫禦
其來如是而求心之治不可得也心既不治矣
如是而求天下之治不可得也昔者考其詩書
竊計古之帝王其於天下莫不綢繆其文物敦
固其典章織密其法制至其告戒之間所謂改
容變色叮嚀而反覆者獨民事爲兢兢而其說
最著於七月無逸二篇七月之篇詳在下而本
punctuated: 是故其分殊而勢不相習也，其勢殊而事不相習也，其事殊而跡不相習也，其跡殊而情不相習也，是之曰褻。謂之玩者，以是爲瑣屑委鄙不足務也。吾從而深求之，民生之所繇以蕃，此也；民俗之所繇以美，此也；禮樂刑政之所繇以四達而不悖，此也。泛而觀之，則以爲是瑣屑委鄙不足務也，是之曰玩。玩始乎上，褻積乎下，其忽然不以留意，無足怪也。夫褻則蔽，蔽則不明；玩則惰，惰則不恭。人主之心，業已惰墮於二者之間，於是乎內之一切謬戾頗僻之端從之而出者，既蕩而莫禁其往；外之一切可欣可喜可矜可羨之欲從之而入者，又紛然投間抵隙而莫禦其來。如是而求心之治，不可得也；心既不治矣，如是而求天下之治，不可得也。昔者考其《詩》《書》，竊計古之帝王，其於天下，莫不綢繆其文物，敦固其典章，織密其法制。至其告戒之間，所謂改容變色、叮嚀而反覆者，獨民事爲兢兢，而其說最著於《七月》《無逸》二篇。《七月》之篇，詳在下而本
translation_en: … Therefore, because their stations differ, their circumstances are unfamiliar to one another; because their circumstances differ, their affairs are unfamiliar to one another; because their affairs differ, their footprints are unfamiliar to one another; and because their footprints differ, their feelings are unfamiliar to one another. This is what is called alienation [壅, misprinted as 褻]. As for what is called trifling neglect, it is regarding these matters as petty, mean, and unworthy of effort. Yet if we probe deeply into them, that by which the people's livelihood flourishes lies herein; that by which the people's customs are made virtuous lies herein; and that by which rites, music, punishments, and governance reach in all four directions without contradiction lies herein. Viewed superficially, however, they are deemed petty, mean, and unworthy of effort—this is what is called trifling neglect. When trifling neglect begins above and alienation [?] accumulates below, it is no wonder at all that the ruler carelessly fails to pay attention to them. Now, alienation [?] leads to obscuration, and obscuration leads to a lack of clarity; trifling neglect leads to indolence, and indolence leads to a lack of reverence. Once the mind of the ruler has lapsed into indolence and degradation between these two, all manner of perverse, erratic, and biased tendencies within issue forth from it, sweeping away without anything to check their departure; meanwhile, all manner of delightful, pleasing, boastful, and enviable desires from without enter into it, thronging through every crack and crevice without anything to ward off their arrival. To seek the ordering of the mind under such conditions is impossible; and once the mind is not ordered, to seek the ordering of the world under such conditions is likewise impossible. In the past, examining the Odes (Shi) and the Documents (Shu), I privately observed that toward the world, the emperors and kings of antiquity without exception closely wove their cultural institutions, solidly established their statutes, and finely meshed their laws and systems. Yet in their admonitions and warnings, where they altered their countenances, changed color, and enjoined repeatedly, it was solely over the affairs of the people that they were cautiously attentive. This teaching is most manifest in the two chapters "Seventh Month" (Qiyue) and "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi). The "Seventh Month" chapter details what is below, yet never…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
始不歸之上實其言可以無疚於壅無逸之篇
詳在上而未始不歸之下實其言可以無疚於
玩爲天下者甚不可不省也是故人主五齊八
珍而爲之民者何其役役然終歲疾耕而不足
於食也試於此有思焉則知憂矣人主重錦文
繡而爲之民者何其汲汲然終歲勤織而不足
於衣也試於此有思焉則知勞矣人主璇宮玉
宇而爲之民者何其閔閔然郊棲露處而不得
寧也試於此有思焉則知艱矣人主出有警入
===
有蹕雍容揖讓而爲之民者何其皇皇然胼手
胝足而不得休也試於此有思焉則知懼矣人
主春有觀夏有游秋有豫冬有息而爲之民者
何其咨咨然吁嗟噫嘅於祁寒暑雨之中而不
得怡也試於此有思焉則知危矣夫人心未有
無所用者也其用也未有無所倚者也夫人主
當其左圖右書義之晝堯之典舜之歌禹之訓
湯之銘文之命武之誓若日月而揭諸前未嘗
不有悚於志也俄然而離去之則其志亦次第
punctuated: 始不歸之上，實其言可以無疚於壅；《無逸》之篇，詳在上而未始不歸之下，實其言可以無疚於玩。爲天下者甚不可不省也。是故人主五齊八珍，而爲之民者，何其役役然終歲疾耕而不足於食也？試於此有思焉，則知憂矣。人主重錦文繡，而爲之民者，何其汲汲然終歲勤織而不足於衣也？試於此有思焉，則知勞矣。人主璇宮玉宇，而爲之民者，何其閔閔然郊棲露處而不得寧也？試於此有思焉，則知艱矣。人主出有警，入有蹕，雍容揖讓，而爲之民者，何其皇皇然胼手胝足而不得休也？試於此有思焉，則知懼矣。人主春有觀，夏有游，秋有豫，冬有息，而爲之民者，何其咨咨然吁嗟噫嘅於祁寒暑雨之中而不得怡也？試於此有思焉，則知危矣。夫人心未有無所用者也，其用也未有無所倚者也。夫人主當其左圖右書，義之晝、堯之典、舜之歌、禹之訓、湯之銘、文之命、武之誓，若日月而揭諸前，未嘗不有悚於志也；俄然而離去之，則其志亦次第
translation_en:
…never fails to trace things back to those above; by putting its words into practice, one can be free from the fault of obstruction. The "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) chapter is detailed regarding those above, yet never fails to trace things back to those below; by putting its words into practice, one can be free from the fault of negligence. He who governs the empire must by no means fail to examine this.

Therefore, while the ruler enjoys the five ceremonial wines and eight delicacies, why is it that those who are his people toil so endlessly, plowing rapidly all year long and yet lacking sufficient food? If he but reflects upon this, he will know anxiety. While the ruler wears layered brocades and patterned embroideries, why is it that those who are his people strive so ceaselessly, weaving diligently all year long and yet lacking sufficient clothing? If he but reflects upon this, he will know their toil. While the ruler dwells in halls of jasper and mansions of jade, why is it that those who are his people suffer so pitiably, lodging in the wilds and exposed to the elements without ever finding peace? If he but reflects upon this, he will know their hardship. While the ruler goes out with heralds clearing the way and enters with guards securing the road, bowing and yielding with poised grace, why is it that those who are his people hurry about so anxiously, with calloused hands and feet, never able to rest? If he but reflects upon this, he will know fear. While the ruler has his sightseeing in spring, excursions in summer, pleasure tours in autumn, and repose in winter, why is it that those who are his people sigh and lament so bitterly amid bitter cold and sultry rain, never able to find joy? If he but reflects upon this, he will know peril.

Now, the human mind is never without something to which it applies itself, and in its application it is never without something upon which it relies. When the ruler has charts on his left and books on his right—when the trigrams [?] of Fuxi, the Canon of Yao, the Songs of Shun, the Instructions of Yu, the Inscriptions of Tang, the Charges of King Wen, and the Oaths of King Wu are held up before him like the sun and the moon—he never fails to feel awe in his mind. Yet as soon as he turns away from them, that resolve of his likewise gradually…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而銷落彼所假者遠而不切也當其左三公右
三孤卿獻規史爲書瞽爲詩工誦大夫箴士傳
言苟語及於善未嘗不躍然喜也苟語及於不
善未嘗不瞿然起也儀然而已則其躍然瞿然
者亦次第而無存彼所假者近而有限也故不
若假之於天下夫天下者人主之所有事也無
時而非是也無之而非是也其休戚禍福又遞
相籍也是故知憂則不敢言樂恐其病天下也
知勞則不敢言逸恐其妨天下也知艱則不敢
===
言縱恐其擾天下也知懼則不敢言侈恐其殘
天下也知危則不敢言安恐其亡天下也夫如
是可謂善假而知所以用其心者矣故能祓除
洗濯使精神日奮志慮日澄而其心治心治而
天下治無難也蓋嘗觀三代以還英君誼辟繼
踵而起相望於後先乃其名能知農事者何廑
廑也夫秦皇漢武非不亦雄才大略也徒侈然
聽其意氣之所至以見奇而不能退而自克者
誠未有以檢束其心也西京之元東京之章非
punctuated: 而銷落，彼所假者遠而不切也。當其左三公、右三孤，卿獻規、史爲書、瞽爲詩、工誦、大夫箴、士傳言，苟語及於善，未嘗不躍然喜也；苟語及於不善，未嘗不瞿然起也。儀然而已，則其躍然、瞿然者亦次第而無存，彼所假者近而有限也。故不若假之於天下。夫天下者，人主之所有事也，無時而非是也，無之而非是也，其休戚禍福又遞相籍也。是故知憂則不敢言樂，恐其病天下也；知勞則不敢言逸，恐其妨天下也；知艱則不敢言縱，恐其擾天下也；知懼則不敢言侈，恐其殘天下也；知危則不敢言安，恐其亡天下也。夫如是，可謂善假而知所以用其心者矣。故能祓除洗濯，使精神日奮、志慮日澄，而其心治；心治而天下治，無難也。蓋嘗觀三代以還，英君誼辟繼踵而起，相望於後先，乃其名能知農事者，何廑廑也？夫秦皇、漢武，非不亦雄才大略也，徒侈然聽其意氣之所至以見奇，而不能退而自克者，誠未有以檢束其心也；西京之元、東京之章，非
translation_en: …and fades away, because what he draws upon is distant and lacks immediacy. When he is flanked on the left by the Three Dukes and on the right by the Three Solitaries, while the Ministers present admonitions, the Scribes make records, the Blind Musicians offer poems, the Artisans recite, the Grandees give remonstrances, and the Servitors transmit words—if their talk touches upon the good, he never fails to leap with joy; if their talk touches upon the bad, he never fails to start up in alarm. Yet once it stops [?], that leaping joy and startled alarm also gradually vanish, because what he draws upon is close at hand yet limited in scope. Therefore, nothing compares to drawing upon the realm itself. Now, the realm is that with which the ruler is constantly occupied: there is no time when it is not so, and nowhere that it is not so; moreover, its joys and sorrows, its fortunes and misfortunes, are mutually intertwined with his own. For this reason, knowing sorrow, he dares not speak of pleasure, lest he afflict the realm; knowing toil, he dares not speak of ease, lest he hinder the realm; knowing hardship, he dares not speak of indulgence, lest he disturb the realm; knowing fear, he dares not speak of extravagance, lest he ravage the realm; knowing peril, he dares not speak of security, lest he ruin the realm. One who is like this may truly be called adept at drawing upon external things and knowing how to apply his mind. Thus he is able to cleanse and purify himself, causing his spirit to be daily roused and his intentions and thoughts to grow daily clearer, so that his mind is well-governed; and once his mind is well-governed, there is no difficulty in governing the realm. Indeed, if we observe the eras since the Three Dynasties, heroic lords and righteous sovereigns have risen one after another in continuous succession, yet how exceedingly few are those renowned for understanding the affairs of agriculture! Now, the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han were not without heroic talent and grand strategy, yet they merely gave extravagant rein to wherever their willful spirit carried them in order to display extraordinary feats, and could not step back to master themselves—truly because they lacked the means to restrain their minds. Emperor Yuan of the Western Capital [Former Han] and Emperor Zhang of the Eastern Capital [Later Han] were not…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不亦溫乎其有意也徒煦然務爲聲色之美以
見厚而不能進而自強者誠未有以悚動其心
也有以檢束其心雖剛必柔有以悚動其心雖
柔必剛夫惟剛而知柔柔而知剛然後能克已
能克已然後能正已於是目無越視耳無越聽
口無逸言身無逸動藏於獨而無逸念顯於共
而無逸施其始會不能以方寸而其終明效大
驗浸尋而被天下是故漢文得其什七則幾致
刑措唐太宗得其什五則七年而斗米三錢夜
===
戶不閉宋仁宗得其什四則財不蓄而自富刑
不殺而自威此其彰彰較著者也嗟乎由秦而
漢而唐而宋千有餘年而其名能知農事者三
君而止何其難也夫太宗創業之主也不足爲
異何則創業之主往往起自民間其閱歷也真
其譜練也久一旦而據天下之上宜其兢兢也
若夫守成者生長深宮紛華靡麗之所濡宴安
逸欲之所染左右便佞之所漸磨固不少矣彼
於民事會不及稍試於耳目其孰從而知之是
punctuated: 不亦溫乎其有意也？徒煦然務爲聲色之美以見厚，而不能進而自強者，誠未有以悚動其心也。有以檢束其心，雖剛必柔；有以悚動其心，雖柔必剛。夫惟剛而知柔，柔而知剛，然後能克已；能克已，然後能正已。於是目無越視，耳無越聽，口無逸言，身無逸動，藏於獨而無逸念，顯於共而無逸施。其始會不能以方寸，而其終明效大驗，浸尋而被天下。是故漢文得其什七，則幾致刑措；唐太宗得其什五，則七年而斗米三錢，夜戶不閉；宋仁宗得其什四，則財不蓄而自富，刑不殺而自威：此其彰彰較著者也。嗟乎！由秦而漢、而唐、而宋，千有餘年，而其名能知農事者，三君而止，何其難也！夫太宗，創業之主也，不足爲異。何則？創業之主，往往起自民間，其閱歷也真，其譜練也久，一旦而據天下之上，宜其兢兢也。若夫守成者，生長深宮，紛華靡麗之所濡，宴安逸欲之所染，左右便佞之所漸磨，固不少矣。彼於民事，會不及稍試於耳目，其孰從而知之？是
translation_en: …were they not also gentle and well-intentioned? Yet they merely sought in a genial manner to make a fine display of outward demeanor to show their benevolence, while remaining unable to press forward and strengthen themselves—truly because there was nothing to rouse and stir their minds. When there is something to restrain one's mind, even the unyielding will become gentle; when there is something to rouse one's mind, even the gentle will become firm. Only when the unyielding know how to be gentle, and the gentle know how to be firm, can one overcome the self; and only after overcoming the self can one rectify the self. Thereupon the eyes do not look beyond what is proper, the ears do not listen beyond what is proper, the mouth utters no licentious words, and the body makes no licentious movements; hidden in solitude, there are no licentious thoughts, and manifested in public, there are no licentious measures. At the beginning, it barely fills the square inch of the heart, yet in the end, its clear effects and great proofs gradually spread to cover the entire realm. For this reason, Emperor Wen of Han (Han Wen 漢文) attained seven-tenths of this, and thus nearly brought about the setting aside of punishments; Emperor Taizong of Tang (Tang Taizong 唐太宗) attained five-tenths of it, and thus within seven years a peck of rice cost three cash and doors were not bolted at night; Emperor Renzong of Song (Song Renzong 宋仁宗) attained four-tenths of it, and thus wealth was not hoarded yet naturally abundant, and punishments did not kill yet naturally inspired awe. These are the cases that are brilliantly and manifestly evident. Alas! From Qin through Han, Tang, and Song, over more than a thousand years, those renowned for understanding agricultural affairs were no more than these three rulers—how difficult it is! Now Taizong was a founding ruler, so his case is not surprising. Why is that? Founding rulers often rise from among the common people; their personal experience is genuine and their practical familiarity [?] is long-standing, so once they occupy the supreme position over the realm, it is only natural that they are cautious and apprehensive. As for rulers who preserve an existing dynasty, they grow up deep within the palace; how much they are steeped in luxury and extravagance, tainted by ease and indulgent desires, and gradually worn down by glib flatterers around them is indeed no small matter! When it comes to the affairs of the people, they have never even slightly tested them with their own ears and eyes—how then could they come to know them? For this…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
故非上智不能周公之告成王其稱商也舍成
湯而數三宗其稱周也舍后稷而數太王王季
至於文王蓋舉其難也嗟乎可以監矣
表
擬宋禱雨太乙宮是日雨輔臣賀表〔慶曆七年〕
楊先春
同考試官訓導靳批立格清新敷詞整潔絕無
粉澤態度且模寫當時孚格之誠微婉有致是善言天人之蘊
===
匪特四六之工已也
考試官教諭倫批典鬯流麗
考試官教諭譙批古雅可式
慶曆七年某月某日具官臣某等恭遇
聖駕禱雨
西太乙宮是日雨謹奉
表稱
賀者伏以
聖主勤民方効精誠之格
punctuated:
故非上智不能。周公之告成王，其稱商也，舍成湯而數三宗；其稱周也，舍后稷而數太王、王季至於文王，蓋舉其難也。嗟乎，可以監矣！

表
擬宋禱雨太乙宮是日雨輔臣賀表〔慶曆七年〕
楊先春
同考試官訓導靳批：立格清新，敷詞整潔，絕無粉澤態度。且模寫當時孚格之誠，微婉有致，是善言天人之蘊，匪特四六之工已也。
考試官教諭倫批：典鬯流麗。
考試官教諭譙批：古雅可式。

慶曆七年某月某日，具官臣某等，恭遇聖駕禱雨西太乙宮，是日雨，謹奉表稱賀者。伏以聖主勤民，方効精誠之格；
translation_en:
…Therefore, unless one possesses supreme wisdom, one is incapable of this. When the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) admonished King Cheng (Chengwang 成王), in speaking of the Shang dynasty he passed over Tang the Accomplished (Cheng Tang 成湯) and enumerated the Three Worthy Ancestors (Sanzong 三宗); in speaking of the Zhou dynasty he passed over Houji 后稷 and enumerated King Tai (Taiwang 太王) and Wang Ji 王季 down to King Wen (Wenwang 文王). This was because he cited what was most difficult. Alas, one may take this as a mirror!

Memorial
Imitating a Congratulatory Memorial by Auxiliary Ministers of the Song Dynasty when the Emperor Prayed for Rain at the Taiyi Palace and It Rained that Very Day [7th year of the Qingli era (1047)]
Yang Xianchun 楊先春
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Jin 靳: The structure is fresh and new, the phrasing neat and clean, completely free of affected ornamentation. Moreover, in depicting the sincerity that moved Heaven at that time, it is subtle, gentle, and charming. It excels at expressing the profound connection between Heaven and humankind, and is not merely skillful in parallel prose.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫: Classical, fluent, and gracefully flowing.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙: Classically elegant and worthy of serving as a model.

On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of the Qingli era, your servants [so-and-so], holding full official titles, respectfully encountering the Imperial Carriage praying for rain at the Western Taiyi Palace (Xi Taiyi Gong 西太乙宮) and rain falling on that very day, humbly present this memorial to offer congratulations:

We humbly consider that as the Sacred Sovereign labors diligently for the people, having just demonstrated the utmost sincerity that reaches on high;…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
皇穹眷
德旋霑靈澤之敷合萬姓而咸濡普九天而皆
潤歡騰海宇慶溢臣鄰臣等誠懽誠忭稽
首頓首竊惟天道遠人道邇視徵信以交
孚肅時雨乂時暘鑒明馨而是若惟天心
之仁愛莫測肆人君之對越宜虔六事責
躬殷切桑林之禱孑遺憫下周懷雲漢之
憂夙星駕而税於桑田衛美中興之令主
甘雨祈而介我稷黍詩稱有道之曾孫魯
不焚巫文仲忠言是聽齊嘗避殿晏嬰善
喻猶傳漢皇詔布乾封矯誣彰失唐帝術
行縮水荒誕貽譏蓋應天不貴以文而捄
災亦惟在德自非有
聖敬之昭假焉能致
玄昊之潛通茲蓋伏遇
○○○○
聰明天授
恭儉性成
punctuated: 皇穹眷德，旋霑靈澤之敷。合萬姓而咸濡，普九天而皆潤；歡騰海宇，慶溢臣鄰。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟天道遠、人道邇，視徵信以交孚；肅時雨、乂時暘，鑒明馨而是若。惟天心之仁愛莫測，肆人君之對越宜虔。六事責躬，殷切桑林之禱；孑遺憫下，周懷雲漢之憂。夙星駕而税於桑田，衛美中興之令主；甘雨祈而介我稷黍，詩稱有道之曾孫。魯不焚巫，文仲忠言是聽；齊嘗避殿，晏嬰善喻猶傳。漢皇詔布乾封，矯誣彰失；唐帝術行縮水，荒誕貽譏。蓋應天不貴以文，而捄災亦惟在德。自非有聖敬之昭假，焉能致玄昊之潛通？茲蓋伏遇○○○○，聰明天授，恭儉性成；
translation_en:
…August Heaven looks with favor upon Your virtue and promptly bestows the spreading of its numinous grace. Uniting the myriad people, all are moistened; reaching throughout the Nine Heavens, everything is nourished. Joy surges through the realm within the seas, and celebration overflows among Your ministers and aides. Your servants, truly joyful and truly elated, bow our heads to the ground.

We humbly reflect that the Way of Heaven is distant while the Way of Man is near, yet in observing verifying signs they mutually accord; respectfulness brings timely rain and orderliness brings timely sunshine, for Heaven beholds bright fragrant virtue and complies with it. Because the benevolent love of the Mind of Heaven is unfathomable, the ruler of men must be reverent when standing before It. Reproaching himself on six counts, the ruler of Yin was earnest in his prayer at the Mulberry Grove; pitying the surviving remnant below, the sovereign of Zhou harbored the sorrow of the "Milky Way" ode. Yoking his carriage early by starlight to halt in the mulberry fields, Wei praised the fine ruler of its restoration; praying for sweet rain to bless our millet and grain, the Odes lauded the virtuous great-grandson. Lu did not burn the shaman, heeding the loyal words of Zang Wenzhong; Qi once vacated the main hall, and the apt counsel of Yan Ying is still passed down. The Han emperor issued an edict proclaiming the Qianfeng era, yet his falsity and deception only exposed his failings; the Tang sovereign practiced the art of shrinking water, and its absurdity invited ridicule. Truly, in responding to Heaven one does not prize mere outward form, and in relieving disaster everything depends upon virtue alone. Were it not for the bright reaching of Your sacred reverence, how could it bring about this unseen communion with Mysterious Heaven?

Now we humbly encounter [Your Majesty, ○○○○], whose intelligence and discernment are endowed by Heaven, whose reverence and frugality are formed by nature, …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
治有光於
祖宗
孝克隆於
聖母右文稽古
延義謹無逸之書節用愛人
玉清罷不急之役
觀刈麥於後苑周知稼穡艱難
祀先農於東郊時慮陰陽愆伏
聞雷束帶曾密禱於
===
禁中徒跣沾衣寧露立於堦下邇當溽暑復
值驕陽萬寶未臻告成烝庶憂蘊隆之虐
九重不遑寧處晨昏冀霡霂之施太史具占謂
天時之偶爾諫臣
請禱動
聖意之惻然初卜醮於醴泉繼改祈於
太乙
省鹵簿而
御便輦
punctuated: 治有光於祖宗，孝克隆於聖母。右文稽古，延義謹《無逸》之書；節用愛人，玉清罷不急之役。觀刈麥於後苑，周知稼穡艱難；祀先農於東郊，時慮陰陽愆伏。聞雷束帶，曾密禱於禁中；徒跣沾衣，寧露立於堦下。邇當溽暑，復值驕陽。萬寶未臻告成，烝庶憂蘊隆之虐；九重不遑寧處，晨昏冀霡霂之施。太史具占，謂天時之偶爾；諫臣請禱，動聖意之惻然。初卜醮於醴泉，繼改祈於太乙。省鹵簿而御便輦，
translation_en:
…whose governance sheds lustre upon the Imperial Ancestors, and whose filial piety is richly exalted toward the Sacred Mother [the Empress Dowager]. Valuing civil culture and examining antiquity, in the Yanyi Palace [?] he takes to heart the chapter "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi); economizing in expenditures and loving the people, at Yuqing Palace he halts non-urgent construction projects. Observing the harvesting of wheat in the rear imperial park, he thoroughly understands the hardships of sowing and reaping; sacrificing to the First Agriculturist (Xiannong) in the eastern suburbs, he constantly worries over imbalances of yin and yang. Hearing thunder, he girded his sash, having secretly prayed within the Forbidden Palace; barefoot and with drenched robes, he would rather stand exposed beneath the palace steps.

Recently, during the muggy summer heat, we have again encountered a scorching sun. The myriad crops have not yet reached maturity, and the multitude of commoners grieve over the cruelty of the stifling drought; the Ninefold Palace [the Emperor] has no leisure to rest in peace, morning and evening hoping for the bestowal of gentle, soaking rain. The Grand Scribe (Taishi) prepared a divination, saying it was merely an accident of seasonal weather; the remonstrating officials requested prayers for rain, moving His Sacred Mind to compassion. At first, divination was made to hold a Daoist offering (jiao) at the Liquan [Temple], and subsequently it was changed to praying to the Great Unity (Taiyi). Reducing the grand imperial cortege and riding in an informal palanquin…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
薦圭璧以脩明禋
翠幄嚴凝瑞檢香浮於
寶籙紫壇高峙靈旗風動乎玄冥
熙典畢陳
神功昭貺西海忽飛朱鬣中方頓舞黃龍電掣
豐隆陰帝捲五湖清浪星馳屏翳巨靈曳
四瀆洪瀾俄瞻靉靉油雲忽覩淋淋甘澍
散郊原而優渥遍草樹以芳菲潤沛江河
瞬息春回六合機捷桴鼓須臾望滿三農
===
無事減膳撤樂之虛名自速
旋乾轉坤之妙應起宋苗於既槁何須雨玉
雨珠滋禹甸以流膏會見多黍多秔誠
清朝之希覯爲
盛世之美談也臣等班近星辰久沾
湛露光依
日月深愧作霖叨陪祀於
齋宮覩
休嘉而欣欣有喜幸扈從於
punctuated: 薦圭璧以脩明禋。翠幄嚴凝，瑞檢香浮於寶籙；紫壇高峙，靈旗風動乎玄冥。熙典畢陳，神功昭貺。西海忽飛朱鬣，中方頓舞黃龍；電掣豐隆，陰帝捲五湖清浪；星馳屏翳，巨靈曳四瀆洪瀾。俄瞻靉靉油雲，忽覩淋淋甘澍。散郊原而優渥，遍草樹以芳菲。潤沛江河，瞬息春回六合；機捷桴鼓，須臾望滿三農。無事減膳撤樂之虛名，自速旋乾轉坤之妙應。起宋苗於既槁，何須雨玉雨珠；滋禹甸以流膏，會見多黍多秔。誠清朝之希覯，爲盛世之美談也。臣等班近星辰，久沾湛露；光依日月，深愧作霖。叨陪祀於齋宮，覩休嘉而欣欣有喜；幸扈從於
translation_en: …offering jade tablets and disks to perform the pure sacrifice. The kingfisher-green canopy stood in solemn stillness, as the fragrance of auspicious texts floated over the precious registers; the purple altar towered on high, as spirit banners stirred in the wind toward Xuanming, god of the dark north. Once the grand rites had been fully set forth, divine power made manifest its favor. From the Western Sea a vermilion-maned steed suddenly flew forth, and in the central region a yellow dragon instantly danced; as Fenglong flashed with lightning, the Lord of Yin rolled up the clear waves of the Five Lakes; as Pingyi sped like a shooting star, the Giant Spirit drew forth the surging billows of the Four Great Rivers. Presently, thick, gathering rain clouds were beheld, and suddenly a drenching, sweet downpour was seen. Spreading across the outskirts and plains in soaking abundance, it reached all herbs and trees to make them lush and fragrant. Its moisture swelled the rivers and streams, and in the blink of an eye spring returned to the Six Directions; its response was as swift as drumstick to drum, and in an instant the hopes of the three classes of farmers were fulfilled. Without resorting to the empty gestures of reducing imperial meals or suspending court music, it naturally hastened a wondrous response that turned heaven and earth around. Reviving the sprouts of Song after they had already withered, what need is there to rain down jade or rain down pearls? Nourishing the domains of Yu with flowing richness, we shall surely see abundant millet and abundant rice. Truly, this is a rare sight in a pure dynasty, and a fine story for a flourishing age! Your servants stand in court ranks near the stars, having long been steeped in your generous dew; relying on the light of the sun and moon, we are deeply ashamed that we cannot ourselves act as the timely rain. Having had the undeserved honor of attending the sacrifice at the Palace of Abstinence, we behold this auspicious blessing and rejoice with gladness; fortunate to follow in the retinue of…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
法駕荷
帝德而蕩蕩難名舞効商羊鳴同垤鸛伏願
慮先未雨
戒豫履冰
圖豐大於日中
萃戩穀於天保
恤民瘼常如
命駕出郊之時
敬天心不改
===
却蓋回
鑾之日
玉燭調而三光正永綿
聖曆於無疆金穰足而九土安胥樂
太平於有象臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖忻躍屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
punctuated: 法駕，荷帝德而蕩蕩難名。舞効商羊，鳴同垤鸛。伏願慮先未雨，戒豫履冰；圖豐大於日中，萃戩穀於天保。恤民瘼常如命駕出郊之時，敬天心不改却蓋回鑾之日。玉燭調而三光正，永綿聖曆於無疆；金穰足而九土安，胥樂太平於有象。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、忻躍屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以…
translation_en:
… the Imperial Carriage, we bear the Emperor's virtue, which is vast beyond words. We dance in imitation of the rain-heralding shangyang bird, and cry out like the storks upon the ant-mounds.

We humbly pray that Your Majesty will take thought before the rain falls, and take precaution in advance as if treading on thin ice; plan for abundance and greatness at the zenith of the sun, and gather all blessings of goodness under Heaven's protection. May Your Majesty's compassion for the sufferings of the people always remain as it was when ordering the Imperial Carriage to go out to the suburban altar, and may Your Majesty's reverence for the heart of Heaven never change from the day the royal canopy was put aside on the return of the imperial cortege. When the Jade Candle of the four seasons is in harmony and the Three Luminaries shine in right order, the Sacred Calendar will be perpetuated without limit; when golden harvests are plentiful and the Nine Provinces are at peace, all will rejoice together in the visible signs of Great Peace.

Your servants are overcome with the utmost awe and elation as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to Your Sacred Majesty, and we reverently present this memorial of congratulation to…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
鄒祖孔
同考試官訓導董批更化善治在守法而不在
變法是作援引證據確有定論而敷陳我
聖祖開天立法
皇上守法致治之意婉切詳盡具占經世之學宜錄以式
===
考試官教諭倫批以正大之論發古健之詞
推原治亂得失如指諸掌蓋究心於理道者
考試官教諭譙批沉鬱而有精思簡嚴而有
奇氣博雅士也錄之
帝王之興必立法以垂後世而後之紹鴻
圖臻上理者必善守其法然後善其治於
不窮所謂守法不安無事而怠不喜多事
而擾斯守之善也開基創業之主其歷變
深其揆事熟故穆然淵思者其仁也燦然
punctuated:
聞。

第叁塲
策
第一問
鄒祖孔
同考試官訓導董批：更化善治，在守法而不在變法。是作援引證據，確有定論。而敷陳我聖祖開天立法、皇上守法致治之意，婉切詳盡，具占經世之學。宜錄以式。
考試官教諭倫批：以正大之論，發古健之詞，推原治亂得失，如指諸掌，蓋究心於理道者。
考試官教諭譙批：沉鬱而有精思，簡嚴而有奇氣，博雅士也。錄之。

帝王之興，必立法以垂後世，而後之紹鴻圖、臻上理者，必善守其法，然後善其治於不窮。所謂守法，不安無事而怠，不喜多事而擾，斯守之善也。開基創業之主，其歷變深，其揆事熟，故穆然淵思者，其仁也；燦然
translation_en:
… to the Throne.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zou Zukong 鄒祖孔
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Dong 董: Reforming customs and achieving good governance lie in upholding the laws and not in altering the laws. This essay cites evidence and authorities, firmly establishing a definitive argument. Moreover, in setting forth the meaning of Our Sacred Ancestor's founding the dynasty and establishing the laws, and of His Majesty's upholding the laws to bring about order, it is tactful, earnest, and thorough, fully demonstrating statecraft learning. It should be selected as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫: With upright and grand arguments expressed in ancient and vigorous diction, it traces the origins of order and chaos, success and failure, as clearly as pointing to the palm of one's hand; he is surely one who has devoted his mind to the principles of governance and the Way.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙: Deep and measured yet possessing refined thought, concise and strict yet possessing extraordinary spirit—he is a scholar of broad learning and elegance. Select it.

When emperors and kings arise, they must establish laws to hand down to later generations; and those who come after to inherit the great enterprise and attain supreme governance must be good at upholding their laws, and only then can they perfect their governance inexhaustibly. What is meant by upholding the laws is neither resting content in the absence of affairs and growing lax, nor delighting in a multiplicity of affairs and causing disturbance; this is excellence in upholding them. A ruler who lays the foundation and establishes a dynasty has experienced deep vicissitudes and weighed affairs with mature deliberation; therefore, that which he ponders in profound and solemn contemplation is his benevolence, and that which shines forth in brilliant…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
畢備者其法也夫是乂安海宇而永詒後
範守成之主邃處深宮章縫之士類持獨
見豈無奮發圖治通達國體者藉令竭智
殫慮僅可補偏救敝其大經大法孰能易
之三代而下英君誼辟不少矣若其撫盈
成之運當時稱善後世無貶詞惟曰恪遵
成憲耳已名臣碩輔獻納巖廊亦曰明習
典章耳已喜多事而務更張者不與焉書
曰鑒於先王成憲其永無愆後儒王通氏
===
曰不以三代之禮統天下終危邦也卽三
王之興皆儀鑒先代未有變更自用者況
後王耶夏之興也有典有則詒厥子孫而
曰聖有謨訓明徵定保禹不自作也而嗣
禹之業者不敢變禹也商之興也三風十
愆儆於有位而曰纘禹舊服兹率厥常湯
不自作也而嗣湯之業者不敢變湯也周
之興也立政立事董正治官而曰監於二
代武王周公不自作也而嗣周之業者不
punctuated: 畢備者其法也，夫是乂安海宇而永詒後範。守成之主邃處深宮，章縫之士類持獨見，豈無奮發圖治、通達國體者？藉令竭智殫慮，僅可補偏救敝，其大經大法孰能易之？三代而下，英君誼辟不少矣。若其撫盈成之運，當時稱善，後世無貶詞，惟曰恪遵成憲耳已；名臣碩輔，獻納巖廊，亦曰明習典章耳已，喜多事而務更張者不與焉。《書》曰：「鑒於先王成憲，其永無愆。」後儒王通氏曰：「不以三代之禮統天下，終危邦也。」卽三王之興，皆儀鑒先代，未有變更自用者，況後王耶？夏之興也，有典有則，詒厥子孫，而曰：「聖有謨訓，明徵定保。」禹不自作也，而嗣禹之業者不敢變禹也。商之興也，三風十愆，儆於有位，而曰：「纘禹舊服，兹率厥常。」湯不自作也，而嗣湯之業者不敢變湯也。周之興也，立政立事，董正治官，而曰：「監於二代。」武王、周公不自作也，而嗣周之業者不
translation_en:
…completely provided for is their laws; through this they bring peace and order to the realm within the seas and bequeath an enduring model to posterity. Rulers who preserve an established heritage dwell deep within their secluded palaces, while Confucian scholars in their ceremonial dress and stitched caps tend to hold fast to their own particular views. How could there not be among them men who rouse themselves to strive for good governance and who thoroughly understand the fundamental principles of the state? Yet even supposing they exhaust their wisdom and deplete their deliberations, they can do no more than mend partial defects and remedy existing abuses—as for the great standards and fundamental laws, who could alter them? From the Three Dynasties onward, brilliant rulers and righteous sovereigns have not been few. As for those who presided over eras of abundant fulfillment, who were praised as good in their own time and received no disparaging words in later ages, it was said of them only that they reverently observed the established constitutions, and nothing more. And of the renowned ministers and great counselors who offered advice and counsel in the lofty halls of court, it was likewise said only that they were clearly conversant with the statutes and institutions, and nothing more—those who delighted in meddlesome activity and bent their efforts toward sweeping alterations had no place among them.

The Classic of History (Shu) says: "Take as your mirror the established constitutions of the former kings, and you will forever be free from error." The later Confucian scholar Wang Tong 王通 said: "If one does not unify All under Heaven through the rites of the Three Dynasties, in the end the state will be in peril." Even when the Three Kings arose, they all took the preceding dynasties as their model and mirror; none of them ever made alterations out of self-willed reliance on their own judgment—how much less should later kings do so?

When the Xia arose, it had canons and rules to bequeath to its descendants, yet it was said: "The sage had counsels and lessons, clearly verified for securing stability and preservation." Yu 禹 did not invent them out of himself, and those who succeeded to Yu's enterprise did not dare to alter Yu's way. When the Shang arose, it warned those in official positions against the three evil customs and ten transgressions, yet it was said: "Continuing the old ways of Yu, we now follow his constant norms." Tang 湯 did not invent them out of himself, and those who succeeded to Tang's enterprise did not dare to alter Tang's way. When the Zhou arose, it established government and instituted affairs, supervising and rectifying the governing officials, yet it was said: "We look into the mirror of the two preceding dynasties." King Wu 武王 and the Duke of Zhou 周公 did not invent them out of themselves, and those who succeeded to the enterprise of Zhou did not…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
敢變周也其子孫治安咸數百年而其祖
宗之法實與之相爲終始漢承秦敝而上
討周緒迨及唐宋所因所革同道同事大
可攷見孰有不遵道而興觖道而亂者乎
漢宣綜核名實曰漢家自有制度魏相稱
上意惟條奏漢家故事及賈誼晁錯之言
而已夫漢制襲秦自三章約法十五定賦
數事外君子無取焉後世且惜其不復古
禮然而民安吏稱侔德商周者彼其所守
===
雖非三代之法實漢祖之法也史臣所稱
庶幾無愧矣有宋立國大綱雖正治具未
張神宗勵精圖治排衆論而用安石彼其
君臣之間語道則稱堯舜議法則軌周官
其所置法如經義免役保甲義倉之類至
今用之厥有成效豈無一當於時務然釀
紹聖之紛紛啓靖康之奇禍者以其所行
者安石之法也非藝祖太宗之法也引用
羣小爲一切趨事赴功之計此神宗所以
punctuated: 敢變周也。其子孫治安咸數百年，而其祖宗之法實與之相爲終始。漢承秦敝，而上討周緒，迨及唐、宋，所因所革，同道同事，大可攷見。孰有不遵道而興，觖道而亂者乎？漢宣綜核名實，曰：「漢家自有制度。」魏相稱上意，惟條奏漢家故事，及賈誼、晁錯之言而已。夫漢制襲秦，自三章約法、十五定賦數事外，君子無取焉，後世且惜其不復古禮。然而民安吏稱，侔德商、周者，彼其所守，雖非三代之法，實漢祖之法也，史臣所稱，庶幾無愧矣。有宋立國，大綱雖正，治具未張。神宗勵精圖治，排衆論而用安石。彼其君臣之間，語道則稱堯、舜，議法則軌《周官》。其所置法，如經義、免役、保甲、義倉之類，至今用之，厥有成效，豈無一當於時務？然釀紹聖之紛紛，啓靖康之奇禍者，以其所行者安石之法也，非藝祖、太宗之法也。引用羣小，爲一切趨事赴功之計，此神宗所以
translation_en:
… dare to alter those of the Zhou. Their descendants enjoyed peace and order for several hundred years in each case, and the laws of their ancestors truly accompanied them from beginning to end. The Han succeeded to the failings of the Qin while reaching back to examine the legacy of the Zhou; down to the Tang and Song, what they continued and what they reformed—sharing the same Way and the same undertakings—can largely be investigated and seen. Who has ever risen without following the Way, or fallen into disorder without departing from the Way?

Emperor Xuan of Han (Han Xuan 漢宣) comprehensively verified names and realities, saying, "The House of Han naturally has its own institutional system."
