Wei Xiang 魏相, matching the Emperor's intentions, merely submitted item-by-item memorials on the precedents of the House of Han as well as the words of Jia Yi 賈誼 and Chao Cuo 晁錯, and nothing more. Now, the institutions of the Han were inherited from the Qin; apart from a few matters such as theThree-Article Pact of Laws and fixing the land tax at one-fifteenth, superior men found nothing worth adopting in them, and later generations even regretted that they did not restore ancient rites. Yet the reason the people were at peace, officials were equal to their duties, and their virtue rivaled that of the Shang and Zhou was that what they upheld, though not the laws of the Three Dynasties, were in fact the laws of the Han founder. What the court historians praised was perhaps not undeserved!

When the Song established the state, although its great outlines were upright, its instruments of governance were not yet fully deployed. Emperor Shenzong 神宗 roused his spirit to seek good governance, brushing aside the arguments of the multitude to employ Wang Anshi 王安石. Between that ruler and his minister, when speaking of the Way they cited Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, and when discussing laws they modeled themselves on the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官). The laws they established—such as classic-meaning expositions (jingyi 經義) in the examinations, service exemption (mianyi 免役), mutual security tithings (baojia 保甲), and charitable granaries (yicang 義倉)—are used down to the present day with proven results; how could they have had nothing at all suited to the affairs of the time? Yet the reason they brewed the turmoil of the Shaosheng 紹聖 era (1094–1098) and opened the way to the extraordinary catastrophe of the Jingkang 靖康 era (1126–1127) was that what they put into practice were the laws of Anshi, not the laws of the Founding Ancestor (Yizu 藝祖, Emperor Taizu) and Emperor Taizong 太宗. Drawing in a crowd of petty men and making all manner of schemes to rush into action and chase quick results—this was why Shenzong…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
爲宋室基禍之主也夫天下一入之身也
祖宗之法元氣也氣之强弱稟於有生即
爲定命順其氣而宣燮之保聚之則身安
且壽厭其爲弱而日投丹餌將有裂膚潰
腸之患治天下者觀於身而已矣漢興立
國最强董賈之議時見施行至地節時猶
然壯固也孝宣又以信必守之故强者益
强宋弱不支北兄西父卑卑謹守范仲淹
稍變十數事即以罷去至元豐號錮疾矣
===
神宗顧欲以强政濟弱勢是尪羸之夫而
金丹之餌也其何能濟夫孝宣不敢議漢
法神宗乃輕議於宋仲淹不能得之仁宗
安石於神宗欲行所志多見其不知量也
洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
神武獨秉肅清中華
宵旰思皇怔營
憲令夫是
punctuated: 爲宋室基禍之主也。夫天下一入之身也，祖宗之法，元氣也。氣之强弱稟於有生，即爲定命。順其氣而宣燮之、保聚之，則身安且壽；厭其爲弱而日投丹餌，將有裂膚潰腸之患。治天下者觀於身而已矣。漢興，立國最强，董、賈之議時見施行，至地節時猶然壯固也。孝宣又以信必守之，故强者益强。宋弱不支，北兄西父，卑卑謹守，范仲淹稍變十數事，即以罷去，至元豐號錮疾矣。神宗顧欲以强政濟弱勢，是尪羸之夫而金丹之餌也，其何能濟？夫孝宣不敢議漢法，神宗乃輕議於宋；仲淹不能得之仁宗，安石於神宗欲行所志，多見其不知量也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，神武獨秉，肅清中華，宵旰思皇，怔營憲令，夫是
translation_en:
… became the ruler who laid the foundations of disaster for the House of Song.

Now, the empire is like the body of a single person [reading 入 as 人], and the laws of the ancestors are its vital qi (yuanqi 元氣). The strength or weakness of this qi is endowed at birth and constitutes its fixed destiny. If one follows the course of this qi, channeling and harmonizing it, preserving and gathering it, then the body will enjoy peace and longevity. If, disliking its weakness, one daily doses it with alchemical elixirs, there will be the calamity of splitting skin and ruptured bowels. Those who govern the empire need only observe the human body.

When the Han arose, the founding of the state was most vigorous. The proposals of Dong [Zhongshu 董仲舒] and Jia [Yi 賈誼] were implemented from time to time, and down to the Dijie 地節 era (69–66 BCE) the state was still robust and secure. Emperor Xiaoxuan 孝宣 (Emperor Xuan) furthermore upheld the laws with trustworthiness and certainty, so that what was strong became stronger still. The Song, by contrast, was weak and unable to sustain itself; treating the northern neighbor [Liao] as an elder brother and the western one [Xia] as a father, it humbly and cautiously maintained the status quo. When Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 slightly altered ten or so matters, he was immediately dismissed and sent away; by the Yuanfeng 元豐 era (1078–1085), the condition was called a chronic, incurable malady. Yet Shenzong 神宗 wished to rescue a weak situation with forceful governance—this was like dosing an emaciated, feeble man with golden elixirs! How could that possibly succeed? Now, Emperor Xiaoxuan did not dare to call the laws of Han into question, whereas Shenzong lightly called them into question in the Song; Zhongyan could not win approval from Renzong 仁宗, yet [Wang] An石 王安石 sought to carry out his ambitions under Shenzong—this only shows all the more how little he knew his own measure!

Vast indeed was our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi 太祖高皇帝)! Endowed alone with divine martial prowess, he cleansed and pacified the Central Lands; toiling from before dawn until after dark in anxious thought for the august realm, he labored tirelessly over the constitutional ordinances. Thus these…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
一代典章考衷千古六卿分職則周官之制三
壤定賦則夏王之法五禮節民則周禮之
遺律令採漢租庸準唐經義取宋曆法仍
勝國至於
郊社合祀
宮府一體府部相維內外輕重相制其斟酌
前代參伍
宸衷爲
聖子
===
神孫鞏萬世丕丕基者纖鉅畢舉善美兼盡蓋
我
聖祖之龍興也歷試諸艱閱世也最深其
御天也三十六禩
經制也最審其
立國也有漢之强固而道則純王其
治內也有宋之家法而國無弱政其由身心
而建之天地措之四海眞若元氣含暢於
一身之中心志虛明百體康逸毛髮膚爪
punctuated: 一代典章，考衷千古。六卿分職，則《周官》之制；三壤定賦，則夏王之法；五禮節民，則《周禮》之遺；律令採漢，租庸準唐，經義取宋，曆法仍勝國。至於郊社合祀，宮府一體，府部相維，內外輕重相制，其斟酌前代，參伍宸衷，爲聖子神孫鞏萬世丕丕基者，纖鉅畢舉，善美兼盡。蓋我聖祖之龍興也，歷試諸艱，閱世也最深；其御天也三十六禩，經制也最審；其立國也有漢之强固，而道則純王；其治內也有宋之家法，而國無弱政。其由身心而建之天地、措之四海，眞若元氣含暢於一身之中，心志虛明，百體康逸，毛髮膚爪…
translation_en: …the institutional canons of an entire dynasty, weighing and synthesizing the lessons of all antiquity. The division of offices among the Six Ministers followed the system of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan); the determination of tribute according to the three grades of soil followed the method of the Xia kings; the regulation of the people through the Five Rites preserved the legacy of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli); the statutes and ordinances were adopted from the Han, the land and labor taxes were modeled on the Tang, the exposition of the Classics in examinations was taken from the Song, and the calendrical system was retained from the conquered Yuan dynasty. As for the joint sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the integration of the Inner Palace and the Outer Court into a single body, the mutual coordination between the Five Chief Military Commissions and the Six Ministries, and the system of checks and balances between inner and outer, weighty and light authorities—in deliberating upon previous dynasties and synthesizing them within the imperial mind to consolidate a magnificent foundation for ten thousand generations of sacred sons and divine grandsons—every detail, small and great, was completely instituted, and both goodness and beauty were fully achieved. Indeed, when our Sacred Ancestor rose like a dragon, he experienced all manner of hardships and knew the world most deeply; during the thirty-six years he reigned on the throne, he planned and established institutions most carefully. In founding the state, he possessed the strength and solidity of the Han, yet his Way was that of a pure True King; in governing the inner court, he maintained the family regulations of the Song, yet the state suffered no weak governance. Extending from his own person and mind, he established this order between Heaven and Earth and implemented it throughout the Four Seas—truly like primordial vitality suffusing and flowing freely throughout a single body, where the mind and will are clear and luminous, all the limbs and organs are healthy and at ease, and the hair, skin, and nails…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
無不潤澤其綜之有要行之無壅又若肢
體之咸隸於心心運於中手持足行臂指
相使而無壅腫不通之患當其時
天人協順華夷尊親
道化蒸融禎祥輻輳
身致太平法垂
後世至明備也嗣是
成祖繼統而潤色之
列聖基隆而敬守之
===
一代治法纘為治統肆我
皇上
冲齡睿質
握紀承休
嗣極以來孜孜化理與二三元老飭法
興治不遺餘力是故禋祀
郊廟豫協
慈闈
仁孝孚矣日
punctuated: 無不潤澤。其綜之有要，行之無壅，又若肢體之咸隸於心，心運於中，手持足行，臂指相使，而無壅腫不通之患。當其時，天人協順，華夷尊親，道化蒸融，禎祥輻輳，身致太平，法垂後世，至明備也。嗣是，成祖繼統而潤色之，列聖基隆而敬守之，一代治法，纘為治統。肆我皇上，冲齡睿質，握紀承休，嗣極以來，孜孜化理，與二三元老飭法興治，不遺餘力。是故禋祀郊廟，豫協慈闈，仁孝孚矣；日
translation_en: … none failing to be nourished and moistened. In grasping the essentials and carrying them out without obstruction, it was also as though the limbs and body were all subordinate to the mind: with the mind operating at the center, the hands held and the feet walked, the arms and fingers employing one another without the affliction of swelling or blockage. At that time, Heaven and humanity were in harmonious accord, Chinese and non-Chinese alike showed reverence and affection, moral transformation permeated and blended all things, and auspicious omens converged like spokes at a hub. In his own person he brought about Great Peace, and his laws were handed down to later generations—most luminous and complete! Thereafter, the Chengzu Emperor succeeded to the line of rule and embellished them, and the successive sacred emperors built upon the thriving foundation and reverently guarded them, so that the governing laws of an entire dynasty were carried forward as a continuous tradition of governance. Now Our Sovereign, endowed with sagely qualities at a tender age, grasps the imperial cords and inherits the dynastic blessings. Since ascending the throne, he has been tirelessly devoted to transformative governance, sparing no effort alongside two or three senior statesmen to rectify the laws and promote good rule. Therefore, in offering pure sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, and in bringing joy and harmony to the quarters of the Empress Dowager, his benevolence and filial piety have inspired trust; daily …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
御經筵脩明
典制治本正矣懲貪汰冗卻貢蠲逋
恩澤流矣臣工振肅民物昌阜夷酋款貢
治化隆矣蓋法
聖祖之法而治亦
聖祖之治守
成業而光
前烈先後無兩廼執事舉漢宋之故事籌
昭代之法程若曰法敝相沿治湮所忽誠深慮
===
也夫法之立也未始不肅而終乎弛人之
行法也未始不奮而卒乎怠通變之際聖
人兢兢彼覩乎吏治之偷窳不如先代之
儼翼民俗之澆漓不如先代之龐固邊鄙
之繹騷夷狄之匪茹不如先代之烝皇孔
淑也遂謂法不足以繩天下各以所見而
爭議法聽其言則甚美實無當於事而祇
以取擾天下臣民無所遵守疑耳目而亂
心志則信乎議法之難也攷漢宋往事可
punctuated:
御經筵，脩明典制，治本正矣；懲貪汰冗，卻貢蠲逋，恩澤流矣；臣工振肅，民物昌阜，夷酋款貢，治化隆矣。蓋法聖祖之法，而治亦聖祖之治；守成業而光前烈，先後無兩。廼執事舉漢、宋之故事，籌昭代之法程，若曰法敝相沿、治湮所忽，誠深慮也。

夫法之立也，未始不肅，而終乎弛；人之行法也，未始不奮，而卒乎怠。通變之際，聖人兢兢。彼覩乎吏治之偷窳，不如先代之儼翼；民俗之澆漓，不如先代之龐固；邊鄙之繹騷、夷狄之匪茹，不如先代之烝皇孔淑也，遂謂法不足以繩天下，各以所見而爭議法。聽其言則甚美，實無當於事，而祇以取擾，天下臣民無所遵守，疑耳目而亂心志，則信乎議法之難也！攷漢、宋往事，可
translation_en:
…attends the Classics Mat and clarifies the institutional statutes, so the foundation of governance has been rectified; he punishes the corrupt and eliminates superfluous officials, rejects tribute gifts and remits tax arrears, so his benevolent grace flows forth; officials are roused to discipline, the people and all things flourish, and foreign chieftains submit in tribute, so transformative governance has reached a pinnacle. Indeed, he takes the laws of the Sacred Ancestor as his model, and his governance is likewise the governance of the Sacred Ancestor; in preserving the established enterprise and glorifying the achievements of his predecessors, past and present are without peer. Yet Your Excellency cites the precedents of the Han and Song dynasties to deliberate upon the legal standards of our illustrious dynasty, as if to say that the laws have grown worn out through long continuation and that good governance is submerged by what is neglected—this is truly a profound concern.

Now, when laws are first established, they never fail to be strict, yet they end in laxity; when men implement the laws, they never fail to be energetic at first, yet they end in indolence. At the juncture of continuity and change, the sages are ever cautious. Those who observe that official administration is shiftless and decadent, not matching the dignified reverence of former generations; that popular customs are thin and degenerate, not matching the simple solidity of former generations; and that the frontiers are in constant turmoil and the foreign tribes unsubmissive, not matching the grand and thorough goodness of former generations, thereupon claim that the laws are insufficient to regulate the empire, and each according to his own views clamors to debate the laws. When one listens to their words, they sound most admirable, yet in reality they are unsuited to practical affairs and serve only to invite disturbance. Officials and people throughout the empire are left with nothing to abide by, confounding their ears and eyes and throwing their minds and wills into confusion—truly, then, how difficult it is to debate the laws! Examining past events of the Han and Song dynasties, one can…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
見矣今夫車之宜於陸也舟之宜於水也
彼趨燕而南帆適越而北其轍行愈速而
失道愈遠曰舟車之罪也誰不以爲狂哉
不責行法之人而議法之敝何以異此今
天下臣工確守
憲典皇皇汲汲不敢怠遑孰敢有辯言亂政者
然敝生於積久政壅於習玩者勢之所趨
也玆非法之罪也所以奉行之者有未善
耳不怠不擾振而起之則有
===
聖祖之法在是故吏治之玩也審官之法不核
也儆官邪明廢置玩者脩矣而馭吏之法
勿之易也士習之靡也作人之教不張也
杜干進抑浮薄靡者起矣學校之法勿之
易也兵之不精也倡勇敢足資糧蒐之而
已御戎之法勿之變也民之不安也去其
擾民而已聯戶比甲梳櫛而徽纆之朘削
者售矣非古也四夷之不款也固吾之邊
圉而已喜功生事啓繒帛之邀其漸不可
punctuated: 見矣。今夫車之宜於陸也，舟之宜於水也，彼趨燕而南帆，適越而北其轍，行愈速而失道愈遠，曰：「舟車之罪也。」誰不以爲狂哉？不責行法之人，而議法之敝，何以異此？今天下臣工，確守憲典，皇皇汲汲，不敢怠遑，孰敢有辯言亂政者？然敝生於積久，政壅於習玩者，勢之所趨也。玆非法之罪也，所以奉行之者有未善耳。不怠不擾，振而起之，則有聖祖之法在。是故吏治之玩也，審官之法不核也，儆官邪，明廢置，玩者脩矣，而馭吏之法勿之易也；士習之靡也，作人之教不張也，杜干進，抑浮薄，靡者起矣，學校之法勿之易也；兵之不精也，倡勇敢，足資糧，蒐之而已，御戎之法勿之變也；民之不安也，去其擾民而已，聯戶比甲，梳櫛而徽纆之，朘削者售矣，非古也；四夷之不款也，固吾之邊圉而已，喜功生事，啓繒帛之邀，其漸不可…
translation_en: …be seen. Now, a carriage is suited for land, and a boat is suited for water. Suppose someone heading for Yan sets sail southward, or someone bound for Yue directs his wheel-tracks northward—the faster he travels, the farther he strays from his destination. If he then says, "This is the fault of the boat and the carriage," who would not think him mad? To refrain from holding accountable those who administer the laws, while instead debating the defects of the laws themselves—how is that any different from this? Today, officials throughout the realm steadfastly uphold the constitutional statutes, working anxiously and tirelessly without daring to be negligent or idle; who would dare use specious arguments to throw governance into confusion? Yet that abuses arise over a long accumulation of time, and that governance becomes obstructed through habitual laxity, is the natural tendency of circumstances. This is not the fault of the laws; it is merely that the manner in which they are carried out is less than optimal. To neither grow lax nor cause disruption, but to rouse and invigorate administration—for this, the laws of the Sacred Ancestor are already in place. Therefore, when official administration grows lax, it is because the methods for evaluating officials are not rigorously verified; if we warn against official malpractice and make clear the criteria for dismissal and appointment, the lax will be reformed, and the laws for governing officials need not be altered. When the customs of the literati grow decadent, it is because the teachings that cultivate men of talent are not actively promoted; if we block opportunistic office-seeking and curb superficiality and frivolity, the decadent will be roused, and the laws for the schools need not be altered. When the troops are not elite, we need only encourage bravery, ensure sufficient provisions and pay, and drill them; the laws for commanding the military need not be changed. When the common people are not at peace, we need only remove what disturbs them; binding households into tithing groups, combing through them and tying them down as if with cords, merely allows extortionists to succeed—this is not the way of antiquity. When the surrounding non-Chinese peoples do not submit in tribute, we need only strengthen our frontier defenses; delighting in military exploits and stirring up trouble, thereby inviting demands for silks and tribute gifts, initiates a trend that must not be…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
長非古也凡一切行法之中皆確守
成憲而不敢紊而尤深求立法之意不敢於法
外有所牽合焉出於法者舉成法以正之
故有據而不疑怠於法者振其法以作之
故有漸而不驚舍此不務而輒以己意橫
驚振迅曰立法曰善治云者滋擾而已愚
嘗俯仰古今法久則敝雖三代聖王不能
制其流而守成之君不恃其治安而玩以
廢法則騁其私智而輕以變法不知重熙
===
累洽之後賢人君子之振培雖多而奸宄
不無侵蝕生齒之蕃殖雖夥而物力不無
凋耗譬諸強仕以往者其膚革充盈智識
廣覽非不加於曩時乃精氣之日蝕月銷
者亦不少矣於此而圖攝生葆壽要在用
靜而不用動漢宣用靜者也神宗用動者
也故收効異也我
國家治安二百餘年是
祖法之維持古所希覯者顧忠賢之協賛多矣
punctuated: 長，非古也。凡一切行法之中，皆確守成憲而不敢紊，而尤深求立法之意，不敢於法外有所牽合焉。出於法者，舉成法以正之，故有據而不疑；怠於法者，振其法以作之，故有漸而不驚。舍此不務，而輒以己意橫驚振迅，曰「立法」、曰「善治」云者，滋擾而已。愚嘗俯仰古今，法久則敝，雖三代聖王不能制其流。而守成之君，不恃其治安而玩以廢法，則騁其私智而輕以變法。不知重熙累洽之後，賢人君子之振培雖多，而奸宄不無侵蝕；生齒之蕃殖雖夥，而物力不無凋耗。譬諸強仕以往者，其膚革充盈、智識廣覽，非不加於曩時，乃精氣之日蝕月銷者，亦不少矣。於此而圖攝生葆壽，要在用靜而不用動。漢宣用靜者也，神宗用動者也，故收効異也。我國家治安二百餘年，是祖法之維持，古所希覯者。顧忠賢之協賛多矣，
translation_en:
… encouraged; this is not the way of antiquity. In all aspects of enforcing the laws, one should firmly adhere to the established constitutions without daring to disrupt them, and even more so, deeply seek out the intent behind the establishment of the laws, not daring to make forced applications beyond the law. For those who overstep the law, bring forth the established laws to correct them, so that there is a firm basis without doubt; for those who are lax toward the law, invigorate the laws to rouse them, so that progress is gradual without causing alarm. To abandon this and not attend to it, instead arbitrarily using one's own ideas to recklessly startle and shake things up—calling it "establishing laws" or "good governance"—merely creates further disturbance.

I have reflected on antiquity and the present: when laws endure for a long time, they inevitably deteriorate; even the sage kings of the Three Dynasties could not halt their decline. Yet sovereigns who inherit an established realm, if they do not presume upon peace and stability to neglectfully abandon the laws, then they indulge their private cleverness to lightly alter the laws. They do not realize that after generations of cumulative peace and harmony, although the nurturing and cultivation by worthy men and gentlemen has been abundant, villains and traitors have not failed to erode the state; although the population has multiplied greatly, material resources have not failed to be depleted and exhausted. Compare this to a person past the age of forty: their flesh and skin are full, and their knowledge and experience are broad—not failing to surpass what they were in earlier days—yet the daily and monthly waning of their vital energy is also not inconsiderable. Under such circumstances, if one seeks to nourish life and preserve longevity, the key lies in employing quiescence rather than activity. Emperor Xuan of Han (Han Xuan 漢宣) was one who employed quiescence; Emperor Shenzong of Song (Shenzong 神宗) was one who employed activity; therefore, the results they reaped were different.

Our Dynasty has enjoyed peace and order for over two hundred years; this maintenance through the ancestral laws is something rarely seen in antiquity. Yet while the supportive assistance of loyal and worthy officials has been abundant, …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
生齒之蕃殖廣矣其陰蝕潜耗容亦有之
亦用靜時也則蕩滌邪穢保聚太和以綿
國脉於無疆者實在於守法而不在於變法
然守法非飭法不可此漢宣之綜核所以
爲善守而輕變如神宗雖有一二小善而
卒無救於其敗甚不可也然天下之事易
怠忽而難振作所謂振作與紛更事若相
類而實不同况習之錮也而人心之私也
有無借作新之說以濟其紛更者乎有無
===
借避紛更以文其苟安怠廢者乎是皆以
私智處事而不以公心視天下故不可不
察也宋儒之言曰祖宗德澤不可恃法度
不可廢然則緣祖宗德意以守祖宗家法
不尤盡善盡美乎我
祖宗功德遠企商周有以延億萬年無疆之緒
聖天子躬行仁儉
厲精圖治
明君賢臣作新化理眞千載一時區區宣帝神
punctuated: 生齒之蕃殖廣矣，其陰蝕潜耗容亦有之，亦用靜時也。則蕩滌邪穢、保聚太和，以綿國脉於無疆者，實在於守法而不在於變法。然守法非飭法不可，此漢宣之綜核所以爲善守；而輕變如神宗，雖有一二小善，而卒無救於其敗，甚不可也。然天下之事，易怠忽而難振作，所謂振作與紛更，事若相類而實不同。况習之錮也，而人心之私也，有無借作新之說以濟其紛更者乎？有無借避紛更以文其苟安怠廢者乎？是皆以私智處事，而不以公心視天下，故不可不察也。宋儒之言曰：「祖宗德澤不可恃，法度不可廢。」然則緣祖宗德意以守祖宗家法，不尤盡善盡美乎？我祖宗功德遠企商、周，有以延億萬年無疆之緒；聖天子躬行仁儉，厲精圖治，明君賢臣，作新化理，眞千載一時，區區宣帝、神
translation_en: … and the population has multiplied broadly, yet unseen erosion and hidden depletion may also be present; this, too, is a time for employing quietude. Thus, to wash away evil and filth, and to preserve and gather supreme harmony so as to prolong the lifeblood of the state without bound, truly lies in upholding the laws rather than in altering the laws. Yet upholding the laws cannot be done without rectifying the enforcement of the laws. This is why Emperor Xuan of Han's comprehensive verification of nominal and actual performance constituted a good upholding of the laws; whereas lightly altering them like Shenzong, even if there were one or two minor merits, in the end could not save him from his failure, and is utterly inadmissible. However, in the affairs of the world, it is easy to become lax and neglectful and difficult to rouse to vigorous action. What is called rousing to vigorous action and what is called disorderly alteration appear similar in practice, yet in reality they are different. Moreover, given the entrenchment of habit and the selfishness of human hearts, are there not those who borrow the doctrine of renewal to further their disorderly alterations? Are there not those who borrow the avoidance of disorderly alteration to gloss over their complacent ease and lazy neglect? All of these handle affairs through private cleverness and do not view the world with a public-spirited mind; therefore, this must be carefully examined. A Song Confucian said: "The virtuous bounty of the ancestors cannot be relied upon passively, and the laws and institutions cannot be abandoned." If that is so, then following the virtuous intentions of the ancestors so as to uphold the family laws of the ancestors—is this not even more consummate in goodness and beauty? The merits and virtues of our Imperial Ancestors reach far back to match those of the Shang and Zhou dynasties, having the means to extend a boundless lineage for hundreds of millions of years. Look upon our Sacred Son of Heaven, who personally practices benevolence and frugality and rouses his spirit to seek good governance; with an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers renewing transformative governance, this is truly a once-in-a-thousand-years opportunity. How could the petty affairs of Emperor Xuan and Shen…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
宗事奚足爲比
第二問
楊先春
同考試官訓導周批天人之理未易言也子能
辨析精微直窺閫奧末復指陳時事剴切明悉忠愛之意藹然
聖天子敬天勤民之心殆無餘蘊且揚厲我
考試官敎諭倫批識見博洽詞藻清新可謂
考試官敎諭譙批雅馴條暢文之有典則者
帝王所以懋德凝圖者豈有他哉亦曰存
===
之爲勅天之實心舉之爲憲天之實政而
彌文不與焉者也何謂實心夙夜基命居
安思危履祥若災無一念弗純乎天者是
已何謂實政側身脩行不恃其未危而恃
吾有待危之方不恃其無災而恃吾有弭
災之道無一事不協乎天者是已內脩於
心外勤其民古之帝王所以斡旋造化統
一人羣者由此道也苟不求諸身心政術
之間而徒規規於粉飾鋪張之具卽條格
punctuated:
宗事，奚足爲比！

第二問

楊先春
同考試官訓導周批：天人之理，未易言也。子能辨析精微，直窺閫奧，末復指陳時事，剴切明悉，忠愛之意藹然〔？〕聖天子敬天勤民之心，殆無餘蘊，且揚厲我〔？〕。
考試官敎諭倫批：識見博洽，詞藻清新，可謂〔？〕。
考試官敎諭譙批：雅馴條暢，文之有典則者。

帝王所以懋德凝圖者，豈有他哉？亦曰：存之爲勅天之實心，舉之爲憲天之實政，而彌文不與焉者也。何謂實心？夙夜基命，居安思危，履祥若災，無一念弗純乎天者是已。何謂實政？側身脩行，不恃其未危，而恃吾有待危之方；不恃其無災，而恃吾有弭災之道，無一事不協乎天者是已。內脩於心，外勤其民，古之帝王所以斡旋造化、統一人羣者，由此道也。苟不求諸身心政術之間，而徒規規於粉飾鋪張之具，卽條格
translation_en:
… the affairs of [Emperor Xuan of Han and] Emperor Shenzong [of Song]—how could they be worthy of comparison!

Second Question

Yang Xianchun 楊先春
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhou comments: The principles of Heaven and humanity are not easy to speak of. You are able to analyze the subtleties, peering straight into their innermost depths, and at the end you further point out and set forth contemporary affairs in a trenchant, clear, and thorough manner, brimming with loyal affection; [in extolling our] Sacred Son of Heaven's mind of revering Heaven and being diligent toward the people, almost nothing is left unexpressed [?].
Examiner and Instructor Lun comments: Broad and well-informed in insight, fresh and pure in diction; it may be called [?].
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: Refined, well-ordered, and fluent—writing that possesses classical standards.

How could that whereby emperors and kings cultivate virtue and consolidate the imperial enterprise be anything else? It is simply this: preserved within, it is the sincere mind of heeding Heaven's admonitions; put into practice, it is the substantive governance of modeling oneself on Heaven—and empty formalities have no part in it. What is meant by a sincere mind? Day and night establishing the Mandate, thinking of danger while dwelling in security, treating auspicious signs as though they were calamities, with not a single thought failing to be purely aligned with Heaven—this is it. What is meant by substantive governance? Humbly cultivating one's conduct, relying not on the fact that danger has not yet arrived, but on our having the means to meet danger; relying not on the absence of calamities, but on our having the Way to avert calamities, with not a single affair failing to harmonize with Heaven—this is it. Cultivating the mind within and being diligent toward the people without: that whereby the emperors and kings of antiquity turned the樞 of creation and unified humankind was by following this Way. title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
日詳詔令數下人將玩之弗信矣而況於
天乎知此則古帝王之克謹天戒曁我
聖祖
皇上之所以
祗德格天者可仰窺萬一而洪範春秋之義
甽如也嘗謂天地爲萬民父母天子者代
天子之其胥爲一體若心志膚革聯貫而
不離互爲保愛若榮衞脉絡宣變而罔間
故天道遠矣祁寒暑雨必感於民民雖眇
===
矣忻戚悲愉常徹於天天之愛民甚矣豈
其使一人侈然於民上而不知所以恤之
哉君人者必體天心以爲吾心而又保合
民心以順天心天戒未形也不敢曰天命
在我而懼天之忘我天戒有象也不敢曰
天道之適然而脩人事之當然蓋無時無
之而非天也古之善言天人之際者必稽
洪範其言休徵曰肅時雨乂時暘哲時燠
謀時寒聖時風其言咎徵曰狂恒雨僭恒
punctuated:
日詳、詔令數下，人將玩之弗信矣，而況於天乎？知此，則古帝王之克謹天戒，曁我聖祖、皇上之所以祗德格天者，可仰窺萬一，而《洪範》、《春秋》之義甽如也。
嘗謂天地爲萬民父母，天子者，代天子之。其胥爲一體，若心志膚革聯貫而不離；互爲保愛，若榮衞脉絡宣變而罔間。故天道遠矣，祁寒暑雨必感於民；民雖眇矣，忻戚悲愉常徹於天。天之愛民甚矣，豈其使一人侈然於民上，而不知所以恤之哉？君人者，必體天心以爲吾心，而又保合民心以順天心。天戒未形也，不敢曰天命在我，而懼天之忘我；天戒有象也，不敢曰天道之適然，而脩人事之當然。蓋無時無之而非天也。
古之善言天人之際者，必稽《洪範》。其言休徵曰：肅，時雨；乂，時暘；哲，時燠；謀，時寒；聖，時風。其言咎徵曰：狂，恒雨；僭，恒
translation_en:
… become more detailed by the day and edicts are issued repeatedly, people will treat them lightly and put no faith in them—how much more so Heaven! Understanding this, one may catch a slight glimpse of how the emperors and kings of antiquity were able to heed the admonitions of Heaven, and how our Sacred Ancestor and His Majesty the Emperor have moved Heaven through their reverent virtue; and the meanings of the "Great Plan" (Hongfan) and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) will be luminously clear [?].

I have heard it said that Heaven and Earth are the parents of the myriad people, and the Son of Heaven governs them as a son on Heaven's behalf. Their mutual integration as a single body is like the mind, will, skin, and flesh being linked together without separation; their mutual protection and care are like the nutritive essence, defensive qi, and vessels circulating and responding without interruption. Thus, although the Way of Heaven is distant, bitter cold and sultry rain inevitably affect the people; and although the people are insignificant, their joys and sorrows, griefs and pleasures constantly reach up to Heaven. Heaven's love for the people is profound indeed! How could it place One Man arrogantly above the people without his knowing how to show them compassion? He who rules over men must embody the mind of Heaven as his own mind, and furthermore preserve and unite the minds of the people in order to comply with the mind of Heaven. When Heaven's admonitions have not yet taken form, he does not dare say, "The Mandate of Heaven rests with me," but instead fears that Heaven may have forgotten him; when Heaven's admonitions manifest in signs, he does not dare say, "This is a mere coincidence of the Way of Heaven," but instead cultivates what ought to be done in human affairs. For there is no time and no place that is not Heaven.

In antiquity, those who spoke well of the relationship between Heaven and humanity always consulted the "Great Plan" (Hongfan). Speaking of auspicious verifications, it says: "Respectfulness is verified by timely rain; orderliness, by timely sunshine; wisdom, by timely warmth; deliberation, by timely cold; sageliness, by timely wind." Speaking of inauspicious verifications, it says: "Wildness is verified by constant rain; presumption, by constant …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
暘豫恒燠急恒寒蒙恒風以五行配五事
休咎各以類應其說精矣乃孔子作春秋
書災異不書事應揆之洪範庶徵之說不
必盡然者玆曷故哉夫人君之事天猶事
親天之愛君猶愛子故義方可教不廢於
克家之子其或弗豫於衷而徵色而發聲
而勞之威之要之不失爲愛而爲愉色爲
順志爲愛其所愛以求自媚於親者亦不
一其道故未然而防者父道也亦天道也
===
先意承志者子道也亦君道也如曰某事
失某災應是父之用愛發於聲者不移於
色徵於色者不移於聲威之勞之舉不相
通此慈父不能瑣瑣於其子天烏得而用
之於君若書大雨必求事之狂書大旱必
求事之僭書無冰必求事之豫書隕霜殺
菽六鷁退飛必求事之急與蒙卽有偶合
所舛必多非所以訓也故春秋不書事應
者以此胡安國氏又謂春秋雖不書事應
punctuated: 暘、豫恒燠、急恒寒、蒙恒風。」以五行配五事，休咎各以類應，其說精矣。乃孔子作《春秋》，書災異不書事應，揆之《洪範》「庶徵」之說，不必盡然者，玆曷故哉？夫人君之事天猶事親，天之愛君猶愛子。故義方可教，不廢於克家之子；其或弗豫於衷，而徵色、而發聲，而勞之、威之，要之不失爲愛。而爲愉色、爲順志、爲愛其所愛，以求自媚於親者，亦不一其道。故未然而防者，父道也，亦天道也；先意承志者，子道也，亦君道也。如曰某事失、某災應，是父之用愛，發於聲者不移於色，徵於色者不移於聲，威之、勞之，舉不相通。此慈父不能瑣瑣於其子，天烏得而用之於君？若書大雨，必求事之狂；書大旱，必求事之僭；書無冰，必求事之豫；書隕霜殺菽、六鷁退飛，必求事之急與蒙。卽有偶合，所舛必多，非所以訓也。故《春秋》不書事應者，以此。胡安國氏又謂：「《春秋》雖不書事應，
translation_en:
… constant sunshine; indolence, by constant warmth; rashness, by constant cold; and obtuseness, by constant wind." By matching the Five Phases with the Five Conducts, so that auspicious and inauspicious signs each respond according to their kind, this doctrine is subtle indeed. Yet when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), he recorded calamities and anomalies without recording the corresponding human affairs. Measured against the doctrine of the "Various Verifications" in the "Great Plan" (Hongfan), they do not necessarily tally in every respect—why is this?

Now, a ruler's serving Heaven is like serving his parents, and Heaven's loving the ruler is like loving a son. Therefore, instruction in righteous ways is not neglected even for a son capable of sustaining the family; and should the parent feel displeasure at heart and show it in his countenance, or utter it in his voice, or toil him, or overawe him, in sum it never ceases to be out of love. Likewise, puts on a cheerful countenance, complies with his wishes, and loves what he loves in seeking to endear oneself to one's parents—there is more than one way to do this. Thus, to guard against things before they happen is the way of a father, and also the way of Heaven; to anticipate wishes and carry out intentions is the way of a son, and also the way of a ruler.

If one were to say that a certain failing in affairs is answered by a certain calamity, this would mean that in a father's exercise of love, what is uttered in his voice never shifts to his countenance, and what is shown in his countenance never shifts to his voice, and overawing him and toiling him have no connection with one another at all. Even a loving father could not deal sofussily and piecemeal with his son—how then could Heaven employ such a method toward the ruler? If, whenever heavy rain is recorded, one must seek an affair of wildness; whenever a great drought is recorded, one must seek an affair of arrogance; whenever the absence of ice is recorded, one must seek an affair of indolence; and whenever frost falling and killing the beans or six water-birds flying backward is recorded, one must seek affairs of rashness and obtuseness—even if there are occasional coincidences, the discrepancies will inevitably be many, and this is no way to provide instruction. Therefore, it is for this reason that the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record the corresponding human affairs.

Master Hu Anguo 胡安國 also said: "Although the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record the corresponding affairs, …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而事應具存如雷電雨雪兆鍾巫之難春
雨木冰兆沙隨之變日食星孛皆有徵應
是春秋志災之意未嘗不與範同特不質
言所應則夫子之慮深矣是故九年之水
豈堯之失德致之而洚水警予堯不以黎
民於變有怠心焉此所以則天也七年之
旱豈湯之失政致之而六事責躬湯不以
九圍承式有侈心焉此所以配命也宣王
赫然中興胡爲有旱魃之虐而靡有孑遺
===
形諸雲漢之什者兢兢焉此所以過曆也
蓋其始也畏天而其終也回天惟其遇災
而懼故能反災爲祥皇皇乎聖喆弗可尚
也已後世誣天旱爲乾封謂天變不足畏
者無論已如京房劉向諸人日討事應以
談災異是泥洪範之旨而失之而僅得春
秋之意者惟日奏水旱之魏相奏四方災
異之李沆而已治之不古無惑也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
punctuated: 而事應具存，如雷電雨雪兆鍾巫之難，春雨木冰兆沙隨之變，日食、星孛皆有徵應。是《春秋》志災之意未嘗不與《範》同，特不質言所應，則夫子之慮深矣。是故九年之水，豈堯之失德致之？而「洚水警予」，堯不以黎民於變有怠心焉，此所以則天也。七年之旱，豈湯之失政致之？而六事責躬，湯不以九圍承式有侈心焉，此所以配命也。宣王赫然中興，胡爲有旱魃之虐？而「靡有孑遺」，形諸《雲漢》之什者兢兢焉，此所以過曆也。蓋其始也畏天，而其終也回天；惟其遇災而懼，故能反災爲祥。皇皇乎聖喆，弗可尚也已。後世誣天旱爲乾封，謂天變不足畏者，無論已。如京房、劉向諸人，日討事應以談災異，是泥《洪範》之旨而失之；而僅得《春秋》之意者，惟日奏水旱之魏相、奏四方災異之李沆而已。治之不古，無惑也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝
translation_en:
…yet the corresponding events are fully present within it: for instance, thunder, lightning, rain, and snow portended the disaster at Zhongwu; spring rain and ice-coated trees portended the upheaval at Shasui; and solar eclipses and comets all had their verified correspondences. Thus, the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in recording calamities was by no means different from that of the "Great Plan" (Hongfan); it merely refrained from explicitly stating what they corresponded to, which shows how profound the Master's consideration was.

Therefore, how could the nine years of floods have been brought about by any lapse in virtue on the part of Yao? Yet, saying "the inundating waters are a warning to me," Yao did not allow his heart to grow lax just because the black-haired people had been transformed; this was how he modeled himself on Heaven. How could the seven years of drought have been brought about by any failure in governance on the part of Tang? Yet, reproaching himself on six counts, Tang did not allow his heart to grow arrogant just because the nine regions took him as their model; this was how he matched the Mandate. King Xuan achieved a glorious restoration—why then was there the tyranny of the drought-demon? Yet the cry that "there is not a single survivor left," as expressed in the ode "Yunhan" (Milky Way), showed his cautious trepidation; this was how the dynasty's allotted span was exceeded. Indeed, in the beginning they stood in awe of Heaven, and in the end they turned Heaven's will around; precisely because they felt fear upon encountering calamity, they were able to turn calamity into auspiciousness. Illustrious indeed were those sage and wise rulers—nothing can surpass them!

In later ages, those who falsely passed off a heavenly drought as a "Dry Feng Sacrifice," or claimed that heavenly anomalies were not worth fearing, need not even be discussed. As for men like Jing Fang and Liu Xiang, who daily investigated corresponding events in order to discourse on calamities and anomalies, they clung rigidly to the purport of the "Great Plan" and thereby lost its true meaning. Meanwhile, those who merely grasped the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals were none other than Wei Xiang, who daily memorialized on floods and droughts, and Li Hang, who memorialized on calamities and anomalies from all quarters. That governance has not matched antiquity is no wonder.

Humbly reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
神聖開天
欽明立極
講洪範庶徵之應曰天道微妙難知人事感
通易見脩德則災害不生不脩則災異疊
見
睿知聖謨誠折衷箕孔洞悉天人之際矣
至治休徵溢爲嘉祥未易殫述而於七曜紊度
京師大旱惕然靡寧
求直言
===
錄獄囚不一而足而又有
精誠錄其旨大約有三以
敬天首焉博採經傳旁及左國用備
省覽昭然顧諟之衷也有
存心錄凡祭祀之有感於災祥者皆載焉思
感召之由求消復之道以祗
天戒惕然時幾之勅也其所以
欽崇畏慎者何其詳且切也故運諸
淵衷沛於事業貽之
punctuated: 神聖開天，欽明立極。講《洪範》庶徵之應，曰：「天道微妙難知，人事感通易見。脩德則災害不生，不脩則災異疊見。」睿知聖謨，誠折衷箕、孔，洞悉天人之際矣！至治休徵，溢爲嘉祥，未易殫述；而於七曜紊度、京師大旱，惕然靡寧，求直言、錄獄囚，不一而足。而又有《精誠錄》，其旨大約有三，以敬天首焉，博採經傳，旁及《左》、《國》，用備省覽，昭然顧諟之衷也。有《存心錄》，凡祭祀之有感於災祥者皆載焉，思感召之由，求消復之道，以祗天戒，惕然時幾之勅也。其所以欽崇畏慎者，何其詳且切也！故運諸淵衷，沛於事業，貽之
translation_en: …with divine sagacity opened the Mandate of Heaven, and with reverent intelligence established the supreme standard. In discussing the responses of the "Various Verifications" in the "Great Plan" (Hongfan), he said: "The Way of Heaven is subtle and hard to know, whereas the sympathetic resonance of human affairs is easy to see. If one cultivates virtue, calamities and harm will not arise; if one does not cultivate it, calamities and anomalies will repeatedly appear." His perspicacious wisdom and sacred counsels truly struck a balance between Jizi and Confucius, thoroughly penetrating the boundary between Heaven and man! The auspicious verifications of his supreme governance overflowed into felicitous omens that cannot easily be recounted in full; yet when the seven luminaries fell out of their regular degrees or when a great drought struck the capital, he was filled with trepidation and knew no peace, seeking forthright remonstrance and reviewing the cases of imprisoned convicts, not merely once or twice. Moreover, there was the Record of Utmost Sincerity (Jingcheng lu), the purport of which consists broadly of three parts, headed by "Revering Heaven"; it gathered widely from the Classics and commentaries, extending laterally to the Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu), so as to provide for his personal inspection—a clear manifestation of his inner heart that kept its gaze upon Heaven's bright mandate. And there was the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu), in which all sacrificial matters bearing upon the sympathetic resonance of calamities and auspicious signs were recorded, reflecting upon the causes by which they were summoned and seeking the way to dispel misfortune and restore harmony so as to respect the admonitions of Heaven—a fearful attentiveness to the caution of every moment and subtle incipience. How detailed and earnest were the means by which he showed reverent exaltation and fearful caution! Therefore, revolving these thoughts in his profound heart, he poured them forth into his grand enterprises, bequeathing them to…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
典則布之四方濬祥集福民殷物阜蓋二百
餘禩而海內宴如也執事謂
功德過堯湯而周宣不足侔者旨哉言乎肆我
皇上躬
上聖之資撫
郅隆之運
御極以來
懋學親賢內寧外謐庶幾哉我
太祖配天之治矣頃因
===
玄象示異雨澤愆期
京輔疫沴之災四方水旱之
奏致塵
宸慮
宮廷有禱同成湯桑林之敬賑恤有
詔敷帝堯不虐之仁羣臣有
勅切周宣雲漢之憂所以焦勞其心思交儆乎
中外者亦至詳且切粹然一我
太祖憲天之心也乃執事猶欲因
punctuated: 典則，布之四方，濬祥集福，民殷物阜，蓋二百餘禩而海內宴如也。執事謂功德過堯、湯，而周宣不足侔者，旨哉言乎！肆我皇上躬上聖之資，撫郅隆之運，御極以來，懋學親賢，內寧外謐，庶幾哉我太祖配天之治矣。頃因玄象示異，雨澤愆期，京輔疫沴之災，四方水旱之奏，致塵宸慮。宮廷有禱，同成湯桑林之敬；賑恤有詔，敷帝堯不虐之仁；羣臣有勅，切周宣雲漢之憂。所以焦勞其心思、交儆乎中外者，亦至詳且切，粹然一我太祖憲天之心也。乃執事猶欲因
translation_en:
…canons and regulations, and promulgated throughout the four quarters; thus he drew forth auspiciousness and gathered blessings, so that the people were prosperous and goods abundant, and for more than two hundred years the realm within the seas has been at peace. When Your Excellency says that his merit and virtue surpassed those of Yao and Tang, and that King Xuan of Zhou is not worthy to be compared with him—how profound are those words!

Now Our Sovereign embodies the endowments of supreme sageliness and presides over an era of the utmost flourishing. Since ascending the throne, he has devoted himself to learning and drawn close to the worthy; within, the realm is tranquil and without, it is at peace—approaching indeed the Heaven-matching governance of Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu). Recently, because the celestial phenomena have displayed anomalies, rain and moisture have missed their season, pestilential calamities have struck the capital region, and memorials reporting floods and droughts have arrived from all quarters, the imperial thoughts have been troubled. In the palace court there have been prayers, sharing the reverence of Cheng Tang at the Mulberry Forest; for relief and compassion there have been edicts, spreading the benevolence of Emperor Yao in not oppressing the helpless; and to the assembled officials there have been commands, earnestly expressing the anxiety of King Xuan of Zhou in the "River in the Clouds" ("Yunhan") ode. Thus, the way he has labored and agonized in his thoughts, and mutually admonished both the court and the provinces, is also most detailed and earnest—purely identical with the mind of Our Grand Progenitor in modeling himself upon Heaven. Yet Your Excellency still wishes, on account of…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天象以陳謨此憂治危明之心匪過計也嘗莊
誦
聖祖有曰天人之理無二人當以心爲天言求
天於心也又曰欲求事
天必先恤民言求天於民也大哉
王言誠昭事之龜鑑也已
皇上心天心而恤民艱得諸
天性固無間然但天道至精天子者必肖天惟
天惠民天子者必恤民是在
===
皇上加之意而已是故
帝典王謨日塵
講幄湛然心之清矣退而
燕閒師保離次清者得無少滓耶
薦圭主鬯昭對
清廟穆然心之敬矣出而御下尊卑易分敬者
得無少肆耶
端冕垂裳
尊臨
punctuated: 天象以陳謨，此憂治危明之心，匪過計也。嘗莊誦聖祖有曰：「天人之理無二，人當以心爲天。」言求天於心也。又曰：「欲求事天，必先恤民。」言求天於民也。大哉王言，誠昭事之龜鑑也已。皇上心天心而恤民艱，得諸天性，固無間然。但天道至精，天子者必肖天；惟天惠民，天子者必恤民，是在皇上加之意而已。是故帝典王謨，日塵講幄，湛然心之清矣；退而燕閒，師保離次，清者得無少滓耶？薦圭主鬯，昭對清廟，穆然心之敬矣；出而御下，尊卑易分，敬者得無少肆耶？端冕垂裳，尊臨
translation_en:
… celestial phenomena in order to set forth counsels—this mind that worries in times of order and feels peril in times of brightness is by no means an excessive precaution. I have reverently recited the words of the Sacred Ancestor [Emperor Taizu], who said: "The principle of Heaven and man is not dual; man ought to take his own mind as Heaven." This means seeking Heaven in one's mind. He also said: "If one wishes to seek to serve Heaven, one must first show compassion for the people." This means seeking Heaven among the people. Great indeed are the King's words! Truly they are a mirror and touchstone for the bright service of Heaven.

His Majesty makes Heaven's mind his own mind and shows compassion for the hardships of the people; having obtained this from his heavenly nature, there is truly no flaw to be found in him. Yet the Way of Heaven is supremely subtle, and the Son of Heaven must resemble Heaven; only Heaven bestows favor upon the people, and the Son of Heaven must show compassion for the people. This rests simply on His Majesty paying ever greater heed to it.

Therefore, when the canons of the Emperors and the counsels of the Kings daily engage the lecturing tent, lucid indeed is the purity of his mind; yet when he retires to leisure and ease, and the Preceptors and Guardians leave their stations, might that purity not become slightly sullied? When he presents the jade tablets and presides over the sacrificial millet wine, brightly facing the Pure Temple, solemn indeed is the reverence of his mind; yet when he goes forth to rule over his subordinates, where the distinction between noble and lowly is easily drawn, might that reverence not become slightly lax? When he straightens his ceremonial cap and lets hang his robes, majestically ascending…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
黼座儼然心之莊矣俄而
宮壺狎昵易溺莊者得無少倦耶語災變問
民畧悚然心之懼矣俄而可喜可樂可玩
可欲者競進於前懼者得無少變耶夫人
君一心攻之者衆始於儉卒入于奢始於
勤常流于惰是不可不爲之防者
皇上誠於此而加儆焉而又務學以明之親正
人君子以養成之則獨觀化源吾心正則
天心亦正而災異有不弭者否也至於民
===
隱猶有可言者東南民力竭矣而水旱相
仍寬租之
令不嫌於屢下西北黠虜臣矣而武備浸弛款
貢之盟恐難以終恃緝捕非不嚴也而攫
金之寇或出股肱之郡安可不防其漸懲
貪非不亟也而吮髓之夫猶然囊槖之腴
安可不禁其欲
欽恤非不勤也而虎冠之吏快心鷹鸇之威安
可不戢其暴誑愚陵上之禁非不肅也而
punctuated: 黼座，儼然心之莊矣；俄而宮壺狎昵易溺，莊者得無少倦耶？語災變、問民畧，悚然心之懼矣；俄而可喜、可樂、可玩、可欲者競進於前，懼者得無少變耶？夫人君一心，攻之者衆：始於儉，卒入于奢；始於勤，常流于惰。是不可不爲之防者。皇上誠於此而加儆焉，而又務學以明之，親正人君子以養成之，則獨觀化源，吾心正則天心亦正，而災異有不弭者，否也。至於民隱，猶有可言者。東南民力竭矣，而水旱相仍，寬租之令不嫌於屢下；西北黠虜臣矣，而武備浸弛，款貢之盟恐難以終恃。緝捕非不嚴也，而攫金之寇或出股肱之郡，安可不防其漸？懲貪非不亟也，而吮髓之夫猶然囊槖之腴，安可不禁其欲？欽恤非不勤也，而虎冠之吏快心鷹鸇之威，安可不戢其暴？誑愚陵上之禁非不肅也，而
translation_en: … the Imperial Throne, His mind is dignified and solemn; yet shortly thereafter, amid the familiarities of the inner palace [宮壺, for 宮壼] where it is easy to indulge, might that solemnity not grow somewhat weary? When speaking of disasters and portents or inquiring into the hardships [畧, for 瘼?] of the people, His mind is struck with fear; yet shortly thereafter, when things that delight, amuse, entertain, and entice vie to be presented before Him, might that fear not be somewhat altered? Now, the ruler has but one mind, while those that assail it are many: what begins in frugality ends in extravagance; what begins in diligence often slips into indolence. One cannot but guard against this. If Your Majesty truly exercises heightened vigilance over this, and furthermore devotes Yourself to study so as to illuminate the mind, and draws close to upright men and gentlemen so as to nurture it, then You will behold alone the source of transformation. When one's own mind is rectified, the mind of Heaven is likewise rectified; would there then be any disasters or anomalies that are not dispelled? Certainly not. As for the hidden sufferings of the people, there are still matters that may be spoken of. In the southeast, the strength of the people is exhausted, and floods and droughts follow one upon another; orders to remit taxes should not be begrudged even if issued repeatedly. In the northwest, the cunning caitiffs have submitted as vassals, yet military preparedness has gradually slackened; it is to be feared that covenants of amity and tribute can hardly be relied upon to the end. Arrests of brigands are not lacking in strictness, yet bandits who snatch gold in broad daylight sometimes emerge even in the vital prefectures of the realm—how can one not guard against the gradual spread of this? The punishment of corruption is not lacking in urgency, yet fellows who suck the marrow of the people still fatten their purses and sacks as before—how can one not curb their greed? Imperial compassion in criminal justice is not lacking in diligence, yet tiger-capped functionaries take pleasure in the ferocity of hawks and falcons—how can one not check their brutality? The prohibitions against deluding the ignorant and offending against superiors are not lacking in severity, yet …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
左道妖僧悍卒頑民蔑如於投鼠之忌安
可不芟刈之而窮其黨夫匹夫匹婦每能
勝予而一夫懷憤天爲飛霜一女抱冤天
爲大旱尤有不可不爲之慮者
皇上誠寬良民而不貸亂民顯良吏而不貸奸
吏使民得遂其有生之樂則怨讟不作民
心悅而天意得而災異有不弭者否也夫
天不以君無失道而忘儆戒之心人君不
以世無疵化而忘脩省之念茲
===
天心垂儆如此
聖心幾微如此民隱之可慮又如此則夫
聖不自聖以心爲天雖休
勿休以勤民爲務使志氣交動清和咸理五
事順而休徵應諸福集而萬邦和近符
聖祖遠媲堯湯
帝德協
天道同流
國祚侔
punctuated: 左道妖僧、悍卒頑民，蔑如於投鼠之忌，安可不芟刈之而窮其黨？夫匹夫匹婦每能勝予，而一夫懷憤，天爲飛霜；一女抱冤，天爲大旱，尤有不可不爲之慮者。皇上誠寬良民而不貸亂民，顯良吏而不貸奸吏，使民得遂其有生之樂，則怨讟不作，民心悅而天意得，而災異有不弭者否也？夫天不以君無失道而忘儆戒之心，人君不以世無疵化而忘脩省之念。茲天心垂儆如此，聖心幾微如此，民隱之可慮又如此。則夫聖不自聖，以心爲天；雖休勿休，以勤民爲務。使志氣交動，清和咸理，五事順而休徵應，諸福集而萬邦和，近符聖祖，遠媲堯、湯，帝德協天道同流，國祚侔
translation_en: …heretical and sorcerous monks, unruly soldiers, and recalcitrant commoners act with utter disregard, taking advantage of officials' hesitation to "throw stones at a rat for fear of breaking the vase"; how can we not weed them out and thoroughly eradicate their factions? Indeed, ordinary men and women can often prevail over a ruler; when a single man harbors resentment, Heaven sends down unseasonal frost, and when a single woman suffers an injustice, Heaven brings about a great drought—these are matters that require even more careful concern. If Your Majesty truly shows leniency to good commoners while not pardoning rebellious ones, and honors upright officials while not pardoning corrupt ones, allowing the people to fulfill the joy of their lives, then resentment and slander will not arise, the people's hearts will be pleased and Heaven's will gained—would disasters and anomalies then ever fail to cease? Indeed, Heaven does not forget its intent to warn and admonish merely because a ruler has not strayed from the Way, and a ruler does not forget the thought of self-cultivation and reflection merely because the age has no flaws in its moral transformation. Now that Heaven's mind sends down warnings like this, the Sage's mind attends to the subtleincipients like this, and the hidden sufferings of the people warrant concern like this, then let the Sage not regard himself as already sage, taking his own mind as Heaven; though things be auspicious, let him not rest in that auspiciousness, taking diligence toward the people as his duty. Thus, will and vital energy will mutually respond, purity and harmony will prevail in governance, the Five Conducts will be in accord and auspicious verifications will respond, all blessings will gather and the myriad states will be in harmony. In recent times matching the Sacred Ancestor, and in distant antiquity rivaling Yao and Tang, Imperial virtue will harmonize and flow together with the Way of Heaven, and the dynasty's longevity will equal…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天運無極是重有望於
皇上者也若粉飾文具是
清朝所斥申飭臣工則
明詔森然愚生安敢復贅
第三問
張輔辰
同考試官敎諭劉批詩之意深矣此作上下古
今折衷人物足定千古權衡大要歸於闡性靈裨風化盡旨哉
乎其言之也敬服敬服
===
考試官敎諭倫批博綜揚扢深得說詩之旨
考試官敎諭譙批有風骨有思致颯颯大雅
之音
論古人之詩者取其詞足以攄性靈義足
以裨風化言與人不得而相掩也夫詩者
言之有律者也六情緘於中百物盪於外
情緣物感物易情遷而言因之揆其要領
惟有關於彝敎之大可以導人於善而袚
除其邪心形之歌詠被之管絃可以中律
punctuated:
天運無極，是重有望於皇上者也。若粉飾文具，是清朝所斥；申飭臣工，則明詔森然，愚生安敢復贅？
第三問
張輔辰
同考試官敎諭劉批：詩之意深矣！此作上下古今，折衷人物，足定千古權衡。大要歸於闡性靈、裨風化，盡旨哉乎其言之也！敬服，敬服。
考試官敎諭倫批：博綜揚扢，深得說詩之旨。
考試官敎諭譙批：有風骨，有思致，颯颯大雅之音。
論古人之詩者，取其詞足以攄性靈，義足以裨風化，言與人不得而相掩也。夫詩者，言之有律者也。六情緘於中，百物盪於外，情緣物感，物易情遷，而言因之。揆其要領，惟有關於彝敎之大，可以導人於善而袚除其邪心，形之歌詠，被之管絃，可以中律…
translation_en:
… [may the] dynastic fortune match the boundless cycle of Heaven—this is what is earnestly hoped of His Majesty. As for whitewashing mere bureaucratic formalities, that is what our pure court rejects; and as for admonishing the officials, the resplendent edicts stand in solemn array, so how would this ignorant student dare to add superfluous words?

Question Three
Zhang Fuchen 張輔辰
Associate Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: The meaning of poetry is profound indeed! This essay ranges across antiquity and the present, weighing and evaluating historical figures, sufficient to establish a standard of judgment for all ages. Its main thrust comes down to illuminating innate sensibility and aiding moral transformation through custom—how thoroughly its words capture the essential purport! Truly admirable, truly admirable.
Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: Broadly synthesizing and critically appraising, it deeply grasps the essential purport of explaining poetry.
Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: Possessing moral vigor and thoughtful refinement, it has the resonant sound of high elegance.

Those who discuss the poetry of the ancients select diction sufficient to express innate sensibility and meaning sufficient to aid moral transformation through custom, so that words and the person cannot be used to conceal one another. Now poetry is speech endowed with regulated measure. The six emotions are sealed within, while the myriad things stir them from without; emotions are moved by things, and as things change, emotions shift, with words following accordingly. Examining its essential point, only when it relates to the great principles of constant moral teaching—capable of guiding people toward goodness and cleansing away their perverse minds, and when given form in song and chant and set to pipes and strings, capable of hitting the musical pitches…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
呂而鼓羣動君子取焉是故列之三經錯
之三緯綜之四始釐之五際發乎性情止
乎禮義可攷而知也已運與世移質隨人
異格緣習靡音逐氣漓言人人殊矣所貴
談詩者尚論其人不徒以言也粤自扶徠
啟咏堯壤行歌詩敎興矣三代盛時采詩
觀風詩爲有用之文三代以下徒騁才情
無當實用而詩之義廢有王者作采而立
敎詎無可以諧宮商薦郊廟嗣百篇之餘
===
響者耶曰匪然也夫詩天地之籟也而人
籟生乎其中矣禮曰感物而動故形於聲
言之不足故長言之嗟嘆之是詩者天籟
之自鳴性術之所流也敎化融徹卽庸孺
矢口有老師宿儒所不能道而亦因政俗
以爲汙隆故先王采之爲之示儉示禮以
防其邪而導之正要之頌其所美則善心
生以善勸善不敎而成頌其所刺則惡心
熄以惡懲惡不肅而嚴是詩之爲敎也聖
punctuated: 呂而鼓羣動，君子取焉。是故列之三經，錯之三緯，綜之四始，釐之五際，發乎性情，止乎禮義，可攷而知也。已運與世移，質隨人異，格緣習靡，音逐氣漓，言人人殊矣。所貴談詩者，尚論其人，不徒以言也。粤自《扶徠》啟咏，堯壤行歌，詩敎興矣。三代盛時，采詩觀風，詩爲有用之文；三代以下，徒騁才情，無當實用，而詩之義廢。有王者作，采而立敎，詎無可以諧宮商、薦郊廟、嗣百篇之餘響者耶？曰：匪然也。夫詩，天地之籟也，而人籟生乎其中矣。《禮》曰：「感物而動，故形於聲；言之不足，故長言之、嗟嘆之。」是詩者，天籟之自鳴，性術之所流也。敎化融徹，卽庸孺矢口，有老師宿儒所不能道；而亦因政俗以爲汙隆。故先王采之，爲之示儉示禮，以防其邪而導之正。要之，頌其所美則善心生，以善勸善，不敎而成；頌其所刺則惡心熄，以惡懲惡，不肅而嚴。是詩之爲敎也，聖
translation_en:
… pitch-pipes and stir the myriad creatures, the superior man selects them. Therefore, arranged into the Three Warp Threads (feng, ya, song) and interwoven with the Three Woof Threads (fu, bi, xing), synthesized into the Four Beginnings and organized into the Five Junctures, they spring from human nature and emotions and halt within the bounds of ritual propriety and righteousness—all of which can be examined and known. Once fortune shifted with the ages and dispositions varied with individuals, poetic styles grew decadent through custom, tones thinned along with the vital ethos, and the words differed from person to person. Thus, what is valued in discussing poetry is critically evaluating the person in the context of their era, not merely judging by their words.

Ever since the Song of Fulai initiated versification and the folk of Yao's realm sang along the roads, the teaching of poetry has flourished. During the heyday of the Three Dynasties, poetry was collected to observe local customs, making poetry a literature of practical use; from the Three Dynasties onward, writers merely gave free rein to talent and sentiment without serving practical utility, and the true meaning of poetry fell into disuse. Should a true king arise to collect poems and establish instruction, how could there be none capable of harmonizing the gong and shang notes, being offered at the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples, and continuing the lingering echoes of the Three Hundred Poems?

Someone may say: It is not merely so. Poetry is the piping of Heaven and Earth, and the piping of humanity is born within it. The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "Moved by external things, it takes form in sound; when plain speech does not suffice, one draws it out in chanting and sighs over it." Thus poetry is the spontaneous sounding of Heaven's piping and the natural outflow of inborn nature. When moral transformation thoroughly permeates the realm, even what ordinary men and children utter on the spur of the moment may contain things that venerable masters and seasoned scholars cannot express; yet poetry also rises and falls in purity according to governance and customs. Therefore the former kings collected poems, using them to display frugality and ritual propriety in order to guard against depravity and guide people toward rectitude. In sum, when one recites what is praised in them, a heart of goodness arises—using goodness to encourage goodness, perfection is achieved without formal instruction; when one recites what is criticized in them, a heart of evil is extinguished—using evil to warn against evil, awe is inspired without harsh severity. Such is the teaching of poetry, and the Sage …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
人刪之為經也是故詩奏於郊廟天神格
地祇出奏於朝廷羣后德讓鳥獸蹌蹌奏
於閨門肅雍溫惠珩璜琚瑀之節備播於
邦國天下以諧萬民以洽賓旅以鼓動植
而乖僻疵厲之氣消故曰感天地動鬼神
莫近於詩季札觀上國而卜德祚盛衰左
丘明以歌詩歷徵大夫善敗詩之義淵乎
深矣然觀詩於三百之中里巷歌謠男女
答贈淫蕩鄙俚之什不妨兼收觀詩於三
===
百之外祈招可以畜君巧笑可以崇質翹
車可以責善清河可以謀國涓水可以防
微而不為聖人所取彼槩言刪後無詩亦
逐場之見非通論也安知當時歌謠贈答
不出於薦紳先生有所託而寄其情夫子
刪之而去其名不可得而見耳後世莊人
雅士孤臣屏子攄忠愛之忱陳感慨之臆
發抒志意陶寫情景豈無一言之幾於道
世無尼父評品乖律取舍靡公人各以意
punctuated: 人刪之為經也。是故詩奏於郊廟，天神格、地祇出；奏於朝廷，羣后德讓，鳥獸蹌蹌；奏於閨門，肅雍溫惠，珩璜琚瑀之節備；播於邦國天下，以諧萬民，以洽賓旅，以鼓動植，而乖僻疵厲之氣消。故曰：「感天地，動鬼神，莫近於詩。」季札觀上國而卜德祚盛衰，左丘明以歌詩歷徵大夫善敗，詩之義淵乎深矣！然觀詩於三百之中，里巷歌謠、男女答贈、淫蕩鄙俚之什不妨兼收；觀詩於三百之外，《祈招》可以畜君，《巧笑》可以崇質，《翹車》可以責善，《清河》可以謀國，《涓水》可以防微，而不為聖人所取。彼槩言刪後無詩，亦逐場之見，非通論也。安知當時歌謠贈答，不出於薦紳先生有所託而寄其情，夫子刪之而去其名，不可得而見耳？後世莊人雅士、孤臣屏子，攄忠愛之忱，陳感慨之臆，發抒志意，陶寫情景，豈無一言之幾於道？世無尼父，評品乖律，取舍靡公，人各以意…
translation_en: …that the Sage edited them into a Classic. Therefore, when the Odes are performed at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, the heavenly spirits descend and the earthly deities emerge; when performed at court, the assembled lords yield in virtue and the birds and beasts dance in rhythm; when performed within the inner quarters, reverence, harmony, gentleness, and kindness prevail, and the regulated measure of jade pendants is complete; when disseminated throughout the states and the empire, they harmonize the myriad people, bring concord to guests and travelers, and animate beasts and plants, so that perverse, noxious, and pestilential influences melt away. Thus it is said: "For moving heaven and earth and stirring ghosts and spirits, nothing comes closer than the Odes." Ji Zha observed the music of the central states and divined the rise and decline of their virtue and fortune; Zuo Qiuming repeatedly verified the success and failure of grandees through the Odes they chanted. Profound indeed is the meaning of the Odes! Yet when we examine the Odes within the Three Hundred, folksongs of the lanes and alleys, exchanges of gifts and replies between men and women, and licentious or vulgar pieces were nonetheless included together. And when we examine poems outside the Three Hundred, the "Qizhao" could restrain a ruler, "Artful Smiles" (Qiaoxiao) could exalt plain substance, "The High-Curving Carriage" (Qiaoche) could urge goodness, "Clear River" (Qinghe) could counsel the state, and "Trickling Water" (Juanshui) could guard against subtle beginnings—yet they were not selected by the Sage. Those who sweepingly claim that after the Sage's editing there was no true poetry merely follow the crowd's view; it is not a comprehensive judgment. How do we know that the folksongs and exchanges of gifts and replies of that time did not come from scholarly gentlemen of official rank who used allegory to lodge their feelings, and that the Master, in editing them, simply removed their names so that they can no longer be known? In later ages, when grave men and refined scholars, isolated ministers and banished sons poured forth their sincere loyalty and affection, set out their deeply felt emotions, expressed their aspirations, and gave form to their scenes and feelings, how could there not be a single word among them that approaches the Way? Because the world no longer has a Confucius (Nifu), critical appraisals violate the standards, selection and rejection lack impartiality, and each person according to his own opinion…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
互相排讚無所取衷焉耳詩變而爲騷騷
變爲五言最後變爲近體極矣騷於詩爲
近以騷言之屈子懷絕代之才抱貞孤之
操不得於君流離放逐而作離騷千載而
下玩其詞探其蘊奧如駕風鞭霆不可得
而窺測嘗考劉勰辨騷謂騷有典誥之體
有規諷之旨有比興之義忠怨之辭四者
同於風雅似也至託詭譚怪狷狹荒淫摘
其四事斥其異於經傳斯誠異矣抑豈知
===
原者哉蓋騷之旨主於規諷而義兼風雅
觀者惟察其情出於忠款而無乖於禮義
至其詞之泛濫假託要當以意攝之譬之
用兵貪詐奸宄頑鈍無恥之夫皆編之部
曲至其用之或動於九天之上或潛於九
地之下使人莫可窺測斯用兵之善者也
今觀於騷如稱堯舜禹湯雅之體也假雲
龍蘭芷風之遺也稱黨人靈脩之類雅之
變也蛾眉謠詠宓妃豐隆之類風之變也
punctuated: 互相排讚，無所取衷焉耳。詩變而爲騷，騷變爲五言，最後變爲近體，極矣。騷於詩爲近，以騷言之：屈子懷絕代之才，抱貞孤之操，不得於君，流離放逐，而作《離騷》。千載而下，玩其詞，探其蘊奧，如駕風鞭霆，不可得而窺測。嘗考劉勰《辨騷》，謂騷有典誥之體，有規諷之旨，有比興之義，忠怨之辭，四者同於《風》《雅》，似也。至託詭譚怪，狷狹荒淫，摘其四事，斥其異於經傳，斯誠異矣，抑豈知原者哉？蓋騷之旨主於規諷，而義兼《風》《雅》，觀者惟察其情出於忠款，而無乖於禮義；至其詞之泛濫假託，要當以意攝之。譬之用兵，貪詐奸宄、頑鈍無恥之夫，皆編之部曲；至其用之，或動於九天之上，或潛於九地之下，使人莫可窺測，斯用兵之善者也。今觀於騷，如稱堯、舜、禹、湯，《雅》之體也；假雲龍、蘭芷，《風》之遺也；稱黨人、靈脩之類，《雅》之變也；蛾眉、謠詠、宓妃、豐隆之類，《風》之變也。
translation_en: … disparaging or praising one another, with no standard by which to reach a balanced judgment. The Odes (Shi) transformed into the Elegies (Sao), the Elegies transformed into five-syllable verse, and finally into modern-style regulated verse, reaching their ultimate development. The Elegies are closest to the Odes. To speak in terms of the Elegies: Master Qu [Qu Yuan 屈原] possessed peerless talent and held to a pure and solitary integrity; failing to win the favor of his ruler, he was cast out and exiled, whereupon he composed "Encountering Sorrow" (Lisao 離騷). A thousand years later, when one savors his words and probes their profound depths, it is like riding the wind and whipping up thunderbolts—impossible to fathom or measure. I have examined Liu Xie's 劉勰 "Evaluating the Elegies" (Biansao 辨騷), which states that the Elegies possess the form of canons and announcements, the purport of remonstrance and admonition, the principles of comparison and evocative image (bi xing 比興), and expressions of loyal resentment—and that in these four respects they are identical to the Airs (Feng 風) and Court Hymns (Ya 雅). This seems plausible. Yet when it comes to their reliance on the uncanny and talk of the strange, or their narrow-mindedness and wild excess, he singles out four such matters and denounces them as diverging from the Classics and commentaries. Those elements are indeed divergent, yet how could he truly understand Qu Yuan? For the main purport of the Elegies lies in remonstrance and admonition, while their principles encompass both the Airs and the Court Hymns. The reader should simply observe that their sentiments spring from loyal sincerity and do not violate ritual propriety and righteousness; as for the overflowing extravagance and allegorical fabrications of their diction, one ought in essence to grasp them through their underlying intent. Compare this to the deployment of troops: greedy, deceitful, treacherous, and villainous men, as well as obtuse and shameless fellows, are all enrolled into the ranks and divisions. When it comes to employing them, one may strike above the nine heavens or lie hidden beneath the nine earths, making it impossible for anyone to fathom or measure—such is someone skilled in the use of troops. Now, if we observe the Elegies: praising Yao 堯, Shun 舜, Yu 禹, and Tang 湯 is in the form of the Court Hymns; borrowing the imagery of cloud-dragons and orchids and angelica is the legacy of the Airs; speaking of "factious men" (dangren 黨人), the "Numina Fair" (lingxiu 靈脩), and the like is a variation (bian 變) of the Court Hymns; and speaking of "moth-eyebrows" (emei 蛾眉), slanderous songs [reading 諑 for 詠], Fufei 宓妃, Fenglong 豐隆, and the like is a variation of the Airs. …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
借怪誕不經之詞以寄幽憂靡訴之衷真
如尚父登壇孫吳在列莫測其攻守之所
自而忠君愛國昌微興墜之緒隱然見於
言外則聞者不怒繹之有餘思焉此騷之
大旨也胡以議之蓋三百篇之詩敦厚溫
柔隆古之希聲也屈子之詞瓌富奇崛文
人之杰也聖人無意於文而屈子乃有意
於文者組織風雅閎放厥詞三百篇之後
一人而已淮南希武皇之意嘉其文而作
===
傳司馬遷拾小山之遺高其人而入記載
所謂蟬蛻溷濁之中蜉蝣塵埃之外泥而
不滓與日月爭光原之心事白矣揚子雲
譏其不能龍蛇班固議其怨懟沉江二子
摹擬騷體如甘泉兩都比之風則詞謝媺
婉擬之雅則裁乏雅嚴於司馬氏猶倒影
滅沒不可望尚談屈子耶而雄之美新固
之黨憲是又原之罪人也嗣後擬騷反騷
紛紜迭作所謂無其事而效其言奚取焉
punctuated: 借怪誕不經之詞，以寄幽憂靡訴之衷。真如尚父登壇，孫、吳在列，莫測其攻守之所自，而忠君愛國、昌微興墜之緒，隱然見於言外，則聞者不怒，繹之有餘思焉。此騷之大旨也，胡以議之？蓋三百篇之詩，敦厚溫柔，隆古之希聲也；屈子之詞，瓌富奇崛，文人之杰也。聖人無意於文，而屈子乃有意於文者，組織風雅，閎放厥詞，三百篇之後，一人而已。淮南希武皇之意，嘉其文而作傳；司馬遷拾小山之遺，高其人而入記載。所謂「蟬蛻溷濁之中，蜉蝣塵埃之外，泥而不滓，與日月爭光」，原之心事白矣。揚子雲譏其不能龍蛇，班固議其怨懟沉江。二子摹擬騷體，如《甘泉》、《兩都》，比之風則詞謝媺婉，擬之雅則裁乏雅嚴，於司馬氏猶倒影滅沒，不可望，尚談屈子耶？而雄之《美新》、固之黨憲，是又原之罪人也。嗣後擬騷、反騷，紛紜迭作，所謂無其事而效其言，奚取焉！
translation_en: … He borrowed bizarre and uncanonical expressions to lodge the deep sorrows and unvoiced feelings of his heart. Truly, it is as if Grand Father Lü (Shangfu 尚父) were ascending the altar of command with Sun Wu 孫武 and Wu Qi 吳起 in the ranks: no one can fathom the source of his attacks and defenses, while the threads of loyalty to his lord, love for his state, flourishing and decline, and rise and fall appear implicitly beyond the words; thus those who hear it are not angered, and those who ponder it find lingering food for thought. This is the main purport of the "Encountering Sorrow" (Sao 騷); how could one find fault with it? For the poems of the Three Hundred Pieces are sincere, generous, gentle, and soft—the rare music of high antiquity; the diction of Master Qu (Qu Yuan 屈原) is magnificent, rich, extraordinary, and towering—the paragon of literary men. The sages had no deliberate intention to craft literature, whereas Master Qu did have a deliberate intention to craft literature; weaving together the Airs (Feng 風) and Odes (Ya 雅) and grandly unleashing his phrasing, after the Three Hundred Pieces he stands alone. The King of Huainan (Liu An 劉安), anticipating the wishes of Emperor Wu, praised his writing and composed a commentary; Sima Qian 司馬遷 gathered what was left by the Lesser Mountain (Xiaoshan 小山), esteemed his character, and entered him into his record. In the words, "shedding his shell amid the turbid filth, floating beyond the dust and dirt, stained by mud yet unsoiled, vying in brilliance with the sun and moon," Qu Yuan's heartfelt intentions were made plain. Yang Ziyun (Yang Xiong 揚雄) ridiculed him for being unable to adapt like a dragon or snake, and Ban Gu 班固 criticized him for resentfully drowning himself in the river. Those two men imitated the Sao style in works such as the "Sweet Springs" (Ganquan 甘泉) and the "Two Capitals" (Liangdu 兩都), yet compared to the Airs their diction lacks delicate grace, and measured against the Odes their structure lacks dignified austerity. Before Mr. Sima (Sima Xiangru 司馬相如) they vanish like inverted reflections and cannot even approach him—how then dare they speak of Master Qu? Moreover, with Yang Xiong's "Praising the Xin Dynasty" (Meixin 美新) and Ban Gu's partisanship with Dou Xian 竇憲, they are furthermore offenders against Qu Yuan! Thereafter, imitations of the Sao and counter-Sao pieces were produced one after another in profusion; as the saying goes, imitating someone's words without having experienced their circumstances—what is there to value in that?

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
漢魏以還河梁贈別實創五言之宗蘇李
之高邁曹劉之卓犖鮑謝之清奧作者無
慮百十家而說者獨稱柴桑之士豈不以
陶潛之為人不事二姓寄傲於壺觴菊松
之間亦屈子之流亞與其詩冲澹蕭散實
開韋柳之門而以鍾嶸所擬三品評之則
公幹升堂思王入室陶子殆以人掩言哉
韓昌黎文起八代而詩遜陶韋可輕議陶
耶栢梁賡詠已開七言之端沈宋之綺麗
===
王岑之壯逸韋孟之冲澹作者亦無慮百
十家而議者獨許浣花之叟豈不以杜甫
之為人間關鳳翔不蹈於廣文輞川之轍
亦有屈子之志行與其詩才奪蘇李氣吞
曹劉掩顏謝孤高雜徐庾流麗集唐人之
大成楊仲弘詮為四唐或謂李杜齊名工
部詎可擅美不知杜兼眾體且以人勝耳
歐陽子文希山斗而詩則陸沉晚唐奚以
議杜為也嘗試評之浣花之作如祥麟威
punctuated: 漢、魏以還，河梁贈別，實創五言之宗。蘇、李之高邁，曹、劉之卓犖，鮑、謝之清奧，作者無慮百十家，而說者獨稱柴桑之士。豈不以陶潛之為人，不事二姓，寄傲於壺觴菊松之間，亦屈子之流亞與？其詩冲澹蕭散，實開韋、柳之門。而以鍾嶸所擬三品評之，則公幹升堂，思王入室，陶子殆以人掩言哉！韓昌黎文起八代，而詩遜陶、韋，可輕議陶耶？栢梁賡詠，已開七言之端。沈、宋之綺麗，王、岑之壯逸，韋、孟之冲澹，作者亦無慮百十家，而議者獨許浣花之叟。豈不以杜甫之為人，間關鳳翔，不蹈於廣文、輞川之轍，亦有屈子之志行與？其詩才奪蘇、李，氣吞曹、劉，掩顏、謝孤高，雜徐、庾流麗，集唐人之大成，楊仲弘詮為四唐。或謂李、杜齊名，工部詎可擅美？不知杜兼眾體，且以人勝耳。歐陽子文希山斗，而詩則陸沉晚唐，奚以議杜為也？嘗試評之：浣花之作，如祥麟威…
translation_en: From the Han and Wei dynasties onward, the parting poems at the river bridge truly founded the lineage of pentasyllabic verse. With the lofty transcendence of Su Wu 蘇武 and Li Ling 李陵, the outstanding brilliance of Cao Zhi 曹植 and Liu Zhen 劉楨, and the pure profundity of Bao Zhao 鮑照 and Xie Lingyun 謝靈運, there were easily a hundred or more authors; yet commentators single out the gentleman of Chaisang 柴桑 for praise. Is this not because Tao Qian 陶潛, as a man, refused to serve two ruling houses, lodging his proud spirit amid wine-pots, cups, chrysanthemums, and pines, making him a peer of Master Qu Yuan 屈原? His poetry is placid and unrestrained, truly opening the gate for Wei Yingwu 韋應物 and Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元. Yet if we judge him by the three grades formulated by Zhong Rong 鍾嶸, where Liu Gonggan 劉公幹 [Liu Zhen] ascends the hall and Prince Si 思王 [Cao Zhi] enters the inner chamber, Master Tao's words were perhaps overshadowed by his person! Han Changli 韓昌黎 [Han Yu 韓愈] revived prose after eight dynasties of decline, yet his poetry yielded to Tao and Wei; how could one lightly criticize Tao? Thelinked verses at the Cypress-Beam Terrace (Boliang tai 栢梁臺) already opened the way for heptasyllabic verse. With the ornate beauty of Shen Quanqi 沈佺期 and Song Zhiwen 宋之問, the vigorous freedom of Wang Wei 王維 [or Wang Changling 王昌齡] and Cen Shen 岑參, and the placid simplicity of Wei Yingwu and Meng Haoran 孟浩然, there were likewise easily a hundred or more authors; yet critics uniquely commend the old man of Huanhua 浣花 [Washing-Flower Brook]. Is this not because Du Fu 杜甫, as a man, traveled through hardship to Fengxiang 鳳翔 and did not tread in the tracks of the Instructor of the Broadly Cultivated (Guangwen 廣文, i.e. Zheng Qian 鄭虔) or Wangchuan 輞川 [Wang Wei], likewise possessing the aspirations and conduct of Master Qu? His poetic talent eclipses Su and Li, his spirit swallows Cao and Liu, he overshadows the solitary loftiness of Yan Yanzhi 顏延之 and Xie Lingyun, and blends in the flowing elegance of Xu Ling 徐陵 and Yu Xin 庾信, synthesizing the great achievements of the men of Tang—whom Yang Zhonghong 楊仲弘 [Yang Zai 楊載] classified into the four Tang periods. Some say that Li Bai 李白 and Du Fu are equal in fame, so how can the Vice Director in the Ministry of Works (Gongbu 工部, i.e. Du Fu) monopolize the praise? They do not realize that Du encompasses all styles, and moreover triumphs through his character. Master Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 aspired to the standard of Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper in prose, yet in poetry he sank to the level of the Late Tang; on what basis could he criticize Du? Let us try to evaluate them: the works of the man of Huanhua [Du Fu] are like an auspicious unicorn and a majestic…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
鳳見者媚焉柴桑之詩悠然孤鶴與其人
俱邈矣靈均出入風雅變化不測其猶龍
乎大都發於性情止於禮義無愧於三百
篇之大旨均之不詭於詩者也藉令離騷
非以靈脩哀志則驚采奪色絕燄埋光雖
使揚雄息喙班固回嘲亦不號詞賦之祖
陶杜非以忠貞鑄詞則晉真無文章唐亦
失詩聖雖使昌黎推轂永叔退舍亦不登
著作之壇知此可以論詩矣我
===
國家道化淪洽風氣淳龐
中和之極建於
上詩書之澤陶於下其奏之
郊廟陳之
宴享洋洋乎雅頌之休聲矣而鴻工哲匠繼
踵摩肩往往孕杜苞陶即靈均且奴隸使
之執事猶欲總異歸同以鳴
國家之盛抑豈有出於三百篇之旨哉蓋詩
首二南以風教也風起於上而動於下惟
punctuated: 鳳，見者媚焉；柴桑之詩，悠然孤鶴，與其人俱邈矣；靈均出入風雅，變化不測，其猶龍乎！大都發於性情，止於禮義，無愧於三百篇之大旨，均之不詭於詩者也。藉令《離騷》非以靈脩哀志，則驚采奪色，絕燄埋光，雖使揚雄息喙、班固回嘲，亦不號詞賦之祖；陶、杜非以忠貞鑄詞，則晉真無文章，唐亦失詩聖，雖使昌黎推轂、永叔退舍，亦不登著作之壇。知此可以論詩矣。我國家道化淪洽，風氣淳龐，中和之極建於上，詩書之澤陶於下。其奏之郊廟，陳之宴享，洋洋乎雅頌之休聲矣！而鴻工哲匠，繼踵摩肩，往往孕杜苞陶，即靈均且奴隸使之。執事猶欲總異歸同，以鳴國家之盛，抑豈有出於三百篇之旨哉？蓋詩首《二南》，以風教也。風起於上而動於下，惟
translation_en:
… majestic phoenix—those who behold them are charmed by them. The poetry of the Master of Chaisang (Tao Yuanming 陶淵明) is like a carefree solitary crane, as aloof and transcendent as the man himself. And Lingjun (Qu Yuan 屈原), moving in and out of the Airs (Feng) and Odes (Ya) with unpredictable transformations—is he not like a dragon! On the whole, their works all issue from human nature and emotion and halt within the bounds of ritual and righteousness; they are worthy of the grand import of the Three Hundred Poems (Book of Odes) and are all alike in not violating the principles of poetry. Suppose that "Encountering Sorrow" (Lisao 離騷) did not express sorrowful devotion toward the Fair One (Lingxiu, his sovereign)—then its startling brilliance would lose its color and its peerless flame would bury its light; even if one made Yang Xiong 揚雄 hold his tongue and Ban Gu 班固 retract his ridicule, it would still not be hailed as the ancestor of lyric exposition (cifu). And if Tao Yuanming and Du Fu 杜甫 had not forged their words out of loyalty and integrity, then the Jin dynasty would truly have had no literature, and the Tang would likewise have lost its Sage of Poetry; even if Han Yu 韓愈 (Changli) had championed them and Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修 (Yongshu) had yielded ground to them, they would still not have ascended the altar of great authors. Once one understands this, one can discuss poetry.

In our Dynasty, moral transformation has permeated everywhere, and customs are pure and grand. The supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony is established above, while the beneficent influence of the Odes and Documents molds those below. The music performed at the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple, and presented at court banquets and feasts, resounds gloriously with the auspicious voices of the Odes (Ya) and Hymns (Song)! Moreover, great masters and wise craftsmen follow closely on one another's heels and rub shoulders, often encompassing Du Fu and embracing Tao Yuanming, and even ordering Qu Yuan (Lingjun) about like a servant. Yet Your Honor still wishes to bring together what is disparate and return it to unity in order to proclaim the flourishing of the Dynasty—how could this go beyond the essential meaning of the Three Hundred Poems? Indeed, the Book of Odes begins with the "Two Souths" (Er Nan) because of their moral instruction through influence. The wind of moral influence arises from above and stirs those below; I only…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
冀
朝廷之上本關雎麟趾之心廣菁莪棫樸之
化崇緇衣素絲之風黜蜉蝣貝錦之習敦
尚爾雅刬滌浮澆則化行俗美歌謠里巷
之詩宜有可采而為之士者又博綜羣籍
涵養性靈本之二南以求其端參之列國
以盡其變正之於雅以大其規和之於頌
以要其止而又推之天下國家以驗其實
際則詩之養性情達政事者此為得之是
===
===
深於詩者也由是而言所志過則風雅及
則騷不及亦不失為陶杜謂之鳴
國家之盛疇曰不宜否則牽性情而逐光景
工藻繪而鑿天真即拾香草於江潭獵奇
葩於楚畹採東籬之落英襲杜陵之賸馥
享其敝帚自謂千金亦優孟之學孫嫫姆
而處子態也識者見且唾矣奚其詩記曰
誦詩三百不足以當一獻而不達於政雖
多奚為致用君子詎可徒詩為也請以是
punctuated: 冀朝廷之上，本《關雎》、《麟趾》之心，廣《菁莪》、《棫樸》之化，崇《緇衣》、《素絲》之風，黜《蜉蝣》、《貝錦》之習，敦尚爾雅，刬滌浮澆，則化行俗美，歌謠里巷之詩宜有可采。而為之士者，又博綜羣籍，涵養性靈，本之二《南》以求其端，參之列國以盡其變，正之於《雅》以大其規，和之於《頌》以要其止，而又推之天下國家以驗其實際。則詩之養性情、達政事者，此為得之，是深於詩者也。由是而言，所志過則《風》、《雅》，及則《騷》，不及亦不失為陶、杜。謂之鳴國家之盛，疇曰不宜？否則牽性情而逐光景，工藻繪而鑿天真，即拾香草於江潭，獵奇葩於楚畹，採東籬之落英，襲杜陵之賸馥，享其敝帚，自謂千金，亦優孟之學孫，嫫姆而處子態也。識者見且唾矣，奚其詩？《記》曰：「誦《詩》三百，不足以當一獻。」而「不達於政，雖多，奚為」？致用君子，詎可徒詩為也？請以是
translation_en: …hope is only that at court above, if they base themselves on the intention of "Crying Ospreys" (Guanju) and "Feet of the Lin" (Linzhi), broaden the transformative influence of "Luxuriant Tarragon" (Jing'e) and "Scrub Oak" (Yupu), exalt the air of "Black Robes" (Zhiyi) and "White Silk" (Susi), banish the habits of "Mayfly" (Fuyou) and "Shell Brocade" (Beijin), esteem elegance and refinement, and pare away frivolity and superficiality, then transformation will proceed and customs will grow fine, so that the songs and ballads of the lanes and alleys will fittingly contain verses worth collecting. And as for those who are scholars, if they further synthesize the multitude of texts broadly and nurture their innate spirit—grounding themselves in the two Nan ("Odes of the South") to seek the beginning, consulting the airs of the various states to exhaust the variations, rectifying them through the Ya ("Court Hymns") to enlarge the scope, harmonizing them through the Song ("Eulogies") to arrive at the ultimate resting point, and furthermore extending them to the realm and the state to verify their practical reality—then as for poetry's capacity to nourish disposition and emotion and to achieve mastery in affairs of governance, in this way they will have attained it, and such men are truly profound in poetry. Speaking from this perspective, when they express their aspirations, if they excel they will attain to the Airs (Feng) and Hymns (Ya); if they reach the mark they will attain to the Elegies (Sao); and even if they fall short they will still not fail to be like Tao Qian 陶潛 and Du Fu 杜甫. To call this sounding forth the flourishing of the state—who would say it is unfitting? Otherwise, if one forces disposition and emotion to chase after passing scenery, or labors at ornate embellishment while chiseling away natural genuineness—even if one gathers fragrant herbs by the river depths, hunts rare blossoms in the gardens of Chu, plucks fallen petals by the eastern fence, or borrows the lingering fragrance of Duling 杜陵 (Du Fu), prizing one's own worn-out broom and boasting that it is worth a thousand pieces of gold—it is merely You Meng 優孟 imitating Sunshu Ao 孫叔敖, or the ugly Momo 嫫姆 putting on the airs of a maiden. Men of discernment will spit upon seeing it; how could that be called poetry? The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "To recite the three hundred Odes is still insufficient to match a single sacrificial offering." And "if one cannot master governance, though one recites much, what use is it?" How could a gentleman devoted to practical service merely occupy himself with making verses? I beg to offer this…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
爲明問復
第四問
劉信徵
同考試官訓導靳批度田均賦我
皇上嘉惠元元
盛心子能博綜古今宣揚
德意且爲滇人畫久遠計匪徒剿說已也具占經濟實用錄之
考試官教諭倫批詳經制酌時宜惟此作得
之
===
考試官教諭譙批良法美意燦然畢陳
爲政之道其猶張弓乎高者仰之下者俯
之高下隨機而應手惟其中而已矣其猶
調瑟乎緩則急之急則緩之緩急隨宜以
諧聲惟其適而已矣養由基之於射也伯
牙之於琴也帝王之於天下也亦大都若
此矣是故高岸爲谷深谷爲陵言時勢之
有變更而不可常也冬日則飲湯夏日則
飲水言處事之貴識時而不可泥也天運
punctuated:
爲明問復。
第四問
劉信徵
同考試官訓導靳批：度田均賦，我皇上嘉惠元元盛心。子能博綜古今，宣揚德意，且爲滇人畫久遠計，匪徒剿說已也。具占經濟實用，錄之。
考試官教諭倫批：詳經制，酌時宜，惟此作得之。
考試官教諭譙批：良法美意，燦然畢陳。
爲政之道，其猶張弓乎？高者仰之，下者俯之，高下隨機而應手，惟其中而已矣。其猶調瑟乎？緩則急之，急則緩之，緩急隨宜以諧聲，惟其適而已矣。養由基之於射也，伯牙之於琴也，帝王之於天下也，亦大都若此矣。是故高岸爲谷，深谷爲陵，言時勢之有變更而不可常也；冬日則飲湯，夏日則飲水，言處事之貴識時而不可泥也。天運
translation_en:
… as a reply to the enlightened question.

Fourth Question

Liu Xinzheng 劉信徵

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Jin 靳 comments: "Measuring the fields and equalizing taxes reflects the grand heart of Our Sovereign in graciously benefiting the common people. You are able to synthesize past and present broadly, propagate His virtuous intent, and moreover devise a long-term plan for the people of Yunnan (Dian 滇), rather than merely plagiarizing trite sayings. This fully demonstrates practical utility in statecraft; I select it for publication."

Examiner and Instructor Lun 倫 comments: "Detailing regular institutions and weighing what is appropriate to the times—only this essay captures it."

Examiner and Instructor Qiao 譙 comments: "Sound methods and admirable intentions are brilliantly set forth in full."

Is not the way of governance like drawing a bow? What is high, one raises; what is low, one lowers [or conversely, adjusting elevation according to height]; high and low respond to the hand according to the moment, aiming only to hit the mark. Is it not like tuning a zither (se 瑟)? What is slack, one tightens; what is taut, one loosens; slackness and tautness are adjusted as appropriate to harmonize the sound, aiming only at what is fitting. What Yang Youji 養由基 was to archery, what Bo Ya 伯牙 was to the lute (qin 琴), and what emperors and kings are to the realm—in general, all are like this. Therefore, "high banks become valleys, and deep valleys become hills" speaks of how temporal circumstances undergo change and cannot remain constant; "in winter one drinks hot broth, and in summer one drinks cold water" speaks of how in handling affairs it is vital to recognize the times and not be rigidly bound. As Heaven's cycle…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而人從時至而事起不師古人致治之迹
而師古人用意之精不爲一切苟且之圖
而爲經乆可行之計斯則君子之所以神
化宜民而善其治於不窮者爾夫自載籍
以來其所稱至治之世至周焉極矣周人
致治之法則莫善於井田然而非始於周
也蓋聞黃帝時八家爲井井開四道而分
八宅鑿井於其中是井田之所由來者遠
矣唐虞夏商大率相沿至周而始大備今
===
考其田在鄉遂者掌之以遂人周禮所謂
十夫有畛百夫有洫千夫有澮萬夫有路
者其職也在都鄙者掌之以匠人周禮所
謂二耜爲耦九夫爲井十里爲成百里爲
同者其職也當此之時田有定分民有恒
業雖恣睢武悍之夫無所用其兼併古云
和協輯睦於是乎興敦龐純固於是乎成
其周人制產之法之謂乎夷考其賦則斂
財屬之遂師使入野賦於王府矣而又有
punctuated: 而人從，時至而事起。不師古人致治之迹，而師古人用意之精；不爲一切苟且之圖，而爲經乆可行之計。斯則君子之所以神化宜民，而善其治於不窮者爾。夫自載籍以來，其所稱至治之世，至周焉極矣。周人致治之法，則莫善於井田，然而非始於周也。蓋聞黃帝時八家爲井，井開四道而分八宅，鑿井於其中，是井田之所由來者遠矣。唐、虞、夏、商，大率相沿，至周而始大備。今考其田，在鄉遂者掌之以遂人，《周禮》所謂「十夫有畛，百夫有洫，千夫有澮，萬夫有路」者，其職也；在都鄙者掌之以匠人，《周禮》所謂「二耜爲耦，九夫爲井，十里爲成，百里爲同」者，其職也。當此之時，田有定分，民有恒業，雖恣睢武悍之夫，無所用其兼併。古云：「和協輯睦，於是乎興；敦龐純固，於是乎成。」其周人制產之法之謂乎！夷考其賦，則斂財屬之遂師，使入野賦於王府矣；而又有
translation_en: … moves and men follow; the time arrives and affairs arise. One does not imitate the outward traces of how the ancients achieved order, but rather imitates the essence of the ancients' intentions; one does not make temporary, makeshift schemes, but rather devises enduring, practicable plans. This is how the noble man wonderfully transforms things to suit the people and perfects his governance inexhaustibly. Now, since written records began, what have been praised as ages of supreme governance reached their pinnacle in the Zhou. Among the methods by which the men of Zhou achieved order, none was better than the well-field system (jingtian), yet it did not begin with the Zhou. Indeed, we hear that in the time of the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi), eight families formed a "well" (jing); the well opened up four pathways to divide eight homesteads, with a water well dug in the center—thus the origin of the well-field system goes back very far. Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang generally followed this system in succession, and only in the Zhou did it become fully complete. If we now examine their fields: those in the six districts (xiang) and six outskirts (sui) were managed by the Grand Extensioner (Suiren)—what the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) refers to as "ten households have a footpath along the ditch (), a hundred households have a channel (xu), a thousand households have a canal (kuai), and ten thousand households have a road" was his duty; those in the princely domains and peripheral townships (dubi) were managed by the Master Craftsman (Jiangren)—what the Rites of Zhou refers to as "two plowshares form a pair, nine households form a well (jing), ten li square form a league (cheng), and a hundred li square form a commonality (tong)" was his duty. At that time, fields had fixed allotments and the people had constant livelihoods; even unruly, fierce, and aggressive men had no way to practice land annexation. As the ancients said: "Harmony, cooperation, and concord thereby arose; generosity, simplicity, and steadfastness were thereby achieved." Does this not refer to the Zhou method of regulating property? When we further examine their taxation, the collection of wealth was assigned to the Outskirts Preceptor (Suishi), who was made to deliver the imposts of the open country to the Royal Treasury; and there was also…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
縣師掌邦國都鄙稍甸郊里之地域而辨
其夫家人民田萊之數及其六畜車輦之
稽以歲時徵其賦貢總之皆惟正之供也
任衆屬之鄉大夫使定公事之征舍矣而
又有均人掌均力政豐年則公旬用三日
中年則公旬用二日無年則公旬用一日
凶札則無力政無財賦總之皆撙節之意
也當此之時賦有定法下有常供雖饕餮
猛鷙之吏無所肆其多取古云事之供給
===
於是乎在民之蕃庶於是乎生其周人經
賦之法之謂乎秦不師古佐以商君於是
阡陌開而良法廢人皆以此爲秦罪固也
而說者謂非自秦始蓋自魯宣初稅畝而
什一之制始壞自李悝盡地力而溝塗之
界無存是秦人之阡陌固已濫觴於此矣
嗟夫世道之不古猶水之愈趨而愈下也
秦爲不道蕩滅古法罪蓋未易更僕數乃
其壞井田而阡陌之者勢實使之而於秦
punctuated:
縣師掌邦國、都鄙、稍、甸、郊、里之地域，而辨其夫家人民田萊之數，及其六畜車輦之稽，以歲時徵其賦貢，總之皆惟正之供也；任衆屬之鄉大夫，使定公事之征舍矣，而又有均人掌均力政，豐年則公旬用三日，中年則公旬用二日，無年則公旬用一日，凶札則無力政、無財賦，總之皆撙節之意也。當此之時，賦有定法，下有常供，雖饕餮猛鷙之吏，無所肆其多取。古云：「事之供給，於是乎在；民之蕃庶，於是乎生。」其周人經賦之法之謂乎！

秦不師古，佐以商君，於是阡陌開而良法廢，人皆以此爲秦罪，固也；而說者謂非自秦始，蓋自魯宣初稅畝，而什一之制始壞；自李悝盡地力，而溝塗之界無存，是秦人之阡陌固已濫觴於此矣。嗟夫！世道之不古，猶水之愈趨而愈下也。秦爲不道，蕩滅古法，罪蓋未易更僕數；乃其壞井田而阡陌之者，勢實使之，而於秦
translation_en:
…the Master of the Districts (Xianshi) was in charge of the territories of the feudatory states, capital domains, outer districts, royal domains, suburbs, and neighborhoods, distinguishing the numbers of their households, people, cultivated fields, and fallow lands, as well as auditing their six domestic animals and carts and hand-barrows, so as to levy their taxes and tribute according to the seasons of the year—in short, all of these were solely legitimate statutory contributions. The employment of the multitude belonged to the Township Grandees (Xiang dafu), who were charged with determining who should be conscripted for or exempted from public service; and there were also the Equalizers (Junren), in charge of equalizing labor services: in years of abundance, public corvée employed people for three days; in average years, public corvée employed them for two days; in poor years, public corvée employed them for one day; and in times of famine and epidemic, there were neither labor services nor property taxes—in short, all of this reflected the intention of moderation and restraint. At that time, taxation had fixed laws and those below had regular obligations, so that even rapacious, fierce, and predatory officials had no way to indulge in excessive exactions. As the ancients said: "Herein lies the supply for state affairs; herein arises the flourishing multitude of the people." Surely this refers to the Zhou system of regulating taxes!

Qin did not model itself on antiquity; assisted by Lord Shang (Shang Jun), it opened up the field paths and ridges (qianmo) and abolished the good laws. Everyone considers this the crime of Qin, which is certainly true. Yet commentators say that it did not begin with Qin: for ever since Duke Xuan of Lu first taxed by the acre (mu), the system of the one-tenth tithe began to decay; and ever since Li Kui exhausted the productivity of the soil, the boundaries of ditches and pathways ceased to exist. Thus the opened field paths of the people of Qin had indeed already originated here. Alas! That the ways of the world do not match antiquity is like water flowing ever downward as it rushes on.
