Qin acted without principle and swept away ancient laws; its crimes could hardly be counted even if one changed relays of servants. Yet as for its destroying the well-field system and turning it into open ridges and paths, the trend of circumstances truly made it so, and toward Qin…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
又何誅焉赤帝受命去古未遠顧獨不能
變秦法以復井田人皆以此爲漢咎固也
而說者又曰復古難夫以智如酇侯能收
前代之圖籍賢如子房猶有儒者之氣象
使井田而可復則漢人當先爲之矣嗟夫
書契苟可觀固不必結繩而後爲古也昔
人謂欲復井田非數百年專力不可又云
古者自治其國終嵗惟井田一事今統一
天下吏數代易就使爲之終無成效而於
===
漢又何惑焉自是而後法制代變得失世
殊以田言之漢武行代田之法孝哀下限
田之議唐人有授田之制宋人定方田之
等是皆不失爲一代之美意而求其最近
古者其惟唐之授田乎考其制成人者人
授一頃其田十畝爲口分二十畝爲永業
凡徙鄉及貧無以葬者得鬻世業自狹鄉
徙寛鄉者得鬻口分已鬻者不復受此殆
庶幾於周人一夫百畝之法可謂得矣然
punctuated: 又何誅焉？赤帝受命，去古未遠，顧獨不能變秦法以復井田，人皆以此爲漢咎，固也。而說者又曰：「復古難。」夫以智如酇侯，能收前代之圖籍；賢如子房，猶有儒者之氣象。使井田而可復，則漢人當先爲之矣。嗟夫！書契苟可觀，固不必結繩而後爲古也。昔人謂欲復井田，非數百年專力不可。又云：「古者自治其國，終嵗惟井田一事；今統一天下，吏數代易，就使爲之，終無成效。」而於漢又何惑焉？自是而後，法制代變，得失世殊。以田言之：漢武行代田之法，孝哀下限田之議，唐人有授田之制，宋人定方田之等。是皆不失爲一代之美意，而求其最近古者，其惟唐之授田乎？考其制，成人者人授一頃，其田十畝爲口分，二十畝爲永業。凡徙鄉及貧無以葬者，得鬻世業；自狹鄉徙寛鄉者，得鬻口分；已鬻者不復受。此殆庶幾於周人一夫百畝之法，可謂得矣。然
translation_en:
…what is there to condemn? When the Red Emperor [Liu Bang 劉邦] received the Mandate, antiquity was not yet far off, yet he alone was unable to alter the laws of Qin to restore the well-field system. Everyone takes this to be the fault of Han, and naturally so. Yet commentators also say: "Restoring antiquity is difficult." Now, with someone as wise as the Marquis of Zan [Xiao He 蕭何], who knew to collect the maps and registers of the preceding dynasty, and someone as worthy as Zifang [Zhang Liang 張良], who still possessed the bearing of a Confucian scholar—if the well-field system could have been restored, the men of Han would surely have been the first to do it. Alas! So long as written records can be observed, one certainly need not return to knotted cords in order to be considered ancient. Men of the past said that if one wished to restore the well-field system, it could not be done without several hundred years of dedicated effort. They also said: "In antiquity, rulers governed their own states, and throughout the year the well-field system was their sole affair; today, all under Heaven is unified, and officials are repeatedly replaced, so even if one tried to carry it out, in the end there would be no success." What then is there to be puzzled about regarding the Han?

From this time onward, laws and institutions changed from dynasty to dynasty, and their merits and defects differed from age to age. Speaking in terms of land: Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wu 漢武) practiced the method of alternating fields (daitian 代田), Emperor Xiao'ai (孝哀) sent down proposals for limiting landholdings (xiantian 限田), the men of Tang had the system of land allotment (shoutian 授田), and the men of Song established the grades of square fields (fangtian 方田). None of these failed to be fine intentions of their respective eras, yet if we seek the one closest to antiquity, would it not be solely the land allotment of Tang? Examining its system, each adult was allotted one qing of land, of which ten [sic, for eighty] mu of land were personal share (koufen 口分) and twenty mu were hereditary tenure (yongye 永業). All those who relocated to another district or were too poor to bury their dead were permitted to sell their hereditary tenure; those who moved from congested districts to spacious districts were permitted to sell their personal share; once sold, land was not granted again. This came close to the Zhou method of one hundred mu per husbandman, and can be said to have succeeded. Yet…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其後也羡田無厲禁而鬻田遂多惰民不
嚴驅而遊食日衆此則弊生於法乆亦其
末流之所必至者固不可以是不病授田
也以賦言之漢初十五而稅一光武稅一
於三十唐有租庸調之名宋有均稅之限
是皆不失為一時之良法而求其最近古
者其惟唐之租庸調乎考其制有田則有
租歲無過二石也有家則有調隨其土之
所出也有身則有庸役無過二十日也此
===
===
殆髣髴於周人粟布力役之征可謂得矣
然其失也户口之盛衰不一而怨起於取
盈流移之虛實難稽而奸生於避役故其
後行兩稅而專主資産蓋所以矯其專主
户口之弊固未可以是而病楊炎也洪惟
我
國家法古為治不惟其迹而惟其意田有官
民是殷人助法之遺也賦有等則是夏后
則壤之制也限有夏秋是周官以時徵財
punctuated: 其後也，羡田無厲禁，而鬻田遂多；惰民不嚴驅，而遊食日衆。此則弊生於法乆，亦其末流之所必至者，固不可以是不病授田也。以賦言之，漢初十五而稅一，光武稅一於三十，唐有租庸調之名，宋有均稅之限，是皆不失為一時之良法，而求其最近古者，其惟唐之租庸調乎？考其制，有田則有租，歲無過二石也；有家則有調，隨其土之所出也；有身則有庸，役無過二十日也。此殆髣髴於周人粟、布、力役之征，可謂得矣。然其失也，户口之盛衰不一，而怨起於取盈；流移之虛實難稽，而奸生於避役。故其後行兩稅而專主資産，蓋所以矯其專主户口之弊，固未可以是而病楊炎也。洪惟我國家法古為治，不惟其迹而惟其意。田有官民，是殷人助法之遺也；賦有等則，是夏后則壤之制也；限有夏秋，是周官以時徵財
translation_en:
…later on, there were no strict prohibitions against surplus landholding, and so the selling of land became widespread; idle people were not rigorously driven back to farming, and so vagrant consumers grew more numerous by the day. These were abuses that arose from the system remaining in place for a long time, and were also the inevitable outcome of its later degeneration; yet one certainly cannot on this account refrain from criticizing the land-allotment system.

To speak in terms of taxation: in the early Han, the tax was one-fifteenth of the harvest, while Emperor Guangwu taxed one-thirtieth; the Tang had the system known as grain-tax, corvée, and cloth-tax (zuyongdiao 租庸調), and the Song had quotas for equalized taxation (junshui 均稅). All of these may be considered good laws for their time, yet if we seek the one closest to antiquity, is it not the grain-tax, corvée, and cloth-tax system of the Tang? Examining its regulations: where there was land, there was a grain tax (zu 租), not exceeding two piculs (shi 石) per year; where there was a household, there was a cloth or local-product levy (diao 調), according to what the local soil produced; where there was an adult male, there was corvée labor (yong 庸), with service not exceeding twenty days. This closely resembled the Zhou-dynasty levies of grain, cloth, and labor service, and may well be called a success. Yet in its decline, the flourishing and waning of registered households were uneven, and resentment arose from demands to meet full quotas; the truth or falsity of population displacement and migration became difficult to verify, and fraud grew out of efforts to evade labor service. Therefore, when the Two-Tax system (liangshui 兩稅) was subsequently implemented and based taxation exclusively on property and assets, it was intended to rectify the abuses of basing taxation exclusively on household registration; one certainly cannot on this account criticize Yang Yan 楊炎.

Humbly reflecting on our State, it models its governance upon antiquity—not merely following its outward traces, but grasping its inner intent. That land is divided into official and private fields is a legacy of the mutual-aid (zhu 助) system of the Yin people; that taxation is graded according to ranks and schedules follows the system of grading the soil instituted by the Xia sovereigns; and that collection deadlines are set in summer and autumn embodies the principle of the Zhou Offices (Zhouguan 周官) in levying revenue according to the seasons…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之義也其間經畫之詳意義之精蓋陋漢
唐宋於不足言陸贄所謂其取法也遠其
立意也深其斂財也均其成人也固其裁
規也簡其備患也周此六言者我
國家田賦之法足以當之矣第法行日久弊
亦潜滋侵隱詭射至難究詰我
皇上軫念民瘼謂此弊且不可長會有以度田
請者
上於是可其奏
===
===
令天下遍度民田焉百年來伏奸積弊一旦掃
而更之卽滇省僻在萬里外亦有以荷
天子之仁窮荒父老扶杖相呼願少須臾無死
此千載而一時也執事又欲以此時定經
久之計愚生末學其焉能知之顧聞之道
路則曰稽籍之法不可不嚴也導利之政
不可不講也仁言之頒不可不信也夫今
度田且告竣矣其田畝之廣狹賦額之多
寡業且書之于版籍矣覈之不嚴則奸民
punctuated: 之義也。其間經畫之詳、意義之精，蓋陋漢、唐、宋於不足言。陸贄所謂「其取法也遠，其立意也深，其斂財也均，其成人也固，其裁規也簡，其備患也周」，此六言者，我國家田賦之法足以當之矣。第法行日久，弊亦潜滋，侵隱詭射，至難究詰。我皇上軫念民瘼，謂此弊且不可長，會有以度田請者，上於是可其奏，令天下遍度民田焉。百年來伏奸積弊，一旦掃而更之，卽滇省僻在萬里外，亦有以荷天子之仁，窮荒父老扶杖相呼，願少須臾無死，此千載而一時也。執事又欲以此時定經久之計，愚生末學，其焉能知之？顧聞之道路，則曰：稽籍之法不可不嚴也，導利之政不可不講也，仁言之頒不可不信也。夫今度田且告竣矣，其田畝之廣狹、賦額之多寡，業且書之于版籍矣。覈之不嚴，則奸民
translation_en: …collecting revenues according to the seasons. Within this system, the thoroughness of its planning and the subtlety of its meaning render the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties too crude to be worth mentioning. As Lu Zhi 陸贄 said: "Its model is drawn from afar, its underlying intent is profound, its collection of wealth is equitable, its completion of the people's livelihood is secure, its governing regulations are simple, and its precautions against trouble are comprehensive." The land-tax laws of our Dynasty are fully worthy of these six statements. Yet when laws have been in force for a long time, abuses secretly proliferate; encroachment, concealment, and fraudulent evasion have become extremely difficult to investigate and prosecute. Our Emperor, feeling deep compassion for the sufferings of the people, declared that such abuses must not be allowed to grow. Just then, someone submitted a memorial requesting a land survey; His Majesty thereupon approved the memorial and ordered that private lands be surveyed throughout the empire. The hidden frauds and accumulated abuses of a hundred years were swept away and reformed in a single morning. Even in Yunnan province, remote as it is ten thousand li away, the people have been able to receive the benevolence of the Son of Heaven; elders in the farthest wilderness lean on their staffs and call out to one another, wishing to linger a little longer before dying—truly, this is a once-in-a-thousand-years opportunity! Now you, Sir, wish to take advantage of this moment to establish a permanent plan. As a foolish student of shallow learning, how could I possibly know how to do so? Yet from what I have heard in the streets, people say: the method of auditing the registers must be made strict; policies for guiding beneficial resources must be discussed; and the promulgation of benevolent words must be made trustworthy. Now the surveying of the fields is nearly complete, and the breadth or narrowness of the acreage as well as the size of the tax quotas are already being recorded in the registers. If the verification is not strict, then treacherous commoners…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
富室私與胥吏爲市其田必以廣爲狹其
賦必以多爲寡甚則盡其數而隱之以爲
無而且以其所隱所損之數移而加之貧
懦之夫是小民之所以受毒而無告也至
其尤甚者則或惡其害已而去其籍是故
周官書版之職掌之以司民今而後知聖
人之爲慮遠也爲今之計其必專稽覈之
官而密收藏之地重欺隱之懲而嚴去籍
之禁此弊庶幾少戢乎夫
===
今天下財賦盛於東南而吳越其首稱也以
全滇財賦乃不及彼一大縣此何以故哉
吳越沮洳之地水利弘多故能化荒瘠爲
沃壤滇之爲田者大半皆狐狸嗥聚之區
而荊榛莽棘之所翳也今田則清矣賦則
均矣然或昊天不惠玄冥失職則雖漢陰
丈人何所負而灌焉是故周禮治野之制
必有溝澮以時其畜洩聖人固非樂爲是
多事也玆欲爲久計其必遍山畦而溝洫
punctuated: 富室私與胥吏爲市，其田必以廣爲狹，其賦必以多爲寡，甚則盡其數而隱之以爲無，而且以其所隱所損之數移而加之貧懦之夫，是小民之所以受毒而無告也。至其尤甚者，則或惡其害已而去其籍。是故《周官》書版之職掌之以司民，今而後知聖人之爲慮遠也。爲今之計，其必專稽覈之官而密收藏之地，重欺隱之懲而嚴去籍之禁，此弊庶幾少戢乎！夫今天下財賦盛於東南，而吳、越其首稱也。以全滇財賦，乃不及彼一大縣，此何以故哉？吳、越沮洳之地，水利弘多，故能化荒瘠爲沃壤；滇之爲田者，大半皆狐狸嗥聚之區，而荊榛莽棘之所翳也。今田則清矣，賦則均矣，然或昊天不惠，玄冥失職，則雖漢陰丈人何所負而灌焉？是故《周禮》治野之制，必有溝澮以時其畜洩，聖人固非樂爲是多事也。玆欲爲久計，其必遍山畦而溝洫
translation_en:
…and wealthy households privately strike deals with subofficial functionaries; they will certainly report their broad fields as narrow, and their heavy tax quotas as light. In extreme cases, they conceal the entire amount and claim to have none at all, and furthermore shift the concealed and reduced amounts onto poor and weak men. This is why the common people suffer harm with no one to appeal to. In the most extreme cases, some even destroy the registers because they dislike that the records are detrimental to themselves. For this reason, in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the duty of inscribing the population and land registers was entrusted to the Director of the Multitudes (Simin); only now do we realize how far-reaching was the foresight of the sages! As a plan for today, we must appoint officials dedicated specifically to auditing and verifying, secure the places where the registers are stored, impose heavy punishments for fraudulent concealment, and strictly enforce the prohibition against destroying registers—then perhaps this abuse may be slightly curbed!

Now, in the empire today, revenue and taxes flourish most in the southeast, with Wu and Yue foremost among them. Yet the revenue and taxes of the entire province of Yunnan do not even equal those of a single large county there—why is this so? In the low-lying, marshy lands of Wu and Yue, waterworks are abundant, enabling them to transform barren lands into fertile soil. What serves as farmland in Yunnan, by contrast, is for the most part territory where foxes howl and gather, choked with brambles, thorns, and thickets. Now the fields have been surveyed and cleared, and the taxes have been equalized; yet if August Heaven sends no favor and Xuanming [the god of water and winter] fails in his duty, then even if there were an old man from the south bank of the Han River, what water could he carry in his pitcher to irrigate them? Therefore, in the system for managing the countryside in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), there had to be ditches and channels to regulate the storage and drainage of water according to the seasons; the sages certainly did not take pleasure in creating such extra trouble. If we now wish to make a long-term plan, we must construct ditches and channels across all the mountain fields…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之治之者務擇其官開之者無擇其地不
惜小費以妨大利靡憚一勞而廢永逸斯
則鄭國開渠之惠也滇之民庶幾其有濟
乎夫
今天下之富厚廣大所乏者非財也要在不
爲民病耳頃者度田有
詔謂田必度而賦不加
仁至渥矣民之蚩蚩惟恐度出餘田未免額外
之賦故羣然咻之以爲不便今乃知其必
===
不加也則又欣然以喜而猶未能帖然安
也儻其後有喜事之人謂餘田過多欲稍
稍加其賦而將掠之以爲己功吾恐華夷
雜居之地人貧而多野心苟使重困寧保
其無他虞乎是故周官厚下之政恒薄征
以寬其財力聖人固非樂爲是損上也玆
欲爲久計其必時申不加賦之令而長遵
守之勒之版圖堅於金石毋謂田額之有
餘而盡力以求焉毋謂賦額之未充而竭
punctuated: 之，治之者務擇其官，開之者無擇其地，不惜小費以妨大利，靡憚一勞而廢永逸，斯則鄭國開渠之惠也，滇之民庶幾其有濟乎？夫今天下之富厚廣大，所乏者非財也，要在不爲民病耳。頃者度田有詔，謂田必度而賦不加，仁至渥矣。民之蚩蚩，惟恐度出餘田，未免額外之賦，故羣然咻之以爲不便；今乃知其必不加也，則又欣然以喜，而猶未能帖然安也。儻其後有喜事之人，謂餘田過多，欲稍稍加其賦，而將掠之以爲己功，吾恐華夷雜居之地，人貧而多野心，苟使重困，寧保其無他虞乎？是故《周官》厚下之政，恒薄征以寬其財力，聖人固非樂爲是損上也。玆欲爲久計，其必時申不加賦之令而長遵守之，勒之版圖，堅於金石，毋謂田額之有餘而盡力以求焉，毋謂賦額之未充而竭
translation_en:
… them. Those who manage the work must carefully select the right officials, and those who excavate them should leave no suitable ground untouched—neither begrudging minor expenses so as to obstruct great benefits, nor shrinking from a single effort so as to forfeit lasting ease. This would truly bring the beneficence of Zheng Guo 鄭國 digging his canal, and the people of Yunnan might then find relief!

Now, given the abundant wealth and vast expanse of the realm today, what is lacking is not revenue; the essential point is simply not to burden the people. Recently, an imperial edict ordered the surveying of fields, declaring that while the land must be measured, the tax quota would not be increased. Such benevolence is rich indeed! Yet the ignorant common folk, fearing only that the newly surveyed surplus fields would inevitably incur extra-quota taxes, clamored in unison that the measure was inconvenient. Now that they know taxes will definitely not be increased, they rejoice gladly, though they are still unable to feel completely at ease. Should some meddlesome official hereafter claim that the surplus land is excessive and wish to gradually raise its tax in order to claim the credit for himself, I fear that in this region where Chinese and non-Chinese live intermingled, where the people are poor and harbor unruly ambitions, if they are subjected to redoubled hardship, how can we guarantee that no unforeseen troubles will arise?

Therefore, in the policies for generously favoring those below in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), levies were constantly kept light so as to spare the people's financial strength; the sages certainly did not take pleasure in diminishing the ruler's share for its own sake. If we now wish to form a long-term plan, we must repeatedly reaffirm the order against increasing taxes and abide by it permanently, inscribing it into the population and land registers as firmly as in metal and stone. Let no one say there is a surplus over the land quota and exhaustively seek to extract from it; let no one say the tax quota is unfulfilled and drain…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
澤以求魚斯則魏文侯却賀之意也滇之
民庶幾其有瘳乎夫如是則田不必井而
周人致治之本旨猶在固無害其爲善治
也賦不必周而周官惠民之精義猶存亦
不害其爲宜民也孔子答魯公曰豈弟君
子民之父母未有子富而父貧者也使末
議可以濟滇民其於
國計寧獨無少裨乎哉抑先儒有言曰必有
關雎麟趾之意而後可以行周官之法度
===
是又願治者所當先也執事以爲然否
第五問
趙儒
同考試官訓導董批滇省阻逖西南通道粵蜀
之議久矣乃格於眾見竟成道謀子能大越拘攣條析利害鑿
鑿可行寔萬世之長利也
考試官敎諭倫批卓犖之見閎博之議具見
此篇子其識時務者耶
考試官敎諭譙批計慮深遠區畫詳明
punctuated:
澤以求魚，斯則魏文侯却賀之意也，滇之民庶幾其有瘳乎！夫如是，則田不必井，而周人致治之本旨猶在，固無害其爲善治也；賦不必周，而周官惠民之精義猶存，亦不害其爲宜民也。孔子答魯公曰：「豈弟君子，民之父母。未有子富而父貧者也。」使末議可以濟滇民，其於國計寧獨無少裨乎哉！抑先儒有言曰：「必有《關雎》、《麟趾》之意，而後可以行《周官》之法度。」是又願治者所當先也。執事以爲然否？

第五問
趙儒
同考試官訓導董批：〔滇省阻逖西南，通道粵蜀之議久矣，乃格於眾見，竟成道謀。子能大越拘攣，條析利害，鑿鑿可行，寔萬世之長利也。〕
考試官敎諭倫批：〔卓犖之見，閎博之議，具見此篇，子其識時務者耶！〕
考試官敎諭譙批：〔計慮深遠，區畫詳明。〕
translation_en:
… [drain the] marsh to catch fish. This is the very spirit in which Marquis Wen of Wei (Wei Wenhou 魏文侯) declined congratulations; then the people of Yunnan (Dian 滇) may perhaps find some relief! If this is done, then even though the fields need not be organized into the well-field system, the fundamental intent by which the men of Zhou achieved good order will still be present, which certainly does not prevent it from being good governance; and even though the land tax need not follow the Zhou system, the essential meaning of the *Offices of Zhou* (Zhouguan 周官) in showing beneficence to the people will still be preserved, which likewise does not prevent it from suiting the people. Confucius replied to the Duke of Lu, saying: "An easy anderca [amiable] gentleman is the father and mother of the people. Never has there been a case where the children were rich and the father was poor." If my humble proposal can bring relief to the people of Yunnan, how could it fail to be of some slight benefit to the state finances as well? Moreover, a former Confucian scholar once said: "There must first be the moral spirit of the 'Ospreys' (Guanju 關雎) and the 'Unicorn's Hoof' (Linzhi 麟趾) before one can put into practice the institutional regulations of the *Offices of Zhou*." This, again, is what those who desire good governance ought to put first. Does Your Excellency consider this to be so or not?

Fifth Policy Question
By Zhao Ru 趙儒
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Dong comments: "Yunnan Province lies isolated and remote in the southwest. Proposals to open up thoroughfares to Guangdong/Guangxi (Yue 粵) and Sichuan (Shu 蜀) have been discussed for a long time, yet they were obstructed by conventional opinions and ended up as mere roadside talk. You have been able to rise far above narrow constraints and analyze the advantages and disadvantages item by item; your proposals are concrete and practicable, truly a lasting benefit for ten thousand generations."
Examiner and Instructor Lun comments: "Extraordinary insight and broad, far-reaching discussion are fully evident in this essay. Are you not indeed one who understands the affairs of the times!"
Examiner and Instructor Qiao comments: "The deliberation is deep and far-sighted; the planning is detailed and clear."

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
理國猶治身然形氣壯實則精神充盛血
脉流通則痿痺之患不作人民者邦之形
氣山川險要關隘道路者邦之血脉也人
民寡鮮氣勢卑弱則外侮得以侵凌封壤
阻塞鄰援隔絕則窺伺負固之徒萌跋扈
之心而漸不可長善固國者必使吾民生
養蕃息足耕足戰民不改聚而擅富强之
勝至於水陸要害可嚴則嚴可闢則闢使
吾之中國聲勢聯絡唇齒相依出則折衝
===
外侮內則釁孽不萌而磐石之固在我矣
舍此不圖是自坐深穽而不顧凌壓之虞
非計之得者也執事察全滇之形勝籌保
國之令圖咨諏及此遐方之士生長四塞
之中日夜念此至熟也夫良醫之治病也
察其形色觀其脉理閼塞不通必加劑砭
以疎决之而後其人可以望壽考而無病
故參苓之與烏附竝行不廢否則人之病
蹶然不瘳矣理國何以異此夫今日之滇
punctuated: 理國猶治身然：形氣壯實，則精神充盛；血脉流通，則痿痺之患不作。人民者，邦之形氣；山川險要、關隘道路者，邦之血脉也。人民寡鮮，氣勢卑弱，則外侮得以侵凌；封壤阻塞，鄰援隔絕，則窺伺負固之徒萌跋扈之心，而漸不可長。善固國者，必使吾民生養蕃息，足耕足戰，民不改聚，而擅富强之勝；至於水陸要害，可嚴則嚴，可闢則闢，使吾之中國聲勢聯絡，唇齒相依，出則折衝外侮，內則釁孽不萌，而磐石之固在我矣。舍此不圖，是自坐深穽而不顧凌壓之虞，非計之得者也。執事察全滇之形勝，籌保國之令圖，咨諏及此。遐方之士，生長四塞之中，日夜念此至熟也。夫良醫之治病也，察其形色，觀其脉理，閼塞不通，必加劑砭以疎决之，而後其人可以望壽考而無病，故參苓之與烏附竝行不廢；否則，人之病蹶然不瘳矣。理國何以異此？夫今日之滇
translation_en: Governing a state is like treating the human body: when the physical form and vital energy are strong and solid, the spirit is full and vigorous; when the blood and vessels flow freely, the ailments of atrophy and numbness do not arise. The people are the physical form and vital energy of the state; the strategic mountains and rivers, passes and roads are the blood and vessels of the state. If the people are few and scarce, and the momentum and vigor are low and weak, then foreign threats are able to encroach and bully; if the territory's borders are blocked and obstructed, and aid from neighbors is cut off, then those who spy for opportunities and rely on natural strongholds will sprout domineering and rebellious intentions, a tendency that must not be allowed to grow. Those who are skilled at securing a state must ensure that our people are nurtured and multiply, sufficient for farming and sufficient for fighting, so that without altering the gathering of the people, the state commands the advantage of wealth and strength; as for strategic points by land and water, where they should be strictly guarded, guard them strictly, and where they should be opened up, open them up, so that our central realm has its prestige and momentum connected, mutually dependent like lips and teeth—going forth, it repels foreign aggression; within, dissension and rebellion do not sprout, and rock-solid security rests with us. To set this aside and not plan for it is to sit oneself down in a deep pit while ignoring the danger of being crushed from above; this is not a sound plan. Your Excellency has examined the strategic topography of all Yunnan, planned admirable schemes for preserving the state, and inquired into this matter. As a scholar of a distant region, born and raised amidst barriers on all four sides, I have pondered this day and night until I am thoroughly familiar with it. Now, when a good physician treats an illness, he examines the patient's physical appearance and complexion and observes the courses of the pulse; where there is blockage and obstruction so that nothing passes through, he must apply medicinal doses and stone needles to clear and open them, and only afterward can the person hope for longevity and freedom from illness. Therefore, ginseng and poria are used alongside aconite without either being discarded; otherwise, a person's illness will end in collapse without being cured. How is governing a state any different from this? Now, the Yunnan of today…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
土可謂晏然寧謐如强壯之人也無故而
煩民畚鑿以興得已之役不以爲紆則擾
故曰非常之原黎民懼焉然深憂遠慮之
士玄究往牒指畫方輿圖險易於目前計
興衰於事外安能徇尋常之尠議而忽豪
傑之沉謀哉何者滇土天下之遠藩處夷
落之中爲中國屏蔽其守與內地異周禮
孟冬之月有司坏城郭固封疆完要塞塞
蹊徑此爲備外者言之也若滇則孤懸萬
===
里恃中國以爲聲援其地遼闊廣遠實東
則西虛南顧則北單弱不患無地而患無
人以守外有窺伺之虞而內有負固之漸
如秦之函谷蜀之劒門一夫當關萬夫莫
開非如中州之四通五達一號召之間士
馬雲集無仰哺待救之難也甞考自古入
滇之路有三楚將莊蹻略巴黔以西威定
屬楚其所由入則今之貴州古之牂牁郡
也南越以財物役屬夜郎漢王然于乘誅
punctuated: 土，可謂晏然寧謐，如强壯之人也。無故而煩民畚鑿，以興得已之役，不以爲紆則擾，故曰「非常之原，黎民懼焉」。然深憂遠慮之士，玄究往牒，指畫方輿，圖險易於目前，計興衰於事外，安能徇尋常之尠議，而忽豪傑之沉謀哉？何者？滇土，天下之遠藩，處夷落之中，爲中國屏蔽，其守與內地異。《周禮》孟冬之月，有司坏城郭、固封疆、完要塞、塞蹊徑，此爲備外者言之也。若滇則孤懸萬里，恃中國以爲聲援。其地遼闊廣遠，實東則西虛，南顧則北單弱，不患無地，而患無人以守。外有窺伺之虞，而內有負固之漸，如秦之函谷、蜀之劒門，一夫當關，萬夫莫開，非如中州之四通五達，一號召之間，士馬雲集，無仰哺待救之難也。甞考自古入滇之路有三：楚將莊蹻略巴黔以西，威定屬楚，其所由入，則今之貴州、古之牂牁郡也；南越以財物役屬夜郎，漢王然于乘誅
translation_en: … territory can be said to be calm and tranquil, like a strong and healthy person. To trouble the people without cause with baskets and chisels in order to undertake dispensable public works would be regarded as either circuitous or disruptive; hence it is said, "At the inception of extraordinary undertakings, the common people are afraid." Yet how could men of deep concern and far-reaching foresight—who profoundly investigate past records, map out the geography on the ground, assess what is perilous and what is easy right before their eyes, and calculate rise and decline beyond immediate events—yield to ordinary, shallow opinions and neglect the deep designs of heroic minds? Why is this? The territory of Dian is a distant bulwark of the empire; situated amidst non-Chinese settlements, it serves as a protective screen for the Central Kingdom, and its defense differs from that of the interior. According to the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) [note: actually the "Monthly Ordinances" in the Record of Rites], in the first month of winter the authorities repair city walls and outer ramparts, secure borders and frontiers, fortify strategic passes, and block up mountain paths—this is spoken with reference to guarding against external foes. Dian, however, hangs isolated ten thousand li away, relying on the Central Kingdom for support and reinforcement. Its territory is vast and far-flung: if we reinforce the east, the west is left empty; if we attend to the south, the north becomes thin and weak. The worry is not a lack of land, but a lack of men to defend it. Without, there is the danger of enemies spying for an opening, while within, there is the gradual tendency to rely on natural fastnesses for defiance—like Hangu Pass in Qin or Jianmen Pass in Shu, where if one man holds the pass, ten thousand men cannot force it open. It is not like the Central Plains, where roads connect in every direction so that at a single summons troops and horses gather like clouds, without the difficulty of relying on others for provisions or waiting for relief. I have examined the routes for entering Dian since antiquity and found there are three. When the Chu general Zhuang Qiao conquered the region west of Ba and Qian, bringing it under Chu rule by his military might, the route by which he entered was present-day Guizhou, the ancient commandery of Zangke. Later, Southern Yue (Nanyue) used wealth and goods to bring Yelang into subjection, and Wang Ranyu of the Han took advantage of the prestige from executing [the rebels of]…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
南越之威脅取滇土史稱牂牁江出番禺
城下其源在田州泗城之境與雲之廣南
貴之普安實相接壤輕舟東下徑達南海
所謂南路也司馬相如持檄喻西南夷諸
葛武侯渡瀘深入皆由益部取道南中非
古所謂西路耶自昔經略西南掃蕩草竊
其故道章章若是此三道不通則全滇郡
縣四望阻塞而扼我之吭拊我之背勢所
必致矣又以其形勢言之東爲黔中在今
日爲内地固勿論若南蔽元江元江之外
爲車里此又外則爲交阯西蔽永昌永昌
之外爲麓川又外則爲緬甸西北則羈縻
麗江以爲捍蔽此外則爲吐蕃氣勢稍弱
則吐蕃西伺南交外竊西南諸夷不受約
束此又其小者天寶間張虔陀暴使滇人
唐有南詔之衂連結吐蕃終唐之世不入
職貢宋室不競遂棄爲異域蒙段二氏崛
據數百年計其士馬不足當中國一大郡
punctuated: 南越之威，脅取滇土。史稱牂牁江出番禺城下，其源在田州、泗城之境，與雲之廣南、貴之普安實相接壤，輕舟東下，徑達南海，所謂南路也。司馬相如持檄喻西南夷，諸葛武侯渡瀘深入，皆由益部取道南中，非古所謂西路耶？自昔經略西南，掃蕩草竊，其故道章章若是。此三道不通，則全滇郡縣四望阻塞，而扼我之吭，拊我之背，勢所必致矣。又以其形勢言之，東爲黔中，在今日爲内地，固勿論；若南蔽元江，元江之外爲車里，此又外則爲交阯；西蔽永昌，永昌之外爲麓川，又外則爲緬甸；西北則羈縻麗江以爲捍蔽，此外則爲吐蕃。氣勢稍弱，則吐蕃西伺，南交外竊，西南諸夷不受約束，此又其小者。天寶間，張虔陀暴使滇人，唐有南詔之衂，連結吐蕃，終唐之世不入職貢；宋室不競，遂棄爲異域。蒙、段二氏崛據數百年，計其士馬不足當中國一大郡，
translation_en:
… the prestige of having destroyed Southern Yue (Nanyue 南越) to intimidate and seize the territory of Dian 滇. The histories state that the Zangke River 牂牁江 emerges below the city walls of Panyu 番禺, and its source lies within the borders of Tianzhou 田州 and Sicheng 泗城, actually bordering Guangnan 廣南 in Yunnan and Pu'an 普安 in Guizhou; light boats going east downstream reach the Southern Sea directly—this is what is called the Southern Route. Sima Xiangru 司馬相如 carried a proclamation to instruct the Southwestern Barbarians, and Martial Marquis Zhuge (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮) crossed the Lu River 瀘水 and penetrated deeply; both started from Yizhou 益州 and took the road through Nanzhong 南中—is this not what in antiquity was called the Western Route? Since antiquity, in pacifying and administering the Southwest and sweeping away bandits and rebels, the old routes have been as clearly evident as this. If these three routes are blocked, then the prefectures and counties of all Dian look out in four directions only to find obstruction, and choking our throat and striking our back will be the inevitable outcome of the strategic situation.

Furthermore, speaking in terms of its topography: to the east is Qianzhong 黔中, which today is interior territory, so we need not discuss it. As for the south, it is shielded by Yuanjiang 元江; beyond Yuanjiang is Cheli 車里, and beyond that is Jiaozhi 交阯 (Annam). To the west, it is shielded by Yongchang 永昌; beyond Yongchang is Luchuan 麓川, and beyond that is Burma (Miandian 緬甸). To the northwest, we hold Lijiang 麗江 under loose-rein (jimi 羈縻) rule to serve as a defensive screen, and beyond this is Tibet (Tubo 吐蕃). Whenever our vigor and strength slightly weaken, Tibet spies from the west, Southern Jiao (Annam) pilfers from the outside, and the various southwestern chieftains refuse to submit to restraint—and these are still the minor matters. During the Tianbao 天寶 era (742–756), Zhang Qiantuo 張虔陀 tyrannically abused the people of Dian, and the Tang suffered the defeat at the hands of Nanzhao 南詔, which allied itself with Tibet and to the end of the Tang dynasty never again entered to present tributary obligations. The Song house was militarily weak and consequently abandoned it as foreign territory. The two clans of Meng 蒙 and Duan 段 rose up and held it for several hundred years; reckoning their troops and horses, they were not enough to match one large prefecture of the Central Plains, …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
然窮天下之力不能下者則以憑恃險遠
下流仰攻形不便勢不利也我
太祖高皇帝削平僭偽混一區宇戡定西夷置
立州郡二百年來夷靺之風變為中土編
辮之習易為冠裳一方之人如脫陰翳而
覩日月之昭融
神功
聖德輝映古今矣然執事之問若有隱憂然者
何也為滇人之慮遠也且執事所謂紆遲
===
驛遞則病於官踔遠侵掠則病於民是固
然矣然又有甚者焉中原之人入滇其道
里自西至者上荊門涉瀘水登陸陟烏撒
自南至者遡流上郴桂泛洞庭巨浸又數
千里始達沅州攀緣關嶺其鳥道盤鬱苗
夷出沒四旁於危磴中壘土築堡憑高瞭
遠晝柝宵鉦日晏啓關游徼之兵負弩尾
躡而後敢啓行士旅往來若履虎尾而蹈
春冰猶或白晝之中剽人而奪之金如此
punctuated: 然窮天下之力不能下者，則以憑恃險遠，下流仰攻，形不便、勢不利也。我太祖高皇帝削平僭偽，混一區宇，戡定西夷，置立州郡。二百年來，夷靺之風變為中土，編辮之習易為冠裳，一方之人，如脫陰翳而覩日月之昭融，神功聖德，輝映古今矣。然執事之問，若有隱憂然者，何也？為滇人之慮遠也。且執事所謂紆遲驛遞則病於官，踔遠侵掠則病於民，是固然矣；然又有甚者焉。中原之人入滇，其道里自西至者，上荊門，涉瀘水，登陸陟烏撒；自南至者，遡流上郴、桂，泛洞庭巨浸，又數千里始達沅州，攀緣關嶺。其鳥道盤鬱，苗夷出沒四旁，於危磴中壘土築堡，憑高瞭遠，晝柝宵鉦，日晏啓關，游徼之兵負弩尾躡，而後敢啓行。士旅往來，若履虎尾而蹈春冰，猶或白晝之中剽人而奪之金。如此
translation_en: … Yet the reason the exhausted strength of the entire empire could not subdue them was that they relied on their险僻 (perilous and remote terrain); attacking upward from downstream, the topography was inconvenient and the strategic position unfavorable. Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, r. 1368–1398), swept away pretenders and usurpers, unified the realm, pacified the western barbarians, and established prefectures and counties. For two hundred years, the customs of the barbarian tribes have been transformed into those of the Central Lands, and the habit of braiding hair has been changed for caps and robes. The people of this region are as though freed from dark gloom to behold the bright radiance of the sun and moon; such divine achievements and sagely virtue shine across past and present alike! Yet Your Excellency's question seems to harbor a hidden concern—why is this? It is out of far-reaching consideration for the people of Yunnan. Moreover, what Your Excellency refers to—that circuitous and slow postal relay routes are detrimental to officials, and that raiding across vast distances is detrimental to the common people—is certainly true; yet there is something even worse than this. For people from the Central Plains entering Yunnan, as for the routes: those arriving from the west ascend Jingmen, cross the Lu River, go ashore, and climb up to Wusa; those arriving from the south travel upstream to Chen and Gui, cross the vast waters of Lake Dongting, and only after another several thousand li reach Yuanzhou, scaling mountain passes and ridges. Their bird-paths twist through dense thickets, while Miao and other non-Chinese tribes appear and disappear on all sides. Amid the perilous stone steps, earth is piled up to build forts, occupying high ground to keep watch into the distance, sounding wooden clappers by day and gongs by night. The passes are opened only late in the morning, and patrolling soldiers must carry crossbows and follow closely behind before travelers dare set out. Scholars and merchants traveling back and forth are as if treading on a tiger's tail or walking on spring ice, and even so, in broad daylight brigands sometimes rob people and seize their gold. Under circumstances like these…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而謂保百年無事是目聽而耳食云耳不
特紆遲而危險特甚故議者紛然皆謂欲
開通西南二路非無所考見而漫為言也
甞考求故道在昔故多岐矣其小小間捷
之徑人不得並肩車不得方軌者置勿論
金沙江寬廣數里自麗江而下吞納滇洱
諸水徑達蜀江其為舟楫利涉行道之人
能言之
太祖高皇帝諭頴川侯謂關索嶺本非正道正
===
道乃在西北
聖謨具存乃土夷射利倡言為梗一疏鑿之民
固樂從昆明威楚羅婺之境皆可揚帆至
矣詢之土人稱僅有一二梗澀之處稍加
轉搬不過尋丈以天造地設之利棄之無
用舛也若東南之勢又大異是廣南一郡
便於入粤而艱於入滇去泗城不二百里
而近普安安龍商旅往來自粤者日夜不
絕在今仍為通衢且山徑平夷無盜賊出
punctuated: 而謂保百年無事，是目聽而耳食云耳。不特紆遲，而危險特甚。故議者紛然皆謂欲開通西南二路，非無所考見而漫為言也。甞考求故道，在昔故多岐矣。其小小間捷之徑，人不得並肩、車不得方軌者，置勿論。金沙江寬廣數里，自麗江而下，吞納滇、洱諸水，徑達蜀江，其為舟楫利涉，行道之人能言之。太祖高皇帝諭頴川侯，謂關索嶺本非正道，正道乃在西北。聖謨具存，乃土夷射利，倡言為梗。一疏鑿之，民固樂從，昆明、威楚、羅婺之境皆可揚帆至矣。詢之土人，稱僅有一二梗澀之處，稍加轉搬，不過尋丈。以天造地設之利，棄之無用，舛也。若東南之勢，又大異是。廣南一郡，便於入粤而艱於入滇，去泗城不二百里，而近普安、安龍，商旅往來自粤者日夜不絕，在今仍為通衢。且山徑平夷，無盜賊出
translation_en:
…and yet to claim that this guarantees a hundred years free of trouble is merely listening with one's eyes and eating with one's ears! Not only is the route circuitous and slow, it is also extraordinarily perilous. Therefore, commentators in great numbers all argue for opening up the two routes to the west and the south; they are not speaking groundlessly without investigation.

I have examined the old routes: in former times there were indeed many branching roads. Setting aside those minor shortcuts where men cannot walk shoulder to shoulder and carriages cannot travel abreast, the Jinsha River (金沙江) is several *li* wide; flowing down from Lijiang (麗江), it takes in the waters of Dianchi (滇) and Erhai (洱) and reaches straight to the Yangzi River in Sichuan (蜀江). Even passersby on the road can speak of the advantage it offers for boat navigation. Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (太祖高皇帝), instructed the Marquis of Yingchuan (頴川侯) that Guansuoling (關索嶺) was originally not the main route, and that the true main route lay to the northwest. The Sacred Counsels remain intact, yet native chieftains, seeking profit, spread talk to obstruct the plan. Once it is dredged and cut through, the people will surely follow gladly, and the territories of Kunming (昆明), Weichu (威楚), and Luowu (羅婺) can all be reached under full sail. When locals are questioned, they say there are only one or two obstructed spots, requiring slight portage of no more than a few *xun* or *zhang*. To cast aside as useless an advantage fashioned by Heaven and Earth is an error.

As for the topography of the southeast, it differs greatly from this. The prefecture of Guangnan (廣南) offers easy access into Guangdong and Guangxi (粵) but difficult access into Yunnan (滇). It is less than two hundred *li* from Sicheng (泗城) and is close to Pu'an (普安) and Anlong (安龍). Merchants and travelers going back and forth from Guangdong and Guangxi continue day and night without cease, and even today it remains a thoroughfare. Moreover, the mountain paths are level and even, without bandits appearing…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
沒所少者亭驛憩息耳土曠人稀原產銀
礦誠於此郡邇封許土著之民開鑿取利
以其七與民徵其三以為經營之費客貨
往來仍禁土人私斂官為定額稍資其入
以助官費之不足移維摩州於險地以彈
壓草竊不加賦於民而事集與跋涉黔中
﨑嶮之徑遠甚何憚而久不為此愚謂開
通此二道無大費而有巨利滇土故饒笮
馬僰童髦牛礦碌諸產舟車輻輳省負輓
===
之煩百貨增直一利也通二廣綿枲繒帛
貝釜遠方難至之物自此踵集滇民益以
富實二利也歲有荒歉可移民移粟三利
也士旅往來無紆遲間關剽掠之警人樂
遊其土四利也流落邊徼老幼孤寡得襁
負生還五利也水浮與陸走勞逸相縣人
情孰不舍勞而趨逸者自此傳置資糧皆
可次第裁縮紓官民之困六利也此又其
小者西南有事調發滇南勁卒西可制蜀
punctuated: 沒，所少者亭驛憩息耳。土曠人稀，原產銀礦，誠於此郡邇封，許土著之民開鑿取利，以其七與民，徵其三以為經營之費；客貨往來，仍禁土人私斂，官為定額，稍資其入以助官費之不足；移維摩州於險地，以彈壓草竊，不加賦於民而事集，與跋涉黔中﨑嶮之徑遠甚，何憚而久不為此？愚謂開通此二道，無大費而有巨利：滇土故饒笮馬、僰童、髦牛、礦碌諸產，舟車輻輳，省負輓之煩，百貨增直，一利也；通二廣，綿枲、繒帛、貝釜遠方難至之物，自此踵集，滇民益以富實，二利也；歲有荒歉，可移民移粟，三利也；士旅往來，無紆遲、間關、剽掠之警，人樂遊其土，四利也；流落邊徼老幼孤寡，得襁負生還，五利也；水浮與陸走，勞逸相縣，人情孰不舍勞而趨逸者？自此傳置資糧，皆可次第裁縮，紓官民之困，六利也。此又其小者，西南有事，調發滇南勁卒，西可制蜀，
translation_en:
… [no bandits] appear or disappear; all that is lacking are pavilions and postal stations for rest. The land is vast and the population sparse, and it originally produces silver ore. If in the nearby territories of this prefecture we truly permit the native inhabitants to mine and profit from it, giving seven-tenths to the people and levying three-tenths to serve as the expenses of management; if for the coming and going of merchant goods we still prohibit private exactions by the locals, while the authorities set a fixed quota, drawing slightly on those revenues to supplement the shortfall in official funds; and if we relocate Weimo Subprefecture (維摩州) to a strategic site to suppress petty brigands—then without increasing taxes on the people the project will be accomplished. This is far superior to trekking along the rugged, perilous paths through Guizhou; what is there to fear that this has not been done for so long?

In my humble opinion, opening up these two routes entails no great expense and brings immense benefits. The land of Yunnan is naturally rich in products such as Zuo horses, Bo servants, yaks, and mineral ores and malachite; when boats and carts converge like spokes at a hub, sparing the trouble of carrying on backs and pulling carts, all kinds of goods will increase in value—this is the first benefit. By connecting with Guangdong and Guangxi, goods from afar that previously reached here only with difficulty—such as cotton, hemp, silk fabrics, cowries, and cauldrons—will henceforth arrive in steady succession, and the people of Yunnan will grow ever more prosperous and substantial—this is the second benefit. In years of dearth and famine, people and grain can be shifted back and forth—this is the third benefit. Officials and travelers coming and going will be free from circuitous delays, arduous passes, and the alarm of pillage, so that people will gladly travel to the region—this is the fourth benefit. The aged, the young, the orphaned, and the widowed who have been stranded on the frontier marches will be able to return home alive with their children strapped on their backs—this is the fifth benefit. Traveling by water and trudging by land differ vastly in toil and ease, and in human nature who would not abandon toil and hasten toward ease? Henceforth postal relay horses and provisions can all be progressively curtailed and reduced, relieving the distress of both officials and the common people—this is the sixth benefit.

And these are still the lesser matters. Should trouble arise in the southwest, by mobilizing the strong troops of southern Yunnan, to the west we can hold Sichuan in check, …

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
東南可控百粵其或滇中有負固內訌反
側之憂如蒙段之割據皮羅思平之僭竊
呼召川蜀之兵自岷瀘西入揚旗搗壘則
邛笮以南無堅壁南檄百粵左言鳥章之
士不數日抵安龍廣南則鉦鼓相望於昆
池其或外侮窺我門庭連掣三省戰旅麻
列蝟合西指則吐蕃徙幕南馳則交夷不
敢高枕而臥施長組問包茅不入則哀牢
以西稽首納琛不敢猶豫趦趄利害較然
===
明若觀火執事者毅然行之吾滇人萬世
之利也豈特士旅之便已哉雖然此明問
之所及也愚生之憂又有深於此者荒服
之外氣運初開民多刀耕火耨其耕作不
及中國也土多磽确蕪萊相屬其生殖不
及中國也山谷冞阻民鮮懋遷其貨賄不
及中國也
祖宗淵思逖覽徙中國之人以充實此地官有
圭田民有分土二百年來生齒日繁衣冠
punctuated:
東南可控百粵。其或滇中有負固內訌反側之憂，如蒙、段之割據，皮羅、思平之僭竊，呼召川蜀之兵自岷、瀘西入，揚旗搗壘，則邛、笮以南無堅壁；南檄百粵左言鳥章之士，不數日抵安龍、廣南，則鉦鼓相望於昆池。其或外侮窺我門庭，連掣三省戰旅，麻列蝟合，西指則吐蕃徙幕，南馳則交夷不敢高枕而臥；施長組，問包茅不入，則哀牢以西稽首納琛，不敢猶豫趦趄。利害較然，明若觀火。執事者毅然行之，吾滇人萬世之利也，豈特士旅之便已哉？

雖然，此明問之所及也，愚生之憂又有深於此者。荒服之外，氣運初開，民多刀耕火耨，其耕作不及中國也；土多磽确，蕪萊相屬，其生殖不及中國也；山谷冞阻，民鮮懋遷，其貨賄不及中國也。祖宗淵思逖覽，徙中國之人以充實此地，官有圭田，民有分土。二百年來，生齒日繁，衣冠
translation_en:
…and to the southeast they can command the Hundred Yue. Or suppose that within Yunnan there should arise the trouble of rebels relying on natural strongholds and stirring up internal strife—like the separatist regimes of the Meng 蒙 and Duan 段 clans, or the usurpations of Piluoge 皮羅閣 and Duan Siping 段思平. One could summon the troops of Sichuan to enter westward from the Min 岷 and Lu 瀘 rivers, raising their banners to smash the rebel ramparts, and then south of Qiong 邛 and Zuo 笮 no stronghold would remain standing; and to the south one could dispatch a summons to the warriors of the Hundred Yue, with their foreign tongues and bird-emblazoned banners, who in a few days would reach Anlong 安龍 and Guangnan 廣南, so that gongs and war drums would be within sight and sound of one another all the way to Kunming Lake (Kunchi 昆池). Or suppose foreign aggressors should spy upon our frontier gates: by jointly mobilizing the combat forces of the three provinces, arrayed thick as hemp and gathered like bristles on a hedgehog, if we point westward the Tibetans (Tubo 吐蕃) will shift their tents afar, and if we gallop southward the Jiaozhi barbarians (Jiaoyi 交夷) will not dare sleep high on their pillows; if we cast the long cord of submission and call them to account for failing to send their tribute of bundled sedge, then from Ailao 哀牢 westward they will bow their heads to the ground and present their treasures, not daring to hesitate or falter. The advantages and disadvantages are crystal clear, as plain as looking at fire. If those in charge resolutely carry this out, it will be a benefit to us people of Yunnan for ten thousand generations—how could it merely be a convenience for traveling officials and merchants?

Even so, this is what Your enlightened question has touched upon; yet this foolish student has worries that go still deeper than this. Beyond the wild domain (huangfu 荒服), the civilizing influence has only newly opened up; the people mostly practice slash-and-burn farming, so their agriculture does not match that of the Central Plains (Zhongguo 中國). The soil is mostly stony and barren, with overgrown wastelands stretching one after another, so its productivity does not match that of the Central Plains. The mountain valleys are deeply obstructed and the people rarely engage in trade, so its wealth and goods do not match those of the Central Plains. Our Imperial Ancestors, with profound thought and far-reaching vision, relocated people from the Central Plains to populate and strengthen this region, granting official lands (guitian 圭田) to officials and allotting plots to the common people. Over the past two hundred years, the population has grown daily more numerous, and caps and robes of office…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
相望大抵皆中國之人耳邇者中土之民
攜負移徙就此耕鑿誠見土曠徵薄足以
容之耳萬一司計者不爲深慮度田定賦
一如內地則失其所望轉徙而之他可待
也愚生隱憂嘗謂滇之所患有二道路開
塞其患在外若其腹心之疾則在夷氛漸
勝而漢人不敵也蓋自宋人畫斧之外爲
僰濮夷玀盤據數百年一旦驅之爲我服
役蛟困涸溪虎號中野豈一日而忘巢穴
===
哉吾之氣勢日盛文敎日敷浸淫漸染則
彼皆良民吾之氣勢稍弱且賦斂煩重夷
漢離心則蕭墻之憂又有出於執事所詢
之外者譬之養身者宣暢其外而頤養其
中而後元氣與形神俱固爲國者開通其
險要保護其人民而後可以望鞏固而無
患至於邊徼之外夷情叵測譬之瘍癬之
疾閉關絕之不使詞喝我疆埸則內固外
攘如人身得兼養之術斯尤滇人所深望
punctuated: 相望，大抵皆中國之人耳。邇者中土之民，攜負移徙，就此耕鑿，誠見土曠徵薄，足以容之耳。萬一司計者不爲深慮，度田定賦，一如內地，則失其所望，轉徙而之他可待也。愚生隱憂，嘗謂滇之所患有二：道路開塞，其患在外；若其腹心之疾，則在夷氛漸勝，而漢人不敵也。蓋自宋人畫斧之外，爲僰、濮、夷、玀盤據數百年，一旦驅之爲我服役，蛟困涸溪，虎號中野，豈一日而忘巢穴哉？吾之氣勢日盛，文敎日敷，浸淫漸染，則彼皆良民；吾之氣勢稍弱，且賦斂煩重，夷漢離心，則蕭墻之憂又有出於執事所詢之外者。譬之養身者，宣暢其外而頤養其中，而後元氣與形神俱固；爲國者，開通其險要，保護其人民，而後可以望鞏固而無患。至於邊徼之外，夷情叵測，譬之瘍癬之疾，閉關絕之，不使詞喝我疆埸，則內固外攘，如人身得兼養之術，斯尤滇人所深望
translation_en: … in sight of one another, they are for the most part all people from the Central Lands. Recently, commoners from the interior, carrying their children and belongings, have migrated here to plow and dig wells, truly seeing that the land is vast and the exactions light enough to accommodate them. If by chance those in charge of fiscal planning do not give this deep thought, and measure the fields and fix the taxes just like in the interior, the people will lose hope, and we can expect them to move on to other places. In my private anxiety, I, a foolish student, have held that Yunnan suffers from two afflictions: the opening and blocking of roads is an external affliction; as for the disease of its heart and vitals, it lies in the native climate growing gradually stronger while the Han people are no match for them. Indeed, since the Song people drew the boundary with their jade axe, this region outside it was entrenched for several hundred years by the Bo, Pu, Yi, and Luo tribes. Once they were driven to perform labor service for us, they were like flood-dragons trapped in a dried-up creek or tigers roaring in the open wilds—how could they forget their lairs for even a single day? When our momentum and strength grow daily more flourishing and civilizing education spreads daily wider, gradually permeating and influencing them, they all become good subjects. But if our momentum and strength weaken even slightly, and moreover if taxes and exactions become heavy and burdensome, causing the native tribes and Han people to become alienated in heart, then troubles within our own walls will arise beyond what Your Excellency has inquired about. Compare this to nourishing the body: one must clear and circulate the exterior while nurturing the interior, and only then will the primordial vitality and the physical form and spirit both be secure. So too for those who govern the state: they must open up its strategic passes and protect its people, and only then can they hope for consolidation without peril. As for the unfathomable dispositions of the tribes beyond the frontier boundaries, they are like diseases of ulcers and ringworm: close the passes and cut them off, not allowing them to spy upon or threaten our borders [? 詞喝]. Then, with the interior secured and the exterior repelled, it will be like the human body attaining the art of dual nourishment. This is especially what the people of Yunnan deeply hope for…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text: 者惟執事財擇幸甚
punctuated: 者。惟執事財擇，幸甚。
translation_en: … for. Should Your Excellency judge and select from this, it would be a most fortunate thing.

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
萬曆壬午秋滇南復大比郡
國士御史董裕祗奉
明詔諸凡虔毖而其申飭文體特
勤貞一惟文章關乎世運蓋
自古記之考信先代始未嘗
不務體要而後乃漸漓也在
===
人挽之而已我
國家以經術取士洪永之文醇
朴蘊藉雖有巧心不可論工
拙所傳可覩也已更而奇再
更而麗乃今又異焉羣率而
爲玄虛謂之近體甚者去離
經傳踰越準繩以爲鮮而氣
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序
萬曆壬午秋，滇南復大比郡國士。御史董裕祗奉明詔，諸凡虔毖，而其申飭文體特勤。貞一惟文章關乎世運，蓋自古記之。考信先代，始未嘗不務體要，而後乃漸漓也，在人挽之而已。我國家以經術取士，洪、永之文，醇朴蘊藉，雖有巧心，不可論工拙，所傳可覩也。已更而奇，再更而麗，乃今又異焉，羣率而爲玄虛，謂之近體；甚者去離經傳，踰越準繩，以爲鮮，而氣
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the renwu year of the Wanli era (1582), Yunnan once again held the triennial examination to select scholars from the prefectures and principalities. The Censor Dong Yu 董裕 reverently obeyed the illustrious imperial edict; in all matters he was devout and cautious, and he was especially diligent in his injunctions regarding literary style. I, Zhenyi 貞一, reflect that literature is bound up with the fortunes of the age—a fact that has been recorded since antiquity. Examining the verifiable records of former dynasties, at the beginning they never failed to strive for fundamental substance, yet later on they gradually degenerated into superficiality; it simply depends on men to turn the tide back. Our Dynasty selects scholars on the basis of mastery of the Classics. The prose of the Hongwu (1368–1398) and Yongle (1403–1424) eras was pure, unadorned, and deeply reserved; even where there was ingenious thought, one could not judge it merely in terms of technical skill or clumsiness, as can be seen from what has been handed down. Afterward it changed toward the strange, and changed again toward the florid. Now today it has become different once more: people follow one another in bands to engage in abstruse emptiness, calling it the "modern style." In extreme cases, they depart from the Classics and their commentaries and transgress established standards, taking this to be novel, while the vital spirit…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
薄矣雖數勤
詔旨則曰有司者悅是也若是是
以訓之之道戒之也又何異
焉貞一今不自意獲執事於
此貞一不佞竊有慕夫王師
旦歐陽脩之能任也滇卽非
四方所視夫孰非聲教之區
焉拜聘以來矢天自許以爲
明
上指信士心是在今日故頃所推
擇主於矯偏習有能持循矩
矱雖質必錄非是雖工必黜
卽雅有時名或不在選然貞
一無顧也嗟夫亦足明貞一
punctuated: 薄矣。雖數勤詔旨，則曰：「有司者悅是也。」若是，是以訓之之道戒之也，又何異焉？貞一今不自意獲執事於此。貞一不佞，竊有慕夫王師旦、歐陽脩之能任也。滇卽非四方所視，夫孰非聲教之區焉？拜聘以來，矢天自許，以爲明上指、信士心，是在今日。故頃所推擇，主於矯偏習。有能持循矩矱，雖質必錄；非是，雖工必黜。卽雅有時名，或不在選，然貞一無顧也。嗟夫！亦足明貞一
translation_en: …has grown thin. Although imperial edicts have repeatedly urged reform, people say, "This is what the examiners are pleased with." If it is like this, then the very means of instructing them is used to warn them away from it—so what wonder is it? Now I, Zhenyii, unexpectedly have the honor of officiating here. Unworthy as I am, I privately admire how Wang Shidan 王師旦 and Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 were able to shoulder this responsibility. Even if Yunnan is not a place toward which the four quarters look as a model, how is it not a region within the reach of imperial prestige and moral instruction? Ever since receiving my letter of appointment, I have sworn before Heaven and promised myself that making clear the Sovereign's intent and winning the trust of the scholars' hearts rests upon this very day. Therefore, in our recent selection, we have aimed primarily at rectifying lopsided habits. Those able to uphold and follow standard rules and measures, even if plain, were certainly selected; those who did not, even if artfully wrought, were certainly rejected. Even some who have long enjoyed contemporary renown may not be among those chosen, yet I, Zhenyii, have paid that no heed. Alas! This is quite enough to show that I, Zhenyii,…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之不量其力也而又私惟滇
僻壤耳假令吳越諸國較短
論長不可同年語也猶然以
實求之未嘗缺人如皆有意
世運不以爲細故也者而力
挽之則所稱體要何渠不如
往也文既錄御史又顧而問
===
士行貞一則沉思乆之然後
敢對卽不盡中其實也庶幾
得五乎嚮者貞一觀其文矣
夫士之注思也神行其間其
平其陂若或傳之此非在其
聲律色澤也又非在其能深
談理趣而慷慨當時也貞一
punctuated: 之不量其力也。而又私惟滇僻壤耳，假令吳、越諸國較短論長，不可同年語也，猶然以實求之，未嘗缺人。如皆有意世運，不以爲細故也者，而力挽之，則所稱體要，何渠不如往也？文既錄，御史又顧而問士行。貞一則沉思乆之，然後敢對：「卽不盡中其實也，庶幾得五乎！嚮者貞一觀其文矣。夫士之注思也，神行其間，其平其陂，若或傳之。此非在其聲律色澤也，又非在其能深談理趣而慷慨當時也。貞一
translation_en:
…of not measuring my own strength. Yet I also privately reflected that although Dian [Yunnan] is merely a remote frontier—and were one to compare its shortcomings and merits with regions like Wu and Yue, they could not be spoken of in the same breath—nonetheless, when one seeks men here on the basis of substance, there is never a lack of talent. If all who are mindful of the course of the age, not regarding this as a trifling matter, exert themselves to restore standards, then why should what we call essential substance and form suddenly prove inferior to the past?

Once the essays had been selected for recording, the Censor again turned to ask about the moral conduct of the scholars. I, Zhenyi, pondered deeply for a long time before daring to reply: "Even if I cannot hit the mark of their reality entirely, perhaps I have grasped five out of ten! Just now, I, Zhenyi, have examined their writings. When a scholar concentrates his thoughts, his spirit moves within them; whether his mind is level or inclined, it is as though something conveys it into the text. This does not lie in its tonal meter or ornamental luster, nor does it lie in being able to discourse profoundly on the subtleties of principle or to speak with impassioned indignation on current affairs. I, Zhenyi,…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
嘗虛以遇之十不失一二惟
是今有心而求或不逮無心
也故曰五之云耳雖然固才
是求一或不適貞一又焉逃
貞一請以實要之夫實言乎
心之眞也知其一不知其二
之謂眞勵其始不倦其成之
===
謂眞故祿爵有所不動毀譽
有所不摇髮膚有所不愛惟
我
社稷之有利焉如營家室其有
二於事也若是者自古帝王
所側席而求拊髀而思者也
諸士無亦是務乎且今
punctuated: 嘗虛以遇之，十不失一二。惟是今有心而求，或不逮無心也，故曰五之云耳。雖然，固才是求，一或不適，貞一又焉逃？貞一請以實要之。夫實，言乎心之眞也。知其一不知其二之謂眞，勵其始不倦其成之謂眞。故祿爵有所不動，毀譽有所不摇，髮膚有所不愛，惟我社稷之有利焉，如營家室，其有二於事也？若是者，自古帝王所側席而求、拊髀而思者也。諸士無亦是務乎？且今
translation_en: … have received them with an open and unprejudiced mind, and in ten cases I would not miss more than one or two. Only, now that I seek them out with deliberate intent, perhaps I cannot match what happens without deliberate intent; therefore I said I might get about half right. Even so, since it is truly talent that we seek, if even a single one proves unsuitable, how can I, Zhenyi, escape blame? I, Zhenyi, beg to hold them to the standard of substance. Now, "substance" speaks of the genuineness of the mind. Knowing the one thing without being distracted by a second is what is called genuineness; striving from the beginning and not growing weary through to completion is what is called genuineness. Therefore, there are stipends and ranks by which they are not moved, slander and praise by which they are not shaken, and even their own hair and skin which they do not begrudge; they care only that our altars of soil and grain be benefited, tending to them as though managing their own households—how could they be of two minds in their service? Men such as this are those whom emperors and kings since antiquity have waited for on the edge of their mats to seek out, and slapped their thighs in longing to find. Should you scholars not devote yourselves to this as well? Moreover, at present…

title: 萬曆十年雲南鄉試錄
text:
主上加意名實其所登進必其朴
忠者其所廢辱必其儇媚者
固不得復藉云用非其求也
諸士勗哉貞一望諸士遠且
大不敢爲一方之說以隘若
心若無忘不佞之祝詞惟
天子使具能有裨世運則爾無畔
===
質貞一無虛要不佞與多士
果相與以有成也顧不休與
諸士勗哉
浙江處州府青田縣儒學教
諭倫貞一謹序
punctuated:
主上加意名實，其所登進，必其朴忠者；其所廢辱，必其儇媚者，固不得復藉云「用非其求」也。諸士勗哉！貞一望諸士遠且大，不敢爲一方之說以隘若心。若無忘不佞之祝詞，惟天子使，具能有裨世運，則爾無畔質，貞一無虛要，不佞與多士果相與以有成也，顧不休與？諸士勗哉！
浙江處州府青田縣儒學教諭倫貞一謹序。
translation_en:
… His Majesty pays close attention to matching reputation with reality. Those whom he elevates and advances are invariably the simple and loyal, while those whom he casts aside and disgraces are invariably the slick and fawning. One certainly can no longer make the excuse that "what is put to use is not what was sought." Strive on, gentlemen!

I, Zhenyi, hold far-reaching and great hopes for you gentlemen, and do not dare to offer parochial words that would narrow your minds. If you do not forget my words of exhortation, and in answering the Son of Heaven's call to service you are all able to benefit the fortunes of the age, then you will not have betrayed your pledge, and I, Zhenyi, will not have made an empty pact. You many gentlemen and I will truly have helped one another to achieve success—would that not be splendid? Strive on, gentlemen!

Respectfully prefaced by Lun Zhenyi 倫貞一, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qingtian County in Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.
